measurements.name: Appendiceal diameter
measurements.method: Measure outer wall to outer wall on a true short axis.
measurements.pitfall: Diameter alone does not distinguish a faeces-filled normal appendix from inflammation.

measurements.name: Abscess
measurements.method: Measure three dimensions and document location and adjacent structures.
measurements.pitfall: Phlegmon without liquefaction is not a drainable fluid collection.

sources.title: Appendicitis - Pitfalls in US and CT diagnosis

steps.label: Identify the appendix
steps.detail: State whether the appendix is completely, partially or not visualised, and where it lies.

normal.APPENDIX IDENTIFICATION: Normal appendix visualised from base to tip.

findings: Appendix visualised in a [retrocaecal / pelvic / subhepatic] position; tip included.
Appendix only partially visualised; the tip is not seen.
Appendix not visualised; this does not exclude appendicitis.
steps.look: Ultrasound: follow the caecum to the appendiceal base with graded compression and trace to the tip, including retrocaecal and pelvic positions. CT: follow the caecal pole to the tip on multiplanar images.
steps.tip: A non-visualised appendix is not a normal appendix; say which part was not seen.

steps.label: Wall, lumen and appendicolith
steps.detail: Assess outer diameter, compressibility, wall layers, flow or enhancement and appendicolith.

normal.WALL AND LUMEN: Appendix compressible with an outer diameter below 6 mm and a preserved layered wall.

findings: Non-compressible appendix with outer diameter __ mm and mural hyperaemia, compatible with acute appendicitis.
Appendicolith __ mm at the [base / mid / tip].
Loss of the layered wall structure, raising concern for gangrenous appendicitis.
steps.look: True short-axis image of the appendix with and without compression; Doppler of the wall; CT axial and coronal images.
steps.tip: Inflammation can be confined to the tip; examine the whole length.

steps.label: Periappendiceal fat and fluid
steps.detail: Look for inflamed (echogenic, non-compressible) fat, local fluid and caecal wall reaction.

normal.PERIAPPENDICEAL CHANGE: No periappendiceal fat inflammation or fluid.

findings: Echogenic, non-compressible inflamed fat surrounding the appendix.
Small volume of periappendiceal fluid.
Reactive thickening of the caecal pole.
steps.look: Ultrasound around the appendix and caecal pole with compression; CT fat stranding around the appendix.
steps.tip: Inflamed fat is one of the most reliable ultrasound signs; the appendix is often found at its centre.

steps.label: Complications
steps.detail: Assess wall defect, extraluminal gas or appendicolith, phlegmon, abscess and obstruction.

normal.COMPLICATIONS: No perforation, abscess, phlegmon or obstruction.

findings: Periappendiceal abscess __ × __ × __ mm in the [right iliac fossa / pelvis].
Focal wall defect with extraluminal gas or appendicolith, compatible with perforation.
Inflammatory phlegmon without a drainable collection.
Small-bowel dilatation from the inflamed appendix (adynamic or mechanical).
steps.look: Ultrasound and CT around the appendix and in the pelvis for collections; bowel calibre for obstruction.

steps.label: Mimics and alternative diagnoses
steps.detail: Review the terminal ileum, caecum and colon, epiploic fat, ureter and adnexa when the appendix is normal or not seen.

normal.ALTERNATIVE FINDINGS: No alternative cause for the symptoms identified.

findings: Terminal ileal and caecal wall thickening with enlarged nodes, compatible with bacterial ileocaecitis.
Enlarged mesenteric nodes without another abnormality (mesenteric lymphadenitis).
Epiploic appendagitis: oval non-compressible fat lesion with a hyperechoic or hyperattenuating rim at the site of tenderness.
Right-sided colonic diverticulitis.
steps.look: Terminal ileum and caecal wall; colonic diverticula; focal fat lesions; right ureter and kidney; adnexa in women.
steps.tip: Right-sided diverticulitis, epiploic appendagitis and omental infarction mimic appendicitis clinically but are usually treated conservatively.

protocol: Review trauma mechanism, haemodynamic context and the phases actually acquired.
Use arterial/venous comparison for vascular injury and appropriate delayed evaluation for suspected urinary leakage.

Record actual contrast route, phases/timing, opacification, source coverage, motion/metal artefact and trauma/intervention timing. Unacquired arterial/excretory phases and absent or inadequate retrograde CT cystography remain unassessed; one phase or a parent model cannot supply temporal bleeding, ductal continuity, perfusion or complete trajectory.

checklist.label: Solid organs
checklist.detail: Map laceration, haematoma, devascularisation and hilar injury.

checklist.label: Bleeding
checklist.detail: Distinguish active extravasation from contained pseudoaneurysm using phase change.

checklist.label: Bowel/mesentery
checklist.detail: Look for wall defect, reduced enhancement, free gas and mesenteric injury.

checklist.label: Urinary tract
checklist.detail: Assess renal collecting system and bladder within protocol limits.

checklist.label: Associated injury
checklist.detail: Review diaphragm, vessels, bones and penetrating trajectory.

measurements.name: Organ injury
measurements.method: Measure laceration depth and haematoma extent using organ-specific grading definitions.
measurements.pitfall: One depth threshold cannot be reused across organs.

measurements.name: Haemorrhage
measurements.method: Record site and extent; compare focal contrast across phases.
measurements.pitfall: Single-phase imaging may not distinguish active bleeding from a vascular lesion.

classification.name: AAST organ injury scales
classification.version: Actual organ-specific scale and revision year; do not apply one year across organs
classification.applicability: Traumatic injury to the organ covered by the selected scale.
classification.summary: Describe the observed injury and unresolved extent first. Apply only the actual named organ-specific scale/revision supported by available source findings; grade remains limited or unassigned when its required evidence is unavailable. CT grade alone does not determine treatment.

pitfalls: A negative early CT does not exclude all bowel or pancreatic duct injury.
Routine excretory contrast in the bladder is not equivalent to a properly performed CT cystogram.
An early or limited CT cannot exclude every bowel, mesenteric, pancreatic duct or associated injury; retain injury timing, unavailable phases and unresolved interfaces.

Observed phase change must use actual corresponding anatomy, acquisition timing and blood-pool context. Absent growth or a single focal contrast appearance does not independently establish a contained vascular lesion or exclude active bleeding.
CT enhancement changes require actual acquired comparison and physiological context; a source colour or normal parent organ cannot establish perfusion, viability or infarction extent.

Free gas/fluid and a suspected tract require source-supported location and clinical interpretation; absent gas does not exclude contained or evolving injury, and dense clot does not independently prove its source.
A source-visible injury track, projected object or skin wound does not establish the full penetrating trajectory or every organ crossed; retain unresolved entry/exit and interfaces.

AAST revisions are organ-specific. The official resource lists renal 2025 and pancreatic 2024 revisions as well as the earlier 2018 spleen/liver/kidney revision; a generic 2018 label cannot supply every current scale. Numeric grade criteria require the actual applicable source and complete observations.
impression_prompts: Lead with active bleeding and immediately consequential injury.
Describe organ injury features before any named grade.
State urinary/bowel assessment limits and associated injuries.
escalation: Immediately communicate active haemorrhage, major vascular injury, hollow-viscus injury or urinary tract disruption.

steps.label: Solid organs
steps.detail: Map lacerations, haematomas, devascularisation and hilar injury in the liver, spleen, kidneys and pancreas.

normal.SOLID ORGANS: Solid-organ assessment: [adequate actual coverage/phases / limited / unassessed]. Each assessed organ/site, observations and unresolved duct/hilar extent: [ ].

findings: Splenic laceration __ cm deep with subcapsular haematoma covering about __% of the surface.
Liver laceration of segment [ ], __ cm deep, [not] involving the hepatic veins.
Renal laceration extending into the collecting system [with urinary extravasation on the excretory phase].
Pancreatic laceration at the [neck / body] raising concern for duct injury.
steps.look: Review each actually covered organ and acquired phase, source timing and artefacts. Record unresolved pancreatic duct, renal collecting-system and hilar interfaces; an early/limited CT cannot become intact organ/duct anatomy.
steps.tip: Describe the injury features first; the grade follows from them.

steps.label: Vascular injury
steps.detail: Distinguish active extravasation from a contained pseudoaneurysm or arteriovenous fistula using the change between phases.

normal.VASCULAR INJURY: Vascular/bleeding assessment: [adequate acquired phases / limited / unassessed]. Actual source phase/timing, observed vessels/contrast change and limits: [ ].

findings: Active arterial extravasation from the [ ] enlarging on the portal venous phase.
Contained vascular injury (pseudoaneurysm) in the [ ], __ mm.
Injury of the [renal artery / hilum] with [devascularisation / thrombosis].
steps.look: Compare actual corresponding source sites and acquired phases with timing and blood-pool context; record missing phases and uncertain vascular/bleeding extent.
steps.tip: Phase-change patterns support interpretation in context. A single phase, absent apparent growth or schematic colour cannot independently establish lesion containment, complete bleeding exclusion or tissue viability.

steps.label: Haemoperitoneum and haematoma
steps.detail: Describe haemoperitoneum distribution, retroperitoneal haematoma and the sentinel clot.

normal.HAEMORRHAGE: Haemorrhage assessment: [adequate actual field / limited / unassessed]. Assessed compartments, observed fluid/clot and unresolved extent/source: [ ].

findings: Haemoperitoneum in the [ ], with a sentinel clot adjacent to the [spleen / liver / mesentery].
Retroperitoneal haematoma in zone [1 / 2 / 3].
Small volume of free fluid without a solid-organ injury; bowel or mesenteric injury should be considered.
steps.look: Perihepatic, perisplenic, paracolic and pelvic spaces; the densest clot is usually next to the bleeding organ.
steps.tip: Fluid/clot patterns require source and clinical context. A dense adjacent clot suggests a possible source but does not independently establish every injured organ or exclude other bleeding.

steps.label: Bowel, mesentery and urinary tract
steps.detail: Look for bowel wall discontinuity, abnormal enhancement, free gas, mesenteric haematoma and urinary tract leak.

normal.BOWEL AND URINARY TRACT: Bowel/mesenteric assessment: [adequate source / limited / unassessed], observations/unresolved extent [ ]. Collecting-system/excretory assessment: [assessed / limited / unassessed]. Retrograde bladder cystography: [adequate actual study / limited / not performed], observations/limits [ ].

findings: Focal bowel wall defect with extraluminal gas at the [ ], compatible with perforation.
Mesenteric haematoma with bowel wall thickening and reduced enhancement.
Extraperitoneal bladder rupture with contrast extravasation into the perivesical space (CT cystography).

protocol: State the actual modality, clinical location of pain and contrast or ultrasound coverage; tailor the search to the supplied acute presentation.

Record actual CT/US/MRI or supplied radiographic source, coverage, contrast route/phases/sequences, distension, motion/gas/metal limits and patient/postoperative context. Ultrasound compression, tenderness/Murphy, motion and Doppler require actual assessment; CT attenuation/enhancement and MRI signal/diffusion require their acquired sources. Missing examinations/features remain unassessed rather than inferred from another modality or a parent model.

checklist.label: Pain Localisation
checklist.detail: Correlate the symptomatic site with the imaged abnormality.

checklist.label: Bowel And Appendix
checklist.detail: Review appendicitis, diverticular inflammation, obstruction and focal bowel disease.

checklist.label: Solid Organs
checklist.detail: Inspect liver, biliary tract, pancreas and spleen within the examination.

checklist.label: Urinary And Pelvic Structures
checklist.detail: Check obstructed urinary drainage and relevant pelvic causes.

checklist.label: Peritoneum And Vessels
checklist.detail: Look for free gas, collections, fluid and vascular causes.

pitfalls: A negative examination with incomplete visualisation does not exclude disease in the unseen region.
Pain location helps organise the search but does not independently prove the responsible organ or exclude alternative, remote or evolving pathology.
A nonvisualised appendix is not automatically a normal appendix; retain actual modality/adequacy, secondary observations and unresolved appendiceal extent.
Compression, sonographic Murphy/tenderness, peristalsis and Doppler are not supplied by a static CT/MRI image or source colour; absent or inadequate acquisition remains unassessed.
Wall thickening, adjacent fat change, fluid and nodes overlap between causes; these patterns alone do not identify a pathogen, histological diagnosis, full disease extent or tissue viability.
A negative plain radiograph does not exclude fluid-filled obstruction or every acute abdominal process; projection is not resolved soft-tissue wall/organ anatomy.
Unacquired contrast phases, sequences, limited ultrasound windows or incomplete pelvic coverage cannot supply a complete vascular, organ, urinary or adnexal exclusion.

Apply guidance in its actual patient/scenario scope. The ACR nonlocalised-pain topic primarily addresses adult nonpregnant patients; pregnancy, paediatric, postoperative and localised-pain questions require their applicable source and clinical context.
impression_prompts: An imaging approach to common causes of acute abdominal pain.
State the dominant abnormality, relevant extent and examination limitations.
escalation: Communicate suspected perforation, bowel ischaemia or another immediately consequential finding promptly.

steps.look: Start with the clinical pain site and assess actually covered related structures; record source modality, patient context and unassessed regions. Continue the source-supported survey rather than treating one quadrant as proof of a single cause.

steps.look: Review actual appendix extent, bowel/diverticular wall, lumen/transition and source complications. Nonvisualisation is not automatically normal; record ultrasound dynamic/Doppler or contrast-dependent findings only from their actual source.

steps.label: Primary tumour
steps.detail: Document the epicentre (anal canal or margin), greatest dimension, length and circumferential extent.
findings: Anal canal tumour, epicentre at the [level], greatest dimension __ cm, craniocaudal length __ cm, from __ to __ o'clock.
Anal margin tumour extending to the perianal skin.
Tumour extends cranially into the lower rectum __ cm above the anorectal junction.
steps.look: Small-field T2 oblique axial images perpendicular to the anal canal and coronal images parallel to it; DWI to confirm extent.
steps.tip: T category depends on tumour size: measure the greatest dimension in any plane.

steps.label: Sphincter complex
steps.detail: Map involvement of the internal sphincter, intersphincteric plane, external sphincter and puborectalis.
findings: Tumour confined to the internal sphincter.
Tumour crosses the intersphincteric plane into the external sphincter at __ o'clock.
Involvement of the puborectalis/levator ani.
steps.look: Coronal and axial T2 images through the sphincter layers.
steps.tip: Sphincter involvement is important for treatment planning but is not T4 disease.

steps.label: Adjacent organs
steps.detail: Check for direct invasion of the vagina, urethra, prostate, bladder or skin.

normal.ADJACENT ORGANS: Adjacent-organ assessment: [adequate / limited / unassessed]. Actual source-resolved organ and perineal findings: [ ]. Unresolved invasion or coverage: [ ].

findings: Direct invasion of the posterior vaginal wall (T4).
Tumour abuts the [prostate / urethra] without definite invasion.
Extension to the perianal skin and ischioanal fat.
steps.look: Axial and sagittal T2 images of the anterior boundary; look for loss of the fat plane with tumour signal within the organ wall.

steps.label: Regional nodes
steps.detail: Review mesorectal, internal iliac/obturator, external iliac and inguinal stations; describe non-regional nodes separately.

normal.NODAL STATIONS: Regional-node assessment: [adequate / limited / unassessed]. Actual station/side, node findings and source measurements: [ ]. Unresolved field or nodal characterisation: [ ].

findings: Suspicious [left inguinal] node, short axis __ mm, with [irregular border / heterogeneous signal / round shape].
Suspicious mesorectal and internal iliac nodes.
Enlarged common iliac or para-aortic node (non-regional, M1 if confirmed).
steps.look: Axial T2 and DWI from the aortic bifurcation to the inguinal regions; the field must include the groins.
steps.tip: Inguinal nodes are regional in anal cancer, unlike in rectal cancer.

steps.label: Staging summary
steps.detail: Summarise imaging T and N with the named TNM edition and state what distant staging is available.
findings: Imaging stage cT__ N__ (TNM [edition]); distant staging on [CT / PET-CT] [pending / negative].
Extent uncertain at the [ ]; [ ] would clarify it.
steps.look: Combine size, organ invasion and nodal stations; distant disease needs CT or PET-CT.

protocol: Use multiplanar CT to define the abdominal wall defect, its contents and surgical relationships; document prior repair.

Record actually acquired CT field, contrast/phase, posture, strain/Valsalva if performed, source planes, motion/metal limits and prior repair. checklist.detail: Distinguish primary and incisional defects from rectus diastasis.

checklist.label: Defect Map
checklist.detail: Identify every defect and its position relative to the umbilicus and abdominal wall.

checklist.label: Contents
checklist.detail: Identify herniated structures and adhesional or obstructive effects.

checklist.label: Muscular Relationships
checklist.detail: Assess rectus muscles and the available abdominal wall for repair.

checklist.label: Complications
checklist.detail: Assess bowel enhancement, sac fluid and inflammatory change.

measurements.name: Defect dimensions
measurements.method: Measure the fascial aperture in orthogonal planes; name the level.
measurements.pitfall: Do not substitute sac diameter for defect width.

measurements.name: Source compartment volumes
measurements.method: If measured, report actual HSV and residual ACV, acquisition/posture, segmentation or approximation method, boundaries and explicitly chosen denominator.
measurements.pitfall: HSV/ACV and HSV/(HSV+ACV) are different measures; a sac diameter or guessed proportion is not validated volumetry.

pitfalls: A wide sac and a narrow fascial neck are different measurements.
Rectus diastasis may coexist with a true hernia; record each source-supported finding rather than using one label to exclude the other.
Static sac/content appearance does not independently establish reducibility or clinical incarceration; source-visible obstruction/vascular concerns and actual examination evidence remain separate.
Apparent bowel angulation or contact does not independently identify every adhesion or a specific band; retain unresolved contents, course and host interfaces.

Loss-of-domain definitions and denominators differ: specify hernia sac volume (HSV), residual abdominal cavity volume (ACV), actual method/source and HSV/ACV versus HSV/(HSV+ACV). A vague percentage of visceral volume or unvalidated sketch is not a measured ratio.
Measured aperture/sac/muscle ratios support planning but do not independently predict closure, compliance, pressure, respiratory tolerance or a guaranteed operative result.

Mesh material/plane and operative history may not be fully visible on CT; not visualised is not automatically absent. Fluid/gas near a repair does not independently establish microbiological infection.
Absent or inadequate contrast/dynamic sources cannot provide full enhancement, viability, reducibility or complication exclusion. Retain unresolved endpoints and source posture/field differences.
impression_prompts: Hernia anatomy, defect dimensions and complications for surgical planning.
State the dominant abnormality, relevant extent and examination limitations.
escalation: Communicate suspected strangulation or high-grade obstruction promptly.

protocol: Review prior studies and distinguish a true incidentaloma from an oncology or endocrine investigation.

Record actual noncontrast and contrast acquisitions/times, CT ROI representativeness, paired in-/opposed-phase MRI quality and any prior-study comparability. Do not apply incidentaloma pathways to oncology or endocrine presentations without their separate clinical context.

checklist.label: Context
checklist.detail: Record known cancer, symptoms and prior size.

checklist.label: Morphology
checklist.detail: Describe side, size, homogeneity, necrosis, haemorrhage and fat.

checklist.label: Lipid
checklist.detail: Measure unenhanced attenuation or paired chemical-shift signal.

checklist.label: Behaviour
checklist.detail: Compare growth using consistent planes and review local invasion.

checklist.label: Integration
checklist.detail: Separate imaging characterisation from biochemical function.

measurements.name: Unenhanced attenuation
measurements.method: For a homogeneous lesion, use a representative unenhanced ROI covering most of the lesion (ESE/ENSAT Table 4 specifies at least 75%) without surrounding-tissue contamination. Record heterogeneity; do not select a reassuring component to classify the entire heterogeneous mass.
measurements.pitfall: A postcontrast HU value cannot be used as an unenhanced lipid criterion.

measurements.name: Growth
measurements.method: Report absolute mm change and percentage using dated comparable studies.
measurements.pitfall: Different planes and partial volume may produce apparent growth.

pitfalls: Hormonal activity cannot be excluded by benign imaging morphology.
Washout overlap occurs in non-adenomas; do not diagnose an adenoma from washout alone in a discordant lesion.
A low-attenuation homogeneous adrenal lesion can be benign without proving adenoma histology; a nonenhancing cyst and a fat-predominant myelolipoma require their own composition assessment.
Small foci of macroscopic fat do not uniquely establish myelolipoma, and chemical-shift signal loss is not a universal adenoma or nonfunctioning-lesion diagnosis.
Keep ESE/ENSAT 2023 recommendations separate from the Seow 2025 proposed pathway adopted by the updated source; record the framework and its incidentaloma/endocrine eligibility.

Before considering biopsy, exclude phaeochromocytoma, confirm imaging remains indeterminate and confirm histology would change management. Suspected adrenocortical carcinoma needs expert assessment rather than routine biopsy.
impression_prompts: State whether imaging demonstrates a benign lipid-rich lesion or remains indeterminate.
Describe growth, heterogeneity or invasion that changes concern.
Relate any recommendation to the incidental, oncologic or endocrine context.

steps.label: Clinical context
steps.detail: Record whether the lesion is incidental, found during cancer staging or in an endocrine work-up, and any prior imaging.
findings: Incidental adrenal lesion; no known malignancy.
Adrenal lesion in a patient with known [malignancy], found on staging.
Endocrine work-up for [hypertension / Cushing / hyperaldosteronism / phaeochromocytoma].
steps.look: Referral information and all prior imaging that includes the adrenals.
steps.tip: A benign-appearing lesion can still be hormonally active; imaging does not replace biochemical testing.

steps.label: Morphology
steps.detail: Describe side, size, homogeneity, margins, necrosis, haemorrhage, calcification and macroscopic fat.

normal.MORPHOLOGY: Normal adrenal glands without a focal lesion.

findings: [Right / left] adrenal nodule __ mm, homogeneous and well defined.
Fat-predominant adrenal lesion, compatible with myelolipoma; soft-tissue components and discordant features: [ ].
Heterogeneous adrenal mass __ mm with necrosis and calcification.
Adrenal cyst with a thin wall and fluid attenuation.
steps.look: Axial and coronal images of both adrenals.
steps.tip: Predominant macroscopic fat and confirmed adrenal origin support myelolipoma. Small fat foci can occur in other tumours; assess the complete mass, soft-tissue components and discordant features. Current 3D context has no source adrenal-gland mesh; kidney meshes cannot represent gland or lesion morphology.

steps.label: Lipid characterisation
steps.detail: Measure unenhanced attenuation, or assess signal loss on chemical-shift MRI.
findings: Homogeneous lesion measuring __ HU on true unenhanced CT (10 HU or less), with benign imaging features; endocrine function assessed separately.
Signal loss on opposed-phase MRI, compatible with an adenoma.
Unenhanced attenuation __ HU; lipid-poor lesion, indeterminate.
steps.look: True unenhanced CT, representative ROI over most of a homogeneous lesion without outside-tissue contamination, and actual matched in-/opposed-phase MRI if obtained. Heterogeneity limits whole-lesion classification.
steps.tip: ESE/ENSAT 2023 requires homogeneity and true unenhanced attenuation of 10 HU or less for no further imaging, independently of size. Imaging does not settle hormonal function or uniquely prove adenoma histology.

steps.label: Contrast behaviour and discordant features
steps.detail: Interpret washout only with its protocol and context, and list features that do not fit an adenoma.
findings: Absolute washout __% and relative washout __% on a dedicated adrenal protocol.
Washout values favour adenoma but the lesion is heterogeneous; discordant features remain.
Marked enhancement with high T2 signal; phaeochromocytoma should be excluded biochemically.
steps.look: Record actual acquisition times and matched ROIs if a washout study exists. Historical absolute 60%/relative 40% thresholds have overlap and do not prove adenoma. ESE/ENSAT Table 4 lists cautious relative >58% evidence; the Seow 2025 proposal recommends abandoning washout for true incidentalomas.
steps.tip: Identify the selected framework and clinical population. Do not use a reassuring washout or focal chemical-shift loss to classify a heterogeneous mass as benign; imaging cannot exclude phaeochromocytoma.

steps.label: Growth and local extent
steps.detail: Compare size with prior studies and assess local invasion, nodes and the other adrenal.

normal.CHANGE AND EXTENT: No local invasion identified; contralateral adrenal without a focal lesion. Prior comparison: [date / unavailable]; interval change: [ ].

findings: Growth from __ mm to __ mm since [date] (__ mm, __%).
Invasion of the [IVC / renal vein / kidney], raising concern for adrenocortical carcinoma.
Bilateral adrenal nodules.
steps.look: Same plane and window as the prior study; renal vein and IVC; the contralateral adrenal.
steps.tip: Record size, homogeneity, true unenhanced attenuation and clinical context together. For an indeterminate lesion under ESE/ENSAT follow-up, significant growth requires more than 20% AND at least 5 mm in maximum diameter over 6–12 months. The source model does not depict adrenal/renal venous thrombus or tumour invasion; renal arteries cannot stand for veins.

steps.label: Aneurysm
steps.detail: Define the involved aortic segment, morphology and maximal outer diameter.
findings: Infrarenal fusiform abdominal aortic aneurysm, maximum outer diameter __ mm.
Juxtarenal / suprarenal extension with a __ mm neck.
Saccular aneurysm of the [ ] segment.
steps.look: Double-oblique multiplanar reformats perpendicular to the centreline; measure outer wall to outer wall.
steps.tip: Axial diameters overestimate a tortuous aorta; measure perpendicular to the centreline.

steps.label: Rupture
steps.detail: Identify active extravasation and retroperitoneal or intraperitoneal haemorrhage.

normal.RUPTURE: Rupture assessment: [adequate actual phases/coverage / limited / unassessed]. Source-observed leakage, haemorrhage sites/extent and containment uncertainty: [ ].

findings: Ruptured aneurysm with a left retroperitoneal haematoma extending into the [perirenal / pararenal] space.
Active contrast extravasation from the [left posterolateral] aneurysm wall.
Periaortic stranding without haematoma; contained leak cannot be excluded.
steps.look: Review actual contrast phases for leak and both retroperitoneal and peritoneal spaces for haemorrhage, including psoas, perirenal/pararenal, pelvic, perihepatic and paracolic compartments. State missing phases or coverage.
steps.tip: The absence of active extravasation does not exclude a contained rupture.

steps.label: Wall and thrombus
steps.detail: Describe crescent, fissuration, calcification gaps and posterior wall/vertebral draping in the actual source, with comparison and clinical context. An isolated sign does not establish the timing of rupture.

normal.WALL AND THROMBUS: Wall/thrombus assessment: [adequate actual source and comparison / limited / unassessed]. Observed wall/calcification/thrombus findings and unresolved boundaries: [ ].

findings: Hyperattenuating crescent in the mural thrombus/wall at [ ]; associated findings, symptoms and comparison [ ].
Focal discontinuity of circumferential wall calcification.
Draped aorta: the posterior wall drapes over the vertebral body without an intervening fat plane.
steps.look: Unenhanced images if available for the crescent; contrast images for wall contour and calcification.
steps.tip: An isolated hyperattenuating crescent is not necessarily a sign of imminent rupture. Assess symptoms, aneurysm size/growth and other CT rupture findings together; immediately communicate suspected rupture or contained leak.

steps.label: Branch vessels
steps.detail: Describe renal and visceral artery relationships and organ perfusion.

normal.BRANCH VESSELS: Branch/perfusion assessment: [adequate actual source / limited / unassessed]. Each observed renal/visceral origin, branch patency and organ enhancement finding: [ ]. Uncovered branches, phase and perfusion limits: [ ].

findings: Aneurysm neck __ mm below the lowest renal artery; neck length __ mm.
Accessory renal artery arising from the aneurysm.
Renal or bowel hypoperfusion.
steps.look: Trace actual coeliac, SMA, IMA, bilateral renal and any accessory renal branches through acquired multiplanar images; relate their origins to the neck and sac. Assess covered renal, bowel and visceral enhancement in the actual phase, retaining unassessed branches or organ extent.

steps.label: Iliac arteries and adjacent structures
steps.detail: Assess iliac extension, access-vessel calibre and possible fistulation to bowel or vein.

normal.ILIAC AND ADJACENT STRUCTURES: Iliac/access/fistula assessment: [adequate actual source / limited / unassessed]. Each side, vessel segment, source measurement and bowel/venous interface finding: [ ]. Repair history, unresolved tract/endpoints and planning limits: [ ].

findings: Common iliac artery aneurysm, [right / left], __ mm.
External iliac artery diameter __ mm (access).
Loss of the fat plane with the duodenum and gas in the aneurysm sac, raising concern for aortoenteric fistula.
steps.look: Trace bilateral common/internal/external iliac and common femoral arteries, with actual lumen/wall calibre, tortuosity and calcification. Review source-resolved duodenum/bowel and IVC interfaces and any prior graft/stent-graft. Retain incomplete access, landing-zone, tract or repair coverage.

measurements.method: Measure inner-to-inner, perpendicular to the duct at a stated site.
measurements.pitfall: Interpret with age, prior surgery and biochemical findings.

pitfalls: Duct calibre depends on context; a nonvisualised distal duct cannot be reported as stone-free.
A negative or limited ultrasound cannot establish clearance of unvisualised duct regions; persistent clinical suspicion requires appropriate specialist/risk-pathway assessment.
A dilated or nondilated duct does not uniquely establish or exclude a stone or active obstruction; integrate directly seen material, actual transition, prior surgery and clinical/biochemical context.
Apparent stone mobility, posterior shadowing and Doppler vessel discrimination require their actual source observations; a parent duct model or still frame cannot invent them.
Pancreatitis and cholangitis require clinical/laboratory integration. Morphology alone cannot establish their clinical diagnosis or severity.

steps.label: Duct visibility
steps.detail: State which segments of the common bile duct are directly seen.

normal.DUCT VISIBILITY: Directly visualised duct segments: [proximal / mid / distal]. Outlet/papilla seen: [ ]. Unassessed regions and limitations: [ ].

findings: Proximal and mid common bile duct visualised; the distal duct is obscured by bowel gas.
Distal duct seen to the pancreatic head.
steps.look: Subcostal and intercostal windows, patient in left posterior oblique or upright position to move duodenal gas; follow the duct to the pancreatic head.
steps.tip: A distal duct that is not seen cannot be reported as stone-free.

steps.label: Duct calibre
steps.detail: Measure the common bile duct and assess intrahepatic dilatation.

normal.DUCT CALIBRE: CBD inner diameter: [ ] mm at [site]. Interpretation in clinical/postoperative context: [ ]. Intrahepatic duct assessment and coverage: [ ].

findings: Dilated common bile duct __ mm with intrahepatic duct dilatation.
Common bile duct __ mm after cholecystectomy, without intrahepatic dilatation.
steps.look: Measure inner wall to inner wall, perpendicular to the duct, at its widest visible point; look for parallel-channel sign in the liver.
steps.tip: Duct calibre increases with age and after cholecystectomy; interpret it with the clinical and laboratory context.

steps.label: Intraductal contents
steps.detail: Look for an echogenic stone with shadowing, sludge or mobile contents.

normal.INTRADUCTAL CONTENTS: No stone or sludge identified in the visualised duct regions. Unassessed segments and limits: [ ]; this does not establish whole-duct clearance.

findings: Echogenic __ mm stone with acoustic shadowing in the distal common bile duct.
Intraductal sludge without shadowing.
steps.look: Scan along the duct in longitudinal and transverse planes; change patient position to show mobility. Record whether position changes and mobility were actually assessed, and use adequate Doppler when needed to distinguish vessels from ducts.
steps.tip: Positive source observations and negative-examination limits are separate. A limited ultrasound is not whole-duct clearance; use the actual clinical risk pathway when suspicion remains.

steps.label: Gallbladder
steps.detail: Look for source stones and signs of recent passage or ongoing obstruction.
findings: Multiple gallstones; gallbladder not distended.

measurements.name: Wall thickness
measurements.method: Measure the anterior wall perpendicular to its surface.
measurements.pitfall: Contraction and adjacent fluid can mislead measurement.

pitfalls: Wall thickening alone is nonspecific, especially in a contracted gallbladder or systemic oedema.
A sonographic Murphy sign is a directly assessed tenderness response, not an image feature. Do not prefill a negative result if it was not assessed or cannot be assessed reliably.
TG18 cholecystitis assessment combines local and systemic inflammatory findings with characteristic imaging; ultrasound alone does not establish the complete clinical diagnosis or severity.

A rounded or large gallbladder alone does not establish hydrops or ongoing obstruction; distension and shape require actual measurements, dynamic assessment where appropriate and clinical/timing context.
Apparent sonographic wall layers are not automatically separately resolved histological layers. A parent gallbladder envelope cannot supply wall thickness, intramural lesions or vascularity.

Characteristic intramural spaces and reverberation support adenomyomatosis, but a single comet-tail artefact does not exclude coexisting or mimicking malignancy; inspect complete wall/lesion and hepatic interfaces.
impression_prompts: Obstruction, inflammatory findings and causes of gallbladder wall thickening.
State the dominant abnormality, relevant extent and examination limitations.
escalation: Communicate suspected perforation or complicated acute cholecystitis promptly.

steps.label: Contents and gallbladder neck
steps.detail: Assess the mobility of stones or sludge and look for a stone impacted in the neck.

normal.CONTENTS AND NECK: No stones or sludge identified in the visualised gallbladder. Neck/cystic-duct visibility and examination limits: [ ].

findings: Multiple mobile gallstones, largest __ mm.
Stone impacted in the gallbladder neck, not moving with position change.
Sludge layering in the dependent gallbladder.
steps.look: Supine and left lateral decubitus scanning; follow the gallbladder into the neck and cystic duct.
steps.tip: Immobile neck material may support impaction only after actual position-change assessment. Slow movement, incomplete neck/cystic-duct visibility and clinical/timing context can limit interpretation.

steps.label: Distension
steps.detail: Assess gallbladder size and shape (hydrops).
findings: Distended, rounded gallbladder (transverse diameter __ mm), compatible with hydrops.
steps.look: Measure long and short axes and record shape, fasting/contraction and timing. If feasible, assess actual compressibility; a rounded contour or diameter alone does not establish hydrops.

steps.label: Wall
steps.detail: Describe focal or diffuse wall thickening, layers and vascularity.
findings: Diffuse wall thickening __ mm with a striated appearance.
Focal wall thickening with comet-tail artefacts, compatible with adenomyomatosis.
Irregular focal wall thickening or mass; gallbladder carcinoma should be considered.
steps.look: Measure the anterior wall perpendicular to its surface; Doppler for hyperaemia.
steps.tip: Wall thickening alone is non-specific: a contracted gallbladder, hepatitis, heart failure and cirrhosis all cause it.

steps.label: Local inflammation
steps.detail: Check the sonographic Murphy sign, pericholecystic fluid and inflamed fat.

normal.LOCAL INFLAMMATION: Sonographic Murphy sign: [positive / negative / not assessed or unreliable]. Pericholecystic fluid: [ ]. Clinical/systemic inflammatory context: [ ].

findings: Positive sonographic Murphy sign with pericholecystic fluid: findings support acute cholecystitis when integrated with the clinical and laboratory context.
Intraluminal membranes and irregular wall: gangrenous cholecystitis.
Gas in the gallbladder wall: emphysematous cholecystitis.
Focal wall defect with pericholecystic collection: perforation.
steps.look: Probe pressure directly over the gallbladder; pericholecystic fat and fluid.
steps.tip: Static images cannot prove tenderness response. Document whether and how it was assessed; TG18 diagnosis includes local/systemic inflammatory evidence plus imaging, and severity is not assigned from morphology alone.

steps.label: Bile ducts and systemic context
steps.detail: Review bile duct calibre and systemic causes of wall thickening.

normal.DUCTS AND CONTEXT: Common bile duct not dilated; no ascites.

findings: Common bile duct __ mm with intrahepatic dilatation.
Ascites and liver changes; wall thickening likely secondary to [cirrhosis / hepatitis / heart failure].
steps.look: Common bile duct calibre; liver, ascites and signs of heart failure.

pitfalls: Duct dilatation is a finding, not a specific aetiology; correlate the transition and morphology.

Imaging supports the anatomical component of cholangitis assessment but cannot diagnose or exclude the clinical syndrome alone; systemic inflammation and cholestasis require clinical/laboratory evidence.
Stricture length, shouldering, beading and enhancement overlap between inflammatory and malignant disease; no length threshold or isolated negative brushing proves benignity.

Bismuth–Corlette describes hilar ductal distribution, not complete staging or a standalone operative verdict; actual duct variants, vessel interfaces, lobar change and acquired distant disease remain separate.

escalation: Communicate suspected infected obstruction urgently when clinical deterioration is reported; imaging grades neither sepsis nor organ dysfunction by morphology alone.

steps.label: Duct distribution
steps.detail: Map intrahepatic and extrahepatic abnormalities and whether dilatation is focal, segmental or diffuse.

normal.DUCT DISTRIBUTION: No intrahepatic or extrahepatic bile duct dilatation.

findings: Diffuse intrahepatic and extrahepatic duct dilatation to the level of [ ].
Segmental intrahepatic duct dilatation in [segments].
steps.look: MRCP maximum-intensity projections and source images; CT or ultrasound duct-oriented images. Confirm branches and filling defects on actual source sections; describe unassessed anatomy and projection/partial-volume limitations.

steps.label: Duct morphology
steps.detail: Characterise strictures, beading and cystic dilatation.
findings: Multifocal short strictures with intervening dilatation (beaded appearance), compatible with primary sclerosing cholangitis.
Fusiform extrahepatic duct dilatation, compatible with a choledochal cyst (Todani type [ ]).
Saccular intrahepatic duct dilatation with the central dot sign, compatible with Caroli disease.
steps.look: Stricture site and length; alternating strictures and dilatations; saccular or fusiform cysts.
steps.tip: The central dot sign — portal radicles within dilated ducts — is characteristic of Caroli disease. Neither stricture length nor one imaging sign proves the entire clinical diagnosis; acquired anatomy and alternative causes remain relevant.

steps.label: Obstructing cause
steps.detail: Identify intraductal material, a mural lesion or external compression at the transition.
findings: Hilar stricture with enhancing periductal soft tissue, compatible with hilar cholangiocarcinoma (Bismuth–Corlette type [ ]).
Intraductal stones in the [ ] duct.
Extrinsic compression by [ ].
steps.look: Follow the duct to the transition; look for stone, enhancing wall thickening or an extrinsic mass.
steps.tip: Duct dilatation is a finding, not a diagnosis; the transition and its morphology point to the cause. Hilar ductal classification is anatomical distribution, not a standalone resectability decision.

steps.label: Liver and vessels
steps.detail: Assess lobar atrophy, liver lesions and portal vein and hepatic artery involvement.

normal.LIVER AND VESSELS: No lobar atrophy, liver lesion or vascular involvement.

findings: Atrophy of the [left] lobe with crowded dilated ducts.
Encasement of the [right / left] portal vein by tumour.
Intrahepatic mass with capsular retraction and delayed enhancement.
steps.look: Liver volume by lobe; portal and hepatic arterial relationships at the hilum.

steps.label: Context and complications
steps.detail: Record prior surgery, stents and signs of cholangitis, abscess or nodes.

normal.CONTEXT AND COMPLICATIONS: No imaging evidence of biliary abscess. Visible stents/drains and postoperative anatomy: [ ]. Clinical/laboratory assessment for cholangitis: [ ]; imaging alone cannot exclude it.

findings: Biliary stent in situ with pneumobilia.
Periductal enhancement and liver abscesses, compatible with cholangitis.
Enlarged hepatoduodenal ligament nodes.
steps.look: Surgical anatomy, stents and drains; periductal enhancement and liver abscesses.
steps.tip: Correlate suspected infected obstruction with systemic inflammation and cholestasis. Document device position and actual drainage anatomy; imaging alone does not establish infection or device patency.

classification.name: VI-RADS
classification.applicability: Multiparametric MRI evaluation of bladder-tumour muscle invasion, with treatment timing and quality considered.
classification.summary: Scores 1–5 express increasing likelihood of muscle invasion; combine T2 structure with diffusion and contrast findings using the published algorithm.

pitfalls: Post-TURBT inflammation can mimic muscle or perivesical invasion.

sections.body:
Further evaluation if indicated, with reason and timeframe: [ ].
Critical finding communicated to [ ] at [ ]; method [ ].
[Delete if not applicable].

notes: Treatment and poor bladder distension can impair VI-RADS assessment; state the limiting factor and avoid false precision.
Post-TURBT inflammation can mimic muscle or perivesical invasion.
VI-RADS estimates muscle-invasion likelihood; it is not histological staging.

steps.label: Lesion inventory
steps.detail: Number each lesion, record wall location, size, morphology and stalk.
findings: Single [papillary / sessile] tumour on the [left lateral wall], __ mm, [with / without] a stalk.
Multiple tumours: [locations and sizes].
steps.look: Small-field T2 in three planes with a well-distended bladder.

steps.label: T2 muscle interface
steps.detail: Assess the continuity of the low-T2 muscular layer beneath each lesion.
findings: Tumour with a stalk and thickened inner layer; the low-signal muscle is continuous (T2 score 1–2).
Loss of the low-signal muscle line beneath the tumour (T2 score 4).
Tumour extends through the muscle into the perivesical fat (T2 score 5).
steps.look: High-resolution T2 perpendicular to the tumour base.
steps.tip: A thickened, enhancing inner layer or stalk beneath the tumour indicates it is superficial.

steps.label: Diffusion
steps.detail: Look for concordant extension of restricted diffusion into the muscle.
findings: Restricted diffusion confined to the tumour with a low-signal stalk (DWI score 1–2).
Restricted diffusion extends focally into the muscular layer (DWI score 4).
Restricted diffusion extends to the perivesical fat (DWI score 5).
steps.look: High-b-value DWI and ADC matched to the T2 plane.
steps.tip: When T2 and DWI disagree, DWI is the dominant sequence for the final category.

steps.label: Dynamic contrast enhancement
steps.detail: Assess the early enhancement pattern at the tumour base.
findings: Early enhancement confined to the inner layer (DCE score 1–2).
Early enhancement extends focally into the muscular layer (DCE score 4).
Early enhancement extends through the wall into perivesical fat (DCE score 5).
steps.look: Early dynamic phase at the tumour–muscle interface.

steps.label: Extent and VI-RADS
steps.detail: Give the overall VI-RADS category and assess perivesical spread, adjacent organs, ureters and nodes.
findings: Overall VI-RADS [2]: muscle invasion unlikely.
Overall VI-RADS [4]: muscle invasion likely.
Overall VI-RADS 5 with extravesical extension to the [ ].
Tumour at the [left] ureteric orifice with hydroureteronephrosis.
steps.look: Integrate the three sequences; review the ureteric orifices, prostate or uterus, and pelvic nodes.
steps.tip: VI-RADS estimates the likelihood of muscle invasion; it is not a histological stage.

protocol: Review arterial and venous information available on the CT; state limitations if mesenteric vessel or bowel enhancement assessment is incomplete.

Record actual unenhanced, arterial and venous source acquisitions, vessel opacification, bowel coverage and assessment limits. Baseline high wall attenuation is not itself enhancement; unavailable phases cannot become normal vessel or enhancement statements.

checklist.label: Arteries
checklist.detail: Assess mesenteric arterial patency and any abrupt occlusion.

checklist.label: Veins
checklist.detail: Assess mesenteric and portal venous thrombosis or congestion.

checklist.label: Bowel Enhancement
checklist.detail: Map affected bowel and its enhancement relative to uninvolved segments.

checklist.label: Wall And Mesentery
checklist.detail: Evaluate wall thickness, dilatation and mesenteric oedema.

checklist.label: Advanced Injury
checklist.detail: Look for pneumatosis, portomesenteric gas and perforation.

pitfalls: Pneumatosis is not by itself proof of irreversible bowel injury; interpret the entire vascular and clinical pattern.
Patent large arteries do not exclude non-occlusive ischaemia; assessed vessel extent and clinical/physiological context remain necessary.
Apparent enhancement on a high-attenuation wall must be interpreted with actual unenhanced/enhanced sources when available; a model colour cannot provide perfusion.
Absent enhancement or a paper-thin wall can be highly concerning without independently establishing every layer of histological necrosis or a complete clinical viability verdict.
impression_prompts: Vascular findings and bowel changes in suspected ischaemia.
State the dominant abnormality, relevant extent and examination limitations.
escalation: Immediately communicate suspected acute mesenteric ischaemia, infarction or perforation.

steps.label: Mesenteric arteries
steps.detail: Assess coeliac, SMA and IMA patency, emboli and ostial stenosis.

normal.ARTERIES: Arterial assessment: [adequate arterial data / limited / not assessable]. Visualised coeliac/SMA/IMA regions and branches: [ ]. Patency/abnormalities: [ ].

findings: Abrupt occlusion of the SMA __ cm beyond its origin, compatible with embolism.
Thrombotic occlusion at the SMA origin on a background of atherosclerosis.
Patent vessels with diffuse narrowing (non-occlusive ischaemia in the appropriate setting).
steps.look: Arterial phase axial and sagittal reformats along the SMA; emboli lodge a few centimetres beyond the origin.
steps.tip: An embolus typically lodges beyond the middle colic artery origin, sparing the proximal jejunum.

steps.label: Mesenteric and portal veins
steps.detail: Assess the SMV and portal vein for thrombosis and signs of venous congestion.

normal.VEINS: Venous assessment/opacification: [adequate / limited / not assessable]. Visualised SMV/portal regions and tributaries: [ ]. Findings: [ ].

findings: Thrombus in the SMV extending into the portal vein, with mesenteric congestion.
Mesenteric venous engorgement without thrombus.
steps.look: Portal venous phase; mesenteric venous arcades and mesenteric oedema.

steps.label: Bowel wall enhancement
steps.detail: Map the affected segment and compare its enhancement with normal loops.

normal.BOWEL ENHANCEMENT: Wall enhancement assessment: [adequate actual contrast/phase available / limited / unassessed]. Affected/reference regions and findings: [ ]. Baseline attenuation and comparison limits: [ ].

findings: Reduced/absent enhancement of a __ cm segment of [jejunum / ileum / colon].
Hyperenhancing, thickened bowel wall (reperfusion or venous congestion).
Paper-thin, non-enhancing wall, compatible with transmural infarction.
steps.look: Compare actual contrast phases, source baseline attenuation if available and adequately imaged reference bowel. Record absent/limited phases and affected field rather than assuming enhancement or perfusion.
steps.tip: Reduced or absent enhancement on suitable actual source images is concerning; compare adequately imaged reference wall and baseline attenuation. Unavailable enhancement is unassessed, and source colours or a still frame cannot establish complete clinical viability.

steps.label: Wall, calibre and mesentery
steps.detail: Evaluate wall thickness, dilatation, mesenteric oedema and fluid.

normal.WALL AND MESENTERY: No bowel wall thickening, dilatation or mesenteric oedema.

findings: Thickened oedematous wall with a target appearance and mesenteric fluid.
Dilated fluid-filled loops with mesenteric oedema.
steps.look: Wall thickness in distended segments; mesenteric fat and free fluid.

steps.label: Pneumatosis, venous gas and perforation
steps.detail: Look for pneumatosis, portomesenteric venous gas and perforation.

normal.ADVANCED INJURY: No pneumatosis, portomesenteric venous gas or free gas.

findings: Pneumatosis of the [ ] with portal and mesenteric venous gas.
Free intraperitoneal gas, compatible with perforation.
steps.look: Lung windows for gas in the wall, mesenteric and portal veins, and free gas.
steps.tip: Pneumatosis alone is not proof of infarction; interpret it with enhancement and the vascular findings.

measurements.name: Wall thickness
measurements.method: Measure perpendicular to a well-seen, sufficiently distended wall.
measurements.pitfall: Do not include luminal contents or adjacent fat. State local distension, measurement site/plane and source limitations; chart mean thicknesses are not patient-specific diagnostic thresholds.

pitfalls: Collapsed bowel and incomplete enhancement timing can mimic pathological thickening.
Record measured length and the named source scheme rather than treating differing focal/segmental/diffuse cutoffs as universal diagnoses.
Symmetric regular thickening can occur in neoplasia, including focal adenocarcinoma and segmental small-bowel lymphoma; appearance alone does not establish benignity.

Stratified/target appearance is nonspecific, and observable CT bands do not independently verify every histological wall layer. Intramural fat does not by itself diagnose chronic inflammatory bowel disease.
Wall hyperattenuation must be distinguished from enhancement using actual source acquisitions when available; vessel patency cannot be assessed without adequate opacification/coverage.
impression_prompts: Pattern-based evaluation of thickened bowel and associated mesenteric findings.
State the dominant abnormality, relevant extent and examination limitations.
escalation: Immediately communicate findings concerning for threatened bowel/ischaemia or perforation in the relevant clinical context; record the recipient and time.

steps.label: Length and distribution
steps.detail: Measure the length of involvement and name the affected bowel; length narrows the differential.

normal.DISTRIBUTION: Wall distribution assessment: [adequate / limited / unassessed]. Assessed bowel segments/distension: [ ]. Findings and unassessed extent: [ ].

findings: Thickening of the [ ] over a measured length of __ cm; local distension/coverage [ ], margins [ ].
Separate involved sites and intervening assessed bowel: [ ].
Focal/segmental/diffuse description under the named scheme [ ]; actual measured extent and limits [ ].
steps.look: Coronal reformats; follow the involved segment from start to end.
steps.tip: Record actual length and the named source scheme; length categories overlap across diseases and differ between teaching frameworks. A length band or diffuse colonic extent does not establish a specific diagnosis.

steps.label: Wall thickness and symmetry
steps.detail: Measure wall thickness and describe symmetry, regularity and margins.
findings: Symmetric, regular wall thickening of __ mm at [ ]; distension/measurement limits [ ]. Neoplasia is not excluded by symmetry alone.
Asymmetric, irregular or lobulated thickening of __ mm at [ ]; inflammatory and neoplastic possibilities require the actual distribution, adjacent findings and clinical context.
steps.look: Measure perpendicular to a distended wall; compare with adjacent loops.
steps.tip: Judge thickness in its actual distension and measurement context. Collapsed segments may limit assessment; regular/symmetric morphology and source chart averages do not establish a benign diagnosis.

steps.label: Attenuation pattern
steps.detail: Describe the mural attenuation pattern: white (hyperenhancing), grey, water target, fat target or gas.
findings: White/high-attenuation pattern: [observed wall and suitable reference]; actual enhancement versus baseline high attenuation [assessed / limited / unassessed].
Grey attenuation: [observed mild/reduced wall enhancement relative to suitable source reference on the acquired phase]; this pattern is nonspecific.
Stratified/target appearance: [actually visible inner/outer bands and intervening attenuation]. Histological layer assignment and cause remain interpretation, not proof from the pattern.
Intramural fat/halo appearance at [ ]; this finding alone does not diagnose chronic inflammatory bowel disease.
steps.look: Review the actual acquired unenhanced/contrast phases and adequately imaged reference wall. Record missing phases, baseline attenuation and unresolved wall bands.
steps.tip: Combine observed attenuation with actual phases, distension, distribution, mesentery and clinical context. Model colours and a still image cannot establish perfusion, every histological wall layer or complete bowel viability.

steps.detail: Assess surrounding fat, vessels and nodes.

Mesenteric fat stranding disproportionate to the wall thickening.
Mesenteric venous thrombosis.
steps.look: Mesenteric fat, vascular patency and engorgement (comb sign), and nodes.

steps.label: Lumen and complications
steps.detail: Review narrowing, upstream dilatation, collections and free gas.

checklist.label: Level
checklist.detail: Identify small versus large bowel and proximal/distal calibre change.

checklist.label: Transition
checklist.detail: Find one or two transition points and describe the cause.

checklist.label: Closed loop
checklist.detail: Look for a C/U configuration, converging vessels and mesenteric twist.

checklist.label: Viability
checklist.detail: Assess enhancement, wall thickness, fluid and pneumatosis.

checklist.label: Complication
checklist.detail: Search for perforation and an obstructing hernia or tumour.

measurements.name: Calibre
measurements.method: Measure maximum bowel diameter and name the segment.
measurements.pitfall: Diameter alone does not distinguish ileus from mechanical obstruction.

measurements.name: Transition/lesion
measurements.method: Record level, lesion length and separate transition points.
measurements.pitfall: A subtle second point may establish a closed loop.

pitfalls: A closed loop can involve only a short segment without generalised dilatation.
Preserved enhancement does not exclude evolving strangulation.
Adhesions may be suspected from context and exclusion of visible alternatives but are not proved simply by an unseen cause at a transition.
Pneumatosis, fluid, oedema or a whirl require complete anatomical and clinical context; no single sign supplies histological necrosis or a universal diagnosis.
The absence of suitable contrast/phase data must not become a normal-enhancement statement or proof of viability.
impression_prompts: State obstruction level, degree and likely cause.
Explicitly report whether a closed loop is present or suspected.
Describe ischaemic or perforation features.
escalation: Communicate suspected closed-loop obstruction, strangulation or perforation immediately.

steps.label: Level and calibre
steps.detail: Identify small- or large-bowel obstruction and distal decompression.
findings: Dilated small bowel to __ mm with collapsed distal ileum and colon: small-bowel obstruction.
Dilated colon to __ mm at the [caecum] with collapsed distal colon: large-bowel obstruction.
steps.look: Coronal reformats; small bowel over 25 mm and colon over 60 mm (caecum over 90 mm) are dilated. Calibre thresholds are descriptive; trace actual continuity, transitions and distal decompression rather than diagnosing mechanical obstruction from size alone.

steps.label: Transition point and cause
steps.detail: Find the transition point and name its cause.
findings: Transition in the [right lower quadrant] without a visible cause, most likely adhesional.
Transition at an [inguinal / incisional] hernia neck.
Transition at an obstructing mass in the [ ].
steps.look: Follow dilated bowel to collapsed bowel on multiplanar images; the small-bowel faeces sign usually lies just proximal to the transition.
steps.tip: The small-bowel faeces sign helps locate the transition point. An unseen cause is not proof of an adhesive band; assess actual alternative causes and clinical/surgical context.

steps.label: Closed loop
steps.detail: Look for two adjacent transition points, a C- or U-shaped loop, radial mesenteric vessels and a whirl.
findings: Closed-loop obstruction: U-shaped dilated loop with two adjacent transition points and converging mesenteric vessels.
Whirl sign of the mesentery, compatible with volvulus.
Caecal / sigmoid volvulus.
steps.look: Coronal and axial images of the loop configuration; mesenteric vessels converging towards one point.
steps.tip: A closed loop can involve a short segment without generalised dilatation.

steps.label: Viability
steps.detail: Assess wall enhancement, thickening, pneumatosis, mesenteric oedema and free fluid.

normal.WALL AND MESENTERY: Wall enhancement assessment: [adequate contrast/phase available / limited / not assessable on this study]; findings: [ ]. Mesenteric oedema/free fluid: [ ]. Viability limitations: [ ].

findings: Reduced wall enhancement with mesenteric oedema and fluid, raising concern for strangulation.
Pneumatosis of the obstructed loop.
steps.look: On appropriate actually acquired contrast images, compare the affected wall with adequately imaged reference bowel and examine mesenteric vessels/soft tissue. Without suitable contrast, state enhancement is unassessed.
steps.tip: Preserved enhancement does not exclude evolving strangulation; mesenteric oedema and fluid are early signs. Normal-looking enhancement is not a clinical guarantee of viability, and unavailable enhancement is not normal.

steps.label: Complications and cause
steps.detail: Search for perforation and an obstructing hernia or tumour, and any additional transition.

normal.COMPLICATIONS: No free gas; no hernia or mass.

findings: Free gas, compatible with perforation.
Incarcerated small bowel in a [left inguinal] hernia.
Internal hernia: small bowel clustered in the [left paraduodenal] fossa.
steps.look: Hernia orifices, free gas and all bowel segments.

checklist.label: Bowel Map
checklist.detail: Map involved small-bowel segments, skip areas and prior anastomoses.

checklist.label: Mural Activity
checklist.detail: Integrate oedema, ulcers and enhancement with diffusion.

checklist.label: Strictures
checklist.detail: Identify fixed narrowing and upstream dilatation.

checklist.label: Penetrating Disease
checklist.detail: Trace tracts, their endpoints and collections.

checklist.label: Mesentery And Comparison
checklist.detail: Assess mesenteric inflammation and interval change.

measurements.name: Disease and stricture length
measurements.method: Measure along the affected segment and record maximum upstream calibre.
measurements.pitfall: Use the same segment and adequate distension on comparison.

pitfalls: Poor distension may mimic disease.
Inflammation and fibrosis can coexist; diffusion alone does not quantify activity.

Describe the predominant observed phenotype and any mixed inflammatory/chronic features; low T2 signal or homogeneous enhancement does not independently quantify fibrosis or exclude superimposed inflammation.
DWI appearance requires actual diffusion and ADC/source context; diffusion alone does not establish activity, histological fibrosis or a malignant diagnosis.
Fixed narrowing requires actual persistence/temporal or repeated-source evidence; one poorly distended still frame cannot prove a fixed stricture.
A partial tract, covered pelvis or source colour does not establish every fistula endpoint or a complete dedicated perianal assessment.
Interval response requires matched source sites, comparable acquisition/distension and actual prior data; missing comparison cannot become no change or remission.
impression_prompts: Small bowel activity, strictures and penetrating complications.
State the dominant abnormality, relevant extent and examination limitations.
escalation: Communicate abscess, high-grade obstruction or suspected perforation promptly.

notes: Poor distension may mimic disease.

measurements.name: Bowel wall thickness
measurements.method: Measure perpendicular to the wall without including lumen or adjacent mesentery.
measurements.pitfall: Pressure, contraction and obliquity change the apparent thickness.

pitfalls: Bowel wall thickening is not specific for inflammatory bowel disease, and an incomplete survey cannot exclude remote disease.
Sonographic bands are acoustic interfaces and do not independently identify every histological layer; lost stratification alone is not proof of transmural inflammation or a specific cause.
Absent Doppler colour without adequate settings, source acquisition and technical assessment does not establish absent perfusion, absent activity or tissue viability.
Peristalsis, compressibility and persistent narrowing require actual real-time or repeated-source evidence; a still image cannot supply dynamic findings.

A source-visible partial tract, inaccessible pelvis or local collection cannot establish all endpoints or exclude remote penetrating disease; routine transabdominal IUS is not a complete dedicated perianal examination.

Bowel thickening, ulcers, nodes and fat changes can overlap between inflammatory, infectious and other causes; ultrasound alone does not identify the pathogen, quantify fibrosis or establish complete remission.
Comparison requires actual prior data, corresponding segment and comparable technique/compression/Doppler; missing comparison is not no interval change.
impression_prompts: Bowel inflammation and mimics on focused gastrointestinal ultrasound.
State the dominant abnormality, relevant extent and examination limitations.
escalation: Communicate suspected obstruction, abscess or perforation urgently in the relevant clinical context; technically limited or incomplete ultrasound requires appropriate further assessment rather than a blanket exclusion.

protocol: Use thin-section multiplanar CT with appropriate bowel and intravenous contrast assessment; state distension limitations.

Record actual bowel coverage/distension, source acquisitions and contrast phases, lesion/reference attenuation and vascular opacification. Unavailable phases or unassessed bowel/spread sites remain unknown; routine CT can miss small or similarly enhancing lesions.

checklist.label: Primary Site
checklist.detail: Localise the lesion and identify multiplicity.

checklist.label: Morphology
checklist.detail: Describe mural, polypoid or exophytic growth and enhancement.

checklist.label: Luminal Effect
checklist.detail: Assess obstruction, intussusception and aneurysmal dilatation.

checklist.label: Mesentery
checklist.detail: Assess desmoplastic reaction and nodal disease.

checklist.label: Spread
checklist.detail: Inspect adjacent structures, liver and peritoneum.

measurements.name: Tumour dimensions
measurements.method: Record maximum orthogonal dimensions and involved bowel length.
measurements.pitfall: Separate primary tumour from adjacent mesenteric mass. Record each actual lesion/component, acquisition plane, bowel distension and assessment limits; do not combine separate primary, mesenteric or nodal observations.

pitfalls: Different tumours can share appearances; describe the growth pattern rather than asserting histology from CT alone.
Small or similarly enhancing lesions may be missed on routine CT; a negative limited examination or parent bowel model does not exclude every tumour.

Growth/enhancement patterns overlap among GIST, adenocarcinoma, lymphoma, neuroendocrine tumours and benign mimics. Imaging cannot independently establish histology, mitotic/molecular grade or biological risk.
Describe actual vessel contact, residual lumen, source encasement and adjacent-organ interfaces; CT contact or a coloured model does not prove microscopic invasion or operative resectability.
Record the actual liver/peritoneal phases and field; absent visible deposits or enlarged nodes do not exclude small, occult or microscopic spread.
impression_prompts: Small bowel mass morphology, distribution and associated disease.
State the dominant abnormality, relevant extent and examination limitations.
escalation: Communicate suspected perforation, threatened bowel, clinically significant obstruction or active bleeding urgently in the relevant clinical context; record the finding, recipient and time.

protocol: Use the actual radiograph or CT coverage to localise the object; inspect CT multiplanar images for subtle sharp material.

Record actual modality, projection/planes, coverage, object visibility, source slice/window limitations and contrast availability. Radiographic overlap, magnification, CT partial volume and source artefacts can limit object number, extent and wall/vessel relationships; unassessed regions remain unknown.

checklist.label: Object
checklist.detail: Describe number, shape and visibility.

checklist.label: Location
checklist.detail: Identify the gastrointestinal segment and precise relationship to its wall.

checklist.label: Bowel Effect
checklist.detail: Assess wall thickening and obstruction.

checklist.label: Perforation And Collection
checklist.detail: Look for local gas, inflammatory change and abscess.

checklist.label: Migration And Adjacent Organs
checklist.detail: Trace proximity to vessels and organ penetration.

measurements.name: Object dimensions
measurements.method: Measure each actual source-visible object extent and relevant cross-sectional dimensions on suitable source planes, recording modality, calibration and complete-end visibility.
measurements.pitfall: Projection/magnification, partial volume, metal or motion artefacts and an unseen endpoint limit measurement; a model ruler cannot provide patient-specific object size.

pitfalls: Small sharp objects can perforate without extensive free gas; absence of a radiopaque object does not exclude ingestion.
Object composition and total number cannot be established from radiopacity, CT attenuation or a schematic alone; radiographic overlap can conceal additional objects.
Absent free gas does not exclude a contained or early perforation. State local wall, inflammatory and collection assessment limits.
A projected tip near a vessel or organ does not prove contact or penetration; use the actual source planes, opacification and interface visibility.
Migration requires reliable source comparison; differences in projection, coverage or bowel position cannot be treated as proven movement.
The cited ESGE 2016 framework concerns adults and upper-GI management; its timing/threshold rules are not universal paediatric or lower-GI instructions.
impression_prompts: Localisation of sharp foreign bodies and related complications.
State the dominant abnormality, relevant extent and examination limitations.
escalation: Communicate a perforating sharp object or threatened adjacent vessel promptly.

Escalate suspected oesophageal sharp-object or battery impaction, magnet-related injury, obstruction or other high-risk findings promptly in the appropriate age/location-specific clinical framework; document uncertainty and communication.

normal.OBJECT: Object assessment: [adequate actual modality/coverage / limited / unassessed]. Assessed regions and visible observations: [ ]. Overlap/conspicuity and unassessed extent: [ ].

findings: Linear source-visible object __ mm long at [ ]; actual attenuation/radiographic visibility, endpoints and measurement limits [ ].
Poorly conspicuous object or candidate structure at [ ]; actual modality/windows, differential material and uncertainty [ ].
steps.look: CT with thin sections and multiplanar images in bone and soft-tissue windows; radiographs for opaque objects.
steps.tip: Review suitable actual source windows and planes. Fish bones, wood and other thin objects vary in conspicuity; appearance alone does not establish material or exclude ingestion.

steps.label: Location
steps.detail: Identify the segment and the relation of the object to the bowel wall.
findings: Object within the lumen of the [ ].
Object traversing the wall of the [terminal ileum / rectosigmoid].
steps.look: Multiplanar images along the object: inside the lumen, crossing the wall or outside it.
steps.tip: Perforation usually occurs at angulations and narrowings: the ileocaecal region and rectosigmoid.

steps.label: Bowel effect
steps.detail: Assess wall thickening and obstruction.

normal.BOWEL EFFECT: Bowel-effect assessment: [adequate actual coverage / limited / unassessed]. Assessed wall/lumen and observed effects: [ ]. Limits: [ ].

findings: Focal wall thickening around the object.
Obstruction at the level of the object.
steps.look: The bowel wall around the object and upstream calibre.

steps.label: Perforation and collection
steps.detail: Look for local gas, inflammatory stranding and abscess.

normal.PERFORATION AND COLLECTION: Local injury/collection assessment: [adequate / limited / unassessed]. Assessed regions, wall/inflammatory/gas/collection findings: [ ]. Unassessed extent: [ ]. Absence of free gas alone does not exclude perforation.

findings: Localised perforation with a few extraluminal gas bubbles and fat stranding.
Abscess __ mm around the object.
steps.look: Lung windows for small gas bubbles; fat stranding and collections.
steps.tip: Sharp objects can perforate with little free gas; localised stranding may be the only clue.

steps.label: Migration and adjacent organs
steps.detail: Trace proximity to vessels and organ penetration, and change since prior imaging.

normal.MIGRATION AND ADJACENT ORGANS: Adjacent-organ/vascular and migration assessment: [adequate actual interfaces and source correspondence / limited / unassessed]. Assessed sites and findings: [ ]. Limits: [ ].

findings: Object penetrates into the [liver], with an abscess.
Tip lies adjacent to the [ ] vessel.
steps.look: Relationship of the tip to the liver, vessels and adjacent organs; the prior study.
steps.tip: Projected proximity is not proof of organ/vessel penetration. Record actual interface planes, opacification and reliable prior correspondence; a schematic cannot establish injury or migration.

protocol: Extend the abdominal examination to the lung bases, pleura, pericardium (subxiphoid window) and the chest wall at the site of maximal tenderness, using curvilinear and high-frequency probes.
Record patient position and the regions examined; ultrasound only shows lung that reaches the pleural surface.

checklist.label: Lung bases
checklist.detail: Look above each hemidiaphragm for consolidation with air bronchograms.

checklist.label: Pleura
checklist.detail: Assess pleural fluid, its echogenicity and lung sliding.

checklist.label: Peripheral lung lesions
checklist.detail: Look for pleural-based hypoechoic lesions that may represent infarcts in suspected pulmonary embolism.

checklist.label: Pericardium
checklist.detail: Assess pericardial fluid from the subxiphoid window and signs of tamponade.

checklist.label: Chest wall and ribs
checklist.detail: Examine the point of maximal tenderness for cortical discontinuity and haematoma.

measurements.name: Fluid depth
measurements.method: Measure the maximal perpendicular depth of pleural or pericardial fluid and state the patient position.
measurements.pitfall: Depth is not volume; report position and distribution.

measurements.name: Lesion size
measurements.method: Measure the largest dimension of a consolidation or peripheral lung lesion in two planes.
measurements.pitfall: Only the pleural-based portion of a lesion is visible.

pitfalls: A normal thoracic ultrasound does not exclude central pneumonia or central pulmonary embolism; CT pulmonary angiography remains the test for embolism.
Pleural-based hypoechoic lesions are not specific; interpret them with the clinical probability of pulmonary embolism.
impression_prompts: Is there a thoracic cause — consolidation, pleural or pericardial fluid, a peripheral lung lesion or a rib fracture — at the site of pain?
Is further imaging, such as CT pulmonary angiography or chest radiography, needed?
Which abdominal causes remain unexcluded?
escalation: Immediately communicate features of cardiac tamponade or a large pericardial effusion; communicate lesions suggesting pulmonary embolism promptly.

steps.label: Lung bases
steps.detail: Look above each hemidiaphragm for consolidation with air bronchograms.

normal.LUNG BASES: Normal aerated lung bases with A-lines; no consolidation.

findings: [Right / left] lower-lobe consolidation __ mm with dynamic air bronchograms, compatible with pneumonia.
Parapneumonic consolidation with an adjacent small effusion.
steps.look: Intercostal scanning above the liver and spleen in longitudinal planes.
steps.tip: Dynamic air bronchograms (moving with respiration) favour pneumonia over atelectasis.

steps.label: Pleura
steps.detail: Assess pleural fluid, its echogenicity and lung sliding.

normal.PLEURA: No pleural effusion; lung sliding present.

findings: [Right / left] pleural effusion, depth __ mm, [anechoic / complex / septated].
Absent lung sliding at [ ]; pneumothorax should be considered.
steps.look: Posterior costophrenic angles in the sitting or supine position; high-frequency probe for sliding.

steps.label: Peripheral lung lesions
steps.detail: Look for pleural-based hypoechoic lesions that may represent infarcts in suspected pulmonary embolism.
findings: [Number] pleural-based, wedge-shaped hypoechoic lesions of __ mm in the [ ], suspicious for pulmonary infarcts; CT pulmonary angiography recommended.
steps.look: Systematic intercostal scanning of the painful area and both lower lobes.
steps.tip: A normal thoracic ultrasound does not exclude pulmonary embolism.

steps.label: Pericardium
steps.detail: Assess pericardial fluid from the subxiphoid window and signs of tamponade.
findings: Pericardial effusion, __ mm, [circumferential / localised].
Right ventricular diastolic collapse with a plethoric inferior vena cava: tamponade physiology.
steps.look: Subxiphoid view of the heart; inferior vena cava for plethora.

steps.label: Chest wall and ribs
steps.detail: Examine the point of maximal tenderness for cortical discontinuity and haematoma.

normal.CHEST WALL AND RIBS: No rib fracture or chest-wall abnormality at the site of tenderness.

findings: Cortical step in the [ ] rib with an adjacent haematoma, compatible with a fracture.
steps.look: High-frequency probe along the rib at the point of tenderness.
