normal.PREGNANCY CONTEXT: No intrauterine or ectopic pregnancy identified [pregnancy test negative].

findings: Intrauterine gestational sac with yolk sac [and embryo].
Positive pregnancy test with an empty uterus and an adnexal mass separate from the ovary, compatible with ectopic pregnancy.
Pregnancy of unknown location: no intrauterine or ectopic pregnancy seen.
steps.look: Endometrial cavity for a gestational sac; adnexa for an extraovarian mass.
steps.tip: An ectopic pregnancy moves separately from the ovary; a corpus luteum lies within it.

steps.label: Ovaries
steps.detail: Identify both ovaries and compare size, morphology and perfusion.

normal.OVARIES: Both ovaries normal in size and appearance.

findings: Haemorrhagic cyst of the [right] ovary, __ mm, with a lace-like internal pattern and no internal flow.
Enlarged [right] ovary __ mm with peripheral follicles and oedematous stroma, suspicious for torsion.
Ruptured corpus luteum with surrounding echogenic fluid.
steps.look: Transvaginal scanning of each ovary with Doppler.
steps.tip: Preserved Doppler flow does not exclude torsion; an enlarged ovary with peripheral follicles is the key finding.

steps.label: Adnexa and tubes
steps.detail: Assess masses, tubal changes and torsion-related findings such as a twisted pedicle.

normal.ADNEXA: No adnexal mass or tubal abnormality.

findings: Thick-walled, fluid-filled tube (hydrosalpinx / pyosalpinx).
Complex adnexal collection, compatible with tubo-ovarian abscess in the appropriate clinical setting.
Whirlpool sign of the vascular pedicle.
steps.look: Adnexal region between the uterus and pelvic sidewall; the pedicle for a whirlpool sign.

steps.label: Free fluid and other causes
steps.detail: Assess the amount and echogenicity of pelvic fluid and visible non-gynaecological causes.

normal.FREE FLUID AND OTHER CAUSES: Small physiological amount of free fluid only.

findings: Moderate echogenic free fluid extending to Morison pouch, compatible with haemoperitoneum.
Alternative cause: [appendicitis / ureteric stone / ovarian vein thrombosis].
steps.look: Pouch of Douglas, then Morison pouch if haemoperitoneum is suspected; appendix and ureters.
steps.tip: Echogenic fluid in the upper abdomen in a pregnant patient suggests significant haemorrhage.

steps.label: Anterior compartment

normal.ANTERIOR COMPARTMENT: Bladder wall and vesicouterine pouch normal; distal ureters normal.

findings: Bladder wall nodule __ mm at the [dome / base] with T2 low signal and bright foci.
Obliterated vesicouterine pouch with fibrosis.
Ureteric involvement with hydroureteronephrosis.
steps.look: Sagittal and axial T2 through the bladder dome and base.

steps.label: Posterior compartment
steps.detail: Map uterosacral ligaments, torus uterinus, rectovaginal septum and pouch of Douglas.

normal.POSTERIOR COMPARTMENT: Uterosacral ligaments, torus and rectovaginal space normal; pouch of Douglas patent.

findings: Thickened, nodular uterosacral ligaments [right / left / both].
Retrocervical (torus) nodule __ mm with fibrotic T2 low signal.
Obliteration of the pouch of Douglas.
steps.look: Sagittal and axial T2 along the uterosacral ligaments and behind the cervix.

steps.label: Bowel
steps.detail: Define the involved segment, depth of wall involvement and stenosis.
findings: Rectosigmoid nodule __ mm long, __ cm from the anal verge, involving the muscularis propria (mushroom-cap appearance).
Luminal narrowing of __%.
steps.look: Sagittal T2 along the rectosigmoid; distance from the anal verge.

steps.label: Uterus and complications
steps.detail: Assess adenomyosis, hydronephrosis and other implants or adhesions.
findings: Adenomyosis with junctional zone thickening __ mm and T2-bright foci.
Hydroureteronephrosis from ureteric involvement.
Abdominal wall endometriosis in the caesarean section scar.
steps.look: Sagittal T2 of the junctional zone; kidneys for hydronephrosis; abdominal wall scars.
steps.tip: A normal MRI does not exclude superficial peritoneal endometriosis.

steps.label: Primary tumour
steps.detail: Identify the cervical epicentre and measure the tumour in three axes.
findings: Cervical tumour __ × __ × __ mm centred on the [anterior / posterior] lip.
Distance from the tumour to the internal os __ mm.
steps.look: High-resolution T2 perpendicular (oblique axial) and parallel to the cervical canal; DWI.
steps.tip: FIGO stage IB depends on size (2 cm and 4 cm thresholds); measure in three planes.

steps.label: Stroma and parametria
steps.detail: Assess the low-signal stromal ring and true extension into the parametrium on each side.

normal.STROMA AND PARAMETRIA: Preserved low-signal stromal ring; no parametrial invasion.

findings: Full-thickness stromal invasion with an intact outer stromal ring.
Disruption of the stromal ring with nodular tumour in the [left] parametrium (FIGO IIB).
steps.look: Oblique axial T2 perpendicular to the cervix.
steps.tip: Parametrial invasion needs tumour beyond the disrupted stromal ring; expansion or oedema alone is not enough.

steps.label: Vagina and pelvic sidewall
steps.detail: Describe vaginal extent, pelvic sidewall involvement and hydronephrosis.

normal.VAGINA AND SIDEWALL: No vaginal, sidewall or ureteric involvement.

findings: Extension to the upper two-thirds of the vagina (FIGO IIA).
Extension to the lower third of the vagina (FIGO IIIA).
Pelvic sidewall involvement or hydronephrosis (FIGO IIIB).
steps.look: Sagittal T2 for vaginal extent; axial for sidewall and ureters.

steps.label: Bladder and rectum
steps.detail: Differentiate contact from mucosal invasion of the bladder or rectum.

normal.ADJACENT ORGANS: Fat planes with the bladder and rectum preserved.

findings: Tumour abuts the bladder wall with preserved low-signal muscle.
Tumour invades the bladder mucosa (FIGO IVA).
steps.look: Sagittal T2 of the bladder and rectal walls next to the tumour.
steps.tip: Bullous oedema of the bladder mucosa without tumour signal is not stage IVA.

steps.label: Nodes and other spread
steps.detail: Map suspicious pelvic and para-aortic nodes and other disease in the field.

normal.NODES AND SPREAD: No suspicious pelvic or para-aortic nodes.

findings: Suspicious [right external iliac] node, short axis __ mm, round with heterogeneous signal (FIGO IIIC1r).
Suspicious para-aortic node (FIGO IIIC2r).
steps.look: Axial T2 and DWI from the renal veins to the inguinal regions.
steps.tip: Nodal involvement upstages to IIIC regardless of the local extent; label it r (radiological).

measurements.method: Measure the thickest relevant enhancing component on a well-resolved image.
measurements.pitfall: Debris and motion on subtraction can imitate enhancement.

classification.name: Bosniak cystic renal mass classification
classification.applicability: Cystic renal masses in the general population characterised with an appropriate CT/MRI protocol, after excluding infection, inflammatory/vascular causes and necrotic solid masses; known hereditary RCC syndromes require individual specialist assessment.
classification.summary: Classify from enhancing wall, septa and nodules using v2019 definitions; record the feature driving the category.

criteria_table.title: Bosniak 2019 morphological quick key
criteria_table.scope: For appropriately characterised cystic renal masses with <25% enhancing tissue, after excluding other causes. This abbreviated structural key does not list every homogeneous CT/MRI benign exception; consult the full criteria for those patterns.

rows.criteria: Simple fluid, smooth wall ≤2 mm; no septa or nodules.
rows.report_note: A thin smooth wall may enhance.

rows.criteria: Up to three smooth thin (≤2 mm) septa; calcification may occur.
rows.report_note: Enhancing thin septa are allowed; see full benign exceptions.

rows.criteria: Smooth 3 mm enhancing wall/septum, or ≥4 thin enhancing septa.
rows.report_note: Check the additional MRI-defined IIF patterns.

rows.criteria: Enhancing wall/septa ≥4 mm, or irregular thickening with obtuse protrusions ≤3 mm.
rows.report_note: An enhancing nodule instead qualifies for IV.

rows.criteria: Enhancing nodule: ≥4 mm with obtuse margins, or any size with acute margins.
rows.report_note: State the nodule size and enhancement evidence.

pitfalls: Bosniak does not apply to a necrotic solid mass or an unexcluded infection.
impression_prompts: Cyst wall, septa, nodules and enhancement using Bosniak 2019.
State the dominant abnormality, relevant extent and examination limitations.

steps.label: Location and size
steps.detail: Localise the cystic mass and compare with prior size.
findings: [Right] upper-pole cystic mass __ mm, [exophytic / endophytic].
Unchanged in size since [date].
steps.look: Axial and coronal images of both kidneys; the prior study.
steps.tip: Bosniak applies to cystic masses; confirm that the lesion is not a necrotic solid mass or an infection.

steps.label: Contents and enhancement
steps.detail: Assess fluid, haemorrhagic or proteinaceous contents and true enhancement.
findings: Homogeneous fluid attenuation (−9 to 20 HU), no enhancement.
Well-defined homogeneous mass ≥70 HU on unenhanced CT with a smooth thin wall (Bosniak II pattern when the full v2019 criteria are met).
Enhancement of [wall / septa] (increase __ HU).
Heterogeneously hyperintense cystic mass on unenhanced fat-suppressed T1 MRI (Bosniak IIF pattern if no III/IV feature is present).
steps.look: Compare matched precontrast and postcontrast acquisitions: enhancement may be unequivocally visible or quantitatively confirmed (CT increase ≥20 HU; MRI signal increase ≥15% when reliably measurable with the same technique). Check subtraction for motion and misregistration.
steps.tip: Pseudoenhancement, partial volume and subtraction misregistration can mimic enhancement. A feature too small to measure and not clearly visibly enhancing is considered nonenhancing only on adequate source imaging; a non-diagnostic acquisition remains limited.

steps.label: Wall and septa
steps.detail: Describe the number, thickness and smoothness of the wall and septa.
findings: Thin (≤2 mm), smooth wall; no septa (Bosniak I).
1–3 thin enhancing septa (Bosniak II).
Minimally thickened (3 mm) smooth enhancing wall or septum, or ≥4 thin (≤2 mm) smooth enhancing septa (Bosniak IIF).
Thick (≥4 mm) enhancing wall/septa, or irregular enhancing obtuse protrusions ≤3 mm (Bosniak III if no enhancing nodule).
steps.look: Measure the wall and septa perpendicular to their surface on the best-resolved image.

steps.label: Nodules
steps.detail: Characterise enhancing protrusions and their margin with the wall or septum.
findings: Enhancing nodule __ mm with an [acute / obtuse] margin (Bosniak IV).
steps.look: Look for a convex protrusion: 4 mm or larger with an obtuse margin, or any size with an acute margin.

steps.label: Bosniak category
steps.detail: Give the Bosniak 2019 category and the feature that determines it.
findings: Bosniak v2019 category [ ], determined by [feature].
Category limited by [technique]; [MRI / CT] would clarify it.
steps.look: The highest-category feature present decides the category.

steps.label: Location and shape
steps.detail: Describe side, pole, exophytic or endophytic growth and whether the mass is ball- or bean-shaped.
findings: [Right] interpolar ball-shaped solid mass __ × __ mm, [exophytic / endophytic].
Bean-shaped infiltrative mass preserving the renal contour.
steps.look: Axial and coronal images; ball-shaped masses expand the kidney, bean-shaped masses infiltrate and preserve its shape.
steps.tip: Ball-shaped masses are usually renal cell carcinoma or oncocytoma; bean-shaped infiltration suggests urothelial carcinoma, lymphoma, infection or infarction.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Assess macroscopic fat, haemorrhage, calcification and necrosis.
findings: Macroscopic fat within a renal-origin mass, favouring classic angiomyolipoma in the appropriate imaging context; assess calcification, suspicious soft tissue and engulfed adjacent fat.
Central necrosis and calcification.
No macroscopic fat; homogeneous hyperattenuating mass (possible fat-poor angiomyolipoma).
steps.look: Unenhanced CT (fat below −10 HU) or MRI with and without fat suppression.
steps.tip: Macroscopic fat strongly supports classic angiomyolipoma but rare RCC exceptions exist. Opposed-phase signal loss alone does not establish macroscopic fat or a benign diagnosis.

steps.label: Enhancement and signal
steps.detail: Describe the enhancement pattern and relevant MRI signal.
findings: Avid heterogeneous enhancement (clear-cell pattern).
Low, homogeneous enhancement with low T2 signal (papillary pattern).
Central scar with segmental enhancement inversion (oncocytoma features, not diagnostic).

Invasion of the renal sinus fat.
Perinephric fat invasion within Gerota fascia.

findings: Contralateral kidney: [ ].

Metastases in the [ ].

steps.label: Background liver
steps.detail: Assess liver morphology, steatosis, cirrhosis and the clinical risk context.

normal.BACKGROUND LIVER: Normal liver morphology; no steatosis or cirrhosis.

findings: Cirrhotic morphology with signs of portal hypertension; verify LI-RADS eligibility and exclusions before applying it to observations.
Diffuse hepatic steatosis.
Known primary malignancy: [ ].
steps.look: Liver contour, caudate size, steatosis and signs of portal hypertension.
steps.tip: In a patient without cirrhosis or known cancer most small lesions are benign.

steps.label: Lesion map
steps.detail: Number each lesion and localise it by Couinaud segment.
findings: Lesion 1: segment [ ], __ mm (series __ image __).
Multiple lesions in both lobes, the largest __ mm in segment [ ].
Too small to characterise (under 1 cm) hypodensity in segment [ ].
steps.look: Use the hepatic veins (vertical) and portal vein bifurcation (horizontal) to name segments.
steps.tip: Clinical risk, prior malignancy, lesion features and acquired technique govern interpretation; small size alone cannot establish benignity.

steps.label: Enhancement
steps.detail: Describe arterial and later-phase behaviour.
findings: Peripheral nodular discontinuous enhancement with centripetal fill-in following the blood pool: haemangioma.
Homogeneous arterial enhancement, isoattenuating on later phases, with a central scar: focal nodular hyperplasia.
Arterial enhancement with washout: hepatocellular carcinoma should be considered.
Rim enhancement: metastasis or abscess.
steps.look: Compare the lesion with liver and blood pool on each phase.
steps.tip: A haemangioma follows the blood pool on every phase.

steps.label: Tissue characteristics
steps.detail: Assess fluid, fat, haemorrhage, T2 and diffusion signal and the hepatobiliary phase.
findings: Very high T2 signal (light-bulb), compatible with haemangioma or cyst.
Intralesional fat on opposed-phase images: adenoma or hepatocellular lesion.
Iso- or hyperintense on the hepatobiliary phase: focal nodular hyperplasia.
Restricted diffusion with hypointensity on the hepatobiliary phase.
steps.look: MRI T2, in- and opposed-phase, DWI and hepatobiliary phase when a liver-specific agent was used.

steps.label: Associated findings
steps.detail: Review bile ducts, vessels, capsular retraction, nodes and extrahepatic disease.

normal.ASSOCIATED FINDINGS: Bile ducts and vessels normal; no extrahepatic disease.

findings: Capsular retraction and peripheral duct dilatation (cholangiocarcinoma pattern).
Portal vein tumour thrombus.
Growth from __ to __ mm since [date].
steps.look: Portal and hepatic veins, bile ducts, the liver capsule and nodes.

steps.label: Eligibility and technique
steps.detail: Confirm the at-risk population, untreated observation and adequate multiphasic technique.
findings: Patient at risk for HCC (cirrhosis); multiphasic MRI with [extracellular / hepatobiliary] agent; adequate arterial phase.
Treated observation: the LI-RADS treatment-response algorithm applies.
steps.look: Cirrhosis, chronic hepatitis B or prior HCC; late arterial, portal venous and delayed or transitional phases.
steps.tip: Diagnostic LI-RADS applies only to the at-risk population and untreated observations.

steps.label: Observation map
steps.detail: Identify each observation by segment with its size and prior measurements.
findings: Observation 1: segment [ ], __ mm (previously __ mm on [date]).
steps.look: Measure on the phase where the margin is sharpest, avoiding the arterial phase if possible.

steps.label: Major features
steps.detail: Describe non-rim arterial phase hyperenhancement, washout, enhancing capsule and threshold growth.
findings: Non-rim APHE, washout and an enhancing capsule.
Non-rim APHE without washout or capsule.
Threshold growth: size increase of 50% or more in 6 months or less.
steps.look: Use the acquired late arterial phase for non-rim APHE. Washout: portal venous or delayed phase with extracellular agents or gadobenate; portal venous only with gadoxetate. Transitional or hepatobiliary hypointensity is not washout. Enhancing capsule: assess separately on portal venous, delayed or transitional phases as applicable.

steps.label: LR-M and ancillary features
steps.detail: Assess targetoid features suggesting non-HCC malignancy and ancillary features.
findings: Targetoid appearance (rim APHE, peripheral washout): LR-M.
Ancillary features favouring HCC: [nodule-in-nodule / mosaic architecture / fat / blood products].
Ancillary features favouring benignity: [ ].
steps.look: Rim APHE, peripheral washout, delayed central enhancement, targetoid diffusion; ancillary features such as fat, blood, restricted diffusion.
steps.tip: Ancillary features can adjust the category by one step but cannot upgrade to LR-5.

steps.label: Tumour in vein and category
steps.detail: Assess tumour in vein separately, then give the category and its defining features.
findings: Observation __ mm: non-rim APHE [ ]; nonperipheral washout on eligible phase [ ]; enhancing capsule [ ]; growth [ ]. Category [ ] after applying the v2018 size/feature table and checking LR-M/TIV.
LR-TIV: enhancing tumour in the [right portal vein].
LR-3: intermediate probability of malignancy.
steps.look: Portal and hepatic veins for enhancing soft tissue in the lumen.

steps.label: Pancreatic enhancement and necrosis
steps.detail: Distinguish interstitial oedematous pancreatitis from non-enhancing necrosis, with time since onset.

normal.PANCREATIC MORPHOLOGY: Pancreas normal in size and enhancement.

findings: Interstitial oedematous pancreatitis: diffuse enlargement with homogeneous enhancement and peripancreatic stranding.
Necrotising pancreatitis: non-enhancing [body/tail] involving about [<30% / 30–50% / >50%] of the gland.
Extrapancreatic necrosis only, with preserved pancreatic enhancement.
steps.look: Portal venous phase: pancreatic parenchymal enhancement; CT within the first days underestimates necrosis.
steps.tip: Necrosis may not be visible in the first 72 hours; early CT can underestimate it.

steps.label: Collections
steps.detail: Name and describe each collection by location, content, wall and time from onset.
findings: Acute peripancreatic fluid collection in the [lesser sac], __ mm, fluid only, no wall.
Acute necrotic collection __ mm with non-liquid debris.
Walled-off necrosis __ mm with a mature enhancing wall.
Gas within the collection raises concern for infection; correlate with instrumentation and possible enteric fistula.
steps.look: Assess each actual collection: fluid/debris, location, complete or incomplete encapsulation and symptom-onset interval. Do not classify maturity from calendar age alone.
steps.tip: A collection does not automatically become walled-off necrosis on day 28; describe the observed wall and necrotic content. Uncertain content or onset remains explicit.

steps.label: Vascular complications
steps.detail: Search for venous thrombosis, pseudoaneurysm and bleeding.

normal.VASCULAR COMPLICATIONS: Splenic, portal and superior mesenteric veins patent; no pseudoaneurysm.

findings: Splenic vein thrombosis.
Pseudoaneurysm of the [splenic / gastroduodenal] artery, __ mm.
Haemorrhage into a collection.
steps.look: Splenic, portal and superior mesenteric veins; arterial phase for pseudoaneurysm of the splenic or gastroduodenal artery.

steps.label: Duct and cause
steps.detail: Review the main duct, disconnected duct, gallstones and common bile duct obstruction.

normal.DUCTAL AND BILIARY FINDINGS: Main pancreatic duct normal; no gallstones or bile duct dilatation.

findings: Gallstones and bile duct dilatation raise concern for a biliary cause or retained obstruction; assess the actual duct and clinical context.
Necrosis across the pancreatic neck with viable upstream gland, raising concern for disconnected duct.

steps.label: Primary tumour and ducts
steps.detail: Localise and measure the tumour and describe duct obstruction and upstream atrophy.
findings: Hypoattenuating mass in the pancreatic [head], __ mm.
Double duct sign: dilated common bile duct and main pancreatic duct.
Upstream parenchymal atrophy.
steps.look: Pancreatic phase for the hypoattenuating tumour; curved reformats of the ducts.
steps.tip: An abrupt duct cut-off with upstream atrophy can indicate a small isoattenuating tumour.

steps.label: Arterial contact
steps.detail: Describe contact with the coeliac axis, common hepatic artery and SMA, including degrees and variant anatomy.

normal.ARTERIAL CONTACT: No contact with the coeliac axis, common hepatic artery or SMA; conventional arterial anatomy.

findings: Tumour contact with the SMA of __° over __ mm.
Encasement of the common hepatic artery (more than 180°).
Replaced right hepatic artery from the SMA.
steps.look: Review adequate pancreatic-protocol contrast phases and planes perpendicular to each vessel; record the actual contact angle, length, contour and named arterial variants. Do not assign resectability from the 180° descriptor alone.
steps.tip: Record variant artery origins, courses and tumour contact explicitly. Name the current resectability framework/version and treatment time point; imaging descriptors require multidisciplinary interpretation.

steps.label: Venous contact
steps.detail: Assess SMV and portal vein contact, contour deformity and occlusion.

normal.VENOUS CONTACT: No contact with the SMV or portal vein.

findings: Contact with the SMV of __° over __ mm without contour deformity.
Tear-drop deformity of the SMV.
Occlusion of the SMV with collateral veins.
steps.look: Review the portal venous phase and orthogonal vessel planes; record contact angle/length, contour, filling defect or occlusion, collateral routes and patent proximal/distal segments. Describe anatomy relevant to possible reconstruction; feasibility requires multidisciplinary surgical assessment.
steps.tip: After neoadjuvant treatment, persistent perivascular soft tissue or venous narrowing is not by itself proof of viable tumour or unresectability. Compare the actual prior examination and state uncertainty.

steps.label: Local extension
steps.detail: Inspect the duodenum, stomach, colon, mesocolon and retroperitoneum.
findings: Extension into the root of the mesentery.
Invasion of the duodenal wall.
Infiltrating soft tissue along the [named perivascular/neural pathway], concerning for perineural spread; CT does not establish microscopic invasion.
steps.look: Fat planes around the tumour and along the mesentery root.

steps.label: Metastatic disease
steps.detail: Assess the liver, peritoneum, nodes and other distant sites.

normal.METASTATIC DISEASE: No liver or peritoneal metastases; no suspicious nodes.

findings: Hypoattenuating liver lesions suspicious for metastases.
Ascites with peritoneal nodularity.
Suspicious para-aortic node (distant).
steps.look: Liver on portal venous phase; peritoneum and ascites; regional and distant nodes.
steps.tip: Resectability requires vessel, local-extension and metastatic review under a stated current framework and multidisciplinary judgement. Tumour size or contact angle alone is insufficient, especially after treatment.

measurements.name: Cyst, nodule and main duct
measurements.method: Measure each separately on matching planes and sequences.
measurements.pitfall: Apparent nodule size can include adjacent wall or nonenhancing debris.

classification.name: IPMN risk assessment — framework-qualified descriptors
classification.applicability: Presumed IPMN; not a universal algorithm for all pancreatic cysts or proof of histological malignancy.
classification.summary: For presumed IPMN, assess actual nodule/solid-component enhancement and exact duct calibre under the named framework. Imaging risk findings require clinical/cytological context and specialist assessment; this overview is not the complete guideline.

pitfalls: A pseudocyst diagnosis needs a compatible clinical context; cyst classification is separate from solid pancreatic cancer staging.
Duct communication alone does not establish IPMN; inflammatory collections may also communicate.
Presumed cyst type alone does not mandate resection; distinguish framework-specific assessment and complete clinical suitability.
Subtraction artifact, debris and wall partial volume can mimic a nodule; adequate source enhancement evidence is required.

steps.label: Cyst map
steps.detail: Identify location, number and size of each cyst and compare with prior studies.
findings: Solitary cyst in the pancreatic [head], __ mm.
Multiple cysts, largest __ mm in the [body].
Growth from __ to __ mm since [date].
steps.look: MRCP with T2 in two planes; CT for calcification.

steps.label: Morphology
steps.detail: Describe locules, septa, wall and internal contents.
findings: Microcystic (honeycomb) lesion with a central scar: serous cystadenoma pattern.
Unilocular or few-loculated cyst with a thick wall in the body or tail: mucinous cystic neoplasm pattern.
Cluster of grape-like cysts communicating with the duct: branch-duct IPMN pattern.
steps.look: T2 for septa and microcysts; CT for central scar calcification and peripheral calcification.

steps.label: Enhancing components
steps.detail: Distinguish an enhancing mural nodule from dependent debris.

normal.ENHANCING COMPONENTS: No mural nodule or solid component.

findings: Enhancing mural nodule __ mm; for presumed IPMN under Kyoto 2024, at least 5 mm is a high-risk stigma. State the actual enhancement evidence and framework.
Non-enhancing dependent debris.
Thickened, enhancing cyst wall.
steps.look: Use actually acquired pre/post-contrast source images and adequate subtraction; distinguish a real enhancing tissue component from debris, partial volume and subtraction/motion artifact.
steps.tip: Neither dependent location nor a single image proves debris or nodule enhancement. Report source-phase/sequence adequacy and uncertainty; no automatic treatment decision follows from this descriptor alone.

steps.label: Pancreatic duct
steps.detail: Assess communication with the duct, main duct calibre and abrupt change.

normal.DUCTS: No communication with the main pancreatic duct; main duct normal.

findings: Cyst communication with the pancreatic duct; branch-duct IPMN is a possibility in the appropriate context, not a diagnosis from communication alone.
Main pancreatic duct __ mm; for presumed IPMN under Kyoto 2024, 5 to under 10 mm is worrisome and at least 10 mm is high-risk. Assess other causes and the complete framework.
Abrupt change in duct calibre with distal atrophy.
steps.look: MRCP thick-slab and source images.

steps.label: Pancreas and context
steps.detail: Review pancreatitis history, other pancreatic lesions and interval change.

normal.PANCREAS AND CONTEXT: No other pancreatic abnormality; no signs of previous pancreatitis.

findings: Signs of previous pancreatitis; pseudocyst is a possibility.
Solid pancreatic lesion separate from the cyst.
steps.look: The rest of the pancreas; peripancreatic changes of previous pancreatitis.
steps.tip: A pseudocyst needs a history of pancreatitis; without it, treat the cyst as a possible neoplasm.

steps.label: Peritoneal spaces
steps.detail: Localise fluid or lesions to named peritoneal compartments.

normal.PERITONEAL SPACES: No free fluid or peritoneal lesion.

findings: Fluid in the [right subphrenic space / lesser sac / pouch of Douglas].
Loculated collection in the [ ].
steps.look: Supramesocolic (subphrenic, subhepatic, lesser sac) and inframesocolic spaces, paracolic gutters and pelvis.
steps.tip: Peritoneal fluid flows along predictable routes; the right paracolic gutter connects the pelvis with the subphrenic space.

steps.label: Omentum and mesentery
steps.detail: Describe infiltration, masses and vessel relationships.
findings: Misty mesentery with a fat halo around vessels (sclerosing mesenteritis pattern).
Omental infiltration / cake.
Mesenteric mass __ mm encasing vessels.
steps.look: Greater omentum, small-bowel mesentery and transverse and sigmoid mesocolon.

steps.label: Bowel relationships
steps.detail: Identify displacement, tethering, retraction and associated bowel wall abnormality.
findings: Tethering and retraction of small-bowel loops towards a mesenteric mass.
Displacement of bowel loops by a cystic mass.
steps.look: Bowel loops around the lesion; mesenteric retraction.

steps.label: Lesion composition
steps.detail: Assess enhancement, fat, cystic change and calcification.
findings: Thin-walled multiloculated cyst insinuating between structures (lymphangioma pattern).
Low-attenuation mucinous ascites scalloping the liver surface (pseudomyxoma peritonei pattern).
Solid enhancing nodules (peritoneal metastases).
steps.look: Attenuation and enhancement of the lesion; thin-walled versus complex cysts.
steps.tip: Scalloping of the liver and spleen surfaces suggests mucinous ascites rather than simple fluid.

steps.label: Associated disease
steps.detail: Review the retroperitoneum, organs, nodes and complications.

normal.ASSOCIATED DISEASE: No associated organ abnormality or nodes.

findings: Possible primary in the [appendix / ovary / stomach].
Enlarged mesenteric nodes.
Small-bowel obstruction from peritoneal disease.
steps.look: Primary organ sources, nodes and bowel obstruction.

protocol: Check T2, high-b DWI/ADC and DCE quality separately and record prior biopsy/treatment.
Use the comprehensive prostate template; match lesion numbers and sector locations across every sequence.

checklist.label: Clinical context
checklist.detail: Record PSA/date, gland volume, prior biopsy and relevant treatment.

checklist.label: Zonal anatomy
checklist.detail: Locate each lesion by zone, side, level and sector.

checklist.label: Scoring
checklist.detail: Use DWI as dominant in peripheral zone and T2 in transition zone with v2.1 adjustment rules.

checklist.label: Local extension
checklist.detail: Assess capsule, neurovascular bundles, seminal vesicles and adjacent organs.

checklist.label: Beyond gland
checklist.detail: Review pelvic nodes and imaged bones, acknowledging their assessment limits.

measurements.name: Gland volume and PSA density
measurements.method: Use ellipsoid AP×transverse×longitudinal×0.52 in cm or segmentation; PSA density=PSA/volume.
measurements.pitfall: Record the PSA date and volume method; density is not a PI-RADS scoring input.

measurements.name: Lesion dimension
measurements.method: Measure largest dimension on ADC for PZ or T2 for TZ where adequately defined; record plane/sequence.
measurements.pitfall: DWI score 5 needs the specified ≥1.5 cm size or definite invasive behaviour criterion.

measurements.name: Capsular contact
measurements.method: Record contact length and direct extension findings separately.
measurements.pitfall: Contact length alone does not prove extraprostatic extension.

classification.name: PI-RADS
classification.applicability: Detection and localisation of clinically significant prostate cancer in the untreated prostate using an adequate examination.
classification.summary: Use the zone-specific dominant sequence and published adjustment rules. The category expresses suspicion, separately from PSA density, stage and management.

pitfalls: Prostatitis, BPH nodules and haemorrhage can imitate cancer.
PI-RADS v2.1 is not the post-treatment recurrence scoring system.
impression_prompts: State index lesion number, sector and PI-RADS category.
Summarise local extension and pelvic findings separately from suspicion score.
Record gland volume, PSA density when available and material image-quality limits.

criteria_table.title: PI-RADS v2.1 zonal combination rules
criteria_table.scope: Use diagnostic-quality T2 and DWI, with sequence scores already established. These are combination rules, not definitions of sequence scores. Mark absent or inadequate components X and use the official fallback tables.

sections.body:
Lesion [number]; index [yes/no].
Location [side, base/mid/apex, zone and sector(s)].
Size [ ] mm; sequence/plane [ ]; series/image [ ].

ADC/high-b DWI appearance [ ]; DWI score [1–5].

Margin contact [ ]; extension [ ].
Overall PI-RADS [1–5]; scoring rationale [ ].
Comparison change [ ].

sections.heading: SCORING CHECK
sections.body:
PZ: DWI determines the category; DWI 3 becomes PI-RADS 4 only with positive DCE. Positive DCE requires focal early enhancement corresponding to the suspicious finding.
TZ: T2 determines the category, except T2 2 with DWI ≥4 becomes PI-RADS 3, and T2 3 with DWI 5 becomes PI-RADS 4. DCE does not upgrade TZ lesions.
A score-4-pattern lesion is score 5 on the relevant sequence at ≥1.5 cm or with definite extraprostatic extension/invasion.
No DCE means no DCE-based upgrade. If DWI is inadequate, consult the PI-RADS alternative-assessment table and state the limitation.

sections.heading: LOCAL EXTENT
sections.body:
Extraprostatic extension [absent / equivocal / present: site and evidence].
Neurovascular bundles [ ]; seminal vesicles [ ]; bladder neck [ ]; external sphincter [ ]; adjacent organs [ ].
MRI local-stage assessment when applicable [ ].

sections.heading: NODES / BONES / OTHER PELVIC FINDINGS
sections.body:
Suspicious nodes [none / station, short axis and morphology].
Bones within coverage [ ]. Other pelvic findings [ ].

sections.heading: IMPRESSION
sections.body:
1. Index lesion [site, size], PI-RADS [ ]; additional lesions [ ].
2. Local extension [ ]; suspicious nodes/bone findings [ ].
3. Volume [ ] mL; PSA density [ ].
4. Comparison and material limitation [ ].
5. Individualised next-step discussion, if appropriate [ ].

notes: PI-RADS categories express imaging suspicion: 1 very low; 2 low; 3 equivocal; 4 high; 5 very high likelihood of clinically significant cancer. They do not independently prescribe biopsy or treatment.
Choose the index lesion by highest PI-RADS category; resolve ties by extraprostatic extension, then size. Map up to four principal suspicious lesions and identify all sectors involved.
Measure AP and longitudinal gland dimensions on mid-sagittal T2, transverse on axial T2. Avoid mixing millimetres and centimetres in the ellipsoid formula.
PI-RADS diagnostic scoring is not a post-treatment recurrence system. A negative MRI does not exclude clinically significant cancer; interpret with clinical risk.
If both DWI and DCE are unavailable or inadequate, do not imply a complete PI-RADS assessment; the formal guidance limits assessment to staging for extraprostatic extension.
Use actual study images in the image slots and retain matching series/image references in the report.

steps.label: Breast composition
steps.detail: Record breast composition (A–D) and whether density could mask a lesion.

normal.COMPOSITION: The breasts are [almost entirely fatty / scattered fibroglandular density] (category [A / B]).

findings: Heterogeneously dense breasts, which may obscure small masses (category C).
Extremely dense breasts, which lower the sensitivity of mammography (category D).
steps.look: CC and MLO views of both breasts together; tomosynthesis when acquired.
steps.tip: Dense tissue can mask a lesion; a negative mammogram does not resolve a palpable abnormality.

steps.label: Masses
steps.detail: Describe any mass by side, clock position or quadrant, depth, size, shape, margin and density.
findings: [Right] breast [upper outer quadrant, 10 o'clock], [middle] depth: [oval / round / irregular] mass __ mm with [circumscribed / obscured / microlobulated / indistinct / spiculated] margins, [high / equal / low / fat-containing] density.
Fat-containing mass (e.g., lipoma, oil cyst, hamartoma).
steps.look: Both projections: a mass is seen on two views with convex outward borders; spot compression or tomosynthesis for margins.
steps.tip: Spiculated or indistinct margins and irregular shape are the most suspicious mass features.

steps.label: Asymmetry and architectural distortion
steps.detail: Classify any asymmetry (asymmetry, global, focal, developing) and look for architectural distortion.

normal.ASYMMETRY AND DISTORTION: No architectural distortion or suspicious asymmetry.

findings: Focal asymmetry in the [ ] seen on both views, [persistent / resolving] on spot compression.
Developing asymmetry: new or larger since [date].
Architectural distortion at [ ] without a history of surgery at that site.
Summation (superimposed tissue) resolving on additional views.
steps.look: Compare both breasts side by side and with prior studies; confirm persistence on additional views or tomosynthesis.
steps.tip: A developing asymmetry has a meaningful malignancy rate and usually needs further work-up.

steps.label: Calcifications and associated features
steps.detail: Describe calcification morphology and distribution, and skin, nipple, trabecular and axillary findings.

normal.CALCIFICATIONS AND ASSOCIATED SIGNS: No suspicious calcifications; skin, nipple and axillae unremarkable.

findings: Typically benign calcifications ([vascular / coarse / rod-like / rim / skin / layering]).
[Amorphous / coarse heterogeneous / fine pleomorphic / fine linear or fine-linear branching] calcifications in a [grouped / linear / segmental / regional] distribution spanning __ mm.
Skin thickening and trabecular thickening of the [ ] breast.
Enlarged dense axillary node without fatty hilum.
steps.look: Magnification views for morphology; distribution across the whole breast; skin, nipple and axillary tail.
steps.tip: Linear or segmental distribution follows a duct and raises suspicion even for less suspicious morphology.

steps.label: Correlation and assessment
steps.detail: Correlate with the clinical site and prior studies and give the final BI-RADS category with the matching management.

normal.CORRELATION AND ASSESSMENT: No mammographic abnormality at the clinical site; stable compared with [date]. BI-RADS 1: negative.

findings: BI-RADS 0: incomplete — additional imaging [views / ultrasound] needed.
BI-RADS 2: benign finding(s).
BI-RADS 3: probably benign — short-interval follow-up.
BI-RADS 4 / 5: suspicious / highly suggestive of malignancy — tissue sampling recommended.
steps.look: Clinical marker or site; prior studies of comparable projection.
steps.tip: The final category and the recommendation must match.

steps.label: Localisation
steps.detail: Map each lesion by side, clock position, distance from the nipple and depth.

normal.LOCALISATION: No focal lesion in the area examined.

findings: [Right] breast [10 o'clock], __ cm from the nipple, [superficial / middle / posterior] depth.
steps.look: Radial and antiradial scans; record the clock face and distance from the nipple in cm.
steps.tip: Correlate the ultrasound location with the mammographic and clinical site; a mismatch means the finding may be different.

steps.label: Shape, orientation and margin
steps.detail: Describe shape, orientation and margins.
findings: Oval, parallel, circumscribed mass __ × __ × __ mm.
Irregular, not parallel (taller than wide) mass with [angular / microlobulated / indistinct / spiculated] margins.
steps.look: Two orthogonal planes: parallel (wider than tall) or not parallel; circumscribed or not.
steps.tip: Not-parallel orientation and non-circumscribed margins are the most suspicious ultrasound features.

steps.label: Echo pattern and posterior features
steps.detail: Assess the echo pattern, posterior features and calcifications.
findings: Anechoic simple cyst with posterior enhancement.
Complicated cyst with homogeneous low-level echoes.
Hypoechoic solid mass with posterior shadowing and an echogenic rim.
Complex cystic and solid mass.
steps.look: Compare the echogenicity with fat; look behind the lesion for enhancement or shadowing.

steps.label: Vascularity and associated features
steps.detail: Review Doppler, ducts, skin and surrounding tissue.

normal.VASCULARITY AND ASSOCIATED FINDINGS: No internal vascularity; ducts, skin and surrounding tissue normal.

findings: Internal vascularity on Doppler.
Duct extension from the mass.
Skin thickening and oedema of the [ ].
steps.look: Colour Doppler with low pressure; adjacent ducts, skin thickness and oedema.

steps.label: Nodes and assessment
steps.detail: Assess the axillary nodes and give the BI-RADS assessment with recommendation.

normal.NODES AND ASSESSMENT: Axillary nodes normal with a thin cortex and fatty hilum. BI-RADS [1 / 2].

findings: Axillary node with cortical thickening of __ mm [and effaced hilum].
BI-RADS 3: probably benign; follow-up in [ ] months.
BI-RADS 4: suspicious; ultrasound-guided biopsy recommended.
steps.look: Axilla: cortical thickness, hilum and shape of each node.
steps.tip: A negative targeted ultrasound does not cancel a suspicious finding on another modality.

steps.label: Index tumour
steps.detail: Localise the known malignancy and measure its extent.
findings: Known [right] breast carcinoma at [ ], __ mm, with biopsy clip in the lesion.
steps.look: The modality that shows the tumour best (mammography, ultrasound or MRI); biopsy clip position.

steps.label: Additional disease and span
steps.detail: Assess separate foci, associated calcifications and the total disease span; check the contralateral breast.

normal.ADDITIONAL BREAST DISEASE: No additional ipsilateral or contralateral disease.

findings: Associated calcifications extend __ mm beyond the mass (total span __ mm).
Additional focus in the same quadrant (multifocal) / different quadrant (multicentric).
Contralateral finding: [ ].
steps.look: Measure from the furthest edge of related disease; contralateral breast on the same examination.
steps.tip: Report the index lesion and the total span separately; surgery is planned on both.

steps.label: Skin, nipple and chest wall
steps.detail: Describe skin, nipple, pectoralis and chest wall relationships.

normal.LOCAL INVASION: No skin, nipple, pectoralis or chest wall involvement.

findings: Skin thickening and oedema (inflammatory pattern) over the [ ].
Nipple retraction and involvement.
Invasion of the pectoralis muscle without chest wall invasion.
steps.look: Posterior margin against the pectoralis; skin and nipple.
steps.tip: Pectoralis involvement alone is not chest wall invasion; chest wall means ribs, intercostal muscles or serratus anterior.

steps.label: Regional nodes
steps.detail: Map suspicious axillary nodes by level and internal mammary and supraclavicular nodes.

normal.REGIONAL NODES: No suspicious axillary, internal mammary or supraclavicular nodes.

findings: Suspicious level [I] axillary node with cortical thickening __ mm [clip placed].
Enlarged internal mammary node __ mm.
Supraclavicular node __ mm.
steps.look: Axillary levels I–III relative to pectoralis minor; internal mammary chain; supraclavicular fossa.

steps.label: Distant disease and response
steps.detail: Report the distant sites covered and, when restaging, the response compared with baseline.

normal.DISTANT DISEASE AND RESPONSE: No distant disease within the imaged field.

findings: Liver / bone / lung lesions suspicious for metastases.
Partial response: index tumour decreased from __ to __ mm.
steps.look: Staging CT, bone imaging or PET-CT when available; baseline for comparison.

steps.label: Implant type and position
steps.detail: Identify silicone or saline implants and their position relative to the pectoralis muscle.

normal.IMPLANT TYPE AND POSITION: Bilateral [silicone / saline] implants in [subglandular / subpectoral] position.

findings: [Single / double] lumen [silicone / saline] implant on the [right].
steps.look: MRI silicone-selective sequences or ultrasound; mammography with implant-displacement (Eklund) views.

steps.label: Shell and contour
steps.detail: Inspect implant contour and shell integrity; separate radial folds from rupture.

normal.SHELL AND CONTOUR: Smooth implant contour; normal radial folds only.

findings: Focal contour bulge (herniation) of the [ ] implant.
Radial fold extending to the outer shell (normal).
steps.look: MRI and ultrasound along the implant surface.
steps.tip: Radial folds extend to the periphery of the implant; a rupture line floats inside the gel.

steps.label: Intracapsular rupture
steps.detail: Assess the implant contents for signs of intracapsular rupture.
findings: Intracapsular rupture: curvilinear lines within the gel (linguine sign).
Stepladder sign on ultrasound.
Droplets of water within silicone (salad-oil sign) — possible early rupture.
steps.look: MRI silicone-selective images; ultrasound for stepladder echoes.
steps.tip: The linguine sign — collapsed shell floating in the gel — is the most reliable sign of intracapsular rupture.

steps.label: Extracapsular silicone and peri-implant fluid
steps.detail: Look for silicone beyond the capsule, peri-implant fluid and capsular masses.

normal.EXTRACAPSULAR FINDINGS: No extracapsular silicone, peri-implant fluid or capsular mass.

findings: Extracapsular silicone in the [ ] breast (snowstorm on ultrasound).
Late peri-implant effusion __ mm; aspiration for cytology (CD30) is advised to exclude BIA-ALCL.
Capsular mass __ mm.
steps.look: MRI and ultrasound around the capsule and into the breast; late peri-implant fluid raises BIA-ALCL concern.
steps.tip: A late seroma (more than one year after surgery) needs aspiration for BIA-ALCL.

steps.label: Breast and nodes
steps.detail: Assess the surrounding breast tissue and regional nodes within the study scope.

normal.BREAST AND NODES: No suspicious breast finding; axillary nodes normal.

findings: Silicone-laden axillary node.
Breast finding: [ ].
Implant-integrity MRI without contrast: breast cancer assessment not included.
steps.look: Breast parenchyma and axillae; silicone in nodes.

steps.label: Symptomatic site
steps.detail: Identify the palpable or symptomatic site and relate it to the nipple.

normal.SYMPTOM LOCALISATION: No abnormality at the symptomatic site.

findings: Palpable abnormality in the [right] [retroareolar / eccentric] region.
steps.look: Mammography with a skin marker; targeted ultrasound.

steps.label: Retroareolar tissue
steps.detail: Distinguish gynaecomastia (nodular, dendritic or diffuse) from fatty enlargement.

normal.RETROAREOLAR TISSUE: Normal male breast with fat only; no gynaecomastia.

findings: Nodular gynaecomastia: fan-shaped retroareolar density [unilateral / bilateral].
Dendritic gynaecomastia with branching strands.
Pseudogynaecomastia: fatty enlargement without glandular tissue.
steps.look: Retroareolar density centred behind the nipple; compare both sides.
steps.tip: Gynaecomastia is centred behind the nipple; an eccentric mass is not gynaecomastia until proven otherwise.

steps.label: Focal lesion
steps.detail: Describe any eccentric or discrete mass separately.
findings: Eccentric irregular mass __ mm with [spiculated / indistinct] margins, suspicious for carcinoma.
Circumscribed mass __ mm (e.g., epidermal inclusion cyst, lipoma).
steps.look: Mammography and ultrasound of any mass eccentric to the nipple.

steps.label: Nipple and skin
steps.detail: Look for nipple retraction, skin lesions and inflammatory change.
findings: Nipple retraction.
Skin thickening over the mass.
Subareolar abscess.
steps.look: Nipple and skin on mammography and ultrasound.

steps.label: Nodes and correlation
steps.detail: Review axillary nodes and concordance between imaging and clinical findings; give the assessment.
findings: Suspicious axillary node.
BI-RADS 4/5: biopsy recommended.
steps.look: Axilla on ultrasound.

steps.label: Background and quality
steps.detail: Assess the amount of fibroglandular tissue, background parenchymal enhancement and technical quality.

normal.BACKGROUND AND QUALITY: [Scattered] fibroglandular tissue with [minimal] background parenchymal enhancement; no significant artefact.

findings: [Marked] background parenchymal enhancement, reducing sensitivity.
Motion or misregistration limits the subtraction images.
steps.look: Precontrast T1 for fibroglandular tissue; early subtraction for background enhancement; check motion and registration.

steps.label: Lesion location
steps.detail: Identify each finding by side, quadrant or clock position, depth and size.
findings: Finding 1: [right] breast [ ] o'clock, __ cm from the nipple, [ ] depth, __ mm.
steps.look: Axial and sagittal subtraction images.

steps.label: Mass or non-mass enhancement
steps.detail: Distinguish focus, mass and non-mass enhancement and describe shape, margin, distribution and internal pattern.
findings: Irregular mass with spiculated margins and heterogeneous / rim enhancement.
Oval circumscribed mass with dark internal septations (fibroadenoma pattern).
Non-mass enhancement in a [segmental / linear] distribution with clumped internal enhancement.
steps.look: Early subtraction and MIP images.
steps.tip: Segmental or linear clumped non-mass enhancement is suspicious for DCIS.

steps.label: Signal and kinetics
steps.detail: Correlate T2 signal, diffusion and the enhancement time course.
findings: High T2 signal, no restricted diffusion, persistent enhancement (favours benign).
Low T2 signal, restricted diffusion (ADC __) and washout kinetics (suspicious).
steps.look: T2, DWI/ADC and time–intensity curves.
steps.tip: Kinetics and diffusion support, but do not replace, morphological assessment.

steps.label: Extent and assessment
steps.detail: Review total span, skin, nipple, chest wall and nodes, then give the MRI BI-RADS assessment.

normal.EXTENT AND ASSESSMENT: No skin, nipple or chest wall involvement; normal nodes. BI-RADS [1 / 2].

findings: Total extent of disease __ mm.
Invasion of the pectoralis / chest wall.
BI-RADS [4 / 5 / 6] with recommendation [ ].
steps.look: Sagittal images for span and chest wall; axillae.

protocol: Record actual cine/tissue coverage, cardiac and respiratory gating, temporal/spatial sampling, contrast/sequence and artefact limits. Quantify only adequately acquired data; a still image or generic model does not supply function.
Compare native and enhanced sources in matching actual locations/planes and phase context. Record contour, basal/apical, papillary/trabecular conventions and applicable indexed reference context.

Use actual field strength, sequence, processing, ROI and comparable reference method for mapping/ECV. Record haematocrit source/date or explicitly named alternative method when used; unavailable acquisitions are not normal.

checklist.label: Function
checklist.detail: Assess both actual ventricular blood-pool/wall contours across obtained phases; report source ED/ES selection, indexed volumes/function and regional motion with uncertainty.

checklist.label: Geometry
checklist.detail: Assess actual chamber/atrial geometry, each covered myocardial region and maximal thickness/mass with named landmarks, phase, contours and variant anatomy.

checklist.label: Tissue
checklist.detail: Assess actual oedema/T1/T2/T2-star or ECV acquisitions if available, with raw-source quality, local/method-comparable references, ROI/calibration and unresolved regions.

checklist.label: Scar
checklist.detail: Localise actual LGE by named region/layer/extent and acquisition/nulling quality; distinguish pattern-based differential from histology and account for mixed disease and uncertainty.

checklist.label: Ancillary
checklist.detail: Assess source-resolved valves, atria, appendages, thrombus, pericardium and covered extracardiac findings; physiology and clinical significance require actual evidence.

measurements.name: Ventricular volumes and EF
measurements.method: Contour actually obtained end-diastolic/end-systolic sources with complete coverage and documented basal/apical, papillary/trabecular convention; report EDV/ESV/SV/EF and applicable index/reference context.
measurements.pitfall: Basal slice and trabeculation conventions alter results.

measurements.name: Mapping
measurements.method: Report only valid obtained mapping values with field strength, sequence/processing, ROI/source quality and method-comparable reference; ECV must identify its calculation/data/haematocrit or named alternative source.
measurements.pitfall: Values from another scanner are not an interchangeable threshold.

pitfalls: Incomplete coverage, arrhythmia and contour convention can change apparent volume/function; no normal quantitative result is inferred from a still or unavailable sequence.

Ischaemic-type LGE commonly involves subendocardium in a coronary distribution; other patterns, global subendocardial involvement, mixed disease and acquisition artefact require a differential, not an exclusive cause.
Absent LGE does not exclude every cardiomyopathy or diffuse tissue abnormality. Poor nulling/ghosting/partial volume can mimic or obscure enhancement.
Map colours or another scanner/site threshold are not independently calibrated normality; actual raw source quality and reference method matter.
Static jet, effusion or filling-defect appearance does not quantify regurgitation, tamponade or prove thrombus; appropriate functional/tissue/clinical evidence is separate.
impression_prompts: State biventricular size and systolic function.
Summarise tissue/LGE pattern and the supported differential.
Identify clinically consequential thrombus, valve or pericardial findings.
escalation: Communicate an unexpected intracardiac thrombus or another acutely consequential finding directly.

sections.heading: RECOMMENDATION AND COMMUNICATION
sections.body:
Recommended next step and rationale: [ ].
Direct communication, when indicated: [recipient, time, method].

notes: Incomplete coverage, arrhythmia and contour convention can change apparent volume/function; no normal quantitative result is inferred from a still or unavailable sequence.

Ischaemic-type LGE commonly involves subendocardium in a coronary distribution; other patterns, global subendocardial involvement, mixed disease and acquisition artefact require a differential, not an exclusive cause.
Absent LGE does not exclude every cardiomyopathy or diffuse tissue abnormality. Poor nulling/ghosting/partial volume can mimic or obscure enhancement.
Map colours or another scanner/site threshold are not independently calibrated normality; actual raw source quality and reference method matter.
Static jet, effusion or filling-defect appearance does not quantify regurgitation, tamponade or prove thrombus; appropriate functional/tissue/clinical evidence is separate.

sources.title: Radiology Assistant — Ischemic and non-ischemic cardiomyopathy

steps.label: Ventricular volumes and function
steps.detail: Quantify both ventricles from the short-axis cine stack.
findings: Dilated left ventricle (LVEDVi __ mL/m²) with reduced ejection fraction (__%).
Right ventricular dilatation with reduced RVEF __%.
steps.look: Short-axis cine from base to apex; contour end diastole and end systole; compare with sex- and age-specific references.
steps.tip: Quantify actual temporal/source contours with complete coverage; document ED/ES and basal/apical/papillary/trabecular conventions plus reference/indexing context. Do not infer EF or normality from a still/model.

steps.label: Wall thickness and regional motion
steps.detail: Assess wall thickness, mass and regional wall motion by segment.
findings: Asymmetric septal hypertrophy with maximal wall thickness __ mm at [basal anteroseptum].
Akinesia of the [anterior] wall in the [LAD] territory.
Apical ballooning with basal hyperkinesia (takotsubo pattern).
steps.look: Inspect obtained short/long-axis cines with actual named segment/region and apical coverage; state the model/convention and any region where motion/thickening cannot be assessed.
steps.tip: Locate actual maximal thickness and distinguish endocardial/trabecular/papillary boundaries from compact myocardium; phase and source sampling limit thin regions.

steps.label: Oedema and mapping
steps.detail: Review T2-weighted oedema, native T1 and T2 mapping and ECV if acquired.
findings: Regional oedema in the [ ] segments with raised T2 (__ ms).
Diffusely raised native T1 (__ ms) and ECV (__%).
steps.look: T2-weighted and mapping sequences with the local reference range and field strength.
steps.tip: Mapping and ECV require actual sequence/field strength, raw-source/ROI quality and comparable references. ECV identifies its haematocrit/date or explicitly named alternative method; colour pictures are not calibrated measurements.

steps.label: Late gadolinium enhancement
steps.detail: Map LGE by segment, layer, transmurality and coronary territory.
findings: Subendocardial / transmural LGE in the [LAD] territory, __% transmural (ischaemic pattern).
Midwall LGE in the septum (non-ischaemic pattern).
Subepicardial LGE in the inferolateral wall (myocarditis pattern).
Patchy LGE at the RV insertion points in hypertrophied segments (HCM pattern).
steps.look: Short- and long-axis LGE in matching planes; check the myocardium is correctly nulled.
steps.tip: Coronary-pattern subendocardial LGE supports an ischaemic differential, but global subendocardial, midwall/epicardial, mixed or artefactual patterns do not uniquely establish cause. Absent LGE does not exclude all cardiomyopathy; record nulling, quality and actual coverage.

steps.label: Atria, valves, thrombus and pericardium
steps.detail: Inspect the atria, valves, thrombus, pericardium and extracardiac findings.
findings: Left ventricular apical thrombus __ mm (non-enhancing on early post-contrast images).
Pericardial effusion __ mm.
Mitral regurgitation jet on cine.
steps.look: Long-axis cines and early post-contrast images for thrombus.
steps.tip: Assess actual tissue/contrast/temporal source for suspected thrombus and valve/pericardial effects. No single filling defect, jet or effusion proves functional severity or tamponade.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging. Role of inversion time in LGE imaging: On the left panel which is a magnitude (non-PSIR) LGE image, normal myocardium has a faint  “ etched ”  appearance (darkest at the border with higher signal intensity centrally) signifying an inversion time that was set too short and which will lead to underestimation of LGE. On the right panel, the image was repeated with a longer inversion time and demonstrates a larger LGE zone in the inferior wall. For non-PSIR magnitude imaging, always use the longest inversion time possible that still nulls normal myocardium

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: T2* imaging to assess myocardial iron overload.  a  T2* scan of a normal heart showing slow signal loss with increasing TE.  b  Decay curve for normal heart. T2* = 33.3 ms.  c  Heavily iron overloaded heart. Note there is substantial signal loss at TE = 9.09.  d  Decay curve for heavily iron overloaded heart showing rapid signal loss with increasing TE. The curve plateaus as myocardial SI falls below background noise.  e  Values for higher TEs are removed (truncation method) resulting in a better curve fit and a lower T2* value

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Cardiac MRI of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). A case of a 38-year-old male with a history of premature ventricular beats. Panel ( a ) (SSFP sequences) represents a four-chamber and short axis views (top left panel and top middle panel, respectively) showing a marked and asymmetric hypertrophy of the interventricular septum (white arrowheads). Panel ( b ) (TIR t2 sequence) represents a short-axis view showing a higher signal al the level of the septum (white arrowheads) compared to the remote myocardium. Panels ( c , d ) represent increased values on T1 mapping sequences at the level of the basal and middle septum (white arrowheads), respectively. Panel ( e ) represents increased values on extracellular volume (ECV) sequence at the level of middle septum (white arrowheads black outlines). Panels ( f – h ) (LGE sequences) display a non-ischemic pattern of hyperenhancement at the level of septum (white arrowheads). Taken together, these findings are diagnostic of asymmetric HCM.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Cardiac amyloidosis. A case of a 79-year-old man, with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showing a hypertrophic (white arrows) left ventricle (LV) of 17 mm in the steady-state free precession (SSFP) sequences (panels ( a – c ) show four-chamber, three-chamber, and two-chamber views, respectively). Mid panels show diffuse high values at T1 mapping sequences, represented by the orange tonality as indicated by the white arrows (panels ( d , e ) at the level of the basal and mid-LV short-axis views, respectively) and diffuse high values at extracellular volume (ECV) sequence, represented by the yellow tonality as indicated by the white arrows (panel ( f ) at the level of the basal LV short-axis view). Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequences showed a non-ischemic enhancement pattern in both ventricles (white arrows), a hyperenhancement of the atrio-ventricular valves (red stars), of the left atrium wall and the interatrial septum (white arrowheads) (panels ( g – i ) show four-chamber, three-chamber, and two-chamber views, respectively). All these findings are diagnostic of cardiac amyloidosis.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Anderson–Fabry disease. One case involves a 67-year-old man who was diagnosed with Anderson–Fabry disease through genetic testing during family screening (because of his affected brother). He remains completely asymptomatic. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging showed concentric LV hypertrophy with a mild reduction in ejection fraction (EF) in steady-state free precession (SSFP) sequences (panels ( a – c ) show three-chamber, four-chamber, and short-axis views at the basal level, respectively). Panel ( d ) shows oedema (white arrowheads) at the level of the mid-LV short-axis view (T2-weighted sequence). Panels ( e , f ) display T1 mapping sequences with a low value in the septum (white arrowheads) and higher values in the lateral wall (white arrowheads with black outlines) at the level of LV papillary muscles and the mid-LV short-axis view, respectively. Panels ( g , h ) display T2 mapping and extracellular volume (ECV) sequences, respectively, with low values in the septum (white arrowheads) and higher values in the postero-lateral wall (white arrowheads with black outlines) at the level of the mid-LV short-axis view. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequences display a non-ischemic hyperenhancement pattern (white arrowheads) at the level of the lateral wall (panels ( i – l ) show three-chamber, four-chamber, mid-LV short-axis, and apical LV views, respectively).

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy. A case of a 50-year-old female with a history of premature ventricular beats. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging showed multiple bulging of both LV and RV ventricles (white arrowheads) in steady-state free precession (SSFP) sequences (panels ( a , b ) show 2 slightly different four-chamber views). Possible fat infiltration of posterolateral wall emerged by proton density (PD) sequences (white arrows in panel ( c ) displaying a mid-LV short-axis view). Panels ( d – f ) show short-axis views of the mid-LV at T1 and T2 mapping and ECV, respectively, with evidence of a higher value at the level of the lateral wall compared to the remaining myocardium (white arrows). Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequences displayed a non-ischemic hyper-enhancement pattern (white arrows) at the level of the septum, LV, and RV multiple positions (panels ( g – i ) show four-chamber, three-chamber, and mid-LV short-axis views, respectively). These findings are diagnostic for biventricular arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Iron overload. A case of a 38-year-old man in follow-up for thalassemia. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging showed a mild reduction in left ventricle ejection fraction (LVEF) in steady-state free precession (SSFP) sequences (panels ( a – c ) show four-chamber, two-chamber, and mid-LV short-axis views, respectively). The T2* sequences showed a normal value of iron in the heart (T2* > 20 msec), with a pathological value of iron in the liver (T2* 9 mg/g); panels ( d – f ) show the mid-LV short-axis view, the colorimetric display of T2* at the same level, and the graphical curve of T2* decay expressed in msec, respectively. T1 mapping showed a lower value of T1 (mean T1 900 msec), suggesting iron overload in the heart; panels ( g – i ) show the basal-LV short-axis, mid-LV short-axis, and apical-LV short-axis views, respectively (white stars).

protocol: Review ECG phase quality, source images, curved MPR and orthogonal lumen cross-sections.
Use the comprehensive CCTA template below, keeping anatomical stenosis, plaque burden and physiology separate.

checklist.label: Quality
checklist.detail: Name each non-evaluable segment and its effect on excluding significant stenosis.

checklist.label: Anatomy
checklist.detail: Establish dominance, origins, proximal course and coronary anomalies.

checklist.label: Stenosis
checklist.detail: Record vessel/segment, plaque composition and highest confident stenosis.

checklist.label: Burden
checklist.detail: Assess CAC/SIS/visual burden with the method identified; no plaque is not P1.

checklist.label: Additional findings
checklist.detail: Assess stents/grafts, physiology when available and extracoronary findings.

measurements.name: Stenosis
measurements.method: Compare the minimum orthogonal lumen with an appropriate reference segment.
measurements.pitfall: Calcific blooming and motion can overestimate narrowing.

measurements.name: Plaque burden
measurements.method: Record CAC and/or plaque-containing segment count; use the most severe reliable burden method.
measurements.pitfall: Zero CAC does not exclude non-calcified plaque.

measurements.name: CT-FFR
measurements.method: Record lesion-specific value 1–2 cm beyond the lesion and distinguish the distal nadir.
measurements.pitfall: The lowest distal value alone should not drive lesion attribution.

classification.name: CAD-RADS
classification.applicability: Coronary CTA interpreted with the full diagnostic quality and clinical context.
classification.summary: Report stenosis category with plaque burden and applicable N, HRP, I, S, G or E modifiers. CAD-RADS 0 has no plaque burden category.

pitfalls: HRP requires at least two specified high-risk plaque features in a plaque.
When a relevant segment is non-diagnostic, apply the N category/modifier rules rather than treating it as normal.
impression_prompts: State the most important stenosis and its vessel/segment.
Summarise plaque burden and the complete applicable CAD-RADS 2.0 notation.
Describe anomaly, graft/stent, physiology and significant extracardiac findings.
escalation: Communicate a suspected acute coronary complication or critical unexpected coronary anatomy in the relevant clinical context.

criteria_table.title: CAD-RADS 2.0 stenosis key
criteria_table.scope: Apply after reviewing all evaluable segments. Plaque burden, HRP, physiology and other modifiers are separate; use the complete report template for those rules.

rows.criteria: No coronary plaque or stenosis.
rows.report_note: Do not append a P category.

rows.criteria: 1–24% stenosis, or plaque without narrowing.
rows.report_note: Describe the plaque.

rows.criteria: 25–49% stenosis.
rows.report_note: Record the dominant lesion.

rows.criteria: 50–69% stenosis.
rows.report_note: Correlate with symptoms and any physiology.

rows.criteria: 70–99% stenosis in one or two vessels.
rows.report_note: Specify vessel and segment.

rows.criteria: Left main ≥50%, or severe three-vessel disease.
rows.report_note: State the qualifying anatomy.

rows.criteria: At least one total occlusion.
rows.report_note: Describe occlusion and distal vessel.

rows.criteria: Relevant segment non-evaluable; no ≥50% stenosis shown elsewhere.
rows.report_note: If ≥50% is demonstrated elsewhere, retain that category and add N.

P3 severe: CAC 301–999 or SIS 5–7.
P4 extensive: CAC ≥1000 or SIS ≥8.
Overall plaque burden: [no plaque / P1 / P2 / P3 / P4 / not reliably assessable].
If reliable methods disagree, use the most severe plaque assessment and document the contributing methods. CAD-RADS 0 has no P category; zero plaque is not P1.

sections.heading: CAD-RADS 2.0
sections.body:
CAD-RADS category:
0: no plaque or stenosis.
1: 1–24% stenosis, or plaque with positive remodelling but no luminal narrowing.
2: 25–49%.
3: 50–69%.
4A: 70–99% in one or two vessels.
4B: LM ≥50% or severe three-vessel disease.
5: total occlusion.
N: non-diagnostic.
Final CAD-RADS: CAD-RADS [0/1/2/3/4A/4B/5/N] / [P1/P2/P3/P4 when applicable] / [N / HRP / I+ / I− / I± / S / G / E as applicable].
If a relevant segment >1.5 mm is non-evaluable and evaluable segments show only <50% stenosis, use category N. If ≥50% stenosis is demonstrated elsewhere, retain the stenosis category and append N. Report P only if reliable.

sections.body:
Clinical setting: [stable / acute chest pain / other]. Suggested next step: [ ], considering symptoms, ECG/troponin where relevant, prior treatment, comorbidity and patient preference.
Stable chest pain prompts: [0: usually no additional CAD testing / 1–2: preventive risk discussion / 3: consider functional assessment / 4A: consider ICA or functional assessment / 4B: consider ICA / 5: consider ICA with viability/functional assessment where appropriate / N: additional evaluation if clinically indicated].
Acute chest pain prompt: [integrate stenosis and image quality with the ACS pathway; do not diagnose or exclude ACS from CAD-RADS alone].
Document the individualised recommendation and rationale; delete unused options.

notes: Complete bracketed fields and remove unused alternatives before issuing a report. Use the study’s own de-identified images in the final report; the gallery contains independent published teaching examples.
The user-supplied CCTA example provides the report foundation. Classification clarifications are referenced to CAD-RADS 2.0.
S and G record the presence of stents and bypass grafts. E identifies a relevant non-atherosclerotic coronary exception that requires a narrative description.
A fixed perfusion defect should be described separately from reversible ischaemia. Record failed or non-diagnostic physiology explicitly.

steps.label: Calcium score
steps.detail: If a non-contrast scan was acquired, record the total and per-vessel Agatston scores.

normal.CALCIUM SCORE: CAC: total 0 Agatston units (LM 0 | LAD 0 | LCx 0 | RCA 0). A zero CAC score does not exclude non-calcified plaque.

findings: CAC: total ___ Agatston units (LM ___ | LAD ___ | LCx ___ | RCA ___).
CAC: not performed.
steps.look: Non-contrast ECG-triggered images; confirm that each calcified focus is assigned to the correct vessel before accepting the total.
steps.tip: Agatston scoring is defined on the non-contrast acquisition; do not derive it from contrast-enhanced images.
steps.anatomy_note: Gross artery surfaces provide orientation only. They do not depict calcific foci or permit Agatston scoring; use the acquired non-contrast CT.

steps.label: Dominance and anatomy
steps.detail: Establish dominance, origins, proximal course and coronary anomalies.

normal.CORONARY ORIGINS / COURSE: Normal origins of the left main and right coronary arteries from the left and right coronary sinuses, with a normal proximal course. No myocardial bridge or fistula.

findings: Anomalous origin of the [RCA / LCA] from the [opposite / non-coronary] sinus with an [interarterial / retroaortic / prepulmonic / septal] course.
High-risk anomaly features: [slit-like ostium / acute take-off / intramural segment / proximal narrowing].
Myocardial bridge of the [mid LAD], __ mm long and __ mm deep.
Coronary artery fistula from the [ ] to the [ ].
steps.look: Axial source images and volume rendering at the sinuses of Valsalva; follow each ostium and its proximal course relative to the aorta and pulmonary trunk; find which artery supplies the PDA.
steps.tip: Name an interarterial course between the aorta and pulmonary trunk explicitly, with any intramural segment or slit-like ostium.
steps.anatomy_note: Only gross left/right coronary trunks, LAD, circumflex and an RCA-derived posterior branch are available. Individual ostia, sinus anatomy, branch origins and anomalous courses are not independently resolved. Determine patient dominance from the images; do not assume the example circulation.

steps.label: Stenosis by segment
steps.detail: Record vessel and segment, plaque composition and the highest confident stenosis category.

normal.CORONARY FINDINGS: LM, LAD and diagonal branches, LCx and obtuse marginal branches, and RCA/PDA/PLV: no plaque or stenosis.

findings: [Vessel/segment]: [calcified / non-calcified / partially calcified] plaque with [minimal 1–24% / mild 25–49% / moderate 50–69% / severe 70–99%] stenosis; series __ image __.
[Vessel/segment]: total occlusion, __ mm long, [with / without] distal reconstitution.
[Segment] non-diagnostic because of [motion / blooming calcification / poor opacification]; significant stenosis cannot be excluded.
steps.look: Curved MPR along each vessel, then orthogonal cross-sections at the tightest point and at a normal reference segment; check the axial source images for artefact.
steps.tip: Blooming from dense calcification overestimates stenosis; grade on orthogonal cross-sections with a wide window.
steps.anatomy_note: Gross artery surfaces do not establish the lumen, reference diameter, individual branch segments, plaque or stenosis. Use acquired orthogonal CT lumen sections and document non-evaluable segments.

steps.label: Plaque and burden
steps.detail: Describe plaque type and high-risk features, then state burden with the method used; no plaque is not P1.

normal.PLAQUE BURDEN: No plaque; no plaque-burden category is assigned.

findings: High-risk plaque in the [segment]: [positive remodelling / low attenuation / spotty calcification / napkin-ring sign]; at least two features are present, so the HRP modifier applies.
Predominantly [calcified / non-calcified / partially calcified] plaque in __ segments.
Segment involvement score __ ([method]); overall plaque burden P__.
steps.look: Cross-sections through each plaque for attenuation, remodelling and spotty calcification; count plaque-containing segments for SIS, or use the CAC score.
steps.tip: HRP needs at least two high-risk features within the same plaque.
steps.anatomy_note: No plaque geometry, calcific distribution or high-risk plaque morphology is represented in this atlas. Normal surface meshes cannot prove absence of plaque or its burden.

steps.label: Stents, grafts and physiology
steps.detail: Assess stent and graft patency, and record CT-FFR or perfusion when available.

normal.STENTS / GRAFTS: No coronary stents or bypass grafts.

findings: Stent in the [vessel/segment]: [patent / in-stent restenosis __% / occluded / non-diagnostic].
[LIMA / RIMA / SVG] to [target]: [patent / stenosis at __ / occluded]; distal anastomosis [ ].
CT-FFR __ measured 1–2 cm distal to the [segment] lesion; lowest distal value __ in [vessel].
steps.look: Sharp-kernel reconstructions with a wide window for the stent lumen; follow each graft from origin through its body to the distal anastomosis and run-off.
steps.tip: Report the lesion-specific CT-FFR value 1–2 cm beyond the lesion, separately from the lowest distal value.
steps.anatomy_note: Stents, grafts, anastomoses and physiological measurements are not supplied by these meshes. The source aorta and coronary trunks are orientation context only.

steps.label: Cardiac and extracardiac findings
steps.detail: Review chambers, valves, pericardium, aorta and the whole acquired field of view.

normal.EXTRACORONARY CARDIAC FINDINGS: Cardiac chambers normal in size; pericardium normal; no significant valvular calcification; aortic root and ascending aorta normal in calibre.
normal.EXTRACARDIAC FINDINGS: No significant finding in the imaged lungs, mediastinum, upper abdomen or bones.

findings: Aortic valve calcification, [mild / moderate / severe].
Pulmonary nodule __ mm in the [lobe]; follow-up according to the applicable guideline.
Pericardial effusion, [small / moderate].
steps.look: A full field-of-view reconstruction, not only the cardiac field, in lung and soft-tissue windows.
steps.anatomy_note: Only gross ventricular/atrial wall and ascending-aorta context is highlighted. Valves, pericardial layers, coronary sinuses, lungs and other acquired extracardiac anatomy are not independently represented.

steps.label: CAD-RADS 2.0
steps.detail: Assign the final category, plaque burden and modifiers from the findings already recorded.
findings: Final CAD-RADS: CAD-RADS __/P__ [/HRP] [/S] [/G] [/I+ / I− / I±] [/E].
Final CAD-RADS: CAD-RADS N — non-diagnostic; obstructive disease cannot be excluded.
steps.look: Use the highest-grade stenosis from the segment review, the burden step and each applicable modifier (N, HRP, I, S, G, E).
steps.tip: The category follows the highest-grade stenosis; when reliable burden methods disagree, use the most severe.
steps.anatomy_note: The atlas supplies anatomical orientation only. CAD-RADS, plaque burden, diagnostic quality and physiology must follow acquired evidence; a mesh selection cannot establish the classification.

steps.label: Extent and Stanford type
steps.detail: Identify actual proximal/distal disease extent and ascending/root involvement. Name the classification framework; retain arch-only or atypical patterns anatomically.

normal.AORTIC SEGMENT: Aortic extent assessment: [adequate actual coverage/reconstruction / limited / unassessed]. Source-observed disease and proximal/distal limits: [ ]. Ascending/root involvement and unresolved extent: [ ].
