steps.look: Unenhanced and arterial phase images from the root to the iliacs; sagittal oblique reformats.
steps.tip: Classic Stanford classification is based on ascending-aortic involvement, irrespective of tear origin. Describe arch-only/atypical patterns and the named framework explicitly; immediately communicate suspected acute aortic syndrome, rupture or malperfusion.

steps.label: Dissection, intramural haematoma or ulcer
steps.detail: Distinguish dissection with a flap from intramural haematoma and penetrating atherosclerotic ulcer.
findings: Intimal flap from [ ] to [ ]; source-supported lumen identity/supply [ ] and actual beak/cobweb or continuity findings [ ].
Intramural haemorrhagic wall thickening at [ ], __ mm in the stated plane; classic flap [seen / not seen / unresolved], focal tear/ULP evidence and limits [ ].
Penetrating atherosclerotic ulcer of the [descending aorta], __ mm deep and __ mm wide.
steps.look: Unenhanced images for crescentic hyperattenuating wall thickening; contrast images for flap, lumina and ulceration.
steps.tip: Beak/cobweb morphology and continuity with undissected aorta can support lumen identification. Confirm actual source course, enhancement phase and thrombus; lumen size alone is not definitive, and IMH, tiny tears or ulcerative features may overlap.

SMA compromised with poorly enhancing bowel (malperfusion).
steps.look: Coronary ostia, supra-aortic, coeliac, SMA, renal and iliac arteries; organ enhancement.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Impact of ECG-gated CT angiography (CTA). Non-gated ( a ,  b ) and ECG-gated ( c ,  d ) CTA in a 66-year-old man with limited intimal tear.  a  Non-gated axial CT image shows a ‘dissection-like’ motion artifact ( arrow ) on the contour of the aorta because of pulsatile motion of the aorta.  b  Oblique sagittal slab maximum intensity projection (slab-MIP) image shows an undulating contour of the aorta caused by misregistration from the pulsatile motion.  c  ECG-gated CTA, performed 1 day after the non-gated CT, eliminates the pulsatile motion artifact. The image clearly reveals a hidden focal intimal tear ( arrowhead ).  d  Slab MIP image of ECG-gated CTA demonstrates visualization of the ascending aorta without misregistration artifacts. A focal bulge with a tiny intimal tear is revealed ( curved arrow )

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Discriminating and overlapping features of acute aortic syndrome. In addition to the certain discriminating features as revealed by recent advances in imaging, each disease in acute aortic syndrome (AAS) may show overlapping features and transition from one to another. In such overlapping and transitional features of aortic diseases, the diagnosis may be affected by the time point at which the imaging has been examined and also by the detectability of tiny pathology by the imaging modality. structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Acute Stanford type A classic aortic dissection in a 71-year-old woman with abrupt, severe retrosternal chest pain.  a – c  Transverse images from an ECG-gated CTA demonstrate an extensive intimo-medial flap involving the entire thoracic aorta. structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Dissection variant intramural haematoma (IMH) in a 54-year-old man who presented with acute chest pain.  a  Non-contrast CT image shows a crescent-shaped high-density area in the ascending aorta and descending aorta ( arrowhead ).  b  On the axial contrast-enhanced CT image, neither the flow channel nor intimal flap is detected along the entire aorta, consistent with IMH.  c  Oblique sagittal MPR image demonstrates widespread extension of type A IMH throughout the whole thoracic aorta. An ‘ulcer-like projection,’ the radiological finding of a focal disruption of the surface of the aortic wall from the true lumen into the thrombosed false lumen, is identified at the mid ascending aorta ( arrow ). During surgery, a small thrombosed focal primary intimal tear (PIT) was identified at the corresponding site

Note the thick calcification and plaque on the aortic wall (*), suggesting an atherosclerotic background of the patient.  b  Axial ECG-gated CTA demonstrates the ulcerative lesion at the proximal ascending aorta ( arrowhead ) into the aortic media, which shows associated haemorrhage.  c  3D-VR image depicts the crater-like ulceration ( arrowhead ) and atherosclerotic calcification (*) on the aortic arch. The condition is considered as an overlapping feature between IMH (in the broad sense) and penetrating atherosclerotic ulcer

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Impending rupture of an atherosclerotic aortic aneurysm in an 83-year-old man. The patient had been followed for stable aortic aneurysm for many years and suddenly presented with acute chest pain.  a  Non-contrast CT demonstrates ballooning of the aorta at the aortic arch. The aortic wall shows haemorrhagic content within the aortic wall ( arrow ), which suggests an acute process of this event.  b  Axial CTA depicts bulged dilatation of the aorta on the right side of the aortic arch ( arrowheads ), which was not depicted on the previous follow-up CT images.  c  Oblique coronal MPR image demonstrates dilatation of the aorta ( arrowheads ) with a thickened aortic wall with haemorrhagic content. The aortic lumen shows an eccentric bulge, a sign of impending rupture of an atherosclerotic aortic aneurysm

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Aneurysmal dilatation of the aorta secondary to dissection variant IMH in a 66-year-old woman.  a  Oblique sagittal contrast-enhanced CT demonstrates IMH extending from the ascending aorta through the proximal descending aorta.  b  Axial image depicts a streak-form ulcer-like projection (primary intimal tear) in the descending aorta ( arrowhead ).  c  Two days after onset, an ulcer-like projection was enlarged to form an outpouching cavity into the thrombosed false lumen ( small arrow ).  d  One week later, the haemorrhagic content is resolved and the ulcer-like projection not been detected. On the other hand, the aorta shows aneurysmal dilatation. Note that the dilatation starts from the location where the haematoma was present ( large arrow ). Although the pathological features and clinical course are different, such aneurysmal dilatation of dissection variant IMH might be confused with an atherosclerotic aortic aneurysm if an ulcer-like projection is not detected on the initial CT examination

steps.look: Define the actual annular basal plane from source-resolved cusp attachment landmarks, retaining bicuspid/other morphology. Use the appropriate available systolic reconstruction, record the exact phase/quality, and retain limits if the optimal phase is unavailable.
steps.tip: Record area, perimeter and both diameters from an actual defined plane; retain cardiac phase, edge/calibration and source limits. Prosthesis sizing is device-specific heart-team planning, not a single diameter or generic model result.

steps.look: Short-axis view of the valve in systole and diastole; calcium distribution on the non-contrast and contrast images.
steps.tip: Qualitative calcium on contrast CT is not an automatically valid Agatston score. Record the actual scoring acquisition/method and clinical context; calcification alone does not establish functional stenosis or a complication.

steps.look: Measure each ostium from the defined annular basal plane to its inferior margin; preserve side, sinus/leaflet geometry, coronary origin/course and any prior valve/graft. Retain unavailable coronary/device relations.
steps.tip: Coronary height alone does not determine obstruction risk. Include actual leaflet/cusp geometry, sinus/STJ dimensions, calcium and prior valve/device relationships; any virtual-device distances require explicit simulation assumptions and source-based heart-team review.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full:
The plane in which the sinus of Valsalva should be measured (A,B). The measurements
of the sinus, from cusp to commissure, are shown in blue (C). Measurements should be
performed in triplicate, and, if the anatomy is symmetric, the average of the three
measurements can be reported. A sinus of Valsalva with a small diameter (< 30 mm)
is associated with a greater likelihood of coronary occlusion.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Standard reconstructions for assessment of peripheral vascular pathway. The approach includes first creation of a curved reformat of each artery, including the aorta ( a ), as well as 3D volume-rendered images ( b ). Those reconstructions provide landmarks to display the sites of subsequent measurements of luminal diameter and 3D volume-rendering maximum intensity projection (MIP) reformats ( c ) demonstrate the severity of aortic and ileo-femoral calcifications. Curved multiplanar reformats, obtained with a centreline approach, serve as the source for multiple luminal measurements made in a plane orthogonal to the vessel.  d, e, f  show the process of assessing orthogonal axial planes with measurements of the smallest diameters at each vessel level [common iliac artery ( d ), external iliac artery ( e ), common femoral artery ( f )]

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Planning of the direct aortic approach. Assessment of entire ascending aorta is crucial to exclude the presence of thoracic aneurysm or anterior aortic wall calcifications that might potentially interfere with direct puncture of the aorta. Typically, the aorta is punctured within the most proximal 8.5 cm.  a  The 3D VR reconstructions of the ascending aorta for assessment of the diameter and presence of anterior aortic wall calcifications. Bone structures provide landmarks for future thoracotomy. Blue line, aortic valve plane; red line, 8.5 cm above the plane of the aortic valve, showing the area of potential direct aortic access.  b  Magnified view of 3D VR of the ascending aorta with the 8.5-cm landmark, ( c ) curvilinear reconstruction of the ascending aorta with ( d ) automatically created perpendicular to ( c ) the aortic plane with aortic diameter measured at this level

spatial_model.title: CT TAVI / TAVR planning · spatial orientation
spatial_model.instructions: Drag to rotate; choose a reporting landmark and move the section plane. Relate root and ascending aorta to the arch and access vessels; valve sizing must use patient-specific double-oblique measurements.
spatial_model.reporting_aim: Relate root and ascending aorta to the arch and access vessels; valve sizing must use patient-specific double-oblique measurements.

protocol: Use contrast-enhanced CT or MR angiography timed to the vessels in question, with multiplanar and 3D reconstructions of the arch, pulmonary arteries and veins.
Record symptoms of airway or oesophageal compression, prior surgery and whether the question is arterial, venous or shunt-related.

checklist.label: Aortic arch
checklist.detail: Establish arch side, branching order, aberrant subclavian artery, diverticulum, double arch and coarctation.

checklist.label: Airway and oesophagus
checklist.detail: Describe each vascular/ductal component around the trachea and oesophagus, compression level and length, and associated tracheobronchial branching or cartilage abnormalities; distinguish directly seen from inferred ring components.

checklist.label: Pulmonary arteries
checklist.detail: Trace each actual pulmonary artery origin, proximal and covered distal course; distinguish proximal interruption from whole-lung agenesis, identify sling, systemic collaterals and ductal connection.

checklist.label: Pulmonary veins
checklist.detail: Trace every actual lobar/segmental pulmonary venous channel to each drainage site, including accessory veins, common trunks, dual drainage, obstruction and relevant septal/cardiac associations.

checklist.label: Systemic veins
checklist.detail: Trace systemic venous pathways and actual drainage, including both SVCs, bridging vein, coronary sinus/atrial endpoint, IVC/hepatic connections, azygos/hemiazygos continuation and left superior intercostal vein.

measurements.name: Vessel calibre
measurements.method: Measure the minimum orthogonal diameter at named segments, such as a coarctation and the adjacent normal aorta.
measurements.pitfall: Oblique axial measurements overestimate calibre; use a plane perpendicular to the vessel.

measurements.name: Airway narrowing
measurements.method: Measure the minimum tracheal or bronchial lumen at the level of compression and its length.
measurements.pitfall: Expiratory phase and patient position change airway calibre.

pitfalls: A complete ring depends on the actual arch, branch and ductal/ligamentous configuration; a non-opacified or atretic component may be inferred from secondary signs but must not be presented as directly visualised.
Poor opacification or incomplete coverage does not establish absence. Tailor acquisition to the clinical question rather than automatically adding a delayed radiation exposure.
Static CT/MRI airway narrowing does not establish dynamic malacia or its clinical severity; respiratory phase and appropriate dynamic/bronchoscopic assessment matter.
Pulmonary venous number and drainage vary; four separate ostia are not required for normal anatomy. Trace accessory/common/dual channels before labelling return normal.
Persistent left SVC can drain to the coronary sinus/right atrium or to the left atrium; confirm the actual endpoint and relevant coronary-sinus/septal anatomy.

steps.label: Aortic arch
steps.detail: Establish arch side, branching order, aberrant subclavian artery, diverticulum, double arch and coarctation.
findings: Right aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian artery arising from a Kommerell diverticulum (__ mm).
Left arch with aberrant right subclavian artery passing behind the oesophagus.
Double aortic arch with a dominant [right] arch.
Coarctation distal to the left subclavian artery, minimum diameter __ mm, with collaterals.
steps.look: Axial images above the arch for the four-artery sign; volume rendering of the arch and branches.
steps.tip: Describe each patent or inferred atretic component and ductal/ligamentous attachment. The four-artery sign and flat volume rendering do not independently prove all ring components or the actual anomaly geometry.

steps.label: Airway and oesophagus
steps.detail: Look for a vascular ring or sling compressing the trachea or oesophagus.
findings: Tracheal narrowing to __ mm at the level of the [double arch / innominate artery].
Posterior oesophageal impression by the aberrant subclavian artery.
steps.look: Minimum-intensity projections of the trachea; oesophagus behind the arch.
steps.tip: Record respiratory phase and actual level/length of narrowing. Static narrowing alone does not diagnose dynamic tracheobronchomalacia; cartilage and bronchial anomalies require source-resolved assessment.

steps.label: Pulmonary arteries
steps.detail: Assess the pulmonary artery origin and course, agenesis, sling and patent ductus.
findings: Left pulmonary artery arises from the right pulmonary artery and passes between the trachea and oesophagus (pulmonary sling).
Unilateral pulmonary artery [agenesis / hypoplasia].
Patent ductus arteriosus.
steps.look: Axial and coronal images of the main and branch pulmonary arteries.
steps.tip: Distinguish proximal pulmonary artery interruption from absence of lung and bronchus; trace distal arteries and systemic collateral supply. Ductal patency/flow needs adequate acquisition and appropriate functional evidence.

steps.label: Pulmonary veins
steps.detail: Trace every pulmonary vein to its drainage and look for anomalous return.
findings: Partial anomalous return of the right upper-lobe vein to the superior vena cava (often with a sinus venosus defect).
Scimitar vein draining the right lung to the IVC.
Left upper-lobe vein draining via a vertical vein to the brachiocephalic vein.
steps.look: Trace each actual lobar/segmental venous channel, common/accessory trunks, dual drainage and the complete collector route to its atrial or systemic endpoint. Record opacification and coverage limits.
steps.tip: Do not assume four separate pulmonary veins. Morphology and right-heart enlargement do not quantify shunt flow or determine haemodynamic significance. Single-phase contrast density does not independently quantify flow direction or Qp/Qs; report the actual functional source.

steps.label: Systemic veins
steps.detail: Identify a left superior vena cava, azygos continuation of the IVC and the left superior intercostal vein.
findings: Persistent left superior vena cava draining into a dilated coronary sinus.
Azygos continuation of the IVC with an enlarged azygos arch.
Prominent left superior intercostal vein (aortic nipple).
steps.look: Follow each SVC and bridging vein to its actual endpoint, assess the coronary sinus/septum and trace covered IVC/hepatic and azygos/hemiazygos connections.
steps.tip: A left SVC usually drains through the coronary sinus to the right atrium, but left-atrial drainage occurs. Do not infer its endpoint from a single left mediastinal vessel or coronary-sinus enlargement. Trace vertical/levoatriocardinal, pericardiophrenic and postoperative mimics to their actual endpoints; single-phase density is not a calibrated flow measurement.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Development of the aorta and branch vessels.  a  Illustration showing the schematic development of the aorta and arch branch vessels from six pairs of aortic arches. Please note that the six arches are never seen together in the foetus, since they develop and regress in a craniocaudal direction. Also, the fifth arch is not present in most foetuses.  b  Illustration showing the fully developed normal left aortic arch and branch vessels, with corresponding colour codes.  a  The left arch between the left common carotid and left subclavian ( red ) is derived from the left fourth arch ( red ). The ventral aorta ( purple ) forms the ascending aorta and the right brachiocephalic trunk while the dorsal aorta ( green ) forms the descending thoracic aorta. The left subclavian artery is derived from the left seventh intersegmental artery ( brown ), while the right subclavian artery is derived proximally from the right fourth arch ( red ), in the mid portion from the right dorsal aorta ( green ) and the distal portion from the right seventh intersegmental artery ( brown ). The aortic root and main pulmonary artery are derived from division of the truncus arteriosus ( pink ). The ductus arteriosus ( blue ) is formed from the dorsal portion of the left sixth arch, while the right and left pulmonary arteries are derived from ventral portions of the right and left sixth arches ( yellow ) respectively. Common carotid arteries are derived from the third arches ( orange ), while internal carotid arteries are formed from the third arches ( orange ) and the dorsal aorta ( green ). External carotid arteries are derived from the third arch branches ( black )

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Double aortic arch.  a  Illustration showing the appearances of a double aortic arch, with a dominant right arch. The right arch gives off the right subclavian ( RSC ) and right common carotid ( RCC ) branches, while the left arch gives off the left subclavian ( LSC ) and left common carotid ( LCC ) arteries. Both the trachea and oesophagus are completely encircled and compressed by the vascular ring.  b  Axial CT scan shows the four-vessel sign. The first branch is the right subclavian ( RSC ) artery, the second is the right common carotid artery ( RCC ), the third is the left common carotid ( LCC ) artery and the fourth is the left subclavian ( LSC ) artery.  c  Axial MIP image shows bilateral aortic arches encircling the trachea and oesophagus. The right aortic arch ( arrow ) is larger than the left aortic arch ( arrowhead ).  d  Coronal reconstructed CT image at the level of the trachea shows a larger right arch ( long arrow ) and a smaller left arch ( smaller arrow ) encircling the trachea ( asterisk ).  e  Coronal MIP CT image at the level of the trachea shows similar-sized double arches in another patient ( arrows ).  f  3D volume-rendered image exquisitely demonstrates the double aortic arch, with a dominant right arch ( arrow ) and a smaller left arch ( arrowhead ), both of which join the descending thoracic aorta (*), which is located on the left.  g  3D volume-rendered image in another patient (same patient as  e ) demonstrates the double aortic arch, with similar sizes of the right arch ( arrow ) and the left arch ( arrowhead ), both of which join the descending thoracic aorta (*), which is located on the left.  h  Coronal volume-rendered image of the airway shows severe narrowing of the airway ( arrow ) by the double aortic arch

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Clinical importance and different drainage sites of PLSVC and possible anatomical changes.  a, b  Posterior-anterior (PA) chest X-ray ( a ), and sagittal-oblique reformatted CT image ( b ) of different patients depict the course of central venous catheters inserted into the PLSVC (red arrows) draining into the right atrium via the coronary sinus (blue star).  c  CT imaging performed to evaluate the cardiac anatomy and possible variations of pulmonary veins draining to the left atrium (LA) before the radiofrequency catheter ablation in a patient with atrial fibrillation. The three-dimensional volume rendering technique (3D VRT) image shows that PLSVC (red arrow), which is detected incidentally, drains to the coronary sinus (CS).  d  Coronal-oblique maximum intensity projection CT image indicates PLSVC (red arrow), which indirectly drains into the left atrium via the left upper pulmonary vein (blue arrow).  e  Sagittal-oblique reformatted CT image shows PLSVC (red arrow) draining into the left atrium via the unroofed coronary sinus (blue arrows). Since ASD (not shown) is also present, the findings are compatible with Raghib syndrome.  f  Sagittal-oblique maximum intensity projection CT image demonstrates that the coronary sinus is connected to the left atrium with an aberrant vein as a collateral drainage pathway in a patient with coronary sinus ostial atresia (not shown). Thus, PLSVC (red arrow) drains into the left atrium through the coronary sinus (red star) and interatrial aberrant vein (blue arrow).  g ,  h  Axial CT ( f ) and 3D VRT images with different views ( g ,  h ) indicate the coronary sinus aneurysm (blue arrows) in a patient with PLSVC (red arrow) draining into the coronary sinus

measurements.name: Aortic annulus
measurements.method: Identify the virtual basal/hinge plane from the actual cusp attachment nadirs in multiplanar imaging; measure the annular contour and orthogonal dimensions in the stated phase. Record variant anatomy and unresolved nadirs.
measurements.pitfall: A fixed one-slice offset or the last visible leaflet is not a reproducible basal-plane definition; slice thickness, phase and cusp/valve morphology matter.

measurements.name: Sinus of Valsalva
measurements.method: Record the maximum sinus-to-sinus root diameter on the appropriate short-axis plane, with named edge convention and cardiac phase. Report multiple dimensions for an asymmetric root; retain any legacy average or alternative axis separately for comparison.
measurements.pitfall: Sinus-to-commissure, mid/maximum sinus-to-sinus and averages are not interchangeable; an average must not silently replace the maximum root diameter.

measurements.name: Thoracic aortic diameter
measurements.method: Use a plane perpendicular to the local aortic axis at every named level. For CT/MRI root and ascending assessment, record inner-edge measurements with ECG synchronisation; report outer-edge dimensions for abnormal thickened wall segments, retaining the actual convention.
measurements.pitfall: Axial slices cut the curved aorta obliquely and give elliptical, overestimated diameters.

measurements.name: Interval change
measurements.method: Compare the same level on the prior study using the same modality and method; give the change in millimetres and the interval.
measurements.pitfall: Small differences can reflect acquisition, phase, edge or plane variability; record comparability and uncertainty before assigning growth or applying clinical thresholds.

pitfalls: Raw axial sections may obliquely sample a curved aorta; retain orthogonal plane/centreline and selected level.
Edge conventions, cardiac phase and root-axis/summary method are not interchangeable; preserve maximal and asymmetric dimensions.
TTE leading-edge and CT/MRI inner/outer-edge methods have different conventions; document the actual method and patient/reference framework rather than treating all values as equivalent.
impression_prompts: What is the maximal diameter, at which level and by which method?
Is the aorta dilated against the sex-specific reference values used locally?
What has changed since the previous study measured the same way, and over what interval?
escalation: Communicate rapid growth, or a diameter at the local surgical threshold, to the referring team.

protocol: Identify every actual device and component using imaging plus available procedure/device records. State projection, coverage, prior revision and limits; unfamiliar or partly visible hardware remains unresolved.

Assess each visible route and landing interface using the appropriate acquired modality and intended device-specific anatomy. Radiographic projection is not exact 3D localisation or proof of function.

If MRI is considered/performed, use actual complete generator/lead/system identification, manufacturer conditions and specialist institutional protocol. Appearance or a generator marker alone does not clear MRI; historical blanket statements about retained leads are not applied as current universal rules.

checklist.label: Device Identification
checklist.detail: Identify each generator, connected/abandoned lead, valve/repair, occluder, stent, pump/cannula, catheter or surgical marker; state actual model/type if supported and unresolved components.

checklist.label: Course
checklist.detail: Trace each actual component from connection/entry to endpoint, including alternative venous/arterial, epicardial, coronary sinus or postoperative routes; record incomplete coverage, bends, slack, separation and uncertainty.

checklist.label: Tip Or Landing Position
checklist.detail: Assess each actual tip, inflow/outflow, electrode, coil, prosthesis, disc or landing zone relative to intended device-specific anatomy and acquisition/projection limits.

checklist.label: Local Complications
checklist.detail: Assess each relevant pocket, access vessel, cardiac/vascular wall, pericardial/pleural compartment and adjacent structure for displacement, perforation, haemorrhage/collection, obstruction and source-supported infection findings.

checklist.label: Comparison And Functional Limits
checklist.detail: Compare actual components at named timepoints with projection/phase differences recorded; state what electrical, valve, pump, haemodynamic and MRI-condition information remains unavailable.

pitfalls: A familiar generator silhouette or MRI symbol does not establish every component, system compatibility or current manufacturer conditions.

A coronary-sinus lead targets a cardiac vein for epicardial LV stimulation; it is not an assumed intracavitary LV lead. Other intended septal/conduction-system/epicardial configurations require actual device/procedure evidence.
Projection and incomplete coverage can mimic displacement or discontinuity; radiographic position cannot exclude subtle perforation, pocket infection or thin-wall complications.
LV assist-device inflow is at the ventricular inlet/cannula and outflow follows its actual graft to the arterial endpoint; temporary left- and right-sided pump configurations are not interchangeable.
A balloon pump requires actual proximal/distal marker and covered balloon/access relationships; a generic distance below the arch is not proof of whole-device suitability.
Static morphology does not establish electrical capture/sensing, valve motion/regurgitation, pump performance, shunt/flow, pressure gradient or clinical tamponade.
impression_prompts: Device recognition, expected position and complications.
State the dominant abnormality, relevant extent and examination limitations.
escalation: Communicate suspected perforation, dangerous displacement, haemorrhage or clinically significant device-related obstruction promptly through the actual clinical pathway; document uncertainty and relevant confirmatory assessment.

steps.label: Device identification
steps.detail: Identify each implanted or inserted cardiovascular device.
findings: Dual-chamber pacemaker with right atrial and right ventricular leads.
Cardiac resynchronisation device with a coronary sinus lead.
Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator with a shock coil in the right ventricle.
[Mechanical / bioprosthetic] valve in the [aortic / mitral] position.
steps.look: Whole radiograph or CT: generator, leads, valves, closure devices, stents, pumps and catheters.
steps.tip: Count and identify every actual component, including abandoned/retained hardware; verify model and intended configuration from records rather than generator shape alone.

steps.label: Course
steps.detail: Trace leads, catheters and conduits along their full course for kinks, fractures and abnormal routes.
findings: Lead fracture at the [clavicle–first rib crossing].
Twisted leads with generator rotation (Twiddler syndrome).
Lead passing through a persistent left superior vena cava.
steps.look: Follow each lead from the generator to the tip on frontal and lateral views.
steps.tip: Follow every component and connection, including nonstandard routes; bending/slack is device-specific and not automatically fracture or malfunction. Identify actual ECMO drainage and return routes and documented circuit type; cannula projection alone does not establish VV/VA configuration, return-jet alignment or recirculation.

steps.label: Tip and landing position
steps.detail: Assess each tip or landing zone relative to the intended anatomy.
findings: Right ventricular lead tip projects beyond the cardiac contour, raising concern for perforation.
Balloon-pump proximal/distal markers and covered balloon/access course: [ ]; named arch/branch-vessel relationships and device-specific position uncertainty: [ ].
Coronary sinus lead in a [lateral] cardiac vein.
steps.look: Use the intended device-specific site: actual atrial, ventricular, conduction-system, coronary sinus/epicardial, valve/closure/stent interface or pump/catheter route. Review balloon markers and covered branch-vessel relationships.
steps.tip: Distinguish LV-assist inflow from arterial outflow; left- and right-sided temporary pump positions differ. A projected tip or a generic arch distance does not validate complete 3D position or safety. For a dual-lumen RA-PA system, distinguish drainage and return lumens/ports using the actual model/source. ProtekDuo manufacturer describes proximal RA drainage and distal main-PA return; the source Figure 12 RV-outlet wording is not adopted as a normal target.

steps.label: Local complications
steps.detail: Review perforation, pericardial effusion, pneumothorax, haematoma and infection.
findings: New pericardial effusion after lead placement.
Pneumothorax after device insertion.
Pocket haematoma or collection.
steps.look: Pericardium and pleura; generator pocket.
steps.tip: State actual modality/coverage limits. A radiograph alone cannot exclude subtle perforation, pocket infection, effusion or physiological tamponade.

steps.label: Comparison and limits
steps.detail: Compare positions with prior imaging and state what function imaging cannot assess.
findings: Lead retraction since [date].
Device migration of __ mm.
steps.look: Prior radiographs and CT.
steps.tip: Compare actual component identity, projection, phase and source calibration. Functional performance requires appropriate interrogation/clinical imaging. Generator appearance alone does not clear MRI; specialist complete-system assessment is separate. Distinguish documented decommissioning/intentional driveline division from unplanned discontinuity. Historical HVAD recognition is not current new-implant suitability; full device-team/advisory review is separate.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP). Chest AP radiograph ( a ) demonstrating the upper radiopaque marker (white arrow) projecting over the aortic knob superior to the carina. This is the expected position based on radiography. Abdomen AP radiograph ( b ) in the same patient demonstrates the IAPB with the inferior radiopaque marker (white arrow) projecting over the L1-L2 Intervertebral space, which is low. Oblique coronal CT ( c ) demonstrates the IAPB in the descending aorta. The radiopaque marker is visible within the descending aorta about 5 cm from the origin of left subclavian artery. Sagittal CT abdomen image ( d ) demonstrates the low position of the IABP with its inferior radiopaque marker (black marker) below the level of the diaphragm at the level of the L1–L2 Intervertebral space. This can be seen when there is anatomic-to-balloon length mismatch

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Complication from low IABP. AP chest radiograph ( a ) of a patient with an intra-aortic balloon pump. The upper radiopaque marker is below the carina (white arrow) which suggests a low position. Sagittal image ( b ) of a contrast enhanced chest and abdomen CT at the level of the celiac trunk and superior mesenteric artery (SMA) origin demonstrates high grade obstruction of the SMA and celiac trunk ostia by the distended IABP. Axial CT image ( c ) identifies complication from hypoperfusion: pneumatosis and contained perforation of the cecum (white arrow), due to the hypoperfusion from the high grade celiac trunk and SMA ostial occlusion. (IABP—Intra-aortic balloon pump)

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Malposition of axillary IABP. AP chest radiograph with contrast limited adaptive histone equalization (CLAHE) filter demonstrating an axillary approach IABP ( a ,  b ). The IABP is malpositioned with the upper marker in the brachiocephalic artery (white arrow on image  a ). The black arrow indicates the location of the sheath. The inflated balloon is seen in the aortic arch and upper descending aorta. The inferior marker is within the descending aorta (dashed arrow).  b  AP chest radiograph after attempted advancement of the IABP, the superior marker is malpositioned and is now in the ascending aorta (white arrow). The inferior marker is in the descending aorta (dashed arrow). (IABP = Intra-aortic balloon pump, CLAHE = Contrast limited adaptive histone equalization)

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Complication from Impella. AP Chest radiograph with a left ventricle Impella device ( a ). The inlet port of the Impella is not in expected location on this radiograph, outlet port is much below the carina (white arrow) and the pigtail portion is coiled in the left ventricle cavity (white dashed arrow). The pigtail portioned is coiled, this is a sign of malposition. This can indicate entrapment within the papillary muscle apparatus. Non-contrast coronal CT at the level of the LVOT ( b ) confirms low positioned of the Impella device. The tip of the device has perforated the left ventricular wall (white arrow) and high density fluid can be seen in the pericardium, compatible with hemopericardium. (LVOT—Left ventricle outflow tract)

protocol: Tailor acquired cardiac CT/MRI/echo assessment to the actual lesion and clinical question. Record source coverage, cardiac phase, temporal/spatial resolution, contrast timing and sequence/artefact limits; no unperformed acquisition or function is assumed.

Compare source history, prior studies and available operative/pathology or clinical findings. Distinguish an actual lesion from normal structures, mixing, artefact and extracardiac mimics; tissue patterns support a differential rather than automatically establish histology.

checklist.label: Location And Attachment
checklist.detail: Localise every actual lesion/pseudomass to its chamber, wall, valve, septum, vessel or pericardial/extracardiac origin; trace each attachment and adjacent interface with unresolved extent recorded.

checklist.label: Morphology
checklist.detail: Describe each lesion component, orthogonal dimensions, contour, stalk/base and local spread; mobility or prolapse requires actual temporal acquisition, not a static picture.

checklist.label: Tissue Characteristics
checklist.detail: Describe actual CT attenuation/calcification and MRI fat, blood, fluid/fibrous or other signal components with sequence, phase, calibration and reference tissues; appearances alone are not histology.

checklist.label: Enhancement
checklist.detail: Assess only obtained first-pass, early/delayed or late enhancement and persistence of filling defects with actual timing/sequence quality; lack of enhancement or a single phase is not a universal diagnosis.

checklist.label: Effects And Spread
checklist.detail: Assess every relevant valve/inflow/outflow, coronary/venous and wall/pericardial interface, obstruction or invasive feature, and covered extracardiac sites; haemodynamic significance and staging need actual source evidence.

measurements.name: Mass dimensions
measurements.method: Measure in orthogonal planes and distinguish attachment from the mobile component.
measurements.pitfall: Cardiac phase and motion can alter apparent size.

pitfalls: Normal ridges, trabeculations, valve remnants, aneurysms and extracardiac structures can mimic a lesion; trace the actual structure and adjacent anatomy.
Thrombus usually lacks enhancement, but organised chronic thrombus can rarely show peripheral enhancement. Tumour-associated thrombus and mixed components must be assessed separately.
A single early filling defect may reflect mixing; resolution/persistence needs appropriate actual timing and quality. Additional phases are not automatic.
Signal, enhancement, FDG uptake, size or attachment pattern alone does not prove tumour type or malignancy; clinical/operative/pathology context and uncertainty matter.
Static position, effusion or apparent narrowing does not quantify mobility, obstruction, regurgitation, haemodynamic significance or tamponade.
impression_prompts: Cardiac mass location, tissue features and non-neoplastic mimics.
State the dominant abnormality, relevant extent and examination limitations.
escalation: Communicate source-supported critical obstruction, suspected embolic complication, severe clinically concerning pericardial involvement or other urgent finding through the actual clinical pathway; record uncertainty and required clinical assessment.

steps.label: Location and attachment
steps.detail: Identify the chamber, tissue of origin, attachment and number of masses.
findings: Left atrial mass attached to the interatrial septum at the fossa ovalis (myxoma pattern).
Left atrial appendage filling defect.
Mass arising from the [ ] valve leaflet.
steps.look: Cine images to show attachment; multiplanar CT.
steps.tip: Trace actual attachment and nearby ridges, remnants, valves and vessels. Typical location is a differential clue, not automatic histology; no normality is inferred from an uncovered interface.

steps.label: Morphology
steps.detail: Describe dimensions, contour and mobility if assessed.
findings: Mass __ × __ mm with a [smooth / lobulated / villous] surface, [mobile / fixed].
Prolapse through the mitral valve in diastole.
steps.look: Orthogonal measurements; cine for mobility and prolapse.
steps.tip: Report actual measurement plane/phase. Mobility and valve prolapse require the obtained cine/echo temporal study; a still image or generic model cannot establish them.

steps.label: Tissue characteristics
steps.detail: Evaluate fat, blood, calcification and MRI signal.
findings: Fat-containing lesion of the interatrial septum sparing the fossa ovalis (lipomatous hypertrophy).
High T2 signal heterogeneous mass (myxoma pattern).
Calcified mass along the mitral annulus (caseous calcification).
steps.look: CT attenuation; MRI T1, T2 and fat-suppressed images.
steps.tip: Use actual CT/MRI sequence and reference tissues. T1/T2, fat/calcification or uptake patterns overlap; clinical/operative/pathology evidence may be required.

steps.label: Enhancement
steps.detail: Assess first-pass perfusion and late enhancement.
findings: No enhancement on the obtained adequately assessed acquisitions: [ ]. Differential confidence and unresolved organised/mixed lesion components: [ ].
Heterogeneous enhancement.
Early appendage filling defect [resolves / persists / remains uncertain] on the actual delayed acquisition; timing, quality and diagnostic confidence: [ ].
steps.look: First-pass perfusion and late gadolinium enhancement; long-inversion-time images for thrombus.
steps.tip: Thrombus usually does not enhance, but organised chronic thrombus may rarely enhance peripherally. Assess actual acquired contrast timing/sequence quality and mixed components; one phase does not establish thrombus or mixing.

steps.label: Effects and spread
steps.detail: Assess obstruction, invasion, pericardium and extracardiac disease.
findings: Obstruction of mitral inflow.
Invasion of the myocardium and pericardium (malignant features).
Pulmonary or pleural deposits.
steps.look: Inflow and outflow on cine; pericardium, mediastinum and lungs.
steps.tip: Document actual covered spread and suspicious interfaces; static appearances do not prove histology, haemodynamic obstruction or tamponade. Correlate appropriate clinical/function/staging evidence.

protocol: Record the actual clinical question, symptom/limb-threat context supplied by the clinical team, side, acquired arterial territory and prior intervention. State CE-MRA or actual noncontrast method, source sequences and per-station coverage/quality.

Record source voxel calibration and acquired versus reconstructed resolution, mask/arterial phases, station overlap and contrast agent/dose/timing if given. Use original source images with multiple reconstructions; unperformed acquisitions and uncovered segments remain unassessed.

checklist.label: Inflow
checklist.detail: Trace the actually covered aortic and iliac inflow, each side and branch configuration; identify unassessed proximal segments.

checklist.label: Segmental Disease
checklist.detail: Map every covered common/deep/superficial femoral and popliteal segment, lesion and variant by side and actual anatomical endpoints.

checklist.label: Lesion Morphology
checklist.detail: Describe each lesion and its native-source minimum lumen, reference, length, morphology and uncertainty; distinguish signal loss from confirmed occlusion.

checklist.label: Runoff And Collaterals
checklist.detail: Trace each actual tibial/peroneal artery to its resolved distal endpoint and each pedal/plantar connection, collateral and reconstitution; do not assume three patent channels.

checklist.label: Technical Limitations
checklist.detail: State per-station acquisition, coverage, source quality, contrast/flow timing, venous overlap and artefact; distinguish a non-diagnostic segment from disease.

measurements.name: Lesion length
measurements.method: Measure each lesion along its actual vessel axis between named source-supported proximal/distal landmarks; record minimum orthogonal lumen, reference site/convention, units and uncertainty if assessed.
measurements.pitfall: Signal loss is not automatically occlusion; an unsupported percentage or projection width is not a calibrated lumen measurement.

pitfalls: An unopacified or uncovered artery is not automatically absent or occluded. Record variant origins and the source evidence for lumen continuity.
Branch names describe actual observed anatomy; hypoplasia, high origin, trifurcation, dominant peroneal supply and postoperative anatomy must be traced rather than substituted with a normal tree.

Stenosis percentage requires a stated measurement/reference convention and adequate native source. MIP overlap, subtraction and flow or metal artefacts can mimic or exaggerate disease; missing lumen evidence remains uncertain.

Tibial channel count does not establish uninterrupted supply to the foot, a complete pedal arch, wound perfusion or tissue viability. Morphological continuity does not by itself establish flow direction, pressure or clinical effect.

Historical scanner/coil, injection, compression-cuff and pixel-count advice is not a universal current protocol or safety clearance. Suspected acute limb ischaemia requires urgent clinical assessment; do not delay care to obtain a routine MRA.
impression_prompts: Summarise dominant source-supported disease by side, named segment, extent and actual distal continuity.
Describe variants, intervention anatomy and confidence; identify unanswered distal-target or clinical questions and non-diagnostic/uncovered segments.
Do not infer haemodynamic severity, wound perfusion, limb viability or treatment outcome from a static angiographic appearance.
escalation: Urgently communicate source findings and limitations when acute limb ischaemia or threatened limb is suspected; clinical viability assessment and management should not be delayed for routine MRA.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Contrast-enhanced continuous table movement (left) and non-enhanced HR-QISS (right) MRA in a 68 y/o male patient suffering from PAOD stage IV. The examination was performed after percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) of the right superficial femoral artery. Both CE-MRA and HR-QISS depict multiple significant (>50%) stenoses in the right superficial femoral artery, an occlusion of the right anterior tibial artery and a single significant short-distance stenosis in the proximal left anterior tibial artery. Note the slightly better image quality of CE-MRA in the distal aorta due to motion artifacts in the HR-QISS sequence. On the other hand, non-enhanced HR-QISS shows less venous overlay.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Contrast-enhanced (left) and non-enhanced HR-QISS (right) MRA in a 72 y/o male with PAOD stage IIb. CE-MRA and HR-QISS findings show excellent correlation. Both techniques reveal a long-distance occlusion of the right superficial femoral artery. The right superficial femoral artery is reconstituted via collaterals from the deep femoral artery. Further occlusions are found in both fibular arteries and the proximal left anterior tibial artery. High-grade stenoses are located in the right anterior tibial artery and in the left superficial femoral artery.

measurements.name: Visible vessel diameter
measurements.method: Measure each actual source-resolved vessel perpendicular to its local axis at a named level, with stated edge convention, units, phase and calibration; retain non-diagnostic boundaries.
measurements.pitfall: Motion, obliquity and nongated/contrast-phase limits affect root/vascular measurements; diameter does not independently measure pressure or shunt/function.

pitfalls: Go-with-the-flow is an anatomical search mnemonic, not a measurement of flow, shunt direction or haemodynamics. Early contrast mixing can mimic LAA or chamber thrombus; report actual evidence and uncertainty rather than diagnose from one filling defect.

Unknown cardiac phase and oblique nongated planes can overestimate wall thickness. Fat, calcium or focal low attenuation support contextual differentials, not automatic infarct timing, viability, scar volume or cardiomyopathy aetiology.

For adequately covered nongated CT, a whole-patient visual CAC burden may be none/mild/moderate/severe with method/limits. That is not CAD-RADS stenosis grading or an uncalibrated Agatston score. Valve calcium alone does not independently establish haemodynamic valve severity.

No universal vessel size or artery-to-aorta ratio proves pulmonary hypertension, shunt flow or acute/chronic disease. Trace actual number, origin and venous drainage; left SVC drainage and pulmonary vein number are not universal normal configurations.

Fluid, thickening or calcification does not independently establish tamponade, constrictive physiology, infection or histology. Static images and generic geometry do not supply physiological measurements.

investigations.title: CT pulmonary hypertension and thromboembolic disease

protocol: State actual clinical question, contrast/CTPA or other acquired CT method, coverage, bolus timing, motion/metal/partial-volume limits and prior treatment/context. Assess every actually covered territory separately.

Separate source CT morphology from dynamic perfusion, V/Q, echo/MRI, catheter pressures/resistance and clinical/tissue diagnosis; identify the source, date, definition and uncertainty of any supplied measurements.

checklist.label: Adequacy
checklist.detail: Record actual arterial opacification, motion/mixing and most distal reliably evaluable level for each side/territory; unassessed segments cannot be negative.

checklist.label: Thrombus
checklist.detail: Describe every source-supported filling defect by named vessel/side, proximal/distal extent, occlusive component and confidence, including acute-on-chronic or mimic uncertainty.

checklist.label: Chronicity
checklist.detail: Describe webs/bands, eccentric material, narrowing/pouch/recanalisation and collaterals with actual source morphology; chronic thromboembolic disease is distinct from confirmed haemodynamic PH.

checklist.label: Right heart
checklist.detail: Record actual phase/method-defined RV/LV and PA/aortic measurements, septal and source-reflux morphology; separate CT clues from obtained cardiac/haemodynamic results.

checklist.label: Consequences
checklist.detail: Review all covered parenchymal/pleural, small-airway/interstitial, left-heart/valve and congenital/venous connections relevant to the supplied question; keep alternative causes and unavailable perfusion/clinical evidence explicit.

measurements.name: RV/LV ratio
measurements.method: Record source RV and LV diameters with named matching method/planes, cardiac phase if known, units/calibration and ratio uncertainty; compare actual prior method/coverage.
measurements.pitfall: Morphological ratio is not independently measured pressure, EF or unique acute strain/aetiology.

measurements.name: Main pulmonary artery
measurements.method: Measure source-resolved PA perpendicular to its local axis at a named level and source phase; use a stated ascending-aortic/reference measurement method and edge convention if ratio is reported.
measurements.pitfall: PA diameter/ratio alone does not diagnose haemodynamic PH or establish a clinical group; motion and contrast/coverage limits remain.

pitfalls: Absent contrast or severe motion is a technical limitation, not proof of occlusion or a negative embolic examination. Record affected segments and unresolved defect/mixing boundaries.

Acute emboli may be eccentric as well as central. No location/angle alone dates a clot or excludes acute-on-chronic disease; distinguish source filling defects from motion, mixing, partial-volume or other mimics.

CTEPD may occur without PH; CT chronic morphology alone does not establish CTEPH or operability. A limited or negative CTPA does not alone exclude distal chronic disease; clinical/perfusion assessment is separate.

CT dimensions, RV/LV, septal shape and reflux suggest morphology, not measured pressure or EF. In the named 2022 ESC/ERS definition PH requires resting mPAP >20 mmHg by haemodynamic source; precapillary pattern also requires PAWP ≤15 mmHg and PVR >2 WU. No such values are inferred from CT.

Emphysema/fibrosis, mosaic attenuation, septal thickening or a filling mass are differential clues, not automatic WHO-group, PVOD, sarcoma, infarct or viability diagnoses. Trace actual connections and retain clinical/tissue/functional uncertainty; no treatment choice is made from the companion model.
impression_prompts: State actual source-supported defects by side, named vessel and full obtained extent with per-territory technical confidence.
Separate acute, chronic, mixed and uncertain morphology from haemodynamic PH, functional severity and clinical/operability conclusions.
Describe associated cardiac, pulmonary venous, lung/pleural and shunt findings with actual source/clinical correlation and unperformed tests.
escalation: Communicate source-suspected acute PE or significant associated cardiac findings and limitations according to local urgency pathways; clinical severity and management depend on supplied clinical/haemodynamic assessment.

sections.heading: IMPRESSION
sections.body:
1. [State actual source-supported defects by side, named vessel and full obtained extent with per-territory technical confidence.]
2. [Separate acute, chronic, mixed and uncertain morphology from haemodynamic PH, functional severity and clinical/operability conclusions.]
3. [Describe associated cardiac, pulmonary venous, lung/pleural and shunt findings with actual source/clinical correlation and unperformed tests.]

sections.heading: RECOMMENDATION AND COMMUNICATION
sections.body:
Recommended next step and rationale: [ ].
Direct communication, when indicated: [recipient, time, method].

notes: Absent contrast or severe motion is a technical limitation, not proof of occlusion or a negative embolic examination. Record affected segments and unresolved defect/mixing boundaries.

Acute emboli may be eccentric as well as central. No location/angle alone dates a clot or excludes acute-on-chronic disease; distinguish source filling defects from motion, mixing, partial-volume or other mimics.

CTEPD may occur without PH; CT chronic morphology alone does not establish CTEPH or operability. A limited or negative CTPA does not alone exclude distal chronic disease; clinical/perfusion assessment is separate.

CT dimensions, RV/LV, septal shape and reflux suggest morphology, not measured pressure or EF. In the named 2022 ESC/ERS definition PH requires resting mPAP >20 mmHg by haemodynamic source; precapillary pattern also requires PAWP ≤15 mmHg and PVR >2 WU. No such values are inferred from CT.

Emphysema/fibrosis, mosaic attenuation, septal thickening or a filling mass are differential clues, not automatic WHO-group, PVOD, sarcoma, infarct or viability diagnoses. Trace actual connections and retain clinical/tissue/functional uncertainty; no treatment choice is made from the companion model.

steps.label: Opacification and evaluable level
steps.detail: Record actual arterial opacification, motion/mixing and most distal reliably evaluable level for each side/territory; unassessed segments cannot be negative.
findings: Limited opacification: evaluable to the [segmental] level only.
Transient interruption of contrast from inspiration (mixing artefact).
steps.look: Original thin arterial source images with orthogonal confirmation by territory; note bolus phase, transient mixing, cardiac/respiratory/metal artefact and partial volume. Do not extrapolate contrast quality from the main PA to distal branches.
steps.tip: Absent contrast or severe motion is a technical limitation, not proof of occlusion or a negative embolic examination. Record affected segments and unresolved defect/mixing boundaries.

steps.label: Acute pulmonary emboli
steps.detail: Describe every source-supported filling defect by named vessel/side, proximal/distal extent, occlusive component and confidence, including acute-on-chronic or mimic uncertainty.
findings: Acute pulmonary emboli in the [right lower-lobe] arteries, most proximal at the [lobar] level.
Saddle embolus at the bifurcation.
steps.look: Trace actual pulmonary trunk/bifurcation, right/left main, each covered lobar/segmental/subsegmental branch and variants. A defect can be central or eccentric; correlate margins, vessel calibre and source quality across planes.
steps.tip: Acute emboli may be eccentric as well as central. No location/angle alone dates a clot or excludes acute-on-chronic disease; distinguish source filling defects from motion, mixing, partial-volume or other mimics.

steps.label: Chronic thromboembolic features
steps.detail: Describe webs/bands, eccentric material, narrowing/pouch/recanalisation and collaterals with actual source morphology; chronic thromboembolic disease is distinct from confirmed haemodynamic PH.
findings: Webs and eccentric wall-adherent thrombus in the [ ] arteries (chronic).
Abrupt narrowing and pouch defects.
Enlarged bronchial arteries.
steps.look: Inspect actual vessel wall/lumen interfaces, webs/slits/bands, ring/length stenoses, pouch/tapered terminations, calcification, recanalisation and bronchial/nonbronchial systemic collateral routes. Retain mixed acute/chronic patterns and alternative intravascular causes.
steps.tip: CTEPD may occur without PH; CT chronic morphology alone does not establish CTEPH or operability. A limited or negative CTPA does not alone exclude distal chronic disease; clinical/perfusion assessment is separate.

steps.label: Right heart and pulmonary artery
steps.detail: Record actual phase/method-defined RV/LV and PA/aortic measurements, septal and source-reflux morphology; separate CT clues from obtained cardiac/haemodynamic results.
findings: RV/LV ratio __ with septal flattening and contrast reflux into the IVC (right-heart strain).
Main pulmonary artery __ mm, larger than the ascending aorta (suggests pulmonary hypertension).
steps.look: Use declared axial/four-chamber or other source methods at stated planes; record phase/edge/calibration and prior comparison. Review RV/RA/LV/septum, valves/outflow, PA branches, coronary/root relations and caval/hepatic contrast reflux with injection context.
steps.tip: CT dimensions, RV/LV, septal shape and reflux suggest morphology, not measured pressure or EF. In the named 2022 ESC/ERS definition PH requires resting mPAP >20 mmHg by haemodynamic source; precapillary pattern also requires PAWP ≤15 mmHg and PVR >2 WU. No such values are inferred from CT.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Echocardiographic findings associated with CTEPH. Note the dilated RV ( A ) and flattened interventricular septum (called the D-shaped LV, red arrows), which suggest RV pressure overloading ( B ). Pericardial effusion (asterisk) can be observed in advanced cases of CTEPH ( B ). Pulsed-wave Doppler image obtained from the RV outflow tract shows a midsystolic notch (arrow) and shortened acceleration time, which reflect increased pulmonary vascular resistance ( C ). Continuous-wave (CW) Doppler analysis at the tricuspid valve reveals a TR Vmax of 4.2 m/s, which strongly suggests significant PH ( D ).

protocol: Use thin-section inspiratory CT and multiplanar airway views.
Add clinically indicated expiratory or dynamic imaging when assessing air trapping or airway collapse.

checklist.label: Central lumen
checklist.detail: Follow trachea and main/lobar bronchi for narrowing, intraluminal material and extrinsic compression.

checklist.label: Bronchiectasis
checklist.detail: Describe distribution, morphology, lack of tapering and peripheral visibility.

checklist.label: Small airways
checklist.detail: Map centrilobular nodules, tree-in-bud change and mucus plugging.

checklist.label: Mosaic pattern
checklist.detail: Compare expiratory attenuation and vessel calibre before attributing mosaic change to air trapping.

checklist.label: Consequences
checklist.detail: Look for collapse, infection and obstructing mass.

measurements.name: Airway narrowing
measurements.method: Measure minimum orthogonal lumen and length of stenosis.
measurements.pitfall: An oblique section exaggerates calibre.

measurements.name: Bronchoarterial relationship
measurements.method: Compare bronchial lumen with its accompanying artery at the same level.
measurements.pitfall: Arterial size varies with perfusion; use multiple bronchiectasis signs.

pitfalls: Dependent secretions can mimic an endobronchial lesion.
Traction bronchiectasis should be interpreted with the surrounding fibrosis.
impression_prompts: State the dominant airway abnormality and distribution.
Identify an obstruction and its downstream effect.
Report whether expiratory assessment supports air trapping.
escalation: Communicate severe central airway compromise promptly when newly identified.

steps.label: Trachea and central bronchi
steps.detail: Follow the trachea and main and lobar bronchi for narrowing, intraluminal material and extrinsic compression.

normal.CENTRAL AIRWAYS: Trachea and central bronchi patent with normal calibre and wall.

findings: Tracheal stenosis at [ ], __ mm long, minimum lumen __ mm (post-intubation pattern).
Endobronchial lesion in the [ ] bronchus.
Circumferential wall thickening sparing the posterior membrane (relapsing polychondritis / tracheobronchopathia pattern).
steps.look: Thin-section axial images with multiplanar and minimum-intensity projections along the airway.
steps.tip: Diseases of the cartilage spare the posterior membrane; dependent mucus can mimic an endobronchial lesion.

steps.label: Bronchiectasis
steps.detail: Describe distribution and morphology, lack of tapering and bronchi visible near the pleura.
findings: [Cylindrical / varicose / cystic] bronchiectasis in the [ ] lobes.
Traction bronchiectasis within fibrosis.
steps.look: Compare each bronchus with its accompanying artery (signet ring); follow bronchi to the periphery.
steps.tip: Traction bronchiectasis belongs to the surrounding fibrosis and is interpreted with it.

steps.label: Small airways
steps.detail: Map centrilobular nodules, tree-in-bud change and mucus plugging.

normal.SMALL AIRWAYS: No tree-in-bud or centrilobular nodules; no mucus plugging.

findings: Tree-in-bud nodules in the [ ], compatible with infectious bronchiolitis.
Mucus plugging of the [ ] bronchi.
steps.look: Lung windows in the periphery.

steps.label: Expiratory imaging
steps.detail: Assess air trapping and dynamic central airway collapse when expiratory images are acquired.

normal.EXPIRATORY FINDINGS: Expiration: [adequate / limited / not acquired]. Air trapping: [not assessed / none / distribution]. Dynamic central airway collapse: [not assessed / findings].

findings: Lobular air trapping in the [ ].
Expiratory collapse of the trachea by more than __%.
Expiratory imaging not acquired; air trapping not assessed.
steps.look: Paired inspiratory and expiratory images at the same levels.
steps.tip: Mosaic attenuation can reflect air trapping, vascular disease or infiltrates; expiration separates them.

steps.label: Consequences
steps.detail: Look for collapse, post-obstructive infection and an obstructing mass.

normal.SECONDARY FINDINGS: No atelectasis, consolidation or obstructing mass.

findings: [Right upper lobe] collapse distal to an obstructing lesion.
Post-obstructive consolidation.
steps.look: Lobes distal to a narrowed airway.

protocol: Confirm actually acquired views and source position, coverage, acquisition time and processing. Compare prior views with their own geometry/quality; missing lateral or other projections remain unavailable.

checklist.label: Quality
checklist.detail: Record actual source projection, position, acquisition/coverage and quality; distinguish technical limitations and artefacts from disease.

checklist.label: Airways and mediastinum
checklist.detail: Inspect every covered airway, hilar, mediastinal and cardiac silhouette/interface with source projection limits; do not infer resolved chamber/wall anatomy or physiology from overlap.

checklist.label: Lungs
checklist.detail: Describe each actual pulmonary opacity/lucency, vascular or volume-change pattern and covered regional extent; assess hidden and overlapping areas with appropriate uncertainty.

checklist.label: Pleura
checklist.detail: Assess each actually visible pleural/diaphragmatic/recess interface and complication, with projection/position-dependent visibility and source limits.

checklist.label: Devices and review areas
checklist.detail: Trace each actually present device and inspect all covered osseous/soft-tissue/upper-abdominal review regions; record full obtained route/tip/landmark relation and unresolved extent.

measurements.name: Cardiothoracic ratio
measurements.method: Record actual cardiac/thoracic diameter method, acquired projection, position, inspiration and source calibration/uncertainty. Interpret only within a stated appropriate protocol.
measurements.pitfall: AP/supine magnification and low inspiration do not supply a comparable standard PA ratio or measured cardiac function.

measurements.name: Device tip distance
measurements.method: Use actual tip/port and named source landmark on a stated view/position with real calibration; record respiratory/temporal and overlap uncertainty.
measurements.pitfall: A projected distance or single view does not prove full3D intraluminal course, intended device function or unchanged position.

pitfalls: Technical correction, crop or annotation removal can change source presentation; preserve original source and disclose processing. An unavailable or limited view is not an adequately assessed negative study.

CTR interpretation requires the actual method and projection; AP/supine magnification or poor inspiration must not be treated as standard PA size. Silhouette enlargement does not measure pressure, EF, shunt or establish a unique cause.

Consolidation, oedema, infection, haemorrhage, collapse and malignancy can overlap. Air bronchograms or projected volume-loss signs support a differential, not unique pathology or microscopic confirmation.

An inconspicuous pneumothorax/effusion on a limited/supine film is not exclusion. Do not derive an exact fluid volume, tension physiology or fluid chemistry from one projection. Free gas/urgent findings require actual source and clinical assessment.

No device or complication is asserted absent until actual covered sources are assessed. Projected tip distances require named landmarks, phase/position and calibration; lumen/wall/3D course and dynamic function may remain unresolved.

escalation: Communicate suspected urgent pneumothorax, free gas, device complication or acute cardiopulmonary findings through local clinical pathways; tension/instability depends on actual source and clinical assessment.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Correct Positioning of a Nasogastric (NG) Tube on Radiographs Radiographs demonstrating appropriate placement of a nasogastric tube. (A) NG tube coursing midline through the esophagus, crossing the diaphragm, and terminating within the gastric body (arrow). Proper recognition of these features is essential to distinguish correct intragastric positioning from esophageal or airway malposition.

measurements.name: Representative cysts
measurements.method: Measure selected source-resolved lesions in stated orthogonal/local planes, wall/airspace edge convention, reconstruction/window and actual calibration; describe justified range, burden estimate and uncertainty.

pitfalls: Wall thickness or apparent absence alone is not a diagnostic cutoff; partial volume, reconstruction and orientation affect thin walls. Thick/irregular components and a cyst-like cavity require a stated differential.

The source four-cysts/age-forty rule is a contextual heuristic, not a diagnosis or exclusion rule, particularly with recurrent pneumothorax or suspected hereditary disease. Costophrenic distribution supports a differential, not a unique diagnosis.

New/growing mural solid tissue or changing cyst-associated nodules warrant appropriate clinical evaluation. Wall thinning or low/negative PET uptake alone does not establish benignity; no PET finding is borrowed when PET was not obtained.

LAM/BHD-FDS/PLCH/LIP/AMP-DIP patterns overlap with infection, neoplasia, deposition and other causes. Record morphology and uncertainty; source terminology does not prove histology, genotype or functional severity.

No pneumothorax, chylous fluid, renal tumour, systemic disease or hereditary finding may be asserted from unassessed anatomy. CT fluid is not proven chyle; urgency depends on actual findings and clinical context.

steps.label: Cyst morphology
steps.detail: Trace each actual cyst or cyst-like lesion through obtained source planes; describe wall, contents, shape, septa, mural components and airway/vessel continuity with source uncertainty.
findings: Round thin-walled cysts __–__ mm, uniformly distributed (LAM pattern).
Bizarre-shaped cysts with nodules (Langerhans cell histiocytosis pattern).
Lentiform subpleural and paramediastinal cysts (Birt–Hogg–Dubé pattern).
steps.look: Use original thin sections and matching reformats, multiple windows, stated reconstruction/calibration and local axes. Distinguish cysts from cavities, bullae/emphysema, pneumatoceles, honeycombing and cystic bronchiectasis; do not infer epithelial lining or microscopic wall layers from CT.
steps.tip: Wall thickness or apparent absence alone is not a diagnostic cutoff; partial volume, reconstruction and orientation affect thin walls. Thick/irregular components and a cyst-like cavity require a stated differential.

steps.label: Distribution
steps.detail: Record actual count/extent and regional distribution across every covered lobe, axial compartment, pleural recess and fissural/mediastinal interface; identify coverage limits.
findings: Upper-zone predominance with sparing of the costophrenic angles.
Diffuse distribution including the bases.
Lower-zone, subpleural and paramediastinal predominance.
steps.look: Inspect each actual covered side/lobe/region and variant: apical/basal, central/peripheral, peribronchovascular, subpleural/paramediastinal and interlobar relationships. Representative pictures cannot establish full cyst count or exclusion of disease elsewhere.
steps.tip: The source four-cysts/age-forty rule is a contextual heuristic, not a diagnosis or exclusion rule, particularly with recurrent pneumothorax or suspected hereditary disease. Costophrenic distribution supports a differential, not a unique diagnosis.

steps.label: Associated nodules
steps.detail: Describe each solid/cavitating nodule, mural or intracystic component and its relationship to cysts, airways and vessels; assess actual prior change.
findings: Centrilobular and cavitating nodules in the upper zones.
steps.look: Record wall nodularity/irregular thickening, intracystic material, traversing vessels and adjacent nodules/masses. Trace airway continuity and assess prior source images at matched sites without assuming registration.
steps.tip: New/growing mural solid tissue or changing cyst-associated nodules warrant appropriate clinical evaluation. Wall thinning or low/negative PET uptake alone does not establish benignity; no PET finding is borrowed when PET was not obtained.

steps.label: Background lung
steps.detail: Describe intervening parenchyma, ground glass, septa, reticulation, fibrosis, honeycombing, emphysema and airway change with source phase and differential.
findings: Ground glass with perivascular cysts (LIP pattern).
Ground glass with small cysts (DIP pattern).
steps.look: Assess every covered regional airway/interstitial/vascular interface. Expiratory air trapping, perfusion and dynamic behaviour require those actually acquired sources; inspiratory CT alone does not provide them.
steps.tip: LAM/BHD-FDS/PLCH/LIP/AMP-DIP patterns overlap with infection, neoplasia, deposition and other causes. Record morphology and uncertainty; source terminology does not prove histology, genotype or functional severity.

steps.label: Context and complications
steps.detail: Review pleura, pneumothorax/fluid, covered nodes and systemic findings; separate observed CT from supplied history, genetics, microbiology or tissue evidence.
findings: Pneumothorax on the [ ].
Renal angiomyolipomas in the upper abdomen (tuberous sclerosis / LAM).
Renal lesion in the upper abdomen (Birt–Hogg–Dubé context).
steps.look: Assess actual pleura/recesses, mediastinal/hilar nodes and covered upper abdominal organs. Renal, cutaneous, genetic, infection and smoking/autoimmune context must come from supplied current source/history, not the teaching-case diagnosis.
steps.tip: No pneumothorax, chylous fluid, renal tumour, systemic disease or hereditary finding may be asserted from unassessed anatomy. CT fluid is not proven chyle; urgency depends on actual findings and clinical context.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Pulmonary cysts in patients with PJP. CT images (A-E) illustrate that all cysts are located within areas of GGOs. In some cases, the cysts are distributed in a subpleural location (A-B), which may confer a potential risk of cyst rupture and secondary pneumothorax. In other patients, the cysts are surrounded by GGOs with superimposed interlobular and intralobular septal thickening, forming the so-called crazy-paving pattern (C-E, black arrow and arrowhead). Panel F provides a more representative example of the crazy-paving pattern. Abbreviations: PJP =  Pneumocystis jirovecii  pneumonia; GGO = ground-glass opacity.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Common cystic and cyst-like lesions. Bulla (A): large (>1 cm), air-containing structures with very thin walls. Cystic bronchiectasis (B): dilated bronchi manifest as non-tapering tubular structures extending peripherally to within 1 cm of the pleura; their continuity across adjacent axial and coronal planes helps differentiate them from isolated cysts. The “signet ring” sign (red arrow) is evident, with a dilated bronchus appearing as a ring adjacent to a smaller pulmonary artery that mimics the signet of a ring. Emphysema (C-D): centrilobular and paraseptal emphysema (C); panlobular emphysema (D). Honeycombing (E): bilateral, predominantly peripheral, and basal-predominant honeycombing is observed, characterized by clustered cystic air spaces of variable size with well-defined walls. Cystic lung cancer (F): a multilobulated cystic lesion measuring approximately 1.5 cm in the right lower lobe. The lesion shows irregular wall thickening with indistinct margins and contains an eccentric mural nodule and internal septations.

pitfalls: Ground glass alone is not fibrosis, unique inflammation, infection or a specific histology. Motion, under-inspiration, window/reconstruction and partial volume may alter apparent pattern and thin tissue borders.
A representative still cannot establish whole-lung disease absence, burden or a microscopic lobular map. State mixed patterns, each actual region and unassessed coverage.

A CT UIP pattern does not equal idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis; secondary causes and multidisciplinary confidence matter. Honeycombing can overlap other fibrotic diseases; CT appearance is not the histological definition.

Do not assert no air trapping on an unperformed expiration or resolution on an unperformed prone scan. Air trapping/mosaicism alone does not uniquely diagnose HP; bronchiolocentric features can have other causes.

CT progression alone does not establish PPF. The named2022 definition uses at least two of symptoms/radiology/physiology within one year, no alternative explanation, in fibrotic ILD other than IPF. Preserve actual dates and sources; new acute opacity is not unique for exacerbation.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Computed tomography (CT) signs of pulmonary fibrosis. Honeycombing, characterised by destruction of lung parenchyma replaced by well-defined cystic spaces with thick walls, typically clustered in multiple layers in the subpleural region ( a ). Traction bronchiectasis, characterised by bronchial irregular dilatation in a background of intralobular fibrosis. Note the mild volume reduction of the right lower lobe, demonstrated by the posterior displacement of the major fissure ( b ). Fibrotic reticulation with irregular thickening of the interlobular and intralobular septa, associated with distal traction bronchiolectasis, in the subpleural region ( c ). Architectural distortion of the lung is present in all CT images

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Computed tomography (CT) patterns of fibrotic lung diseases with mid-lower zone predominant distribution. Axial and sagittal CT images showing a usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern, characterised by honeycombing and reticular pattern with (or without) traction bronchiectasis, and a typical peripheral predominance in the lower lobes but also in the anterior region of the upper lobes (helical distribution) ( a ,  b ). Axial and sagittal CT images depicting a probable UIP pattern, characterised by a reticular pattern with distal traction bronchiectasis, with the same distribution as typical UIP but lacking honeycombing ( c ,  d ). Axial and coronal CT images of a fibrotic nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (fNSIP), with reticular pattern and traction bronchiectasis showing a typical peribronchovascular distribution. Note the volume reduction of the lower lobes ( e ,  f )

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Computed tomography (CT) patterns of fibrotic lung diseases with upper-mid predominant distribution. Axial and sagittal CT images ( a – c ) showing peribronchovascular conglomerate masses in the upper lobes associated with parenchymal and airways distortion in the right upper lobe in a fibrotic sarcoidosis. Axial and sagittal CT images ( d – f ) demonstrating reticulation and mild traction bronchiectasis with a peribronchovascular predominant distribution, in a fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis. Note the association with centrilobular ground-glass nodules, partially confluent, and a mild ‘three-density pattern’ in the upper-mid zones

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF). Axial and coronal computed tomography (CT) images ( a – c ) showing mild signs of fibrosis without honeycombing in the subpleural areas bilaterally, with mild predominance in the lung bases, suggestive of a probable usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern in a patient with chronic exposure to pigeons. The multidisciplinary discussion provided a provisional diagnosis of fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis (fHP). Due to worsening dyspnoea, the patient underwent a follow-up CT after 13 months. Axial and coronal CT images ( d – f ) demonstrate unequivocal disease progression with respect to the previous exam, with increased extent and coarseness of the irregular interstitial thickening and traction bronchiectasis, predominant at the periphery in the upper lobes and more extensive in the mid-lower lungs, associated with marked ‘three-density pattern’ (in inspiratory scans) and lung volume loss. A diagnosis of fHP with progressive behaviour was confirmed, and antifibrotic treatment was initiated

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF). Axial and coronal computed tomography (CT) images ( a – c ) showing mild reticulation with slight central traction bronchiectasis/bronchiolectasis, predominant in the lung bases, suggestive of a nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) pattern in a patient with systemic sclerosis. Axial and coronal CT images ( d – f ) performed after 15 months due to worsening dyspnoea, demonstrate evident progression to fibrotic NSIP (fNSIP), with increased reticulation coarseness, central traction bronchiectasis and parenchymal distortion, predominant in the lung bases, and increased volume loss ( f ). Note that image analysis is conducted at the same anatomic levels to accurately assess disease progression. Antifibrotic treatment was started
