structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Acute exacerbation of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Axial and sagittal computed tomography (CT) images ( a – c ) depicting a usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern with the typical peripheral predominant distribution, in the mid-lower posterior zones and antero-superior zones of the lungs ( c ). Honeycombing is evident in the anterior segment of the right upper lobe ( a ). Axial and sagittal CT images ( d – f ) performed 15 months later in the emergency department for acute respiratory distress of the patient show the appearance of almost diffuse areas of ground-glass opacity in both lungs, mostly in the areas relatively spared by fibrosis, suggestive of acute exacerbation. After 40 days from the acute phase, a new chest CT scan was requested for persisting chest pain. Axial and sagittal CT images ( g – i ), analysed at the same anatomic levels as before, demonstrate the presence of spontaneous pneumomediastinum, explained by the alveoli rupture and interstitial emphysema due to distress; interesting to note the evident progression of pulmonary fibrosis respect to the previous exam, which is a common occurrence after an acute exacerbation

checklist.label: Confidence

measurements.name: Primary diameter
measurements.method: Measure maximal tumour extent; record the solid component separately in a part-solid primary.
measurements.pitfall: Do not include adjacent atelectasis as tumour without evidence.

measurements.pitfall: Neither size nor FDG avidity is histological confirmation.

steps.tip: In part-solid tumours the T category depends on the solid (invasive) component size.

steps.label: Local extent (T descriptors)
steps.detail: Check airway involvement, atelectasis, pleura, chest wall, mediastinum and separate nodules.
findings: Involvement of the main bronchus without carina involvement, with atelectasis to the hilum (T2).
Chest wall invasion (T3).
Invasion of the mediastinum / great vessels / carina (T4).
Separate nodule in the same lobe (T3) / different ipsilateral lobe (T4).
steps.look: Soft-tissue and lung windows; relation to the main bronchus, carina, pleura and mediastinal structures.

steps.label: Regional nodes
steps.detail: Name suspicious stations and laterality; separate single-station from multiple-station N2 disease.

normal.REGIONAL NODES: No suspicious hilar or mediastinal nodes.

findings: Ipsilateral hilar node (N1).
Single ipsilateral mediastinal station [4R] (N2a).
Multiple ipsilateral mediastinal stations (N2b).
Contralateral mediastinal or supraclavicular node (N3).
steps.look: IASLC nodal map; short axis at each station.
steps.tip: Station 1 (supraclavicular) nodes are N3 on either side.

steps.label: Distant disease
steps.detail: Inspect pleura, pericardium, contralateral lung, adrenals, liver and imaged bones.

normal.DISTANT DISEASE: No pleural, contralateral lung or extrathoracic metastases in the field.

findings: Pleural nodules / malignant effusion (M1a).
Single extrathoracic metastasis in the [adrenal] (M1b).
Multiple extrathoracic metastases in [one / several] organ systems (M1c1 / M1c2).
steps.look: Pleural surfaces; adrenals and liver on the upper abdominal coverage; bones.

steps.label: Imaging stage
steps.detail: Summarise imaging T, N and M with the TNM edition and the findings whose confirmation would change stage.
findings: Clinical imaging stage (TNM 9th edition): cT__ cN__ cM__.

steps.look: Combine the descriptors above; name the edition.

Visceral (middle) mediastinal mass.
Paravertebral (posterior) mass extending into the neural foramen.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Assess soft tissue, fluid, fat, calcification and enhancement.
findings: Fluid-attenuation cyst with a thin wall (e.g., bronchogenic or pericardial cyst).
Fat, fluid and calcification (teratoma pattern).
Homogeneous soft-tissue mass with enhancement.
steps.look: CT attenuation before and after contrast.

steps.label: Local relationships
steps.detail: Assess displacement or invasion of vessels, airway and oesophagus.

normal.LOCAL RELATIONSHIPS: No compression or invasion of adjacent structures.

findings: Compression of the superior vena cava.
Tracheal displacement / narrowing.
Invasion of the pericardium.
steps.look: Fat planes around the mass; vessel and airway calibre.

steps.label: Nodal stations

normal.NODAL MAP: No enlarged mediastinal or hilar nodes.

findings: Enlarged nodes in stations [4R, 7], short axis up to __ mm.
Necrotic nodes.
Calcified nodes.
steps.look: IASLC map: stations 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10; short axis.
steps.tip: Assign stations by their anatomic landmarks, not by proximity to a large vessel.

protocol: Record actually acquired views/modalities, contrast/sequence/phase, coverage, quality and available comparison. Do not substitute CT/MRI/US tissue information when the source is only a radiograph.
Describe observed thoracic morphology and its differential. Infection/disease/resistance are distinct diagnostic domains; supplied clinical and laboratory sources cannot be invented from images.

checklist.label: Parenchyma
checklist.detail: Record every actual consolidation/nodule/cavity or other parenchymal component, source site/extent and quality, with a supported differential.

checklist.label: Spread pattern
checklist.detail: Describe actually resolved airway-centred, random/miliary or other distribution and acquired regional extent; do not infer unique organism or microscopic spread from morphology.

checklist.label: Nodes
checklist.detail: Describe every covered nodal site and source-resolved size/internal/adjacent interface; distinguish projection overlap or unresolved tissue from verified nodes.

checklist.label: Pleura and airways
checklist.detail: Inspect actual pleural, airway and relevant thoracic complications with source modality/phase and full obtained connections; clinical effect/organism remains separate.

checklist.label: Sequelae and comparison
checklist.detail: Record actual sequelae and matching-source change; separate apparent chronic morphology from supplied clinical/microbiological confirmation, activity, infectivity and resistance.

measurements.name: Cavity or collection
measurements.method: Record actual site, source modality/projection, local axes/edge convention/window and calibration for representative dimensions; describe full obtained extent and uncertainty.
measurements.pitfall: One source still does not supply whole3D extent or unique TB diagnosis; measurements depend on actual source technique.

pitfalls: Cavitation, consolidation, nodules or an apparent fungal-ball component are not unique TB or independently proven microbiology. Missing or limited views cannot be negative disease evidence.

Imaging distribution alone does not distinguish new infection from reactivation, establish bacillary viability/infectivity, or prove drug resistance. Actual immune/clinical context must be supplied, not inferred.
Necrotic-appearing/enlarged/calcified nodes have a differential. Imaging alone does not supply tissue histology, acid-fast results, genotype or resistance status.

Imaging fluid is not proven TB/chyle or a physiological severity measurement. Possible haemoptysis-related vascular lesions or other urgent complications require actual acquired evidence and clinical assessment.

Scarring or calcification does not alone exclude coexisting active disease or establish noninfectivity. Normal imaging does not exclude latent infection or unavailable microscopic disease. State uncertainty and missing confirmation; do not infer successful treatment from unmatched stills.
impression_prompts: State actual source-supported morphology, regional extent and examination limits with a differential.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Various appearances of ultrasound (US) imaging in patients with pleural TB. All patients were examined with convex US transducers scanning through the intercostal space. (A) US image in an 85-year-old woman shows homogeneously anechoic effusion with underlying lung atelectasis (open arrows). US-guided thoracentesis was performed (arrowheads indicate needle). L = liver. (B) US image in a 59-year-old man shows smooth pleural thickening (solid arrows) and complex pleural effusion with thin septa (arrowheads). There is also cavitation (open arrows) in the adjacent lung consolidation. (C) US image in a 60-year-old man shows irregular pleural thickening and nodularity (open arrows) with complex thick septations (arrowheads) within the pleural effusion.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Right empyema necessitans with bronchopleural fistula in a 47-year-old woman with disseminated TB. Axial contrast-enhanced CT images obtained in (A) lung and (B) soft tissue windows show the fistulous tract (arrowheads in A) between right lower lobe bronchus and empyema in right pleural space with extension into the chest wall (arrows in A and B). Soft tissue setting image better shows the right hydropneumothorax with associated smooth pleural thickening and heterogeneous enhancement of the atelectatic right lower lobe (asterisk in B), indicating pneumonia in the atelectatic lung. Small left pleural effusion is also seen.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Tuberculous (TB) lymphadenitis in a 56-year-old woman who presented with a palpable right axillary mass. (A) Right medial-lateral oblique (MLO) mammogram image shows multiple enlarged, dense axillary lymph nodes without abnormality in the breast. (B) Corresponding colour Doppler ultrasound (US) image shows an enlarged axillary lymph node with heterogeneous echogenicity and internal cystic component (arrows). US-guided fine-needle aspiration of the internal cystic component showed caseous necrotic material with positive acid-fast bacilli. (C) Right MLO mammogram taken 1 year following anti-TB therapy shows coarse calcifications in the enlarged axillary lymph nodes.

steps.label: Location and shape
steps.detail: Localise to the thymic region and assess contour and size with the patient's age.
findings: Diffusely enlarged thymus with preserved shape (hyperplasia pattern).
Round / lobulated focal mass __ × __ mm in the thymic region.
steps.look: Prevascular mediastinum; normal thymus is triangular or bilobed with straight or concave margins.
steps.tip: Normal and rebound thymus can look mass-like in young patients; age and shape are key.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Identify fat, fluid, soft tissue and calcification.
findings: Fluid-attenuation thymic cyst.
Soft-tissue mass with calcification.
Fat, fluid and calcification (teratoma).
steps.look: CT attenuation.

steps.label: MRI characterisation
steps.detail: Describe chemical-shift signal loss and T1/T2 signal.
findings: Signal loss on opposed-phase images: thymic hyperplasia.
No signal loss: soft-tissue lesion such as thymoma or lymphoma.
steps.look: In- and opposed-phase MRI.
steps.tip: Chemical-shift signal drop indicates fat within the gland and favours hyperplasia over thymoma.

steps.label: Enhancement and invasion
steps.detail: Assess enhancement and relation to vessels and pericardium.
findings: Invasion of the [pericardium / great vessels] (invasive thymoma or thymic carcinoma).
steps.look: Contrast-enhanced images; fat planes with the great vessels and pericardium.

steps.label: Pleura and nodes
steps.detail: Review pleural deposits, nodes and interval change.
findings: Pleural drop metastases.
Mediastinal lymphadenopathy (thymic carcinoma or lymphoma).
Interval change since [date].
steps.look: Pleural surfaces for drop metastases; nodal stations.

steps.label: Space of origin
steps.detail: Localise the epicentre to a named space above or below the hyoid.
findings: Lesion centred in the [parapharyngeal / masticator / parotid / carotid / retropharyngeal / perivertebral / visceral] space.
Lesion extends from the suprahyoid to the infrahyoid neck.
steps.look: Axial T1 without fat suppression to see preserved fat planes; identify the parapharyngeal fat as the key landmark.
steps.tip: The direction in which the parapharyngeal fat is displaced tells you the space of origin.

steps.label: Tissue characteristics
steps.detail: Describe composition, T1 and T2 signal, diffusion and enhancement.
findings: T2-bright, well-defined lesion with heterogeneous enhancement (pleomorphic adenoma pattern).
Flow voids with intense enhancement (paraganglioma: salt-and-pepper pattern).
Restricted diffusion with homogeneous enhancement (lymphoma pattern).
Non-enhancing fluid (cyst).
steps.look: T1, T2, fat-suppressed post-contrast images and DWI.

steps.label: Displacement pattern
steps.detail: Assess how fat planes and the carotid and jugular vessels are displaced.
findings: Parapharyngeal fat displaced [anteromedially / posterolaterally].
Carotid artery displaced anteriorly (post-styloid / carotid space lesion).
Internal and external carotid arteries splayed (carotid body paraganglioma).
steps.look: Axial images at the level of maximal lesion size.
steps.tip: Splaying of the internal and external carotid arteries at the bifurcation indicates a carotid body tumour.

steps.label: Spread and critical structures
steps.detail: Assess airway, skull base, perineural pathways and visceral extension.

normal.SPREAD AND CRITICAL STRUCTURES: No airway compromise; skull base and neural pathways intact.

findings: Extension to the skull base through the [foramen ovale].
Airway narrowed to __ mm.
Invasion of the [larynx / thyroid].
steps.look: Coronal images to the skull base; foramina and nerves; airway calibre.

steps.label: Nodes and complications
steps.detail: Review regional nodes, collections and venous thrombosis.

normal.NODES AND COMPLICATIONS: No suspicious nodes, collection or thrombosis.

findings: Suspicious nodes at level [ ].
Retropharyngeal abscess __ mm with rim enhancement.
Internal jugular vein thrombosis.
steps.look: Nodal levels; rim-enhancing collections; jugular veins.

steps.label: Location
steps.detail: Localise the mass relative to the midline, hyoid and neck spaces, with the child's age.
findings: Midline cystic mass at the level of the hyoid.
Lateral cystic mass anterior to the sternocleidomastoid at the angle of the mandible.
Posterior triangle multiloculated mass.
steps.look: Ultrasound first: midline versus lateral; relation to the hyoid, sternocleidomastoid and thyroid.
steps.tip: Location is the strongest clue: midline suggests thyroglossal duct or dermoid cyst; anterior to sternocleidomastoid suggests a second branchial cleft cyst.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Describe cystic or solid components, septa, debris and calcification.
findings: Unilocular cyst with thin wall and internal debris.
Multiloculated cystic mass with fluid levels (lymphatic malformation).
Solid mass with calcification (pilomatrixoma / teratoma / neuroblastoma).
steps.look: Ultrasound with high-frequency probe; MRI for deep extension.

steps.label: Vascularity
steps.detail: Assess internal and peripheral flow or enhancement and vessel relationships.
findings: Avascular cyst.
Hypervascular solid mass (infantile haemangioma pattern).
Venous malformation with phleboliths and slow flow.
steps.look: Colour Doppler; contrast MRI when performed.

steps.label: Anatomic connections
steps.detail: Look for a tract, gland of origin or other structural connection, and airway effect.
findings: Cyst embedded in the strap muscles with a tract to the hyoid (thyroglossal duct cyst).
Fusiform enlargement of the sternocleidomastoid in an infant (fibromatosis colli).
Ectopic thyroid tissue with an empty thyroid bed.
steps.look: Relation to the hyoid, thyroid, salivary glands and sternocleidomastoid.
steps.tip: Confirm a normal thyroid in its bed before a midline mass is removed; it may be the only thyroid tissue.

steps.label: Nodes and infection
steps.detail: Assess nodal patterns and inflammatory complications such as abscess.
findings: Suppurative lymphadenitis with abscess __ mm.
Necrotic nodes with minimal surrounding inflammation (atypical mycobacterial pattern).
Multiple enlarged nodes without hila (lymphoma to be considered).
steps.look: Nodes: hilum, shape, necrosis; surrounding fat; collections.

steps.label: Primary site
steps.detail: Identify the lesion epicentre, subsite and dimensions.
findings: Mass in the [ ] measuring __ × __ × __ mm.
Enhancing tumour separate from T2-bright retained secretions in the obstructed sinus.
steps.look: Contrast-enhanced MRI or CT; separate tumour from retained secretions on T2 and post-contrast images.
steps.tip: On MRI, retained secretions are T2-bright and non-enhancing; tumour is intermediate and enhances.

steps.label: Growth pattern and local invasion
steps.detail: Inspect fat planes, muscle, bone and cartilage, and whether growth is expansile or destructive.
findings: Destructive bone erosion (aggressive growth pattern).
Smooth expansile remodelling (slow-growing lesion).
Invasion of the [pterygoid muscles / orbit / cartilage].
steps.look: Bone windows on CT; T1 marrow signal on MRI.
steps.tip: Bone destruction suggests malignancy; smooth remodelling suggests a slow benign process such as a mucocele.

steps.label: Perineural spread
steps.detail: Review neural pathways and skull-base foramina for spread.
findings: Obliteration of fat in the pterygopalatine fossa with enhancement along V2.
Enlargement and enhancement of the [ ] nerve through the foramen [ ].
steps.look: Pterygopalatine fossa, foramen rotundum and ovale, Meckel cave; fat-suppressed post-contrast MRI.
steps.tip: Loss of fat in the pterygopalatine fossa is an early sign of perineural spread.

protocol: Use thin-section CT with bone reformats for trauma or foreign body; contrast CT/MRI for inflammatory or mass questions as appropriate.
For MRI, include fat-suppressed orbital planes and optic pathways; establish safety when a metallic foreign body is possible.

checklist.label: Compartment

checklist.label: Globe
checklist.detail: Assess contour, lens, vitreous, retina and visible foreign material.

checklist.label: Muscles and nerve
checklist.detail: Describe extraocular muscle/tendon and optic nerve/sheath findings.

checklist.label: Apex and extension
checklist.detail: Inspect optic canal, superior orbital fissure, cavernous sinus and intracranial spread.

checklist.label: Bone and infection
checklist.detail: Review fractures, entrapment features, sinus source and collections.

measurements.name: Lesion/collection
measurements.method: Record three dimensions and relation to globe and optic nerve.
measurements.pitfall: Small apical lesions may have major visual consequences.

measurements.name: Proptosis comparison
measurements.method: Measure each globe relative to the same interzygomatic reference plane if clinically useful.
measurements.pitfall: Head rotation and baseline facial asymmetry affect the comparison.

pitfalls: Muscle herniation on CT does not alone establish clinical entrapment.
Exclude an intraocular metallic foreign body before MRI in the appropriate trauma setting.
impression_prompts: What compartment and structures are involved?
Is vision threatened by apical compression, infection or globe injury?
What bone, sinus or intracranial extension changes management?
escalation: Immediately communicate suspected globe rupture, orbital compartment syndrome pattern or orbital-apical/intracranial infection.

steps.label: Globes and preseptal tissues
steps.detail: Assess globe contour and size, lens, vitreous, retina, choroid, intraocular material and preseptal swelling.

normal.GLOBES AND PRESEPTAL TISSUES: Globes normal in contour; lenses in place; no intraocular abnormality; no preseptal swelling.

findings: Globe rupture: flattened posterior contour (flat tyre sign) with intraocular haemorrhage.
Intraocular metallic foreign body in the [ ] globe.
Retinal / choroidal detachment.
Calcified intraocular mass in a child (retinoblastoma to be considered).
steps.look: Axial and coronal thin sections; soft-tissue and bone windows for foreign body.
steps.tip: Exclude a metallic intraocular foreign body with CT before MRI after trauma.

steps.label: Orbital compartments
steps.detail: Localise any lesion or collection to the extraconal, conal or intraconal compartment and measure it.

normal.ORBITAL COMPARTMENTS: No orbital mass or collection; no proptosis.

findings: Subperiosteal abscess along the [medial] orbital wall, __ × __ × __ mm.
Intraconal well-circumscribed mass with progressive fill-in enhancement (venous malformation pattern).
Lacrimal gland enlargement.
steps.look: Axial and coronal images; the extraocular muscle cone defines the compartments.

steps.label: Muscles and optic nerves
steps.detail: Describe extraocular muscle and tendon involvement and optic nerve or sheath findings.

normal.MUSCLES AND OPTIC NERVES: Extraocular muscles and optic nerves normal.

findings: Enlargement of the [inferior and medial rectus] bellies sparing the tendons (thyroid eye disease pattern).
Muscle enlargement including the tendon with fat stranding (orbital inflammation).
Optic nerve sheath enhancement (tram-track sign, meningioma pattern).
Optic neuritis: enhancement and T2 signal of the [ ] optic nerve.
steps.look: Coronal images for muscle bellies; axial and coronal fat-suppressed images for the optic nerve.
steps.tip: Thyroid eye disease enlarges the muscle bellies and spares the tendons; inflammation involves the tendon.

steps.label: Orbital apex and intracranial extension
steps.detail: Inspect the orbital apex, optic canal, superior orbital fissure, cavernous sinus and intracranial spread.

normal.APEX AND INTRACRANIAL EXTENT: Orbital apex, optic canal and cavernous sinus normal.

findings: Crowding of the orbital apex with optic nerve compression.
Cavernous sinus thrombosis (filling defect and expansion).
Intracranial extension through the superior orbital fissure.
steps.look: Coronal and axial images at the apex; post-contrast MRI of the cavernous sinus.
steps.tip: Apical crowding threatens vision; report it explicitly.

steps.label: Bones and sinuses
steps.detail: Review fractures, herniated contents, entrapment configuration and sinus source of infection.

normal.BONES AND SINUSES: No orbital fracture; adjacent sinuses clear.

findings: Orbital floor blowout fracture __ mm with herniation of fat and the inferior rectus.
Trapdoor fracture with the inferior rectus caught in the defect (child).
Ethmoid sinusitis as the source of orbital cellulitis.
steps.look: Coronal bone windows of the floor and medial wall; adjacent sinuses.
steps.tip: A muscle in the fracture does not by itself prove clinical entrapment; describe the configuration.

measurements.name: Focal lesion extent
measurements.method: Measure each relevant source-resolved tissue/component on actual orthogonal/local axes, sequence/window/contrast and source calibration, describing obtained extent and uncertainty.
measurements.pitfall: Protein-rich or low-signal material does not uniquely establish tumour/air; selected stills do not supply full3D extent.

measurements.name: Surgical defect/variant
measurements.method: State actual acquired bone source/resolution, named location, orthogonal planes, edge convention/calibration and uncertainty for a supported defect or variant.
measurements.pitfall: Unacquired or unresolved thin-bone information cannot become a negative dehiscence statement or normal operative-risk class.

pitfalls: A low-signal MRI sinus is not automatically aerated; protein-rich/fungal/blood material may simulate air. Hyperdensity or high T2 signal alone does not establish benignity, organism or absence of tumour.
MRI anatomy/visible lumen does not alone prove complete drainage patency; low resolution or overlap must remain explicit. Use each actual source and variant, not an inherited generic sinus outline.

MRI soft-tissue detail cannot substitute for unacquired/unresolved thin-bone integrity. Partial volume can mimic defects; a missing wall on one image is not confirmed dehiscence or a normal operative variant.

Enhancement/diffusion/CT morphology can overlap across inflammation, secretions and neoplasia. DWI needs actual ADC/source technique; no unique histology, restricted diffusion or quantitative values are borrowed from unperformed sequences.

No extrasinus extension is asserted absent from unassessed anatomy. Perineural, orbital/cavernous or intracranial findings require appropriate source extent and clinical correlation; urgency or diagnosis is not inferred solely from the teaching-case label.
impression_prompts: Describe actual source-supported sinus/drainage/tissue/bone morphology and full obtained extent with modality/resolution limits.
Give a supported differential and any supplied tissue/clinical/organism confirmation; signal, hyperdensity, enhancement or diffusion alone does not uniquely diagnose or prove benignity.
Report relevant operative/extrasinus source findings and uncertainty, with unassessed anatomy and appropriate clinical/source-dependent urgency.
escalation: Communicate suspected orbital/apical, intracranial, cavernous/vascular or acute invasive complications according to local clinical pathways; actual source/clinical context and confirmation govern management.

findings: Mucosal thickening of the [maxillary] sinuses bilaterally.
Unilateral complete opacification of the [ ] sinus (consider obstructing lesion or fungal disease).
Air–fluid level in the [ ] sinus.
steps.look: Review every covered side/sinus, including actual frontal/maxillary/sphenoid/ethmoid subdivisions and variants. Trace full source lesion/secretions/mucosal boundaries on obtained sequences/windows; record unilateral/bilateral pattern and unassessed extent.
steps.tip: A low-signal MRI sinus is not automatically aerated; protein-rich/fungal/blood material may simulate air. Hyperdensity or high T2 signal alone does not establish benignity, organism or absence of tumour.

findings: Obstruction of the [left] ostiomeatal unit.
Nasal polyps filling the nasal cavity.
Periapical lucency of the [ ] molar with maxillary sinusitis (odontogenic source).
steps.look: Inspect actual ostia/recesses/infundibular/nasal/choanal routes, turbinates/septum and relevant variants with the acquired source resolution. Contact/opacification is not a complete 3D tract or measured flow; unacquired CT/endoscopic information remains unavailable.
steps.tip: MRI anatomy/visible lumen does not alone prove complete drainage patency; low resolution or overlap must remain explicit. Use each actual source and variant, not an inherited generic sinus outline.

steps.detail: Assess actual operative landmarks/variants with appropriate acquired thin-bone source; do not infer absent dehiscence from unassessed or unresolved MRI.
findings: Asymmetric ethmoid roof, lower on the [ ].
Dehiscent lamina papyracea on the [ ].
Onodi cell with the optic nerve running through it.
Dehiscent carotid canal in the sphenoid sinus.
steps.look: Use actually obtained thin-section bone imaging for relevant skull-base/lateral-lamella/foveal, lamina-papyracea and optic/carotid-canal relationships. Record measured source planes/calibration, asymmetry and uncertainty rather than forcing a normal or operative-risk category.
steps.tip: MRI soft-tissue detail cannot substitute for unacquired/unresolved thin-bone integrity. Partial volume can mimic defects; a missing wall on one image is not confirmed dehiscence or a normal operative variant.

steps.label: Focal tissue and bone
steps.detail: Describe each source tissue/bone component and acquired signal/enhancement/diffusion/CT bone response with technique and differential.
findings: Enhancing mass with a convoluted cerebriform pattern (inverted papilloma pattern).
Expansile non-enhancing sinus with thinned walls (mucocele).
Destructive enhancing mass with restricted diffusion (malignancy to be excluded).
steps.look: Distinguish source signal from true aeration, proteinaceous material, blood/fungal or solid components using actual pre/postcontrast T1/T2/other sequences, CT windows and DWI/ADC if obtained. Separate remodelling/sclerosis/calcification/dehiscence/destruction and marrow replacement.
steps.tip: Enhancement/diffusion/CT morphology can overlap across inflammation, secretions and neoplasia. DWI needs actual ADC/source technique; no unique histology, restricted diffusion or quantitative values are borrowed from unperformed sequences.

Extension into the pterygopalatine fossa.
Dural enhancement / epidural abscess.
steps.look: Inspect covered orbital walls/compartments/apex, pterygopalatine/infratemporal/masticator routes, foramina/cranial nerves, skull-base marrow, cavernous sinus, dura/brain and adjacent soft tissues. source_anatomy_references.label: Regional CT source label interfaces · partial
source_anatomy_references.population_note: One regional source CT case (P001); patient age and native DICOM orientation are not independently verified. These are five original region-label interfaces, not a complete sinonasal atlas or the anatomy of the patient being reported. The source grid is 153×205×52 with declared 0.586×0.586×1.5 mm sampling. This does not establish operative thin-bone effective resolution, raw DICOM/HU lineage or full head coverage. Both original left nasal-cavity components and 98 open nasal-pharynx edges at the acquired boundary are retained. Viewer rotation or uncropped framing cannot restore anatomy outside the scan. Frontal/ethmoid/sphenoid cells, full drainage routes, bone/mucosal thickness, optic/carotid/nerve/vessel boundaries and lesion or extrasinus extension are not independently represented.

normal.ORAL PHASE: Normal bolus control and transfer; no oral residue.

findings: Premature spillage of liquid into the pharynx before the swallow.
Oral residue after the swallow.
steps.look: Lateral fluoroscopy of the oral cavity with each consistency.

steps.label: Pharyngeal phase
steps.detail: Describe swallow initiation, pharyngeal propulsion and clearance.

normal.PHARYNGEAL PHASE: Timely swallow initiation with complete pharyngeal clearance.

findings: Delayed swallow initiation with bolus in the pyriform sinuses.
Residue in the valleculae and pyriform sinuses [bilateral / asymmetric].
steps.look: Lateral and frontal views of the pharynx during the swallow.
steps.tip: Asymmetric residue on the frontal view suggests unilateral pharyngeal weakness.

steps.label: Airway protection
steps.detail: Record penetration or aspiration, its timing and the cough response.
findings: Laryngeal penetration to the vocal folds, cleared.
Silent aspiration of thin liquid [during] the swallow (no cough).
Aspiration after the swallow from pyriform sinus residue.
steps.look: Lateral view of the larynx during each swallow; note before, during or after the swallow.
steps.tip: Silent aspiration — without cough — carries the greatest risk; state the cough response.

steps.label: External and middle ear
steps.detail: Assess the canal, tympanic membrane, scutum, ossicles and middle ear recesses.

normal.EXTERNAL AND MIDDLE EAR: External canal and middle ear clear; scutum sharp; ossicular chain intact.

findings: Soft tissue in Prussak space with blunting of the scutum and medial displacement of the ossicles (pars flaccida cholesteatoma).
Erosion of the [long process of the incus / stapes superstructure].
External auditory canal exostoses.
steps.look: Axial and coronal thin sections; follow malleus, incus and stapes; Prussak space and scutum on coronal images.
steps.tip: Scutum erosion with soft tissue in Prussak space is the classic sign of acquired cholesteatoma.

steps.label: Mastoid and tegmen
steps.detail: Describe aeration, septal erosion, tegmen defects and the mastoid cortex.
findings: Opacified mastoid with erosion of the septa (coalescent mastoiditis).
Tegmen defect __ mm [with soft tissue herniation].
Postoperative mastoid cavity.
steps.look: Coronal images of the tegmen tympani and mastoideum.
steps.tip: Mastoid opacification alone does not prove coalescent mastoiditis; look for septal erosion.

steps.label: Inner ear
steps.detail: Inspect the otic capsule, cochlea, vestibule, semicircular canals, windows and vestibular aqueduct.

normal.INNER EAR: Cochlea, vestibule and semicircular canals normal; otic capsule intact; normal vestibular aqueduct.

findings: Lucency anterior to the oval window (fenestral otosclerosis).
Enlarged vestibular aqueduct (__ mm at its midpoint).
Dehiscence of the superior semicircular canal.
Cochlear malformation: [ ].
steps.look: Axial images at the cochlea and vestibule; Pöschl reformats for the superior canal.

steps.label: Facial nerve and vascular channels
steps.detail: Review the facial nerve canal, carotid canal, jugular bulb and sigmoid plate.

normal.NEUROVASCULAR CHANNELS: Facial nerve canal intact; normal carotid canal, jugular bulb and sigmoid plate.

findings: Dehiscent tympanic segment of the facial nerve canal.
High / dehiscent jugular bulb.
Aberrant internal carotid artery crossing the middle ear.
steps.look: Follow the facial canal (labyrinthine, tympanic, mastoid segments); check the jugular bulb height and plate.
steps.tip: An aberrant carotid or dehiscent jugular bulb is a retrotympanic "mass" that must not be biopsied.

steps.label: Focal lesion, trauma or device
steps.detail: Describe a focal lesion, fracture course, otic-capsule involvement or implant position.

normal.FOCAL LESION, TRAUMA OR DEVICE: No focal lesion, fracture or device.

findings: Otic-capsule-sparing fracture with ossicular disruption.
Otic-capsule-violating fracture through the cochlea.
Cochlear implant electrode array fully inserted in the scala tympani.
Enhancing middle ear mass (paraganglioma pattern).
steps.look: Fracture course relative to the otic capsule; implant electrode position in the cochlea.

steps.label: Symptom and coverage
steps.detail: Record pulsatile or non-pulsatile tinnitus and side, and whether the protocol covers the right structures.
findings: [Right] pulsatile tinnitus: temporal bone CT with CT angiography.
[Left] non-pulsatile tinnitus with hearing loss: MRI of the internal auditory canals.
steps.look: Pulsatile: temporal bone CT and arterial and venous imaging. Non-pulsatile: MRI of the internal auditory canals.
steps.tip: The work-up depends on whether the tinnitus is pulsatile; say what the protocol can and cannot show.

normal.IAC AND CPA: Internal auditory canals and cerebellopontine angles normal.

findings: Enhancing intracanalicular mass __ × __ × __ mm (vestibular schwannoma pattern).
Vascular loop in the internal auditory canal (common, often incidental).
steps.look: High-resolution T2 and post-contrast T1 of the internal auditory canals.

steps.label: Middle ear and bone

normal.MIDDLE EAR AND BONE: No middle ear mass; normal vascular canals.

findings: Enhancing mass on the cochlear promontory (glomus tympanicum).
Dehiscent sigmoid sinus plate / sigmoid sinus diverticulum.
Dehiscent jugular bulb.
steps.look: Temporal bone CT for the jugular bulb, carotid canal and sigmoid plate.

steps.label: Arteries and veins

findings: Transverse sinus stenosis (idiopathic intracranial hypertension context).
Carotid dissection / fibromuscular dysplasia.
Early venous filling with enlarged occipital artery branches, suspicious for a dural arteriovenous fistula.
steps.look: CT or MR angiography and venography; early venous filling as a sign of arteriovenous shunting.
steps.tip: A routine negative MRI does not exclude a dural arteriovenous fistula.

steps.look: Side of the finding versus the side of symptoms.

protocol: Survey thyroid and cervical nodes with grayscale and Doppler as appropriate; record prior FNA/cytology and treatment.
Assign a stable nodule number and location for follow-up; adult ACR TI-RADS recommendations require clinical context.

checklist.label: Nodule identification
checklist.detail: Record side, pole and three dimensions for each selected clinically relevant nodule.

checklist.label: Five features
checklist.detail: Score composition, echogenicity, shape, margin and echogenic foci using the ACR lexicon.

checklist.label: Extension
checklist.detail: Assess extrathyroidal extension and relationship to trachea or adjacent structures.

checklist.label: Nodes
checklist.detail: Survey for suspicious cervical lymph nodes separately from thyroid nodule scoring.

checklist.label: Recommendation
checklist.detail: Combine category, size, prior biopsy and clinical context; state an explicit action and interval if indicated.

measurements.name: Nodule size
measurements.method: Measure three orthogonal dimensions, using the maximum diameter for the ACR size recommendation.
measurements.pitfall: Do not mix different nodules or planes on follow-up.

measurements.name: Growth
measurements.method: Significant growth: at least 20% in two dimensions with at least 2 mm increase, or at least 50% volume increase.
measurements.pitfall: Compare consistent technique and account for cystic change.

classification.name: ACR TI-RADS
classification.applicability: Adult thyroid nodules evaluated by ultrasound, with clinical and cytology context.
classification.summary: TR1–2: no routine FNA/follow-up. TR3: FNA ≥2.5 cm, follow ≥1.5 cm. TR4: FNA ≥1.5 cm, follow ≥1 cm. TR5: FNA ≥1 cm, follow ≥0.5 cm. Confirm schedule and exceptions in the ACR reference.

pitfalls: A suspicious node or invasive feature needs dedicated assessment even if the nodule is small.
The ACR algorithm does not prescribe management of already-biopsied nodules without incorporating cytology.
impression_prompts: What is each index nodule’s point total and TR category?
Does its size and clinical context meet FNA or follow-up criteria?
Are suspicious nodes or invasive features present?
escalation: Promptly flag invasive findings or suspicious nodes for the appropriate thyroid/neck pathway.

findings: Nodule 1: [right] [lower] pole, __ × __ × __ mm (previously __ × __ × __ mm).

steps.label: TI-RADS features and points

findings: Solid (2), hypoechoic (2), wider-than-tall (0), smooth (0), no foci (0): 4 points, TR4.
Spongiform (0): TR1.
Solid (2), very hypoechoic (3), taller-than-wide (3), irregular (2), punctate foci (3): 13 points, TR5.
steps.look: Composition 0–2, echogenicity 0–3, shape 0 or 3 (taller-than-wide on transverse), margin 0–3, echogenic foci 0–3 (add all foci types).
steps.tip: Measure taller-than-wide on the transverse view; comet-tail artefacts score 0.

steps.label: Extrathyroidal extension and nodes
steps.detail: Assess extrathyroidal extension, tracheal relationship and suspicious cervical nodes.

normal.EXTRATHYROIDAL AND NODAL FINDINGS: No extrathyroidal extension; no suspicious cervical nodes.

findings: Extrathyroidal extension into the strap muscles.
Suspicious [right level III / IV] node with microcalcifications / cystic change / loss of hilum.
steps.look: Nodule capsule; central and lateral neck nodal levels.
steps.tip: A suspicious node needs sampling even when the nodule itself is small.

steps.label: Recommendation
steps.detail: Combine TR category, size, prior cytology and context into an explicit recommendation.
findings: TR[ ], __ mm: fine-needle aspiration recommended.
TR[ ], __ mm: ultrasound follow-up in [ ].
Below the ACR thresholds: no follow-up required.
steps.look: ACR thresholds: TR3 FNA ≥2.5 cm (follow-up ≥1.5 cm); TR4 FNA ≥1.5 cm (follow-up ≥1.0 cm); TR5 FNA ≥1.0 cm (follow-up ≥0.5 cm).
steps.tip: The ACR algorithm does not apply to nodules that already have benign cytology unless there is growth.

protocol: Record side, skeletal maturity, comparison and radiographs actually obtained: AP, mortise and lateral views. Describe positioning/coverage limitations and whether images are pre- or post-reduction.
State weight-bearing or stress-view status when such views were clinically obtained. Document whether the proximal fibula, foot and hindfoot were included; do not call an unexamined region normal.

Identify any supplemental CT, MRI or ultrasound actually reviewed and the question it addresses. CT can refine osseous articular extent; direct cartilage or tendon/ligament findings require an appropriate acquired examination, not a radiographic assumption.

checklist.label: Fractures and mortise
checklist.detail: Inspect the medial, lateral and posterior malleoli, distal tibia and talus; describe fibular level, fracture morphology/displacement and tibiotalar alignment.

checklist.label: Syndesmosis and proximal fibula
checklist.detail: Assess tibiofibular alignment, clear spaces/overlap and syndesmotic avulsion fragments as radiographic injury clues. State proximal-fibular coverage and concern for a higher fibular injury.

checklist.label: Osseous articular surfaces
checklist.detail: Describe visible talar-dome/plafond defects, impaction, articular step/gap and posterior-malleolar extent. Separate osseous findings from direct cartilage assessment on supplemental imaging.

checklist.label: Foot and hindfoot when included
checklist.detail: For the clinically indicated region actually imaged, assess hindfoot and tarsometatarsal alignment, navicular, cuneiforms/cuboid and metatarsals. State foot or hindfoot coverage not obtained.

checklist.label: Soft tissues and modality limits
checklist.detail: Describe swelling and radiographic avulsion/alignment clues. Do not grade tendon or ligament discontinuity on radiographs; name direct integrity findings only from an appropriate acquired MRI or ultrasound examination.

measurements.name: Fracture and articular displacement
measurements.method: Measure visible fracture displacement, gap or articular step in mm with the view/plane stated. Report posterior-malleolar extent and any CT-defined impaction or articular extension separately.
measurements.pitfall: Projection limits posterior-fragment and articular measurements. A fragment percentage alone does not determine management or cartilage integrity.

measurements.name: Mortise and syndesmotic relationships
measurements.method: If measured, record medial clear space, tibiofibular clear space/overlap and talar shift with projection, positioning and weight-bearing/stress status.
measurements.pitfall: Rotation and loading alter these measurements. Normal clear spaces do not exclude ligamentous injury, and one cutoff must not be used as an automatic stability decision.

classification.name: Weber / Lauge-Hansen — with maturity and pattern limits
classification.version: Conventional fibular-level and mechanism-pattern classifications; physeal injury described separately when relevant
classification.applicability: Applicable ankle fracture patterns. These are not general foot-injury classifications and do not replace age-appropriate physeal fracture assessment.
classification.summary: Weber A/B/C describes the fibular fracture level relative to the syndesmosis. Lauge-Hansen pattern/stage requires supporting findings and stated uncertainty. Preserve the complete fracture/alignment description; do not assume stability from Weber type or intact soft tissues from radiographs.

pitfalls: A Weber B fracture is not automatically stable. A normal mortise or clear-space measurement does not exclude ligament injury.
Posterior-malleolar fractures may be subtle on a rotated lateral projection; an apparently isolated posterior or medial injury can be a clue to a wider injury pattern.
A higher fibular injury may coexist with medial or syndesmotic injury despite an unremarkable distal fibula. An ankle-only field cannot exclude injury outside its coverage.
In an immature skeleton, identify physeal, epiphyseal and metaphyseal extension and distinguish developmental centres from fragments; do not substitute an adult classification for the actual pattern.
Tendon/ligament continuity and full cartilage injury extent are not directly established on routine radiographs. Keep supplemental MRI/ultrasound findings and their modality separate.
impression_prompts: What fractures, visible articular abnormalities and alignment changes are demonstrated on the radiographs?
What syndesmotic, medial or higher-fibular injury is suspected from the observed pattern, and what remains unconfirmed?
What clinically relevant foot/hindfoot or proximal-fibular region was not imaged, and what focused question remains for supplemental assessment?
escalation: Promptly communicate fracture-dislocation, consequential malalignment or a suspected unstable injury pattern through the acute trauma pathway.
Threatened skin or neurovascular compromise requires clinical assessment; radiographs cannot establish normal skin viability, pulses or neurological function.

steps.label: Fracture map
steps.detail: Locate each malleolar fracture and relate the fibular fracture to the syndesmosis: Weber A below, B at, C above.

normal.FRACTURE MAP: No fracture of the lateral, medial or posterior malleolus.

findings: Oblique fracture of the distal fibula at the level of the syndesmosis (Weber B), running anteroinferior to posterosuperior on the lateral view, displaced __ mm.
Transverse avulsion fracture of the lateral malleolus below the syndesmosis (Weber A) [with / without] a vertical medial malleolar fracture.
Fibular fracture above the syndesmosis (Weber C), __ cm above the joint line.
Posterior malleolar fracture involving approximately __% of the tibial articular surface on the lateral view, displaced __ mm.
steps.look: Mortise and lateral views: follow the lateral malleolar cortex, then the medial malleolus, then the posterior tibial lip on the true lateral.
steps.tip: Reconstruct the mechanism: a Weber B fibular fracture with a medial malleolar fracture or a widened medial clear space is a higher-stage, potentially unstable injury.

steps.label: Mortise and talar position
steps.detail: Check that the talus is centred in the mortise and compare the medial clear space with the superior clear space.

normal.MORTISE AND TALUS: Ankle mortise congruent; medial clear space equal to the superior clear space; no talar shift or tilt.

findings: Widened medial clear space of __ mm on the [mortise / stress] view, compatible with deltoid ligament injury and lateral talar shift.
Lateral talar shift of __ mm with an incongruent mortise.
Posterior subluxation of the talus with the posterior malleolar fragment.
steps.look: True mortise view (about 15 degrees internal rotation) for clear spaces; lateral view for anterior or posterior talar subluxation.
steps.tip: The medial clear space should not exceed the superior clear space; widening without a medial malleolar fracture indicates deltoid ligament rupture.

steps.label: Syndesmosis and proximal fibula
steps.detail: Assess the distal tibiofibular relationship and decide whether the proximal fibula needs imaging.

normal.SYNDESMOSIS AND PROXIMAL FIBULA: Distal tibiofibular relationship normal; no syndesmotic avulsion.

findings: Widening of the distal tibiofibular clear space, compatible with syndesmotic injury.
Avulsion fragment at the anterior tibial tubercle (Tillaux-Chaput) or the fibular attachment of the anterior tibiofibular ligament.
Medial injury without a distal fibular fracture; the proximal fibula is not included and a Maisonneuve fracture should be excluded.
steps.look: Mortise view for tibiofibular overlap and clear space; knee or full-length fibula view when a medial injury has no matching distal fibular fracture.
steps.tip: A medial malleolar fracture or deltoid injury with an intact distal fibula should prompt a look at the proximal fibula (Maisonneuve injury).

steps.label: Articular surface
steps.detail: Describe plafond impaction, articular step or gap, posterior fragment size and talar dome injury.

normal.OSSEOUS ARTICULAR EXTENT: Tibial plafond and talar dome congruent without step, gap or impaction.

findings: Intra-articular extension with __ mm step and __ mm gap at the [plafond / medial malleolus].
Impaction of the [anterior / posterior] plafond; CT would define the fragments for surgical planning.
Osteochondral fracture of the [medial / lateral] talar dome, __ mm.
steps.look: Lateral and mortise views for step and gap; CT sagittal and axial reformats when the posterior malleolus or plafond is involved.
steps.tip: The lateral radiograph underestimates the size and comminution of a posterior malleolar fragment; CT defines it.

steps.detail: Additional foot/hindfoot imaging [not obtained / acquired region and views]; calcaneus/subtalar joint [not included / findings]; navicular/cuboid/cuneiforms [not included / findings]; metatarsals and tarsometatarsal alignment [not included / findings]; Lisfranc-region osseous/alignment clues [not assessed / findings].

steps.detail: Check for dislocation, soft-tissue swelling, other fractures at the film edges and post-reduction alignment.

normal.REDUCTION AND ASSOCIATED FINDINGS: No dislocation; no additional fracture in the imaged foot and ankle; soft tissues unremarkable apart from swelling.

findings: Fracture-dislocation of the ankle with [lateral / posterior] talar dislocation.
Additional fracture of the [base of the fifth metatarsal / anterior calcaneal process / lateral talar process].
Post-reduction: mortise [restored / persistent talar shift of __ mm].
steps.look: The edges of every film: base of the fifth metatarsal, anterior process of the calcaneus and lateral process of the talus.
steps.tip: A fifth metatarsal base or anterior calcaneal process fracture can mimic an ankle sprain and hide at the film edge.

protocol: Acquire axial, coronal and sagittal MRI with T1/PD anatomy and fluid-sensitive fat-suppressed images; tailor coverage to the hindfoot or tendon question.
Review injury mechanism, previous surgery and the precise site of pain before interpreting marrow oedema.

checklist.label: Bones And Osteochondral Surfaces
checklist.detail: Inspect talar dome, tibial plafond and hindfoot for contusion, fracture and osteochondral injury.

checklist.label: Lateral Ligaments And Syndesmosis
checklist.detail: Trace ATFL, CFL, PTFL and anterior/posterior syndesmotic structures.

checklist.label: Medial Ligaments And Sinus Tarsi
checklist.detail: Assess superficial/deep deltoid, spring ligament and sinus tarsi structures.

checklist.label: Tendons
checklist.detail: Follow flexor, extensor, peroneal and Achilles compartments through their visible attachments.

checklist.label: Joints And Soft Tissues
checklist.detail: Assess effusions, capsule, impingement sites, bursae and any mass.

measurements.name: Osteochondral lesion
measurements.method: Measure surface dimensions and depth; describe cartilage continuity, subchondral cysts and fluid at the fragment interface.
measurements.pitfall: Marrow oedema extent is not the osteochondral defect size.

measurements.name: Tendon injury
measurements.method: Record tendon, injury level, longitudinal extent and retraction for a complete tear.
measurements.pitfall: Magic-angle signal and partial volume require correlation with long-TE images and another plane.

pitfalls: Marrow oedema is a finding; relate its distribution to fracture, cartilage or adjacent ligament/tendon injury.
Small physiological joint fluid should not be overcalled as synovitis.
impression_prompts: Which structure is injured and at what level?
Is an osteochondral fragment unstable or a tendon completely disrupted?
Are ligament injuries isolated or combined?

steps.label: Bones and osteochondral surfaces
steps.detail: Inspect the talar dome, tibial plafond and hindfoot for contusion, fracture, osteochondral lesion and accessory ossicles.

normal.BONES AND OSTEOCHONDRAL SURFACES: Normal bone marrow signal; no fracture or osteochondral lesion of the talar dome or tibial plafond.

findings: Osteochondral lesion of the [medial / lateral] talar dome, __ × __ mm and __ mm deep, [with / without] fluid signal at the fragment interface or subchondral cysts.
Bone marrow oedema of the [ ] compatible with contusion; no fracture line.
Fracture of the [lateral talar process / posterior talar process / anterior calcaneal process], seen as a T1-hypointense line.
Os trigonum with surrounding oedema and fluid, in keeping with posterior impingement in the appropriate clinical setting.
steps.look: Coronal and sagittal fluid-sensitive images for marrow oedema; coronal images for the talar dome; T1 images for fracture lines.
steps.tip: Fluid signal undercutting a talar osteochondral fragment, or cysts beneath it, suggests instability.

steps.label: Lateral ligaments and syndesmosis
steps.detail: Trace the anterior and posterior tibiofibular ligaments above the joint, then the anterior talofibular, calcaneofibular and posterior talofibular ligaments.

normal.LATERAL LIGAMENTS AND SYNDESMOSIS: Anterior and posterior tibiofibular ligaments, anterior and posterior talofibular ligaments and calcaneofibular ligament intact.

findings: Complete tear of the anterior talofibular ligament at its [fibular / talar] attachment [with / without] a small avulsion fragment.
Thickened, wavy anterior talofibular ligament without discontinuity, in keeping with a chronic or healed sprain.
Tear of the anterior inferior tibiofibular ligament (syndesmotic injury) [with / without] interosseous membrane involvement.
Calcaneofibular ligament tear, indicating a more extensive lateral ligament injury.
steps.look: Axial images from the tibial plafond (tibiofibular ligaments) down to the malleolar fossa (talofibular ligaments); coronal images for the calcaneofibular ligament deep to the peroneal tendons.
steps.tip: The anterior talofibular ligament is seen at the level of the malleolar fossa; the tibiofibular ligaments lie higher, at the level of the plafond.

steps.label: Medial ligaments, sinus tarsi and plantar fascia
steps.detail: Assess the superficial and deep deltoid ligament, spring ligament, sinus tarsi and plantar fascia.

normal.MEDIAL LIGAMENTS AND SINUS TARSI: Deltoid and spring ligaments intact; sinus tarsi fat preserved; plantar fascia of normal thickness and signal.

findings: Tear of the deep deltoid (posterior tibiotalar) ligament, [partial / complete].
Spring ligament thickening or tear [with / without] posterior tibial tendon dysfunction.
Replacement of sinus tarsi fat by oedema or fibrosis, compatible with sinus tarsi syndrome in the appropriate clinical setting.
Thickened proximal plantar fascia (__ mm) with perifascial oedema, compatible with plantar fasciitis.
steps.look: Coronal and axial images for the deltoid layers; axial images beneath the talar head for the spring ligament; sagittal images for the sinus tarsi and plantar fascia.
steps.tip: The deep deltoid ligament normally looks striated because of interposed fat; this is not a tear.

steps.label: Tendons
steps.detail: Follow the medial flexors, peroneal tendons, anterior extensors and Achilles tendon from muscle to insertion.

normal.TENDONS: Flexor, extensor, peroneal and Achilles tendons of normal calibre and signal; no tenosynovitis; peroneal retinaculum intact.

findings: Posterior tibial tendinosis with [enlargement / longitudinal split / attenuation] from the medial malleolus to the navicular insertion.
Longitudinal split tear of peroneus brevis at the retromalleolar groove [with / without] peroneal tendon subluxation.
Complete Achilles tendon rupture __ cm above the calcaneal insertion with a __ mm gap.
Tenosynovitis of the [ ] tendon sheath with fluid disproportionate to the joint.
steps.look: Axial images tendon by tendon: posterior tibial, flexor digitorum longus and flexor hallucis longus medially; peroneal tendons behind the fibula; extensors anteriorly; sagittal images for the Achilles.
steps.tip: The posterior tibial tendon is normally about twice the diameter of the flexor digitorum longus; fluid in the flexor hallucis longus sheath can communicate with the ankle joint.

steps.label: Joints, impingement and soft tissues
steps.detail: Assess effusion, synovitis, capsular thickening, impingement recesses, bursae, accessory muscles and masses.

normal.JOINTS AND SOFT TISSUES: No significant ankle or subtalar effusion; no synovitis; impingement recesses clear; bursae normal.

findings: Soft-tissue thickening in the anterolateral gutter, compatible with anterolateral impingement in the appropriate clinical setting.
Retrocalcaneal bursitis with [Haglund deformity / insertional Achilles tendinopathy].
Moderate tibiotalar effusion with synovial thickening.
Accessory muscle: [peroneus quartus / accessory soleus / flexor digitorum accessorius longus].
steps.look: Sagittal images for the anterior and posterior recesses; axial images of the anterolateral gutter; sagittal images for the retrocalcaneal bursa.
steps.tip: A small amount of joint fluid is physiological; call synovitis only when the synovium is thickened.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full: MRI appearance of the peroneus quartus (PQ) muscle in the lateral compartment of the leg. (a) Axial fat-suppressed proton density–weighted fast spin echo (FSE) image showing the peroneus brevis (blue arrow), peroneus longus (green arrow), and the accessory peroneus quartus muscle (red arrow). The PQ lies posterior to the fibula and lateral to the other peroneal tendons. Yellow arrows indicate the muscle belly of the PQ. (b) Coronal T1-weighted FSE image demonstrating the longitudinal course of the PQ muscle (yellow arrows) descending toward the calcaneus. (c) Sagittal T1-weighted fast spin echo (FSE) image demonstrating the peroneus quartus (PQ) muscle extending distally toward its insertion on the retrotrochlear eminence of the calcaneus (yellow arrows).

protocol: Review distribution across the imaged joints and comparable priors; state weight-bearing status and clinical inflammatory/crystal/infective context.
Use ultrasound/MRI for the specific active synovitis, tendon or occult infection question when indicated.

checklist.label: Distribution
checklist.detail: Describe symmetry and which joint groups are involved or spared.

checklist.label: Cartilage space
checklist.detail: Distinguish uniform from nonuniform joint-space loss.

checklist.label: Bone response
checklist.detail: Assess marginal/central erosions, osteophytes, periostitis and mineralisation.

checklist.label: Alignment
checklist.detail: Look for subluxation, deformity and ankylosis.

checklist.label: Soft tissue and change
checklist.detail: Describe swelling, calcification/tophi and interval structural progression.

measurements.name: Joint-space comparison
measurements.method: Measure a reproducible minimum joint space only when it answers the question, using the same view/load.
measurements.pitfall: Projection and loading affect apparent narrowing.

measurements.name: Erosion/lesion change
measurements.method: Record site and dimensions of a relevant erosion or tophus on matching studies.
measurements.pitfall: Small apparent changes can be technical rather than true progression.

pitfalls: An arthritis pattern is not a substitute for clinical and laboratory diagnosis.
Septic arthritis may have little early radiographic abnormality.
impression_prompts: Is the pattern degenerative, inflammatory, crystal-associated or indeterminate?
Which joints show progression or major structural damage?
Is an urgent infective or instability complication suspected?
escalation: Escalate suspected septic arthritis or clinically important cervical instability.

An arthritis pattern is not a substitute for clinical and laboratory diagnosis.
Septic arthritis may have little early radiographic abnormality.

steps.label: Distribution
steps.detail: Describe which joints are involved and spared, symmetry, and proximal or distal predominance.

normal.DISTRIBUTION: No joint-space loss, erosion or productive change in the imaged joints.

findings: Symmetric involvement of the MCP, PIP and wrist joints with relative sparing of the DIP joints (proximal, inflammatory distribution).
Predominant DIP and PIP involvement with the first carpometacarpal joint (osteoarthritis distribution).
Asymmetric involvement of DIP joints [in a ray distribution] with productive change (spondyloarthritis / psoriatic distribution).
Radiocarpal and second–third MCP predominance with chondrocalcinosis (CPPD distribution).
steps.look: Survey both hands and wrists joint by joint — DIP, PIP, MCP, carpus, radiocarpal and distal radioulnar — and any other joints included.
steps.tip: Distribution is the strongest single clue: rheumatoid arthritis is proximal and symmetric, erosive osteoarthritis central in the DIP and PIP joints, psoriatic arthritis distal and asymmetric.

steps.label: Joint spaces (cartilage)
steps.detail: Distinguish uniform from non-uniform joint-space loss and name the worst compartment.
findings: Uniform joint-space narrowing of the [ ] joints, a pattern favouring inflammatory arthritis.
Non-uniform joint-space narrowing with osteophytes and subchondral sclerosis, favouring osteoarthritis.
Ankylosis of the [carpus / interphalangeal joints].
steps.look: Well-centred PA views; compare the same joints on the prior study with the same projection and load.

steps.label: Erosions, bone formation and density
steps.detail: Characterise erosions (marginal, central, overhanging edge), osteophytes, periostitis and periarticular mineralisation.

normal.EROSIONS AND BONE RESPONSE: No erosions; no osteophytes or periostitis; normal bone mineralisation.

findings: Marginal erosions at the [ ] with periarticular osteopenia, favouring rheumatoid arthritis.
Central "gull-wing" erosions of the [DIP / PIP] joints, compatible with erosive osteoarthritis.
Erosions with fluffy periostitis and new bone formation (productive change), favouring psoriatic arthritis.
Well-defined punched-out erosions with overhanging edges and soft-tissue tophi, favouring gout.
steps.look: Bare areas at joint margins (MCP joints and ulnar styloid), central subchondral bone and shafts for periostitis; judge periarticular density.
steps.tip: Gout preserves mineralisation and joint space until late; rheumatoid arthritis causes periarticular osteopenia early.

steps.label: Alignment
steps.detail: Look for subluxation, ulnar deviation, swan-neck or boutonnière deformity, carpal collapse and ankylosis.

normal.ALIGNMENT: Normal alignment without subluxation or deformity.

findings: Ulnar deviation and volar subluxation at the MCP joints.
Carpal collapse with [scapholunate dissociation / ulnar translocation of the carpus].
Atlanto-dental interval of __ mm on flexion, compatible with atlanto-axial subluxation.
steps.look: PA and oblique hand views; lateral cervical flexion and extension views when atlanto-axial involvement is in question.
steps.tip: Deformity can be reducible; describe what the projection shows rather than inferring a fixed deformity.

steps.label: Soft tissues, calcification and change
steps.detail: Describe swelling, tophi, chondrocalcinosis or other calcification, and interval structural progression.

normal.SOFT TISSUES AND PROGRESSION: No soft-tissue swelling, calcification or tophi; no interval progression.

findings: Chondrocalcinosis of the triangular fibrocartilage, compatible with CPPD deposition.
Eccentric dense soft-tissue masses compatible with tophi.
New erosions at the [ ] since [date], indicating progression.
Fusiform periarticular soft-tissue swelling of the [ ] joints.
steps.look: Soft tissues around each joint; the triangular fibrocartilage and hyaline cartilage for chondrocalcinosis; direct comparison with the prior study.
steps.tip: Septic arthritis may be radiographically normal early; a single hot joint needs aspiration, not a pattern diagnosis.

steps.label: Location, age and margin
steps.detail: Name the bone, epiphysis, metaphysis or diaphysis, the central, eccentric, cortical or juxtacortical position, and the zone of transition, with the patient's age.

normal.LOCATION AND MORPHOLOGY: No focal bone lesion in the imaged bones.

findings: Well-defined lytic lesion with a narrow zone of transition and sclerotic margin in the eccentric metaphysis of the [bone] (non-aggressive pattern).
Ill-defined permeative or moth-eaten lesion with a wide zone of transition in the diaphysis of the [bone] (aggressive pattern).
Epiphyseal lesion in a skeletally [immature / mature] patient, __ mm.
steps.look: Radiographs in two planes first: find the lesion's centre and inspect its whole margin, then correlate with CT or MRI.
steps.tip: Age and the zone of transition are the two most informative features; a wide transition zone indicates aggressive behaviour but not a specific diagnosis.

steps.label: Matrix, periosteum and cortex
steps.detail: Describe matrix mineralisation, periosteal reaction, cortical thinning, scalloping or breach, and any pathological fracture.
findings: Chondroid matrix with rings-and-arcs calcification.
Cloud-like osteoid matrix [with / without] sunburst periosteal reaction and a Codman triangle.
Solid, uninterrupted periosteal reaction, favouring a slow-growing process.
Lamellated periosteal reaction with cortical breach.
steps.look: Radiographs and CT bone window for matrix and cortex; inspect the periosteal surface along the full length of the lesion.
steps.tip: Solid periosteal new bone suggests slow growth; interrupted, lamellated or sunburst reactions suggest an aggressive process.

steps.label: Local extent and size
steps.detail: Measure the intramedullary lesion and any extraosseous component separately in three planes.
findings: Intramedullary lesion measuring __ × __ × __ mm (series __ image __).
Extraosseous soft-tissue component measuring __ × __ × __ mm.
Peritumoral oedema extending __ cm beyond the lesion margin.
steps.look: MRI T1 for marrow extent against normal fatty marrow and fluid-sensitive images for the soft-tissue component; image the whole bone when sarcoma is suspected.
steps.tip: Measure tumour extent on T1; oedema on fluid-sensitive images overstates it.

steps.label: Joint, physis and neurovascular relationships
steps.detail: State physeal or articular involvement, compartments, and the relationship to the neurovascular bundle.
findings: Tumour crosses the physis into the epiphysis; no intra-articular extension.
Soft-tissue component abuts the neurovascular bundle over less than half its circumference, without encasement.
Extension into the [ ] compartment / joint.
steps.look: Axial MRI through the soft-tissue component for the neurovascular bundle; coronal and sagittal images for the physis and joint.

steps.label: Multiplicity and comparison
steps.detail: Look for further or skip lesions and compare with prior imaging for growth.
findings: Solitary lesion; no skip lesion in the imaged bone.
Multiple lesions in [ ]; metastases, myeloma or a polyostotic benign process according to age.
Unchanged since [date], supporting a non-aggressive lesion.
steps.look: The whole imaged bone and every included bone; prior radiographs for change in size or margin.
steps.tip: In a patient over 40, consider metastasis and myeloma for any lytic lesion.

protocol: Start with radiographs of the whole lesion; use CT for matrix and endosteal detail and MRI for marrow extent, cortex, soft tissue and cartilage-cap thickness.
Record age, symptoms at the lesion, known multiple lesions or syndromes, and the date of any comparison study.

checklist.label: Endosteal and cortical change
checklist.detail: Describe endosteal scalloping depth and length, cortical thickening, expansion, breach and periosteal reaction.

checklist.label: MRI characteristics
checklist.detail: Assess lobulated cartilage signal, entrapped fat, peritumoral oedema and enhancement pattern.

checklist.label: Soft tissue and cap
checklist.detail: Look for a soft-tissue mass; for an osteochondroma confirm cortical and medullary continuity and measure the cartilage cap.

checklist.label: Growth and grade-relevant features
checklist.detail: Compare with prior imaging and look for a non-chondroid aggressive component.

measurements.name: Lesion size
measurements.method: Measure the longest dimension and two orthogonal dimensions of the chondroid lesion on MRI or CT.
measurements.pitfall: Compare like with like; radiographic and MRI extent are not interchangeable.

measurements.name: Endosteal scalloping
measurements.method: Report the depth as a proportion of normal cortical thickness and the craniocaudal length of the scalloping.
measurements.pitfall: Oblique planes exaggerate depth; measure perpendicular to the cortex.

measurements.name: Cartilage cap
measurements.method: Measure an osteochondroma cap perpendicular to the underlying bone at its thickest point on MRI or ultrasound.
measurements.pitfall: An adjacent bursa or perichondrium can be mistaken for cap thickness.

pitfalls: Imaging features of enchondroma and atypical cartilaginous tumour overlap; describe the features that favour one rather than assigning a histological grade.
Deep endosteal scalloping (more than two-thirds of cortical thickness), cortical breach, periosteal reaction or a soft-tissue mass favour a higher-grade tumour and warrant specialist referral.

Which features favour enchondroma, atypical cartilaginous tumour or higher-grade chondrosarcoma?

escalation: Expedite specialist review for an aggressive chondroid lesion, a lytic non-chondroid component or a pathological fracture.

steps.label: Site and matrix
steps.detail: Name the bone, central or surface location and the chondroid rings-and-arcs matrix.
findings: Central chondroid lesion in the [metaphysis / diaphysis] of the [bone] with rings-and-arcs calcification, __ mm.
[Sessile / pedunculated] osteochondroma of the [bone] with cortical and medullary continuity.
Chondroid lesion of the [pelvis / scapula / rib] (axial location).
steps.look: Radiographs of the whole bone and CT for rings-and-arcs calcification; decide whether the lesion is central or a surface lesion.
steps.tip: Location matters: a chondroid lesion of the pelvis, shoulder girdle or axial skeleton is more often malignant than one in the hands or feet.

steps.label: Endosteal and cortical change
steps.detail: Describe endosteal scalloping depth and length, cortical thickening, expansion, breach and periosteal reaction.

normal.ENDOSTEAL AND CORTICAL CHANGE: No endosteal scalloping, cortical change or periosteal reaction.

findings: Endosteal scalloping of about __% of cortical thickness over __ mm, without cortical breach.
Deep endosteal scalloping (more than two-thirds of the cortical thickness) with cortical thickening and expansion.
Cortical breach with periosteal reaction.
steps.look: CT or radiographs perpendicular to the cortex along the full length of the lesion.
steps.tip: Cortical thickening and expansion are signs of an active lesion even without a breach.

steps.label: MRI characteristics
steps.detail: Assess lobulated cartilage signal, entrapped fat, peritumoral oedema and enhancement pattern.
findings: Lobulated T2-hyperintense lesion with entrapped fat and peripheral septal enhancement; no peritumoral oedema.
Peritumoral marrow oedema and [early arterial / nodular] enhancement.
Loss of the lobular pattern with a T1-hypointense non-chondroid component, raising concern for dedifferentiation.
steps.look: T1 for marrow extent and entrapped fat; fat-suppressed T2 for lobulation and oedema; post-contrast (dynamic when acquired) for enhancement.
steps.tip: Preserved entrapped marrow fat favours a low-grade lesion; loss of the lobular pattern or a non-chondroid component raises concern for higher grade.

steps.label: Soft tissue and cartilage cap
steps.detail: Look for a soft-tissue mass; for an osteochondroma confirm continuity and measure the cartilage cap.
findings: Cartilage cap __ mm at its thickest point.
Cartilage cap thicker than 1.5–2 cm in a skeletally mature patient, raising concern for secondary chondrosarcoma.
Soft-tissue mass __ × __ mm extending from the lesion.
Bursa overlying the osteochondroma, __ mm.
steps.look: MRI or ultrasound perpendicular to the underlying bone at the thickest part of the cap; surrounding soft tissues.
steps.tip: Cap thickness is only reassuring after skeletal maturity; caps are normally thicker in growing children.

steps.label: Growth and grade-relevant features

Posterior malleolar fracture involving about __% of the articular surface.
steps.look: Mortise and lateral views: lateral malleolus, medial malleolus, then the posterior tibial lip.

steps.label: Mortise and syndesmosis
steps.detail: Check talar centring, medial clear space and the distal tibiofibular relationship.

normal.MORTISE AND SYNDESMOSIS: Mortise congruent; medial clear space normal; distal tibiofibular relationship normal.

findings: Medial clear space widened to __ mm with lateral talar shift.
Distal tibiofibular widening, compatible with syndesmotic injury.
Proximal fibular fracture (Maisonneuve pattern).
steps.look: True mortise view; compare the medial and superior clear spaces; include the proximal fibula when the pattern requires it.

steps.label: Talus, calcaneus and subtalar joint
steps.detail: Check the talar dome, lateral and posterior talar processes, calcaneus and subtalar joint.

normal.TALAR AND HINDFOOT SURFACES: Talar dome, talar processes and calcaneus intact; subtalar joint congruent.

findings: Fracture of the lateral process of the talus.
Fracture of the anterior process of the calcaneus at the calcaneocuboid joint.
Calcaneal fracture with a reduced Böhler angle of __° and subtalar joint involvement.
Osteochondral lesion of the talar dome, __ mm.
steps.look: Lateral view and CT for the lateral talar process and anterior calcaneal process; Böhler angle for calcaneal compression.
steps.tip: Lateral talar process and anterior calcaneal process fractures mimic an ankle sprain clinically and are easily missed on radiographs.

steps.label: Midfoot and forefoot
steps.detail: Check tarsometatarsal (Lisfranc) alignment, the navicular, the cuboid and the base of the fifth metatarsal.

normal.MIDFOOT AND FOREFOOT: Tarsometatarsal alignment normal; no midfoot or metatarsal fracture.

findings: Lisfranc injury: __ mm widening between the first and second metatarsal bases with a fleck fragment and lateral subluxation of the second metatarsal.
Fracture of the base of the fifth metatarsal: [tuberosity avulsion / metaphyseal–diaphyseal junction (Jones) fracture].
Navicular [body / dorsal avulsion] fracture.
steps.look: AP (weight-bearing when possible) and oblique views: the second metatarsal aligns with the intermediate cuneiform and the fourth metatarsal with the cuboid; CT for subtle injury.
steps.tip: Subtle Lisfranc instability may appear only on weight-bearing views; a normal non-weight-bearing film does not exclude it.

steps.label: Ligaments and tendons
steps.detail: Name any ligament or tendon injury on MRI or ultrasound and distinguish partial from complete tears.

normal.LIGAMENTS AND TENDONS: No ligament or tendon injury on the examinations acquired.

findings: Complete tear of the anterior talofibular ligament.
Longitudinal split tear of peroneus brevis.
Lisfranc ligament [partial / complete] tear on MRI.
steps.look: MRI axial images tendon by tendon, ligament-specific planes, or targeted ultrasound.

measurements.name: Infection map

measurements.pitfall: Reactive oedema may overestimate the extent of osteomyelitis.

measurements.method: Document the continuous tract on orthogonal planes with series/image references.
measurements.pitfall: Neuropathic marrow oedema alone does not establish superimposed infection.

pitfalls: Signal abnormality alone cannot reliably separate osteomyelitis from active neuroarthropathy; distribution and direct ulcer/tract continuity matter.
Previous surgery, fracture and recent treatment can reduce MRI specificity.

steps.label: Ulcer and sinus tract
steps.detail: Find the skin defect (marker) and trace any tract through the soft tissues to bone or joint.

normal.ULCER AND SINUS TRACT: No skin ulcer or sinus tract; subcutaneous tissues unremarkable.

findings: Ulcer beneath the [first metatarsal head / fifth metatarsal head / heel] with a sinus tract extending to the [ ].
Ulcer with surrounding cellulitis; no tract to bone.
Soft-tissue defect in direct contact with the cortex of the [ ].
steps.look: T1 and fluid-sensitive images in two planes from the skin marker to the nearest bone; post-contrast images for the tract wall.
steps.tip: Osteomyelitis in the diabetic foot almost always spreads from an adjacent ulcer; marrow change far from any ulcer suggests another cause.

steps.label: Bone marrow
steps.detail: Separate confluent medullary T1 low signal (replacement of fatty marrow) from isolated fluid-sensitive oedema.

normal.BONE MARROW: Normal marrow signal on T1 and fluid-sensitive sequences; no osteomyelitis.

findings: Confluent T1 hypointensity replacing fatty marrow in the [ ], contiguous with the ulcer tract, with corresponding fluid-sensitive signal and cortical destruction: osteomyelitis.
Fluid-sensitive marrow signal in the [ ] with preserved T1 fatty marrow: reactive osteitis rather than osteomyelitis.
Osteomyelitis extends __ mm from the [distal / proximal] end of the [ ].
steps.look: T1 images first — confluent, medullary, geographic low signal is the key sign — then fluid-sensitive and post-contrast images for extent.
steps.tip: Marrow oedema without T1 replacement of fatty marrow does not establish osteomyelitis.

steps.label: Joints and neuroarthropathy
steps.detail: Describe joint-centred distribution, subchondral oedema, fragmentation, subluxation and deformity.

normal.JOINTS AND NEUROARTHROPATHY: No neuropathic arthropathy; joint alignment normal.

findings: Acute Charcot neuroarthropathy of the [Lisfranc / Chopart] joints: periarticular subchondral marrow oedema centred on the joints, without an ulcer or tract.
Chronic Charcot foot with fragmentation, subluxation and rocker-bottom deformity.
Charcot joint with an adjacent ulcer, tract and diffuse T1 marrow replacement: superimposed osteomyelitis is likely.
steps.look: Sagittal and axial images of the Lisfranc and Chopart joints; compare the location with the ulcer.
steps.tip: Neuroarthropathy is joint-centred and midfoot-predominant; infection is ulcer-centred at pressure points. Bone margins that fade on T1 but reappear after contrast (the ghost sign) favour infection.

steps.label: Abscess and devitalised tissue
steps.detail: Look for fluid collections with rim enhancement, gas and non-enhancing (devitalised) tissue.

normal.COLLECTIONS AND VIABILITY: No abscess, gas or devitalised tissue.

findings: Rim-enhancing collection in the [medial / central / lateral plantar / dorsal] compartment measuring __ × __ × __ mm.
Non-enhancing soft tissue at the [ ], compatible with devitalised tissue.
Soft-tissue gas along the [ ].
steps.look: Fluid-sensitive and post-contrast fat-suppressed images; gas appears as signal void on all sequences.
steps.tip: Without contrast, a collection and devitalised tissue cannot be separated reliably; state this limitation.

steps.label: Tendons, compartments and postoperative changes
steps.detail: Review tenosynovitis, tendon continuity, spread through the plantar compartments and any amputation stump.

normal.TENDONS AND OTHER SOFT TISSUES: Tendons intact without tenosynovitis; no spread along the plantar compartments.

findings: Septic tenosynovitis of the [flexor hallucis longus] sheath extending proximally to [ ].
Infection spreading through the [medial / central / lateral] plantar compartment.
Amputation stump of the [ ] with [no / new] marrow signal change at the resection margin.
steps.look: Axial images along the flexor and extensor tendon sheaths and the plantar compartments.
