spatial_model.title: MRI diabetic foot · spatial orientation
spatial_model.instructions: Drag to rotate; choose a reporting landmark and move the section plane. Relate tibia, fibula and talus to the mortise, hindfoot and major tendon paths.
spatial_model.reporting_aim: Relate tibia, fibula and talus to the mortise, hindfoot and major tendon paths.
spatial_model.population_note: Adult right-foot reference only. The source includes pedal bones and selected neighbouring tissues; it does not provide every plantar-plate component, tendon sheath, postoperative variant or MRI infection finding. Complete reporting coverage and clinical fidelity review remain outstanding.

protocol: Acquire orthogonal planes aligned to the epicondyles with T1/PD and fluid-sensitive sequences; note arthrogram and prior repair.
Review throwing/instability, tendon rupture, osteochondral or nerve symptoms as distinct questions.
For distal biceps assessment, include the radial tuberosity in axial coverage; state if the insertion is not covered.

checklist.label: Tendons
checklist.detail: Assess common flexor/extensor origins at the epicondyles and the distal biceps, brachialis and triceps through their covered course and bony attachments.

checklist.label: Ligaments
checklist.detail: Name UCL and lateral collateral complex components and tear sites.

checklist.label: Osteochondral surface
checklist.detail: Inspect capitellum/trochlea, marrow and loose bodies.

checklist.label: Nerves
checklist.detail: Trace ulnar, median and radial branches with secondary denervation.

checklist.label: Joint mechanics
checklist.detail: Review alignment, impingement features, effusion and postoperative structures.

measurements.name: Tendon tear
measurements.method: Measure partial tear extent or full-thickness retraction in mm.
measurements.pitfall: An intact lacertus fibrosus may limit retraction after distal biceps rupture.

measurements.name: Osteochondral lesion
measurements.method: Measure width, depth and detached fragment; describe fluid interface and cartilage integrity.
measurements.pitfall: Normal posterior capitellar contour can mimic a defect.

measurements.name: Nerve abnormality
measurements.method: Record segment, calibre change and any compressing lesion dimensions.
measurements.pitfall: Signal alone is nonspecific and dynamic subluxation may require ultrasound.

pitfalls: The posterior capitellar pseudodefect is a normal variant.
An accessory ossicle or synovial fold may simulate a loose body.
impression_prompts: Which tendon/ligament component is injured and how severely?
Is there an unstable osteochondral fragment or significant retraction?
Is neuropathy supported and is its cause visible?
escalation: Promptly flag complete acute tendon avulsion, unstable fracture/fragment or unexpected aggressive lesion when clinically consequential.

steps.label: Tendons
steps.detail: Assess the common extensor and flexor origins, the distal biceps at the radial tuberosity and the triceps at the olecranon.

normal.TENDONS: Common extensor and flexor origins, distal biceps and triceps tendons intact with normal signal.

findings: Common extensor origin tendinosis with [partial-thickness / high-grade partial / full-thickness] tear, __ mm (lateral epicondylitis).
Complete distal biceps tendon rupture retracted __ mm [with / without] an intact lacertus fibrosus.
Partial distal biceps tear with radiobicipital bursitis.
Common flexor origin tendinosis (medial epicondylitis).
steps.look: Coronal images for the common extensor and flexor origins; axial and sagittal images for the distal biceps; sagittal images for the triceps.
steps.tip: Lateral epicondylitis can coexist with a tear of the lateral ulnar collateral ligament beneath the extensor origin; look deep to the tendon.

steps.label: Collateral ligaments
steps.detail: Name the ulnar collateral ligament (anterior bundle) and lateral collateral complex components and any tear site.

normal.LIGAMENT COMPLEXES: Ulnar collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex intact.

findings: Tear of the anterior bundle of the UCL at its [humeral / sublime tubercle] attachment.
Undersurface partial tear of the distal UCL with fluid tracking along the sublime tubercle (T-sign).
Lateral ulnar collateral ligament tear, compatible with posterolateral rotatory instability in the appropriate clinical setting.
Avulsion fracture of the sublime tubercle.
steps.look: Coronal images for the anterior bundle of the UCL to the sublime tubercle and for the lateral ulnar collateral ligament behind the radial head; axial images for the annular ligament.

steps.label: Cartilage and bone
steps.detail: Inspect capitellar and trochlear cartilage, osteochondral lesions, marrow and fracture.

normal.CARTILAGE AND BONE: Articular cartilage preserved; no osteochondral lesion, marrow oedema or fracture.

findings: Osteochondral lesion of the capitellum, __ × __ × __ mm, [stable / with fluid undercutting the fragment].
Occult radial head fracture with marrow oedema.
Posteromedial olecranon osteophytes (valgus extension overload).
steps.look: Sagittal and coronal images of the capitellum and trochlea; T1 for fracture lines.
steps.tip: The pseudodefect of the capitellum lies posterolaterally at the junction with the lateral epicondyle and must not be called an osteochondral lesion.

steps.label: Nerves and muscles
steps.detail: Trace the ulnar nerve through the cubital tunnel, the radial nerve and posterior interosseous nerve at the supinator, and the median nerve; look for denervation.

normal.NERVES AND MUSCLES: Ulnar, radial and median nerves normal in calibre and signal; no denervation oedema.

findings: Ulnar nerve enlargement and increased signal in the cubital tunnel [with an anconeus epitrochlearis / osteophytes].
Denervation oedema of the supinator and extensor muscles, compatible with posterior interosseous neuropathy.
Compressing lesion [ ] along the [ ] nerve.
steps.look: Axial images from above the elbow into the proximal forearm, following each nerve.
steps.tip: Mildly increased ulnar nerve signal is common in asymptomatic elbows; enlargement and denervation are more specific.

steps.label: Joint, recesses and loose bodies
steps.detail: Review alignment, effusion, synovitis, loose bodies, synovial folds and postoperative change.

normal.JOINT AND RECESSES: Normal alignment; no effusion, synovitis or loose bodies.

findings: Joint effusion with [number] intra-articular loose bodies in the [olecranon / coronoid] fossa.
Thickened lateral synovial fold [with adjacent chondral change].
Postoperative change after [UCL reconstruction / tendon repair] with [intact / failed] repair.
steps.look: Sagittal images of the anterior and posterior recesses and olecranon fossa; coronal images for a lateral synovial fold.
steps.tip: Synovial folds and accessory ossicles can mimic loose bodies; confirm on two planes.

spatial_model.title: MRI elbow · spatial orientation
spatial_model.instructions: Drag to rotate; choose a reporting landmark and move the section plane. Inspect medial ulnar nerve, anterior distal biceps and lateral radiocapitellar relationships.
spatial_model.reporting_aim: Inspect medial ulnar nerve, anterior distal biceps and lateral radiocapitellar relationships.

protocol: Record age, injured side and views. Assess AP and true lateral coverage of the elbow/distal humerus; document rotation or positioning limitations before interpreting alignment lines.

For suspected lateral condylar injury, consider an oblique view according to the local paediatric pathway. Image additional forearm/wrist sites when the clinical findings warrant it; do not infer their normality from an elbow-only field.

checklist.label: Elbow alignment
checklist.detail: Assess radiocapitellar and ulnohumeral congruity and the anterior humeral line, accounting for age, ossification and projection.

checklist.label: Ossification and growth plates
checklist.detail: Identify visible capitellar, radial-head, medial-epicondylar, trochlear, olecranon and lateral-epicondylar centres and their physes; distinguish normal developmental appearance from injury.

checklist.label: Fracture map and displacement
checklist.detail: Inspect the supracondylar region, condyles/epicondyles, proximal radius and ulna. Describe displacement, angulation, rotation and articular or physeal extension.

checklist.label: Effusion and soft tissues
checklist.detail: Assess anterior/posterior fat pads, periarticular swelling and visible soft-tissue abnormality; a fracture may remain occult.

checklist.label: Associated injury and reduction
checklist.detail: Search for dislocation or an entrapped fragment, review included forearm injury, and describe reduction/fixation when present. Radiographs do not establish normal clinical neurovascular status.

measurements.name: Fragment displacement
measurements.method: Name the fragment, projection and displacement in mm; report angular/rotational deformity separately.
measurements.pitfall: Projection and unossified cartilage can conceal the full articular extent, particularly at the lateral condyle.

measurements.name: Anterior humeral line
measurements.method: On a true lateral image, describe where the anterior humeral cortical line intersects the visible capitellar ossification centre.
measurements.pitfall: The relationship varies with age, especially in younger children. Do not diagnose a fracture solely because the line fails to cross the middle third.

measurements.name: Radiocapitellar line
measurements.method: State the view and radial landmark used; assess the radial-neck axis relative to the visible capitellum and the overall joint relationship.
measurements.pitfall: Age, forearm rotation and imperfect projection affect this line; an isolated line abnormality is not sufficient to establish dislocation.

classification.name: Gartland — when applicable
classification.version: Conventional extension-type supracondylar fracture classification; describe morphology with any assigned type
classification.applicability: Extension-type supracondylar distal humeral fracture only; not lateral condylar, epicondylar, radial-neck or olecranon injuries.
classification.summary: Use the applicable named system only after identifying the fracture pattern. Preserve the observed displacement and cortical-contact description; a classification label alone does not describe neurovascular status or determine treatment.

pitfalls: Normal ossification and unfused growth plates vary with age; an adult elbow model cannot establish paediatric normality.
An elevated anterior fat pad or visible posterior fat pad can indicate an effusion with an occult fracture; absence of a visible fracture line is not proof of no injury.
Alignment lines are age- and projection-dependent; interpret them with the other radiographic and clinical findings.
A displaced medial epicondylar fragment may become incarcerated in the joint after dislocation. Unossified cartilage may hide lateral-condylar articular extension.
impression_prompts: What fracture or dislocation is identified, with which displacement and physeal/articular involvement?
Is there an effusion or other evidence of an occult injury despite an inapparent fracture line?
What associated injury, imaging limitation or reduction/fixation finding changes the next assessment?
escalation: Promptly communicate displaced/unstable fractures, fracture-dislocation or suspected intra-articular fragment entrapment through the local paediatric pathway.
Urgent clinical assessment is required for suspected neurovascular compromise or an open injury; normal radiographic alignment does not exclude these clinical emergencies.

notes: Normal ossification and unfused growth plates vary with age; an adult elbow model cannot establish paediatric normality.
An elevated anterior fat pad or visible posterior fat pad can indicate an effusion with an occult fracture; absence of a visible fracture line is not proof of no injury.
Alignment lines are age- and projection-dependent; interpret them with the other radiographic and clinical findings.
A displaced medial epicondylar fragment may become incarcerated in the joint after dislocation. Unossified cartilage may hide lateral-condylar articular extension.

steps.label: Side, age and technique
steps.detail: Side [ ]; age [ ]; views [ ]; true lateral adequacy [ ]; rotation/coverage limitations [ ]; comparison [ ].
findings: Side [ ]; age [ ]; views [ ]; true lateral adequacy [ ]; rotation/coverage limitations [ ]; comparison [ ].
steps.look: Review the acquired examinations and their coverage before completing this field. For suspected lateral condylar injury, consider an oblique view according to the local paediatric pathway. Image additional forearm/wrist sites when the clinical findings warrant it; do not infer their normality from an elbow-only field.

steps.label: Alignment lines
steps.detail: Check the anterior humeral line on the true lateral and the radiocapitellar line on every view.

normal.ALIGNMENT: Anterior humeral line passes through the middle third of the capitellum; the radiocapitellar line is aligned on all views.

findings: Anterior humeral line passes anterior to the middle third of the capitellum: posterior displacement of the capitellum (extension-type supracondylar fracture).
Radiocapitellar line misses the capitellum: radial head dislocation; examine the ulna for a Monteggia fracture.
steps.look: True lateral: the anterior humeral line should cross the middle third of the capitellum. Every view: the radiocapitellar line should pass through the capitellum.
steps.tip: In very young children with a small capitellum the anterior humeral line may pass through its anterior third; use age and a true lateral before calling displacement.

steps.label: Ossification centres (CRITOE)
steps.detail: Match the visible centres to age in the order capitellum, radial head, internal (medial) epicondyle, trochlea, olecranon, external (lateral) epicondyle.

normal.OSSIFICATION AND GROWTH PLATES: Ossification centres appropriate for age and normally positioned.

findings: Medial epicondyle ossification centre displaced __ mm [distally / into the joint].
Ossicle in the trochlear position without a normally placed medial epicondyle: entrapped medial epicondyle.
Lateral condyle fragment displaced __ mm.
steps.look: AP and lateral: count the centres and confirm the medial epicondyle sits at the medial humerus, not in the joint.
steps.tip: The centres appear at roughly 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 years (earlier in girls); the trochlea does not ossify before the medial epicondyle.

steps.label: Fracture
steps.detail: Name the fracture — supracondylar, lateral condyle, medial epicondyle, radial head or neck, olecranon — and describe displacement.
findings: Extension-type supracondylar fracture, Gartland type [I / II / III], with [posterior displacement / rotation].
Lateral condyle fracture displaced __ mm.
Radial neck fracture with __° angulation.
Medial epicondyle avulsion displaced __ mm.
steps.look: Both views: supracondylar region and posterior cortex on the lateral, lateral condyle on AP and oblique, radial neck and olecranon.
steps.tip: Lateral condyle fractures can be subtle on the AP view; displacement of 2 mm or more usually changes management.

steps.label: Fat pads and effusion
steps.detail: Look for a visible posterior fat pad or an elevated anterior fat pad as signs of a joint effusion.

normal.EFFUSION AND SOFT TISSUES: Anterior fat pad normal; posterior fat pad not visible; no effusion.

findings: Elevated anterior fat pad ("sail sign") and a visible posterior fat pad: joint effusion.
Joint effusion without a visible fracture; an occult fracture is possible, most often supracondylar.
steps.look: True lateral in 90 degrees of flexion: anterior fat pad over the coronoid fossa, posterior fat pad in the olecranon fossa.
steps.tip: On a true lateral in flexion, a visible posterior fat pad is always abnormal.

steps.label: Forearm and associated injury
steps.detail: Look for a forearm fracture with radial head dislocation, a second fracture and post-reduction alignment.

normal.ASSOCIATED AND POST-REDUCTION FINDINGS: No forearm fracture or radial head dislocation.

findings: Monteggia fracture-dislocation: ulnar [fracture / plastic bowing] with anterior radial head dislocation.
Elbow dislocation [posterolateral] [with / without] medial epicondyle avulsion.
Post-reduction alignment [satisfactory / persistent displacement].
steps.look: Include the forearm when the radiocapitellar line is disrupted: look for ulnar fracture or plastic bowing.

measurements.name: Migration/subsidence
measurements.method: Use stable bony landmarks on comparable projections and report change in mm.
measurements.pitfall: A rotated projection can mimic interval component movement.

measurements.name: Lucency map
measurements.method: State zone, maximal width and progression; separate focal osteolysis from a thin stable interface.
measurements.pitfall: Radiographs cannot reliably distinguish aseptic loosening from infection.

pitfalls: Early postoperative appearance and stable expected interface change depend on implant design.
Avoid diagnosing infection solely from a lucent interface.
impression_prompts: Is the implant aligned and stable compared with prior imaging?
Is there wear, progressive loosening, fracture or dislocation?
Does the imaging pattern warrant targeted infection or soft-tissue assessment?
escalation: Promptly communicate prosthetic dislocation or an acute displaced periprosthetic fracture.

steps.label: Component position
steps.detail: Measure cup inclination and describe cup and stem position, migration and subsidence against the earliest postoperative film.

normal.COMPONENT POSITION: Components in satisfactory position, unchanged from [date]; no migration or subsidence.

findings: Acetabular cup inclination __° relative to the inter-teardrop line.
Femoral stem subsidence of __ mm since [date].
Cup migration [medial / superior] with change in inclination since [date].
steps.look: AP pelvis centred on the symphysis: cup inclination against the inter-teardrop line and leg length; lateral view for version; stem position against the greater trochanter on the first postoperative film.
steps.tip: Compare only comparable projections; pelvic tilt and rotation alter apparent cup inclination and version.

steps.label: Bone–implant interfaces
steps.detail: Map lucent lines and osteolysis by acetabular (DeLee–Charnley) and femoral (Gruen) zones and compare with prior films.
findings: Thin, non-progressive lucent line (under 2 mm) in Gruen zone __, unchanged.
Progressive lucency of __ mm in Gruen zones __, compatible with loosening.
Focal scalloped osteolysis in DeLee–Charnley zone __ measuring __ mm, compatible with particle disease.
steps.look: AP and lateral views: acetabular zones 1–3 and femoral zones 1–7 on AP and 8–14 on the lateral.
steps.tip: A lucency wider than 2 mm, progressive widening or a circumferential lucency suggests loosening; a thin stable line can be normal.

steps.label: Bearing surface and hardware
steps.detail: Look for eccentric femoral head position (liner wear), cement mantle defects and broken components.

normal.BEARING AND HARDWARE: Femoral head concentric within the cup; cement mantle intact; no hardware fracture.

findings: Eccentric superolateral position of the femoral head within the cup, compatible with polyethylene wear.
Fracture of the [stem / cement mantle / screw].
Dissociation of the acetabular liner.
steps.look: AP pelvis: femoral head centre relative to the cup centre; cement mantle; screws, wires and stem.

steps.label: Bone stock, fracture and dislocation
steps.detail: Assess periprosthetic fracture, bone stock, dislocation and heterotopic ossification.

normal.BONE AND ALIGNMENT: No periprosthetic fracture or dislocation; no heterotopic ossification.

findings: Periprosthetic femoral fracture [around / below] the stem tip with a [loose / well-fixed] stem.
Posterior dislocation of the femoral head component.
Heterotopic ossification [Brooker class __ / described].
steps.look: The full length of the stem to its tip and the whole acetabulum; the periprosthetic cortex.
steps.tip: The film must include the whole stem tip, where periprosthetic fractures commonly occur.

steps.label: Soft tissues and comparison
steps.detail: Describe soft-tissue findings, periosteal reaction and interval change, and whether the pattern warrants an infection work-up.

normal.SOFT TISSUES AND COMPARISON: Soft tissues unremarkable; no interval change since [date].

findings: Periosteal reaction and rapidly progressive lucency since [date]; infection should be considered and aspiration may be required.
Soft-tissue mass adjacent to the prosthesis; an adverse local tissue reaction should be assessed with ultrasound or MRI.
steps.look: Soft tissues about the hip and comparison with every available prior film.
steps.tip: Infection and aseptic loosening can look identical on radiographs; rapid progression and periosteal reaction raise concern for infection.

protocol: Begin with well-positioned AP pelvis and an appropriate lateral/Dunn view; document projection and pelvic rotation. Assess morphology and coverage on the acquired radiographs.

When MRI or MR arthrography has also been acquired, assess labrum and cartilage on small-field images; state the sequences and arthrogram status. Imaging morphology alone does not establish symptomatic impingement syndrome.

checklist.label: Femoral Morphology
checklist.detail: Assess head-neck sphericity and cam morphology at the relevant clock-face location.

checklist.label: Acetabular Coverage
checklist.detail: Assess lateral coverage and version in the context of pelvic position.

checklist.label: Labrum — if MRI acquired
checklist.detail: If MRI or MR arthrography was acquired, localise tearing, detachment and paralabral cysts. Otherwise state that the labrum is not assessed.

checklist.label: Joint space and cartilage
checklist.detail: Describe radiographic joint-space loss and subchondral change; map cartilage lesions only if MRI was acquired.

checklist.label: Alternative Pain Generators
checklist.detail: Assess additional bone/joint abnormalities on the acquired radiographs. If MRI was acquired, also assess periarticular tendons, bursae, muscles and covered pelvic structures; state limitations of coverage.

measurements.name: Alpha angle
measurements.method: State plane or radial position and the point where the head contour leaves the fitted circle.
measurements.pitfall: A single plane may miss the maximal cam prominence; angle alone does not diagnose symptomatic FAI.

measurements.name: Acetabular coverage
measurements.method: Record centre-edge measurement landmarks and radiographic positioning.
measurements.pitfall: Pelvic tilt and rotation influence apparent version and coverage.

pitfalls: Cam or pincer morphology can occur without symptoms.
Clinical diagnosis requires compatible symptoms, examination signs and imaging findings; do not infer symptomatic FAI syndrome from cam/pincer morphology alone.
impression_prompts: What morphology is present and where is associated labral/chondral damage?
Is there dysplasia or an alternative cause of pain?
Which measurement technique was used?

steps.label: Femoral head–neck morphology
steps.detail: Assess head–neck sphericity and cam morphology at the anterosuperior head–neck junction.

normal.FEMORAL MORPHOLOGY: Normal femoral head–neck offset without cam morphology.

findings: Cam morphology: osseous bump at the anterosuperior head–neck junction; alpha angle __° on the [Dunn view / radial MRI at __ o'clock].
Reduced femoral head–neck offset without a discrete bump.
Herniation pit at the anterior femoral neck.
steps.look: Dunn (45 degree) or cross-table lateral view, and radial MRI reformats at the anterosuperior (about 1–2 o'clock) head–neck junction.
steps.tip: The alpha angle depends on projection and clock-face position; always state where it was measured.

steps.label: Acetabular coverage and version
steps.detail: Measure the lateral centre-edge angle and look for crossover, posterior wall and ischial spine signs, coxa profunda or protrusio.

normal.ACETABULAR COVERAGE: Normal lateral acetabular coverage; no crossover sign, dysplasia or protrusio.

findings: Pincer morphology: lateral centre-edge angle __° [with coxa profunda / protrusio].
Crossover and posterior wall signs indicating acetabular retroversion.
Undercoverage: lateral centre-edge angle __°, compatible with acetabular dysplasia.
steps.look: A well-centred AP pelvis with the coccyx over the symphysis, 1–3 cm above it.
steps.tip: Pelvic tilt and rotation create false crossover signs; check the coccyx–symphysis relationship first.

steps.label: Labrum (if MRI acquired)
steps.detail: If MRI or MR arthrography was acquired, localise tearing, detachment and paralabral cysts; otherwise state that the labrum is not assessed.

normal.LABRUM \u2014 IF MRI ACQUIRED: Acetabular labrum intact without tear, detachment or paralabral cyst.

findings: Labrum not assessed: no MRI acquired.
Anterosuperior labral tear from __ to __ o'clock [with / without] chondrolabral detachment.
Paralabral cyst __ mm adjacent to the [ ] labrum.
steps.look: Radial or oblique small-field MRI (MR arthrography when performed) around the acetabular clock face.
steps.tip: Labral tears in femoroacetabular impingement are usually anterosuperior; relate them to the site of the cam or pincer morphology.

steps.label: Joint space and cartilage
steps.detail: Describe radiographic joint-space loss and subchondral change; map cartilage lesions only if MRI was acquired.

normal.JOINT SPACE AND CARTILAGE: Joint space preserved; no subchondral sclerosis or cysts; cartilage intact where assessed.

findings: Superolateral joint-space narrowing to __ mm with subchondral cysts: secondary osteoarthritis.
Anterosuperior acetabular chondral delamination adjacent to the cam morphology (MRI).
Focal chondral defect of the [femoral head / acetabulum], __ × __ mm.
steps.look: AP pelvis for joint space; MRI proton-density or fluid-sensitive images for acetabular and femoral cartilage.
steps.tip: Established osteoarthritis changes the treatment discussion; report joint-space width even when morphology is the question.

steps.label: Alternative pain generators
steps.detail: Assess periarticular tendons, bursae, muscles and the visible pelvic structures.
findings: Prominent anterior inferior iliac spine extending to the acetabular rim (subspine impingement morphology).
Gluteus [medius / minimus] tendinopathy [with partial tear] at the greater trochanter.
Femoral head subchondral fracture or osteonecrosis.
steps.look: The whole AP pelvis — sacroiliac joints, pubic symphysis, anterior inferior iliac spine — and MRI of periarticular tendons and bursae when acquired.

spatial_model.instructions: Drag to rotate; choose a reporting landmark and move the section plane. Inspect femoral head-neck, acetabulum and labrum from multiple viewpoints before describing a hip finding.
spatial_model.reporting_aim: Inspect femoral head-neck, acetabulum and labrum from multiple viewpoints before describing a hip finding.

protocol: Review multiplanar T1 or PD and fluid-sensitive images with known surgery and injury mechanism.
Record graft/reconstruction or meniscal surgery because postoperative criteria differ.

checklist.label: Menisci
checklist.detail: Inspect both menisci, roots and meniscocapsular attachments for tear and displaced fragments.

checklist.label: Cruciates/collaterals
checklist.detail: Assess continuity, tear location and associated avulsion.

checklist.label: Cartilage and bone
checklist.detail: Map chondral loss, osteochondral lesions, contusions and subchondral fracture.

checklist.label: Extensor mechanism
checklist.detail: Review quadriceps/patellar tendons and patellofemoral stabilisers.

checklist.label: Joint and corners
checklist.detail: Assess effusion, loose bodies, posteromedial/lateral structures and cysts.

measurements.name: Meniscal extrusion/tear
measurements.method: Measure extrusion on a standard coronal plane and describe tear location/morphology.
measurements.pitfall: Extrusion alone does not prove a root tear; inspect the attachment.

measurements.name: Cartilage/osteochondral defect
measurements.method: Measure AP/transverse extent and depth; report instability signs.
measurements.pitfall: Partial-volume signal is not a full-thickness defect.

measurements.name: Tendon or ligament gap
measurements.method: Measure retraction/gap when complete structural discontinuity is present.
measurements.pitfall: Oedema is not equivalent to fibre disruption.

pitfalls: Postoperative meniscal signal may persist without recurrent tear.
Normal variants and intermeniscal ligaments can mimic tears.
impression_prompts: What dominant internal derangement is present?
Which associated injuries or unstable/displaced fragments matter?
Is postoperative interpretation limited?
escalation: Promptly communicate an occult fracture or dislocation-pattern multiligament injury with potential neurovascular implications.

notes: Replace bracketed choices with observed findings. The gallery contains published teaching examples; cite the patient examination series and image numbers in the clinical report.

steps.label: Menisci
steps.detail: Inspect both menisci — anterior horn, body, posterior horn and roots — for tear, displaced fragment and extrusion.

normal.MENISCI: Medial and lateral menisci intact, including the roots; no extrusion or displaced fragment.

findings: [Horizontal / oblique / longitudinal / radial] tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus extending to the [inferior] articular surface.
Bucket-handle tear of the [medial] meniscus with a fragment displaced into the intercondylar notch (double PCL sign).
Posterior root tear of the [medial] meniscus with __ mm extrusion.
Fragment of the [lateral] meniscus flipped into the anterior horn region.
steps.look: Sagittal proton-density images through each meniscus from periphery to root; coronal images for the body, roots and extrusion; search the notch for displaced fragments.
steps.tip: Call a tear only when abnormal signal reaches an articular surface on at least two images, or when the meniscal shape is abnormal.

steps.label: Cruciate and collateral ligaments
steps.detail: Assess the ACL, PCL, MCL and posterolateral corner for continuity, tear site and associated avulsion.

normal.LIGAMENTS: Cruciate and collateral ligaments and posterolateral corner structures intact.

findings: Complete ACL tear with bone contusions of the lateral femoral condyle and posterolateral tibial plateau (pivot-shift pattern).
Segond fracture: avulsion from the lateral tibial rim, associated with ACL tear.
MCL injury: [periligamentous oedema / partial tear / complete tear] at the [femoral / tibial] attachment.
Posterolateral corner injury involving the [LCL / biceps femoris / popliteus tendon]; fibular head avulsion.
steps.look: Sagittal images for the cruciates; coronal images for the collateral ligaments and posterolateral corner (biceps femoris, popliteus); axial images through the posterolateral corner.
steps.tip: Posterolateral corner injuries are easily overlooked alongside an ACL tear but change surgical planning.

steps.label: Cartilage and subchondral bone
steps.detail: Map chondral loss, osteochondral lesions, contusions and subchondral fracture by compartment.

normal.CARTILAGE AND SUBCHONDRAL BONE: Articular cartilage preserved; no contusion, subchondral fracture or osteochondral lesion.

findings: Full-thickness chondral defect of the [medial femoral condyle], __ × __ mm.
Subchondral insufficiency fracture of the [medial femoral condyle] with marrow oedema.
Osteochondritis dissecans of the [lateral aspect of the medial femoral condyle] with fluid undercutting the fragment (unstable).
steps.look: Fluid-sensitive images in all planes for chondral defects and contusions; T1 for fracture lines.
steps.tip: A fluid-bright line or cysts beneath an osteochondral fragment indicate instability.

steps.label: Extensor mechanism and patellofemoral joint
steps.detail: Review the quadriceps and patellar tendons, patellar position, medial patellofemoral ligament and trochlea.

normal.EXTENSOR AND PATELLOFEMORAL STRUCTURES: Quadriceps and patellar tendons intact; patella centred; medial patellofemoral ligament and retinacula intact; normal trochlea.

findings: Transient lateral patellar dislocation: medial patellofemoral ligament tear at the [femoral / patellar] attachment with medial patellar and lateral femoral condyle contusions.
Patellar tendinopathy at the inferior patellar pole.
Complete quadriceps tendon rupture with a __ mm gap.
Trochlear dysplasia with a [shallow / flat] trochlea.
steps.look: Sagittal images for the tendons; axial images for patellar position, the medial patellofemoral ligament and trochlear shape.
steps.tip: The contusion pattern of patellar dislocation (medial patella and lateral femoral condyle) persists after spontaneous reduction.

steps.label: Joint and posterior structures
steps.detail: Assess effusion, synovitis, loose bodies, popliteal cyst, posteromedial structures and postoperative change.

normal.JOINT AND POSTERIOR STRUCTURES: No significant effusion, synovitis or loose bodies; no popliteal cyst.

findings: Moderate joint effusion with [number] loose bodies.
Popliteal cyst __ × __ mm between the medial gastrocnemius and semimembranosus [with rupture and fluid tracking distally].
Parameniscal cyst adjacent to a [horizontal] tear of the [ ] meniscus.
steps.look: Axial and sagittal images of the suprapatellar recess, Hoffa fat pad, popliteal fossa and posteromedial corner.
steps.tip: A popliteal cyst arises between the medial gastrocnemius and semimembranosus; a collection elsewhere needs another explanation.

structure_atlas.alt: Original labeled knee MRI showing Posterior meniscofemoral ligament (Wrisberg), Posterior horn of lateral meniscus (local margin).
structure_atlas.caption: Sagittal PD-weighted MRI in a 43-year-old woman. In a, the posterior meniscofemoral (Wrisberg) ligament (large arrow) parallels the outer margin of the lateral meniscus posterior horn (small arrow). The next medial slice b shows the ligament behind the posterior cruciate ligament. The source presents this relationship as a normal-structure pitfall, not a displaced meniscal fragment.
structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Sagittal proton-density–weighted fast spin echo images in a 43-year-old female patient through the lateral meniscus. At the insertion of the posterior meniscofemoral ligament ( a ), the ligament ( large arrow ) closely parallels the outer posterior margin of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus ( small arrow ). The linear signal between the low-intensity meniscus and the low-intensity ligament may lead to pitfalls and could be confused with a detached meniscal fragment. However, on the next more medial sagittal image ( b ), the ligament ( large arrow ) is clearly visible posteriorly to the posterior cruciate ligament

structure_atlas.limits: Single 25-year-old female cadaveric left knee. Source MRI sampling is 0.5 mm isotropic and approximately 0.35 × 0.35 × 0.7 mm for cartilage; authors processed and smoothed the released surfaces. Rendering resolution adds no anatomical detail. Display scale follows source millimetres, not validated clinical measurements. Whole-object labels do not establish fine components or complete surface coverage; anatomical and clinical review remain pending. Tibial-cartilage mask-version ancestry is unresolved; thickness and subchondral-interface claims remain withheld.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full:
Supplemental Figure 1: Semimembranosus tendon anatomy. A) Schematic drawing and 
B,C) Cadaveric specimens illustrate the direct (d), anterior (a), capsular (c), oblique popliteal 
(o), popliteal, and meniscal (white outlined arrowhead) arms of the semimembranosus 
tendon (SMt). Black arrowhead, oblique popliteal ligament; black outlined arrowhead, 
fabella; SM, semimembranosus muscle; BF, bicep femoris; LG, lateral gastrocnemius; 1

ligament; 3, capsular arm of the posterior oblique ligament. AMt, adductor magnus tendon.

structure_atlas.source_caption_full:
Supplemental Figure 4: Posterior oblique ligament.  A) Schematic drawing and B) Cadaveric 
specimen illustrate the superficial (1), tibial (2), and capsular arms (3) of the posterior oblique 
ligament and their respective relationship with the superficial medial collateral ligament 
(arrowhead) and the anterior (a) and the direct (d) arms of the semimembranosus tendon 
(SMt). Blue stain marks the adductor tubercle. C) Lon g-axis 18 -5MHz US image 
demonstrates the superficial arm (arrowheads) running over the joint line and the body of 
the medial meniscus (Bmm) and  merging with the anterior arm of the semimebranosus 
tendon (arrows) in proximity to its distal insertion on the tibia. D) Long -axis 18-5MHz US 
image shows the relationship of the tibial arm of the posterior oblique ligament (arrowhead) 
with the anterior arm of the semimembranosus (arrows) and the posterior horn of the medial 
meniscus (PHmm). The inserts illustrate the respective probe position.

structure_atlas.caption: Source injury example in a 31-year-old man with recent knee sprain and full-thickness ACL tear. MRI B is a coronal fat-saturated T2-weighted turbo-spin-echo 3 T image: solid arrowheads mark thickening and waviness of the anterolateral ligament; an outlined arrowhead marks the lateral meniscotibial ligament beside its tibial plateau insertion. A is ultrasound from the injured knee; C is contralateral ultrasound with normal ALL appearance. The contralateral normality claim does not apply to MRI B or the whole injured knee.
structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Fig. 4 ALL tear in a 31-year-old male patient with a recent knee sprain and full-thickness ACL tear. A Longitudinal 22-8 MHz US image and ( B) coronal fat-saturated tSE T2-weighted 3 T scan show thickening and wavy appearance of ALL (arrowheads). Note the lateral meniscotibial ligament (outlined arrowhead) inserting into the tibial plateau in close proximity to ALL. C Longitudinal 22-8 MHz US from the contralateral knee of the same patient demonstrates the normal appearance of ALL (arrowheads). Outlined arrowhead, meniscotibial ligament; asterisk, meniscal body. The inserts illust rate the respective probe position

structure_atlas.limits: Only MRI B is selected for clinical-image scope. The author labels local ALL thickening/waviness and the nearby lateral meniscotibial insertion; one slice does not establish either complete course, attachment footprint, physical tissue dimensions or independently verified integrity. No statement in the source establishes the meniscotibial ligament as normal or injured. ACL rupture belongs to the patient context and is not directly illustrated or credited by this selected MRI slice. Ultrasound A/C, including contralateral normal appearance in C, cannot satisfy MRI requirements or transfer normality to B. Side, MRI slice thickness, voxel spacing, TR/TE and complete examination findings are unreported.

protocol: Record mechanism, injury date and symptomatic site; cover the full muscle-tendon unit with T1 and fluid-sensitive sequences.
Include adjacent tendon attachment and the region of maximal oedema or haematoma; compare opposite side if useful.

checklist.label: Injured Unit
checklist.detail: Name muscle, side and compartment, including adjacent involved muscles.

checklist.label: Fibre Disruption
checklist.detail: Separate oedema without definite discontinuity from partial or complete structural disruption.

checklist.label: Tendon And Aponeurosis
checklist.detail: Assess central tendon, aponeurosis and origin/insertion.

checklist.label: Oedema And Haematoma
checklist.detail: Describe extent and compartment of oedema and blood products.

checklist.label: Associated Findings
checklist.detail: Look for neurovascular proximity, contusion, scar and alternative explanations.

measurements.name: Extent of injury
measurements.method: Report cranio-caudal oedema length, structural defect size and maximal cross-sectional involvement separately.
measurements.pitfall: Oedema dimensions are not tear dimensions.

measurements.name: Retraction
measurements.method: Measure along the tendon between the attachment or tear margins with a named plane.
measurements.pitfall: Position and muscle shortening influence the gap.

pitfalls: A generic numeric grade should not replace muscle, location and tendon involvement.
MRI morphology does not determine a precise return-to-sport date.
impression_prompts: Which unit and tissue component are disrupted?
Is there tendon involvement, complete rupture or retraction?
How extensive are oedema and haematoma?

steps.label: Injured muscle–tendon unit
steps.detail: Name the muscle, side and compartment, and whether the injury is myofascial, myotendinous or intratendinous.

normal.INJURED UNIT: Normal muscle signal and architecture; no muscle injury.

findings: Myotendinous junction injury of the [ ] at the [proximal / mid / distal] third.
Myofascial (peripheral) injury of the [ ] with fluid along the epimysium.
Intratendinous injury of the central tendon of the [rectus femoris].
steps.look: Axial fluid-sensitive images to identify the muscle; coronal or sagittal images for the level along the unit.
steps.tip: Name the muscle and the site along the unit; myofascial, myotendinous and intratendinous injuries recover differently.

steps.label: Fibre disruption
steps.detail: Separate oedema with preserved architecture from partial or complete structural disruption.
findings: Oedema with preserved architecture (low-grade strain).
Partial fibre disruption involving approximately __% of the cross-sectional area.
Complete disruption with a __ mm gap and retraction.
steps.look: Axial and longitudinal fluid-sensitive images for loss of the normal feathery fibre pattern and discontinuity.

steps.label: Tendon and aponeurosis
steps.detail: Assess the central tendon, aponeurosis and origin or insertion.

normal.TENDON AND APONEUROSIS: Central tendon, aponeurosis and attachments intact.

findings: Central tendon disruption of the [ ] (intratendinous extension).
Avulsion of the [ ] tendon from its [origin / insertion] [with / without] a bone fragment.
steps.look: Longitudinal images along the intramuscular tendon and aponeurosis to its attachment.
steps.tip: Extension into the intramuscular tendon is associated with longer recovery than a purely myofascial injury.

steps.label: Oedema and haematoma
steps.detail: Describe the extent of oedema and the site and size of any haematoma.
findings: Oedema extends __ cm craniocaudally, involving about __% of the maximal cross-sectional area.
Intramuscular haematoma __ × __ × __ mm.
Closed degloving (Morel-Lavallée) collection between the subcutaneous fat and fascia over the [ ], __ mm.
steps.look: Fluid-sensitive images for craniocaudal oedema length; T1 and fluid-sensitive images for haematoma signal.

steps.label: Associated findings
steps.detail: Look for nerve proximity, bone contusion, scar from earlier injury and alternative explanations.

normal.ASSOCIATED FINDINGS: No associated nerve, bone or fascial abnormality.

findings: Scar from previous injury at the [ ] with new adjacent oedema (re-injury).
Peripheral mineralisation within the haematoma on radiograph or CT, compatible with myositis ossificans.
Haematoma displaces the [sciatic] nerve without nerve signal change.
steps.look: Adjacent nerves, bone and fascia; comparison with earlier injuries at the same site.
steps.tip: Early myositis ossificans can mimic a soft-tissue sarcoma on MRI; radiographs or CT show its peripheral mineralisation.

protocol: Review symptom distribution, weakness, laboratory context, medication and known nerve injury; choose bilateral coverage when distribution is diagnostic.
Include T1 for fatty change and fluid-sensitive sequences for oedema; use contrast for a specific infection or mass question.

checklist.label: Distribution
checklist.detail: Map involved muscles and whether change follows a nerve, compartment or systemic pattern.

checklist.label: Oedema
checklist.detail: Describe fluid-sensitive signal and focal versus diffuse muscle involvement.

checklist.label: Fatty Change And Atrophy
checklist.detail: Use T1 to distinguish chronic fatty replacement from active oedema.

checklist.label: Collection Or Mass
checklist.detail: Identify focal lesions, blood products and enhancement if acquired.

checklist.label: Nerves And Associated Structures
checklist.detail: Inspect visible nerves, entrapment sites, tendons and bone for a cause.

measurements.name: Distribution map
measurements.method: List involved and selectively spared muscles; compare sides and proximal/distal extent.
measurements.pitfall: MRI pattern narrows the differential but does not determine a specific myopathy diagnosis.

measurements.name: Focal collection
measurements.method: Measure in three planes and describe compartment and enhancement if available.
measurements.pitfall: Oedema may occur with inflammation, infection, denervation, ischaemia or exertion.

pitfalls: Do not equate high fluid-sensitive signal with primary inflammatory myositis.
Acute denervation may produce oedema before chronic fatty atrophy appears.
impression_prompts: What distribution and combination of oedema/fatty atrophy is present?
Is a focal infection or mass identified?
Which clinical, nerve or laboratory correlation would resolve the differential?
escalation: Urgently communicate imaging concerning for aggressive soft-tissue infection or a significant abscess.

steps.label: Distribution
steps.detail: Map the involved muscles and whether the change follows a nerve, a compartment or a systemic pattern.

normal.DISTRIBUTION: Normal bulk and signal of all imaged muscles, symmetric.

findings: Symmetric proximal muscle oedema involving [ ] with relative sparing of [ ], compatible with an inflammatory myopathy in the appropriate clinical setting.
Change confined to the muscles supplied by the [ ] nerve, favouring denervation.
Selective involvement of [ ] with sparing of [ ], a pattern that may suggest [a specific myopathy].
steps.look: Bilateral axial T1 and fluid-sensitive images of the symptomatic region, muscle by muscle.
steps.tip: A distribution needs both sides; unilateral coverage can miss symmetric disease.

steps.label: Oedema
steps.detail: Describe fluid-sensitive signal, focal or diffuse involvement, and fascial and subcutaneous change.

normal.OEDEMA: No muscle, fascial or subcutaneous oedema.

findings: Diffuse muscle oedema in [ ] with perifascial fluid.
Thickening and fluid along the deep fascia [with gas]; in the appropriate clinical context this raises concern for necrotising fasciitis.
Patchy intramuscular oedema without fascial involvement.
steps.look: Fat-suppressed fluid-sensitive axial images; note fascial and subcutaneous involvement.
steps.tip: Muscle oedema is non-specific: inflammation, denervation, exertion, radiation and infection can all cause it.

steps.label: Fatty change and atrophy
steps.detail: Use T1 images to separate chronic fatty replacement from active oedema.
findings: Fatty replacement of [ ], [mild / moderate / severe], with volume loss.
Mixed pattern: fatty replacement with active oedema in [ ].
Unilateral fatty atrophy of the [ ] in the [ ] nerve territory (chronic denervation).
steps.look: Axial T1 images for fatty streaks and volume loss; compare sides.
steps.tip: Acute denervation causes oedema within weeks; fatty atrophy takes months.

steps.label: Collection or mass
steps.detail: Identify focal lesions, abscess, blood products and enhancement if acquired.
findings: Intramuscular abscess (pyomyositis) in the [ ] measuring __ × __ × __ mm with rim enhancement.

steps.look: Fluid-sensitive and contrast-enhanced images; diffusion if acquired.

findings: Ganglion cyst at the [ ] compressing the [ ] nerve, with denervation of [ ].

steps.label: Tendon identity
steps.detail: Identify the semimembranosus and the conjoint (semitendinosus and biceps femoris long head) origins separately at the ischial tuberosity.

normal.TENDON IDENTITY: Semimembranosus and conjoint tendon origins intact; hamstring muscles normal.

findings: Injury of the biceps femoris long head at the proximal myotendinous junction.
Semimembranosus origin injury with an intact conjoint tendon.
Both the conjoint tendon and semimembranosus origins involved.
steps.look: Axial images at the ischial tuberosity — semimembranosus anterolateral, conjoint tendon posteromedial — then follow each distally.
steps.tip: The biceps femoris long head is the most frequently injured hamstring; name each involved component.

steps.label: Tear type and location
steps.detail: Assess partial origin injury, full-thickness avulsion and myotendinous injury.
findings: Partial tear of the conjoint tendon origin involving about __% of the footprint, with residual attached fibres.
Complete avulsion of the [conjoint tendon / all three tendons] from the ischial tuberosity.
Intratendinous injury extending __ cm along the free tendon (British Athletics grade __c).
steps.look: Coronal and axial fluid-sensitive images of the free tendon, myotendinous junction and muscle belly.

steps.label: Retraction
steps.detail: Measure each avulsed tendon from its footprint and describe the distal stump.
findings: Conjoint tendon retracted __ cm from the ischial tuberosity (coronal measurement).
Apophyseal avulsion fragment displaced __ mm.
steps.look: Coronal images along the tendon from the ischial footprint to the stump; confirm on sagittal images.
steps.tip: Measure retraction along the tendon course on coronal images; axial images underestimate it.

steps.label: Muscle and haematoma
steps.detail: Map muscle oedema, structural fibre loss and haematoma.
findings: Muscle oedema extending __ cm craniocaudally.
Haematoma __ × __ × __ mm around the retracted tendon.
Retracted muscle belly bunched distally ("dropped ice cream" appearance).
steps.look: Axial and coronal fluid-sensitive images along the hamstring muscles.

steps.label: Sciatic nerve and associated findings
steps.detail: Assess the sciatic nerve relationship and adjacent bone or soft-tissue change.

findings: Haematoma abuts and displaces the sciatic nerve without nerve signal change.
Sciatic nerve thickening and increased signal adjacent to [scar / haematoma].
Ischial tuberosity marrow oedema.
steps.look: Axial images following the sciatic nerve lateral to the ischial tuberosity into the proximal thigh.

measurements.name: Cuff tear
measurements.method: Measure AP width, mediolateral retraction and partial-thickness depth in mm or proportion.
measurements.pitfall: Delamination may make a single retraction measurement incomplete.

measurements.name: Bone loss
measurements.method: State en-face glenoid best-fit-circle or other method and humeral defect measurements if performed.
measurements.pitfall: Glenoid-track assessment requires both glenoid and humeral measurements and a specified method.

measurements.name: Muscle quality
measurements.method: Use a named fatty-infiltration/atrophy scale if helpful and identify each muscle.
measurements.pitfall: Do not infer reparability from tear size alone.

pitfalls: Magic-angle signal on short-TE images can mimic tendinopathy.
Sublabral variants should not be called a labral tear without supporting morphology.
impression_prompts: What tendon/labral injury is present and how extensive is it?
What muscle quality, bone loss or biceps abnormality affects planning?
What incidental findings are unlikely to explain symptoms?
escalation: Promptly communicate acute fracture-dislocation or an unexpected significant destructive process.

steps.label: Cuff
steps.detail: Name involved tendon, tear surface/depth, AP extent and retraction.

normal.ROTATOR CUFF: Supraspinatus, infraspinatus, subscapularis and teres minor tendons intact, with normal thickness, signal and footprint attachment.

findings: Full-thickness supraspinatus tear at the footprint, __ mm anteroposterior, retracted __ mm [lateral to / at / medial to] the humeral head apex.
Partial-thickness [articular-sided / bursal-sided / intrasubstance] [ ] tear involving approximately __% of tendon thickness, __ mm long.
Tendinosis of the [ ] tendon: thickening and intermediate signal without a fluid-signal defect.
Tear of the upper subscapularis fibres [with / without] medial displacement of the long-head biceps tendon.
steps.look: Oblique coronal fluid-sensitive images from the greater-tuberosity footprint to the musculotendinous junction; oblique sagittal images for anteroposterior tear width; axial images for the upper subscapularis fibres.
steps.tip: Magic-angle signal on short-TE images can mimic tendinopathy; confirm a defect on the long-TE fluid-sensitive sequence.

steps.label: Muscle
steps.detail: Describe atrophy and fatty infiltration for each affected cuff muscle.

normal.MUSCLE QUALITY: Normal bulk and signal of the rotator cuff muscles, without fatty infiltration or denervation oedema.

findings: Supraspinatus atrophy with a positive tangent sign.
Fatty infiltration of the [ ] muscle, [less fat than muscle / equal fat and muscle / more fat than muscle].
Oedema-like signal of the [supraspinatus / infraspinatus] muscle without a tendon tear, compatible with denervation; the [suprascapular / spinoglenoid] notch is [clear / contains a paralabral cyst].
steps.look: The most lateral oblique sagittal T1 image on which the scapular spine joins the scapular body (the Y-shaped view); compare each cuff muscle with its fossa.
steps.tip: Read the tangent sign on the most lateral Y-shaped sagittal image; more medial images make an atrophic muscle look fuller.

steps.label: Biceps
steps.detail: Review anchor, pulley, intra-articular segment and groove position.

normal.BICEPS AND PULLEY: Long-head biceps tendon intact and located in the bicipital groove; biceps anchor and pulley unremarkable.

findings: Medial [subluxation / dislocation] of the long-head biceps tendon from the bicipital groove, with an associated upper subscapularis tear.
Tendinosis of the intra-articular long-head biceps tendon with [thickening / partial-thickness tear].
Empty bicipital groove compatible with long-head biceps rupture or tenotomy; tendon stump at [level].
Tear at the biceps anchor extending from __ to __ o'clock.
steps.look: Axial images from the superior labrum down the bicipital groove; oblique sagittal images through the rotator interval for the pulley; coronal images for the biceps anchor.
steps.tip: An empty groove on axial images is a dislocation until the tendon is found medially, anterior to, within or deep to the subscapularis.

steps.label: Labrum/instability
steps.detail: Map labral injury, capsuloligamentous findings and glenoid/humeral defects.

normal.LABRUM AND INSTABILITY: Glenoid labrum intact; capsule and glenohumeral ligaments unremarkable; no Hill-Sachs or osseous Bankart lesion.

findings: Anteroinferior labral tear from __ to __ o'clock [with / without] periosteal stripping ([Bankart / Perthes / ALPSA / GLAD] pattern) and [no / an] osseous glenoid fragment.
Hill-Sachs impaction of the posterosuperior humeral head, __ mm; glenoid bone loss __% by [method].
Humeral avulsion of the inferior glenohumeral ligament (HAGL): J-shaped axillary recess.
Posterior labral tear (reverse Bankart) with reverse Hill-Sachs impaction of the anterior humeral head.
steps.look: Axial images from superior to inferior using the glenoid clock face (3 o'clock anterior); ABER images for anteroinferior labral detachment when acquired; sagittal images for the glenoid contour and the axillary recess.
steps.tip: Sublabral recess, sublabral foramen and Buford complex lie in the anterosuperior quadrant; they do not explain an anteroinferior labral defect.

steps.label: Joint/outlet
steps.detail: Assess cartilage, bursae, AC joint and associated osseous abnormality.

normal.JOINT AND OUTLET: Glenohumeral cartilage preserved; no joint effusion; subacromial-subdeltoid bursa not distended; acromion and acromioclavicular joint unremarkable.

findings: Subacromial-subdeltoid bursal fluid, [small / moderate].
Acromioclavicular joint osteoarthritis with capsular hypertrophy and inferior osteophytes [contacting / not contacting] the supraspinatus musculotendinous junction.
Os acromiale at the [pre-acromion / meso-acromion / meta-acromion] level [with / without] oedema at the synchondrosis.
Glenohumeral cartilage loss, [focal / diffuse], with [osteophytes / subchondral change].
steps.look: Coronal and sagittal images of the acromion, acromioclavicular joint and subacromial-subdeltoid bursa; superior axial images for an os acromiale; all planes for cartilage and effusion.

protocol: Use a high-frequency linear transducer with tendon assessment in two orthogonal planes; correct anisotropy before diagnosing a tear.
Record movements actually assessed, patient limitation, and Doppler when inflammation is suspected.

checklist.label: Long Head Of Biceps
checklist.detail: Follow the tendon in the groove and rotator interval; assess stability during rotation.

checklist.label: Rotator Cuff
checklist.detail: Assess subscapularis, supraspinatus and infraspinatus; describe tear surface, thickness and dimensions.

checklist.label: Bursa And Dynamic Assessment
checklist.detail: Assess subacromial-subdeltoid bursal distension and tendon/bursal movement.

checklist.label: Joint And Acromioclavicular Joint
checklist.detail: Review accessible posterior joint recess and AC joint with focal symptom correlation.

checklist.label: Muscles And Limitations
checklist.detail: Assess visible cuff bulk and any paralabral cyst; state the deep structures not evaluated reliably.

measurements.name: Tear size
measurements.method: Measure maximal orthogonal tear dimensions and retraction with images in two planes.
measurements.pitfall: Anisotropy and a curved tendon surface may mimic a defect.

measurements.name: Calcification or fluid
measurements.method: Record calcification dimensions, shadowing and location; characterise bursal/sheath distension.
measurements.pitfall: Sheath fluid can reflect joint fluid and is not by itself proof of biceps tendinopathy.

pitfalls: A normal ultrasound does not exclude labral or other deep intra-articular disease.
Do not diagnose impingement from acromial appearance alone; describe the observed dynamic finding and symptoms.
impression_prompts: Which tendon or bursa explains the focal complaint?
Is there a full-thickness defect, retraction or dynamic biceps instability?
Is MRI needed to address an unresolved intra-articular question?

notes: Replace bracketed choices with observed findings. The gallery contains published teaching examples; cite the patient examination series and image numbers in the clinical report.

steps.label: Long head of biceps
steps.detail: Follow the tendon in the groove and rotator interval and assess stability during rotation.

normal.LONG HEAD OF BICEPS: Long-head biceps tendon in the groove with a normal fibrillar pattern; no sheath effusion; stable on dynamic rotation.

findings: Long-head biceps tendon absent from the groove, [subluxed / dislocated] medially [superficial to / within] the subscapularis.
Thickened, hypoechoic long-head biceps tendon with sheath fluid and hyperaemia (tenosynovitis).
Empty groove: long-head biceps rupture.
steps.look: Transverse and longitudinal scans in the bicipital groove with the arm externally rotated; follow into the rotator interval; dynamic internal and external rotation.
steps.tip: Anisotropy makes a tendon falsely hypoechoic; angle the probe perpendicular to the fibres before calling tendinopathy.

steps.label: Rotator cuff
steps.detail: Assess the subscapularis, supraspinatus and infraspinatus and describe any tear surface, thickness and dimensions.

normal.ROTATOR CUFF: Subscapularis, supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons intact with normal thickness and echotexture; no calcification.

findings: Full-thickness supraspinatus tear __ × __ mm with loss of the convex bursal contour [and retraction].
Partial-thickness [articular-sided / bursal-sided] supraspinatus tear, __ mm.
Calcific deposit in the [supraspinatus], __ mm, [hard with acoustic shadowing / soft without shadowing].
Tendinosis: thickened hypoechoic supraspinatus without a defect.
steps.look: Subscapularis in external rotation; supraspinatus in the modified Crass position in long and short axis; infraspinatus posteriorly.
steps.tip: A full-thickness tear extends from the bursal to the articular surface, often with a flattened bursal contour; confirm it in two planes.

steps.label: Bursa and dynamic assessment
steps.detail: Assess subacromial–subdeltoid bursal distension and tendon and bursal movement.

normal.BURSA AND DYNAMIC ASSESSMENT: Subacromial–subdeltoid bursa not distended; smooth gliding of the cuff beneath the acromion during abduction.

findings: Subacromial–subdeltoid bursal distension of __ mm [with Doppler hyperaemia].
Bursal fluid pooling at the acromial edge with painful abduction.
steps.look: Longitudinal images over the supraspinatus at rest and during active abduction.
steps.tip: Report the observed dynamic finding and the pain it produced rather than "impingement" as a diagnosis.

steps.label: Glenohumeral recess and acromioclavicular joint
steps.detail: Review the accessible posterior joint recess and the acromioclavicular joint with focal symptom correlation.

normal.JOINT AND ACROMIOCLAVICULAR JOINT: No glenohumeral effusion in the posterior recess; acromioclavicular joint unremarkable.

findings: Glenohumeral effusion of __ mm in the posterior recess.
Acromioclavicular joint capsular distension and osteophytes [with focal tenderness].
Cortical irregularity of the greater tuberosity.
steps.look: Posterior transverse scan of the glenohumeral recess; coronal scan over the acromioclavicular joint.

steps.label: Muscles and limitations
steps.detail: Assess cuff muscle bulk and any paralabral cyst, and state the deep structures not reliably evaluated.

normal.MUSCLES AND LIMITATIONS: Cuff muscle bulk and echogenicity normal; no paralabral cyst. The labrum and deep intra-articular structures are not assessed by ultrasound.

findings: Increased echogenicity and reduced bulk of the [supraspinatus / infraspinatus] (fatty atrophy).
Cyst at the spinoglenoid notch, __ mm; MRI would assess for a labral tear.
Examination limited by [restricted movement / body habitus].
steps.look: Supraspinous and infraspinous fossae in short axis; spinoglenoid notch posteriorly.

protocol: Record the CT and MRI examinations actually reviewed, coverage, reconstruction planes, image quality and comparison. Review CT bone and soft-tissue reconstructions with sagittal and coronal reformats for traumatic alignment and fracture morphology.

When MRI is acquired, review sagittal T1, T2/fluid-sensitive and targeted axial images for ligament, disc, epidural and neural injury. State when MRI was not acquired or is limited; CT alone does not directly establish ligament continuity or spinal cord signal.
Document vertebral numbering, transitional anatomy and any unexamined spinal segment. Review all included levels for additional injuries and identify an ankylosed spine or previous instrumentation.

checklist.label: Numbering and traumatic alignment
checklist.detail: Name the vertebra or motion segment and assess translation, rotation, distraction and focal angulation; document numbering and coverage limits.

checklist.label: Vertebral fracture morphology
checklist.detail: Map vertebral-body walls, one or both endplates and each posterior element. Distinguish compression/burst morphology, posterior-wall retropulsion and a transosseous distraction pattern. Note relevant bone or marrow abnormality and fracture-age evidence using the acquired modality and comparison.

checklist.label: Posterior tension band
checklist.detail: Assess spinous/interspinous and facet relationships on CT. On acquired MRI, assess supraspinous and interspinous ligaments, ligamenta flava and facet capsules separately; distinguish definite disruption from indeterminate oedema.

checklist.label: Discs and longitudinal ligaments
checklist.detail: Assess traumatic disc-space widening or disruption, endplate interfaces and anterior/posterior longitudinal ligaments with the available modality, including anterior distraction in a rigid spine.

checklist.label: Canal, epidural and neural structures
checklist.detail: Localise canal, lateral-recess or foraminal encroachment and epidural abnormality. On acquired MRI, describe cord, conus, cauda equina and named root compression or signal abnormality within coverage.

checklist.label: Paraspinal and associated injury
checklist.detail: Describe paraspinal or prevertebral soft-tissue injury, additional included fractures, postoperative limitations and other relevant visible abnormalities.

checklist.label: Classification inputs and clinical neurology
checklist.detail: Keep imaging morphology and posterior ligamentous complex assessment separate from supplied clinical neurological status. Name the applicable AO/TLICS assessment and document missing clinical information.

measurements.name: Vertebral deformity
measurements.method: At each injured level, describe vertebral height loss and local angulation with the measured surfaces, plane and comparison reference.
measurements.pitfall: Height loss or angulation alone does not determine ligament integrity, neurological status or treatment.

measurements.name: Retropulsion and canal encroachment
measurements.method: Measure posterior-wall retropulsion in mm on a stated plane/reference. If canal narrowing is quantified, identify the diameter or area method and reference level; describe the actual compartment affected.
measurements.pitfall: Do not interchange diameter and area percentages or infer clinical cord injury from osseous canal narrowing.

measurements.name: Distraction and displacement
measurements.method: Record translation, interspinous/facet separation or disc-space opening at the named motion segment, with direction, plane and relevant measurements.
measurements.pitfall: Positioning may reduce visible distraction, especially in an ankylosed spine. A vertical laminar fracture alone does not establish posterior tension-band failure.

classification.name: AO Spine thoracolumbar injury classification / TLICS
classification.version: AO Spine thoracolumbar morphology, neurology and modifiers framework (2013); TLICS (2005)
classification.applicability: Traumatic thoracic/lumbar vertebral or motion-segment injury. Classify each injured level or segment separately using the applicable framework.
classification.summary: AO morphology distinguishes compression, tension-band and translational patterns. TLICS uses morphology, posterior ligamentous complex integrity and clinical neurology. Record uncertainty and supplied clinical modifiers; do not fabricate a complete score from imaging alone or turn a label into an automatic treatment recommendation.

pitfalls: A burst fracture requires posterior vertebral-wall involvement; record which endplate or endplates are involved rather than calling every wedge deformity a burst injury.
A vertical laminar fracture accompanying compression does not by itself prove posterior tension-band failure. Assess the entire injury pattern.
MRI oedema without convincing fibre discontinuity can leave posterior ligamentous complex injury indeterminate; signal change alone must not be labelled a definite rupture.
Small anterior separation in an ankylosed spine may conceal a consequential distraction injury. Report the rigid-spine context and acquisition limitations.
Normal-appearing neural structures on imaging do not supply a clinical neurological examination. Unknown neurological status is not an intact examination.
impression_prompts: Which vertebrae or motion segments are injured, with what compression, distraction or translational morphology?
What is the evidence and certainty of posterior or anterior tension-band injury, and is further soft-tissue assessment unresolved?
What canal, epidural or neural consequence requires communication, and which clinical classification inputs or coverage remain unavailable?
escalation: Promptly communicate traumatic malalignment, suspected consequential tension-band disruption, significant canal compromise or an epidural collection with neural compression through the local trauma/spine pathway.
Report imaging/clinical neurological discordance or an incompletely assessed injury in an ankylosed spine for timely specialist correlation; do not infer clinical neurological status from the images.

steps.label: Level and alignment
steps.detail: Identify each injured level and describe kyphosis, translation or rotation.

normal.NUMBERING, COVERAGE AND ALIGNMENT: Normal thoracolumbar alignment without kyphosis or translation.

findings: Fracture of [ ], counted from [ ].
Local kyphosis of __° at [ ] ([method]).
Translation of __ mm of [ ] on [ ] (translation or rotation injury).
steps.look: Sagittal CT reformats for alignment and kyphosis; count from a documented reference and correlate ribs and transverse processes.
steps.tip: Translation or rotation in any plane indicates a type C injury, whatever the vertebral body looks like.

steps.label: Fracture morphology
steps.detail: Classify the vertebral body injury as compression, split, incomplete or complete burst, and assess the posterior wall.
findings: Wedge compression fracture of [ ] (AO A1) with __% anterior height loss; posterior wall intact.
Split fracture of [ ] (AO A2).
Incomplete burst fracture of [ ] (AO A3): one endplate and the posterior wall involved.
Complete burst fracture of [ ] (AO A4): both endplates and the posterior wall involved, with retropulsion.
steps.look: Sagittal and axial CT: anterior column, each endplate and the posterior wall.
steps.tip: Posterior wall involvement separates a burst fracture from a compression fracture; check it on axial and sagittal images.

steps.label: Posterior ligamentous complex
steps.detail: Assess interspinous widening, facet diastasis or dislocation, horizontal posterior element fractures and MRI ligament signal.

normal.POSTERIOR TENSION BAND: Posterior ligamentous complex intact: no interspinous widening, facet malalignment or posterior element fracture.

findings: Interspinous widening and facet diastasis at [ ], compatible with posterior tension-band disruption (AO B2).
Horizontal fracture through the spinous process, laminae and pedicles (Chance-type, AO B1).
Anterior tension-band (hyperextension) injury with anterior disc space widening (AO B3).
MRI: disrupted supraspinous and interspinous ligaments with fluid signal.
steps.look: CT for interspinous distance, facet alignment and posterior element fractures; MRI fluid-sensitive sagittal images for supraspinous and interspinous ligaments and ligamentum flavum.
steps.tip: A perched or jumped facet is a translation injury; do not classify it by vertebral body morphology alone.

protocol: Record activity change, focal pain site and risk context; review radiographs before targeted MRI.
Use T1 and fluid-sensitive MRI to look for a fracture line and associated marrow/periosteal change; CT may clarify cortical or trabecular fracture anatomy.

checklist.label: Site And Side
checklist.detail: Identify the exact bone and surface, including tension versus compression side where applicable.

checklist.label: Fracture Line
checklist.detail: Look for a cortical or trabecular fracture line and displacement.

checklist.label: Marrow And Periosteum
checklist.detail: Separate fluid-sensitive oedema from T1 marrow abnormality and periosteal reaction.

checklist.label: Articular And Soft Tissues
checklist.detail: Assess joint surface, associated collapse and adjacent tissue.

checklist.label: Comparison And Differential
checklist.detail: Compare evolution and consider insufficiency, infection or another lesion when atypical.

measurements.name: Fracture extent
measurements.method: Record visible line length and displacement; separate it from the oedema envelope.
measurements.pitfall: A normal early radiograph does not exclude a stress injury.

measurements.name: MRI severity description
measurements.method: Record periosteal oedema, marrow oedema, T1 change and visible fracture line.
measurements.pitfall: Do not apply a site-specific grading system to a different bone without stating its limits.

pitfalls: Stress response without a visible line and a completed fracture have different imaging appearances.
An atypical focal lesion warrants assessment beyond exercise-related stress injury.
impression_prompts: Is there a fracture line or only stress-related oedema?
Is the site or surface at higher risk of displacement or delayed healing?
Is there interval progression, collapse or healing?
escalation: Promptly communicate a femoral-neck tension-side injury, displaced fracture or other high-risk stress fracture.

steps.detail: Identify the exact bone and surface, including the tension or compression side where it matters.
findings: Stress injury of the posteromedial tibial cortex (lower-risk site).
Stress injury on the tension (superolateral) side of the femoral neck (high-risk site).
Navicular stress fracture in the central third (high-risk site).
steps.look: Radiographs and coronal and axial MRI for the exact bone and cortex involved.
steps.tip: High-risk sites — femoral neck tension side, anterior tibial cortex, navicular, proximal fifth metatarsal and sesamoids — warrant prompt communication.

steps.label: Fracture line
steps.detail: Look for a cortical or trabecular fracture line and any displacement.
findings: Linear T1-hypointense fracture line extending __ mm into the [ ] without displacement.
Horizontal lucent line in the anterior tibial cortex.
Complete fracture with __ mm displacement.
steps.look: T1 and fluid-sensitive images for a low-signal line; CT or radiographs for a cortical line such as the anterior tibial "dreaded black line".

steps.label: Marrow and periosteum
steps.detail: Separate periosteal oedema, marrow oedema and T1 marrow change, and note periosteal new bone.
findings: Periosteal oedema without marrow oedema (early stress reaction).
Periosteal and marrow oedema with T1 marrow change, without a fracture line.
Solid periosteal new bone and callus on radiographs.
steps.look: Fluid-sensitive images for periosteal and marrow oedema; T1 images for marrow change; radiographs for callus.
steps.tip: Periosteal oedema alone is the earliest MRI finding; T1 marrow change and a visible line indicate a more advanced injury.

steps.label: Articular surface and soft tissues
steps.detail: Assess joint surface extension, collapse, effusion and adjacent soft tissues.

findings: Subchondral insufficiency fracture of the [femoral head / tibial plateau] with [no / __ mm] collapse.
Joint effusion.
Adjacent soft-tissue oedema.
steps.look: Coronal and sagittal images through the adjacent joint.

steps.label: Comparison and differential

steps.look: Prior radiographs and MRI; in an older patient or unusual site, consider insufficiency and an underlying lesion.

protocol: Confirm indication, side, target and consent; review allergy, infection and bleeding-risk context under the local procedure protocol.
Use an aseptic technique and a sonographically identified needle path that avoids vessels, nerves and tendons. Keep the needle tip visible during advancement.

checklist.label: Target And Preprocedure Survey
checklist.detail: Confirm the named joint or bursa and assess fluid, anatomy and access.

checklist.label: Technique
checklist.detail: Document patient position, sterile preparation and needle approach.

checklist.label: Needle Tip And Delivery
checklist.detail: Confirm tip location and observed spread in the intended compartment.

checklist.label: Aspiration If Performed
checklist.detail: Record aspirated amount and appearance and specimens actually submitted.

checklist.label: Outcome And Aftercare
checklist.detail: Describe tolerance, immediate complication and documented aftercare.

measurements.name: Fluid and injectate
measurements.method: Record the exact volume aspirated and the actual agent, concentration and volume delivered.
measurements.pitfall: Do not copy dose or volume from a teaching example; use the prescribed local protocol.

measurements.name: Saved documentation
measurements.method: Retain an image showing the needle tip within the intended target and document spread.
measurements.pitfall: A bright needle shaft alone does not establish tip position.

pitfalls: Confirm whether the intended target is intra-articular, bursal or tendon sheath; these are not interchangeable.
Avoid interpreting a technical injection as proof that the target is the sole pain generator.
impression_prompts: Was the intended compartment accessed successfully?
What was aspirated or administered?
Was there any immediate complication or incomplete delivery?
escalation: Communicate unexpected purulent aspirate or a procedure complication through the local urgent pathway.
