steps.label: Target and preprocedure survey
steps.detail: Confirm the named joint or bursa and assess fluid, anatomy and a safe route.

normal.TARGET AND PREPROCEDURE SURVEY: Target identified on ultrasound; planned route clear of vessels, nerves and tendons on Doppler.

findings: Glenohumeral effusion of __ mm in the posterior recess; posterior approach selected.
Distended subacromial–subdeltoid bursa; lateral approach selected.
Vessel on the anterior approach on Doppler; alternative route chosen.
steps.look: Scan the target in two planes and use Doppler along the planned path; identify tendons and nerves to avoid.
steps.tip: Confirm side and target at the time-out before skin preparation.

steps.label: Technique
steps.detail: Document patient position, sterile preparation, needle approach and local anaesthesia.

normal.TECHNIQUE: Aseptic technique with sterile probe cover and gel; in-plane needle approach under continuous ultrasound guidance.

findings: Patient [supine / lateral decubitus / prone]; [anterior / posterior / lateral] approach.
__ G, __ mm needle; local anaesthesia with __ mL of [agent, concentration].
steps.look: Record position, approach (in-plane or out-of-plane), needle and anaesthetic actually used.

steps.label: Needle tip and delivery
steps.detail: Confirm the needle tip location and the spread observed in the intended compartment.

normal.NEEDLE TIP AND DELIVERY: Needle tip confirmed within the target; injectate seen distending the intended compartment; image saved.

findings: Injected: __ mL of [corticosteroid, dose] with __ mL of [local anaesthetic, concentration].
Extra-articular spread observed; needle repositioned before completing the injection.
steps.look: Keep the needle tip visible; confirm intra-articular or intrabursal spread in real time and save an image.

steps.label: Aspiration
steps.detail: Record the amount and appearance of any aspirate and the specimens actually sent.
findings: __ mL of [clear / straw-coloured / turbid / blood-stained / purulent] fluid aspirated.
Sent for [cell count, Gram stain and culture / crystal analysis] to [laboratory].
steps.look: Aspirate before injecting when fluid is present; note volume and appearance.
steps.tip: If the aspirate looks purulent, follow the local septic-joint pathway before any corticosteroid injection.

steps.label: Outcome and aftercare
steps.detail: Describe tolerance, immediate complication and the aftercare advice given.

normal.OUTCOME AND AFTERCARE: Procedure well tolerated; no immediate complication; aftercare advice given.

findings: Immediate pain relief after local anaesthetic (diagnostic response).
Vasovagal reaction, resolved with [ ].
Advised to seek urgent review for increasing pain, redness, swelling or fever.
steps.look: Record the immediate response and any complication before the patient leaves.

measurements.name: Scapholunate relationship
measurements.method: Measure interval on PA and angle on a true lateral; name the projection and landmarks.
measurements.pitfall: Rotation can mimic widening or abnormal angles.

measurements.name: Carpal alignment
measurements.method: Describe lunate and capitate position even when angles cannot be measured reliably.
measurements.pitfall: A single sign should be interpreted with all alignment relationships.

pitfalls: A normal neutral view does not exclude dynamic instability.
Do not report a lunate dislocation as a perilunate dislocation; specify which bone remains aligned with the radius.
impression_prompts: Is instability static or demonstrated only on stress views?
What is the direction and level of malalignment?
Is there associated fracture, collapse or arthrosis?
escalation: Immediately communicate an acute lunate or perilunate dislocation.

notes: Replace bracketed choices with observed findings. The gallery contains published teaching examples; cite the patient examination series and image numbers in the clinical report.

steps.label: Carpal arcs (Gilula's lines)
steps.detail: Trace all three carpal arcs and check that the intercarpal joint spaces are parallel and symmetric.

normal.CARPAL ARCS: Gilula's three carpal arcs are smooth and uninterrupted; intercarpal joint spaces are parallel and symmetric.

findings: Scapholunate interval widened to __ mm on the PA view, compatible with scapholunate ligament injury.
Break in arcs 1 and 2 at the lunate with a triangular lunate on the PA view (lunate or perilunate dislocation).
Scaphoid ring sign with a foreshortened scaphoid, indicating rotatory subluxation.
steps.look: Neutral PA view: arc 1 along the proximal surfaces of the proximal row, arc 2 along its distal surfaces, arc 3 along the proximal capitate and hamate; intercarpal spaces normally about 1–2 mm.
steps.tip: Compare the scapholunate interval with the other intercarpal spaces; clenched-fist views can unmask a dynamic injury.

steps.label: Lateral alignment
steps.detail: Assess the radius–lunate–capitate relationship on a true lateral view.

normal.LATERAL ALIGNMENT: Radius, lunate and capitate are collinear on the true lateral view.

findings: Perilunate dislocation: the lunate stays aligned with the radius while the capitate is dislocated dorsally.
Lunate dislocation: the lunate is tipped volarly out of the radial fossa while the capitate stays aligned with the radius.
Dorsal tilt of the lunate with a volar-flexed scaphoid (DISI pattern).
steps.look: True lateral (pisiform over the distal scaphoid pole): radius, lunate and capitate should be collinear.
steps.tip: State which bone stays aligned with the radius: the lunate in perilunate dislocation, the capitate in lunate dislocation.

steps.label: Carpal angles
steps.detail: Measure the axes with stated landmarks and describe a DISI or VISI pattern where supported.

normal.CARPAL ANGLES: Scapholunate and capitolunate angles within normal limits; no DISI or VISI pattern.

findings: Scapholunate angle __° (above 60°) with dorsal lunate tilt: DISI.
Scapholunate angle __° (below 30°) with volar lunate tilt: VISI.
Angles not reliably measurable because of [rotation / cast].
steps.look: True lateral: scaphoid axis along its volar poles, lunate axis perpendicular to the line joining its horns, and the capitate and radius axes.
steps.tip: The normal scapholunate angle is about 30–60°; angles need a true lateral projection.

steps.label: Bones
steps.detail: Inspect for associated carpal or distal forearm fracture and chronic collapse.

normal.BONES: No carpal or distal forearm fracture; scaphoid and lunate normal in shape and density.

findings: Scaphoid waist fracture [displaced __ mm / with humpback deformity].
Scaphoid non-union with sclerosis and cysts; proximal pole sclerosis raises concern for osteonecrosis.
Increased density and collapse of the lunate (Kienböck disease).
steps.look: Scaphoid views for waist fractures; lunate density; distal radius and ulnar styloid.

steps.label: Degenerative and dynamic findings
steps.detail: Map arthrosis and compare neutral with stress views.

normal.DEGENERATIVE AND DYNAMIC FINDINGS: No arthrosis; no dynamic change on stress views, or stress views not acquired.

findings: Scapholunate advanced collapse (SLAC) pattern: radial styloid–scaphoid then capitolunate arthrosis, with the radiolunate joint preserved.
Scapholunate interval widens from __ mm to __ mm on the clenched-fist view (dynamic instability).
Scaphoid non-union advanced collapse (SNAC) pattern.
steps.look: PA and lateral for radioscaphoid and capitolunate arthrosis; clenched-fist or deviation views when acquired.

structure_atlas.alt: Normal TFCC composite with labeled anatomical drawings above three coronal, sagittal and axial proton-density fat-suppressed MR panels.
structure_atlas.caption: Normal TFCC anatomy. a Posteroanterior and ( b ) axial diagrams. The TFCC comprises the triangular fibrocartilage (TFC) proper, dorsal and volar DRULs, ulnocarpal ligaments (UL, UT, and ulnocapitate [UC]), UMH, and the ECU subsheath. c Sagittal diagram of the TFC proper and DRUL with capsular attachments (arrows). d Vascular supply: the ulnar artery (UA) and palmar (PAIA) and dorsal (DAIA) branches of the anterior interosseous artery perfuse the peripheral TFCC; the central TFC proper is avascular. e Coronal proton-density fat-suppressed MRI demonstrates the radial and ulnar insertions, including styloid and foveal laminae (arrows), the UMH (arrowhead), and the prestyloid recess (asterisk). f Sagittal proton-density fat-suppressed MRI depicts the TFC proper, volar, and dorsal DRUL with capsular attachments (arrows) and the UT ligament (arrowhead). g Axial proton-density fat-suppressed MRI delineates the DRUL with its capsular attachment (arrows) and the ECU subsheath (arrowhead)
structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Normal TFCC anatomy. a Posteroanterior and ( b ) axial diagrams. The TFCC comprises the triangular fibrocartilage (TFC) proper, dorsal and volar DRULs, ulnocarpal ligaments (UL, UT, and ulnocapitate [UC]), UMH, and the ECU subsheath. c Sagittal diagram of the TFC proper and DRUL with capsular attachments (arrows). d Vascular supply: the ulnar artery (UA) and palmar (PAIA) and dorsal (DAIA) branches of the anterior interosseous artery perfuse the peripheral TFCC; the central TFC proper is avascular. e Coronal proton-density fat-suppressed MRI demonstrates the radial and ulnar insertions, including styloid and foveal laminae (arrows), the UMH (arrowhead), and the prestyloid recess (asterisk). f Sagittal proton-density fat-suppressed MRI depicts the TFC proper, volar, and dorsal DRUL with capsular attachments (arrows) and the UT ligament (arrowhead). g Axial proton-density fat-suppressed MRI delineates the DRUL with its capsular attachment (arrows) and the ECU subsheath (arrowhead)

protocol: Check PA, lateral and appropriate oblique views with injury location; use CT to define complex articular anatomy when acquired.

checklist.label: Fracture Morphology
checklist.detail: Identify bone, level, articular extension and comminution.

checklist.label: Displacement
checklist.detail: Describe angulation, translation and shortening using clear direction.

checklist.label: Articular Surface
checklist.detail: Assess radiocarpal and distal radioulnar articular congruity.

checklist.label: Carpal Alignment
checklist.detail: Assess fracture-associated subluxation, carpal arcs and ligamentous avulsion clues.

checklist.label: Reduction And Soft Tissues
checklist.detail: Describe interval reduction, fixation and surrounding swelling.

measurements.name: Distal radius alignment
measurements.method: Measure tilt on a true lateral and inclination/height on PA, naming the projection.
measurements.pitfall: Apparent change can result from rotation or beam angle.

measurements.name: Articular incongruity
measurements.method: Measure maximal step and gap on the best projection or CT plane.
measurements.pitfall: Do not claim precise articular congruity when overlap or a cast obscures the surface.

pitfalls: A negative initial radiograph does not exclude an occult carpal fracture when clinical suspicion remains.
Describe morphology and displacement even when using an eponym or classification.
impression_prompts: Is the fracture articular and how displaced is it?
Is radiocarpal or DRUJ alignment disrupted?
Is reduction improved and what residual deformity remains?
escalation: Promptly communicate fracture-dislocation or severe malalignment requiring urgent clinical assessment.

steps.label: Fracture morphology
steps.detail: Identify the bone, level, articular extension and comminution.

normal.FRACTURE MORPHOLOGY: No fracture of the distal radius, ulna or carpal bones.

findings: Extra-articular distal radius fracture __ cm proximal to the articular surface with dorsal angulation (Colles type).
Intra-articular distal radius fracture extending to the radiocarpal joint [and distal radioulnar joint], with comminution.
Ulnar styloid [tip / base] fracture.
Torus (buckle) fracture of the distal radial metaphysis.
steps.look: PA, lateral and oblique views: distal radius, ulnar styloid, then each carpal bone — scaphoid first.
steps.tip: Eponyms are optional; direction of displacement and articular involvement are what matter.

steps.label: Displacement
steps.detail: Describe angulation, translation and shortening with clear directions.

normal.DISPLACEMENT: Normal radial inclination, radial height and palmar tilt; no shortening.

findings: Dorsal tilt of __° (normal palmar tilt about 11°); radial inclination __°; radial height __ mm.
Dorsal translation of __ mm and radial shortening with positive ulnar variance of __ mm.
Volar displacement of the distal fragment (Smith type).
steps.look: True lateral for palmar or dorsal tilt; PA for radial inclination, radial height and ulnar variance.
steps.tip: Radial shortening over 3 mm, dorsal tilt beyond 10° or an articular step over 2 mm are commonly used thresholds for unacceptable alignment.

steps.label: Articular surface
steps.detail: Assess radiocarpal and distal radioulnar congruity.

normal.ARTICULAR SURFACE: Radiocarpal and distal radioulnar articular surfaces congruent.

findings: Articular step of __ mm and gap of __ mm at the [scaphoid / lunate] fossa.
Depressed lunate facet (die-punch) fragment, __ mm.
[Volar / dorsal] rim fracture with carpal subluxation (Barton type).
Radial styloid fracture extending to the scaphoid fossa.
steps.look: Lateral and PA views for step and gap; CT for a depressed lunate facet and sigmoid notch involvement.

steps.label: Carpal alignment
steps.detail: Assess fracture-associated subluxation, the carpal arcs and ligamentous avulsion clues.

normal.CARPAL ALIGNMENT: Carpal alignment normal; scapholunate interval normal.

findings: Associated scapholunate widening of __ mm.
Perilunate instability pattern with a [trans-scaphoid] fracture.
Dorsal triquetral avulsion fracture on the lateral view.
steps.look: Carpal arcs on the PA view; lunate and capitate alignment on the lateral; scapholunate interval.
steps.tip: A dorsal flake behind the proximal carpal row on the lateral view is usually a triquetral avulsion.

steps.label: Reduction and soft tissues
steps.detail: Describe interval reduction, fixation and soft-tissue swelling.

normal.REDUCTION AND SOFT TISSUES: Soft tissues otherwise unremarkable; no cast or fixation.

findings: Post-reduction: dorsal tilt improved from __° to __°; radial height __ mm.
Volar plate fixation with screws [not] penetrating the radiocarpal joint.
Loss of reduction since [date].
steps.look: Compare with the pre-reduction film, including cast and fixation.

structure_atlas.caption: A 32-year-old male healthy volunteer ( a , b ), a 22-year-old male healthy volunteer ( c , d ), and a 27-year-old female healthy volunteer ( e , f ). a A 7 T 0.5-mm-thick coronal 3D PD TSE section and ( b ) a 3 T 0.5-mm-thick coronal 3D PD SPACE section with a depiction of the ulnar styloid attachment (arrowheads), the foveal attachment (arrow), and the radial attachment (arrowhead) of the TFCC. c A 7 T 0.5-mm-thick axial 3D PD TSE section and ( d ) a 3 T 0.5-mm-thick axial 3D PD SPACE section with visualization of the dorsal portion (arrow), and the palmar portion (arrowhead) of the SLL. e A 7 T 0.5-mm-thick coronal 3D PD TSE section and ( f ) a 3 T 0.5-mm-thick coronal 3D PD SPACE section depicts the dorsal portion of the SLL (arrowheads). 3D, three-dimensional; PD, proton density; S, scaphoid; SLL, scapholunate ligament; SPACE, “sampling perfection with application-optimized contrasts using different flip angle evolution”; TFCC, triangular fibrocartilage complex; TSE, turbo spin echo

structure_atlas.alt: Normal TFCC composite with labeled anatomical drawings above three coronal, sagittal and axial proton-density fat-suppressed MR panels.
structure_atlas.caption: Normal TFCC anatomy. a Posteroanterior and ( b ) axial diagrams. The TFCC comprises the triangular fibrocartilage (TFC) proper, dorsal and volar DRULs, ulnocarpal ligaments (UL, UT, and ulnocapitate [UC]), UMH, and the ECU subsheath. c Sagittal diagram of the TFC proper and DRUL with capsular attachments (arrows). d Vascular supply: the ulnar artery (UA) and palmar (PAIA) and dorsal (DAIA) branches of the anterior interosseous artery perfuse the peripheral TFCC; the central TFC proper is avascular. e Coronal proton-density fat-suppressed MRI demonstrates the radial and ulnar insertions, including styloid and foveal laminae (arrows), the UMH (arrowhead), and the prestyloid recess (asterisk). f Sagittal proton-density fat-suppressed MRI depicts the TFC proper, volar, and dorsal DRUL with capsular attachments (arrows) and the UT ligament (arrowhead). g Axial proton-density fat-suppressed MRI delineates the DRUL with its capsular attachment (arrows) and the ECU subsheath (arrowhead)
structure_atlas.source_caption_full: Normal TFCC anatomy. a Posteroanterior and ( b ) axial diagrams. The TFCC comprises the triangular fibrocartilage (TFC) proper, dorsal and volar DRULs, ulnocarpal ligaments (UL, UT, and ulnocapitate [UC]), UMH, and the ECU subsheath. c Sagittal diagram of the TFC proper and DRUL with capsular attachments (arrows). d Vascular supply: the ulnar artery (UA) and palmar (PAIA) and dorsal (DAIA) branches of the anterior interosseous artery perfuse the peripheral TFCC; the central TFC proper is avascular. e Coronal proton-density fat-suppressed MRI demonstrates the radial and ulnar insertions, including styloid and foveal laminae (arrows), the UMH (arrowhead), and the prestyloid recess (asterisk). f Sagittal proton-density fat-suppressed MRI depicts the TFC proper, volar, and dorsal DRUL with capsular attachments (arrows) and the UT ligament (arrowhead). g Axial proton-density fat-suppressed MRI delineates the DRUL with its capsular attachment (arrows) and the ECU subsheath (arrowhead)

protocol: Use multiplanar brain images with side markers and anatomic orientation verified. Add angiographic correlation when the question is vascular.
This is a localisation worksheet; select an appropriate disease-specific report for a clinical abnormality.

checklist.label: Surface
checklist.detail: Name lobe, gyrus/sulcus and cortical versus subcortical position.

checklist.label: Deep structures
checklist.detail: Check basal ganglia, thalamus, internal capsule and corpus callosum.

checklist.label: Posterior fossa
checklist.detail: Localise midbrain, pons, medulla, cerebellar hemisphere and peduncles.

checklist.label: Spaces
checklist.detail: Trace ventricles, cisterns, extra-axial spaces and midline relationships.

checklist.label: Supply
checklist.detail: Distinguish arterial territories, border zones and venous drainage without assuming fixed boundaries.

measurements.name: Lesion localisation
measurements.method: Record three orthogonal dimensions and relation to a reproducible landmark.
measurements.pitfall: Anatomic localisation alone does not determine cause.

measurements.name: Midline position
measurements.method: If abnormal, measure perpendicular displacement from the expected midline at a named level in mm.
measurements.pitfall: Oblique reformats or pre-existing asymmetry can mislead.

pitfalls: Vascular territory borders vary with arterial anatomy.
A lesion spanning arterial territories warrants a differential beyond arterial infarction.

steps.label: Cortex and white matter
steps.detail: Name the side, lobe, gyrus or sulcus and cortical, subcortical or deep white matter position.
findings: [Right] [precentral gyrus], cortical and subcortical, anterior to the central sulcus.
Deep white matter of the [left] centrum semiovale.
steps.look: Axial images with sagittal confirmation; find the central sulcus (hand knob, pars marginalis) to separate frontal from parietal lobes.
steps.tip: The hand knob of the precentral gyrus and the pars marginalis of the cingulate sulcus identify the central sulcus.
steps.anatomy_note: Whole hemispheres provide orientation only. Specific gyri, sulci and white-matter regions are not independently identified in this atlas.

steps.label: Deep grey matter and capsules
steps.detail: Localise to the caudate, lentiform nucleus, thalamus, internal capsule limb or corpus callosum segment.
findings: Posterior limb of the [left] internal capsule.
Splenium of the corpus callosum.
[Right] thalamus (posterolateral).
steps.look: Axial images at the level of the foramen of Monro and the thalamus; coronal images.
steps.anatomy_note: The current atlas does not separately represent the deep grey nuclei, internal capsule or corpus callosum. Ventricles must not be used as substitutes for these structures.

steps.label: Brainstem and cerebellum
steps.detail: Localise to midbrain, pons or medulla, and cerebellar hemisphere, vermis or peduncle.
findings: [Left] paramedian pons.
[Right] middle cerebellar peduncle.
Cerebellar vermis.
steps.look: Sagittal and axial images of the posterior fossa; relation to the fourth ventricle.
steps.anatomy_note: Only gross cerebellar and fourth-ventricle context is highlighted. Brainstem subdivisions, cerebellar lobules and peduncles are not separately represented.

steps.label: Ventricles, cisterns and midline
steps.detail: Trace ventricles, cisterns, extra-axial spaces and the midline.

normal.VENTRICLES AND CISTERNS: Ventricles, cisterns and extra-axial spaces normal; midline central.

findings: Midline shift of __ mm to the [left] at the level of the septum pellucidum.
Effacement of the [right] ambient cistern.
steps.look: Ventricular size and symmetry; basal cisterns; midline structures.

steps.label: Vascular territory
steps.detail: Relate the finding to arterial territories, border zones or venous drainage, allowing for variation.
findings: Distribution corresponds to the [left MCA] territory.
Internal border-zone (watershed) distribution.
Distribution does not follow an arterial territory (consider venous or non-vascular causes).
steps.look: Territory maps: ACA medial, MCA lateral, PCA occipital and medial temporal; lenticulostriate deep territory; border zones between them.
steps.tip: Arterial territory boundaries vary between individuals; a lesion crossing territories needs a wider differential.
steps.anatomy_note: Whole hemispheres provide orientation only; these meshes do not define arterial territories, border zones or venous drainage.

source_image.title: Source quantitative MRI and direct model sections
source_image.alt: Native AHEAD group MRI in R1, R2-star and susceptibility contrasts, with direct joint-model section lines for bilateral putamen and pallidal segments.
source_image.caption: Adult group templates, not individual clinical MRI. Twelve median panels: axial, coronal and bilateral sagittal source sections in three quantitative contrasts. Coloured lines intersect the exported joint models directly. Atlas: 97 adults; MRI templates: 105 adults. No fitted alignment or source resampling. Subvoxel interfaces are derived and clinical anatomical accuracy remains unverified.

protocol: Confirm last-known-well, deficit and acquisition times; record noncontrast CT, arch-to-vertex CTA and perfusion or MRI components actually obtained.
For MRI, review DWI with ADC, FLAIR and susceptibility; assess perfusion motion, bolus and coverage before using maps.

checklist.label: Haemorrhage
checklist.detail: Inspect parenchyma, subarachnoid spaces and extra-axial compartments before describing ischaemia.

checklist.label: Parenchyma
checklist.detail: Localise early change or diffusion restriction by side, arterial territory and strategic structures.

checklist.label: Occlusion
checklist.detail: Name artery and segment, tandem cervical disease and distal reconstitution.

checklist.label: Collaterals
checklist.detail: State acquisition type, distribution and delay relative to the opposite side.

checklist.label: Tissue and complications
checklist.detail: Report available core/delay estimates, mass effect, hydrocephalus and relevant alternative diagnoses.

measurements.name: ASPECTS
measurements.method: For an applicable MCA-territory examination, record modality, side and affected regions; score 10 minus affected regions.
measurements.pitfall: Do not apply MCA ASPECTS to posterior circulation or treat a score as an independent treatment decision.

measurements.name: Perfusion volumes
measurements.method: Record software, thresholds, estimated core and delayed tissue in mL, mismatch volume and ratio if valid.
measurements.pitfall: Motion, poor bolus, truncation and reperfusion can invalidate estimates.

classification.name: ASPECTS
classification.version: 10-region MCA score; name CT or DWI application
classification.applicability: Anterior-circulation ischaemic change in the MCA territory.
classification.summary: Record the affected regions with the score. Posterior circulation and perfusion use separate assessments; the score does not alone determine treatment.

pitfalls: A normal early CT does not exclude infarction.
Single-phase CTA may underrepresent delayed collateral filling; describe technique.
Treatment selection depends on the clinical pathway, not a standalone volume or time cutoff.
impression_prompts: Is haemorrhage present, and where?
What artery is occluded and how much established injury is visible?
What critical limitation or urgent complication affects the next decision?
escalation: Immediately communicate acute haemorrhage, large-vessel occlusion or threatening mass effect to the stroke team with time and recipient.

steps.label: Parenchyma and ASPECTS
steps.detail: Look for early ischaemic change and localise it by side, territory and strategic structures; give ASPECTS when applicable.
findings: Loss of the insular ribbon and obscuration of the [left] lentiform nucleus; ASPECTS __ (regions [ ]).
Established hypoattenuation in the [right] MCA territory.
Restricted diffusion in the [ ] with low ADC (acute infarct).
steps.look: Narrow window width (about 30–40 HU) on non-contrast CT: insular ribbon, lentiform nucleus and cortex; DWI with ADC on MRI.
steps.tip: A normal early CT does not exclude infarction; subtle loss of grey–white differentiation needs a narrow window.

steps.label: Haemorrhage
steps.detail: Exclude intracranial haemorrhage in every compartment before treatment decisions.
findings: Acute intraparenchymal haemorrhage in the [ ].
Haemorrhagic transformation of the infarct [petechial / parenchymal haematoma].
Subarachnoid haemorrhage in the [ ].
steps.look: Parenchyma, subarachnoid spaces, ventricles and extra-axial spaces on non-contrast CT or susceptibility MRI.

steps.label: Arterial occlusion
steps.detail: Name the occluded artery and segment, tandem cervical disease and distal reconstitution.

normal.ARTERIAL FINDINGS: No large-vessel occlusion; cervical and intracranial arteries patent.

findings: Occlusion of the [left] M1 segment of the MCA (dense MCA sign on non-contrast CT).
Tandem occlusion: [right] ICA origin and M1.
Basilar artery occlusion.
Cervical ICA dissection with tapered narrowing.
steps.look: CTA from the arch to the vertex; dense artery sign on non-contrast CT.
steps.tip: Look at the cervical arteries too: a tandem ICA lesion changes the endovascular approach.

steps.label: Collaterals and perfusion
steps.detail: Describe collateral filling and, when valid, perfusion core and hypoperfused tissue volumes with the software used.
findings: Good collaterals: filling of more than half of the territory with a one-phase delay.
Poor collaterals with minimal filling.
Perfusion ([software], thresholds [ ]): core __ mL, hypoperfused tissue __ mL, mismatch volume __ mL.
steps.look: Multiphase CTA for delayed collateral filling; perfusion maps checked for motion, bolus and coverage.
steps.tip: Single-phase CTA underestimates delayed collaterals; treatment selection follows the clinical pathway, not a single number.

steps.label: Mass effect and alternative findings
steps.detail: Report oedema, midline shift, cisterns, hydrocephalus and any alternative diagnosis.

normal.MASS EFFECT AND OTHER FINDINGS: No mass effect; no alternative cause for the symptoms.

findings: Malignant oedema with __ mm midline shift and effacement of the basal cisterns.
Cerebellar infarct compressing the fourth ventricle with early hydrocephalus.
Stroke mimic: [tumour / subdural haematoma].
steps.look: Midline, basal cisterns and fourth ventricle (for cerebellar infarcts).

steps.label: Location and compartment
steps.detail: Identify intra-axial, extra-axial, intraventricular or skull-base origin and all involved compartments.
findings: Solitary intra-axial lesion centred in the [right] [frontal] white matter, __ × __ × __ mm.
Extra-axial dural-based mass with a CSF cleft and dural tail (meningioma pattern).
Multiple lesions at the grey–white junction (metastases pattern).
steps.look: Multiplanar images: a CSF cleft, dural tail and buckled grey matter indicate an extra-axial lesion.
steps.tip: First decide intra- or extra-axial; the differential is completely different.

steps.label: Signal and enhancement
steps.detail: Separate enhancing solid tissue, non-enhancing signal abnormality, necrosis, cyst, haemorrhage and calcification.
findings: Thick irregular ring enhancement around central necrosis with surrounding FLAIR signal.
Non-enhancing T2/FLAIR-hyperintense expansile lesion.
Homogeneously enhancing dural-based mass.
Cyst with an enhancing mural nodule.
steps.look: T1, T2/FLAIR, susceptibility and post-contrast T1 in matching planes.

steps.label: Diffusion and perfusion
steps.detail: Describe diffusion and, when acquired, perfusion and spectroscopy in the viable component.
findings: Restricted diffusion in the solid component (highly cellular tumour, e.g., lymphoma).
Restricted diffusion in the cavity with a smooth thin rim (abscess pattern).
Elevated rCBV in the enhancing rim.
steps.look: DWI/ADC of the solid part and cavity; perfusion rCBV in the enhancing rim.
steps.tip: Restricted diffusion in a cavity favours abscess; restricted diffusion in solid tissue suggests a cellular tumour.

steps.label: Extent and dissemination
steps.detail: Assess corpus callosum, deep nuclei and brainstem involvement, dural or skull invasion and ventricular or leptomeningeal spread.

normal.EXTENT AND DISSEMINATION: No callosal, ventricular or leptomeningeal involvement; no additional lesions.

findings: Extension across the corpus callosum to the contralateral hemisphere.
Subependymal enhancement along the ventricles.
Leptomeningeal enhancement in the [ ].
steps.look: Coronal and sagittal post-contrast images; ependymal and leptomeningeal surfaces.

steps.label: Oedema and pressure effect
steps.detail: Report vasogenic oedema, midline shift, cisterns and obstructive hydrocephalus.

normal.OEDEMA AND PRESSURE EFFECT: No significant oedema, mass effect or hydrocephalus.

findings: Vasogenic oedema with __ mm midline shift.
Subfalcine herniation.
Obstructive hydrocephalus at the level of the [foramen of Monro / fourth ventricle].
steps.look: FLAIR extent; midline at the septum pellucidum; ventricular size.

steps.label: Treatment comparison
steps.detail: Compare the same components with the named baseline and describe treatment effect versus progression.
findings: Stable enhancing and non-enhancing components compared with [date].
New enhancing nodule at the resection margin (progression versus treatment effect).
Enhancement within the radiation field with low rCBV, favouring treatment effect.
steps.look: Matched planes and sequences with the post-operative baseline or nadir.
steps.tip: Name the reference study and measure the same component each time.

steps.label: Site and morphology
steps.detail: Identify the side, segment and morphology of narrowing or wall abnormality.

normal.SITE AND MORPHOLOGY: Carotid arteries patent without significant plaque or narrowing.

findings: Calcified / soft plaque at the [right] ICA origin.
Carotid web: shelf-like intraluminal projection along the posterior wall of the ICA bulb.
Floating thrombus in the ICA.
steps.look: CTA or contrast MRA source images and curved reformats along each carotid; Doppler when performed.

steps.label: Residual lumen and distal calibre
steps.detail: Assess the degree of stenosis, near-occlusion and the calibre of the distal ICA.
findings: [Right] ICA stenosis of __% (NASCET).
Near-occlusion: severe stenosis with collapse of the distal ICA (not graded as a percentage).
steps.look: Minimum lumen diameter compared with the normal distal ICA (NASCET method).
steps.tip: Near-occlusion with distal collapse is a separate category; a percentage stenosis is misleading.

steps.label: Occlusion pattern
steps.detail: Describe the stump, length of occlusion and distal reconstitution.
findings: Occlusion of the [left] ICA from the origin with reconstitution of the [petrous / cavernous] segment.
Pseudo-occlusion: slow antegrade filling on delayed images.
steps.look: Delayed images to separate true occlusion from slow flow (pseudo-occlusion).
steps.tip: Slow flow can mimic occlusion on a single early phase; check delayed images.

steps.label: Non-atherosclerotic causes
steps.detail: Look for dissection, fibromuscular dysplasia or other vasculopathy.
findings: Dissection of the [left] ICA with crescentic mural haematoma and tapered narrowing distal to the bulb.
String-of-beads appearance (fibromuscular dysplasia).
steps.look: Crescentic mural haematoma (fat-suppressed T1 on MRI), flap, tapered narrowing sparing the bulb.
steps.tip: Dissection usually spares the bulb and starts 2–3 cm above the bifurcation.

steps.label: Intracranial run-off and comparison
steps.detail: Assess the intracranial vessels within coverage, the contralateral side and interval change.

normal.INTRACRANIAL AND COMPARISON: Normal intracranial run-off; contralateral carotid normal.

findings: Tandem intracranial stenosis of the [ ].
Progression from __% to __% since [date].
steps.look: Circle of Willis collaterals; the prior study.

measurements.name: MTA score
measurements.method: Report right and left 0–4 visual scores on standard coronal T1 planes.
measurements.pitfall: Interpret with age and clinical phenotype; MTA is not specific for Alzheimer disease.

measurements.name: Fazekas score
measurements.method: Record deep/periventricular white-matter burden using the stated visual scale.
measurements.pitfall: FLAIR intensity alone does not establish vascular aetiology.

measurements.name: Microbleeds
measurements.method: Count or describe burden and lobar/deep/infratentorial distribution on the same susceptibility technique.
measurements.pitfall: Different field strength or sequence sensitivity can mimic interval increase.

classification.name: Visual atrophy and white-matter scales
classification.version: MTA 0–4; Fazekas 0–3; name any additional scale
classification.applicability: Descriptive structural MRI assessment in cognitive impairment.
classification.summary: Report individual scores and their anatomic context. They describe burden and pattern; they do not replace clinical diagnosis or biomarker assessment.

pitfalls: An atrophy pattern supports a differential; it does not independently diagnose dementia subtype.
Rapidly progressive symptoms require a different differential even when atrophy is present.

What is the cerebrovascular and haemorrhagic burden?
Is there a structural alternative or urgent finding?
escalation: Escalate acute infarction, mass effect or unexpected rapid-progressive diffusion abnormalities in the clinical context.

steps.label: Global and regional atrophy
steps.detail: Describe global cortical atrophy and any regional predominance, symmetry and age appropriateness.
findings: Global cortical atrophy, GCA [2].
Asymmetric frontal and anterior temporal atrophy (frontotemporal lobar degeneration pattern).
Posterior parietal and precuneus atrophy (Koedam [2]).
steps.look: Axial FLAIR and 3D T1 in three planes; GCA scale 0–3; posterior atrophy (Koedam) on sagittal and coronal images.

steps.label: Medial temporal lobe atrophy
steps.detail: Assess both hippocampi on comparable coronal planes with the MTA score.
findings: MTA right __/4, left __/4 (abnormal for age).
Asymmetric hippocampal atrophy, [left] greater than [right].
steps.look: Coronal T1 through the hippocampal body at the level of the pons.
steps.tip: An MTA score of 2 or more under 75 years, or 3 or more at 75 and above, is usually considered abnormal.

steps.label: Vascular burden
steps.detail: Record white-matter disease (Fazekas), lacunes and strategic or territorial infarcts.

normal.SMALL-VESSEL AND ISCHAEMIC DISEASE: No significant white-matter disease (Fazekas 0–1); no infarcts.

findings: Confluent white-matter hyperintensities, Fazekas 3.
Lacunes in the basal ganglia and thalami.
Strategic infarct in the [left thalamus].
steps.look: FLAIR for white-matter lesions and lacunes; strategic sites: thalamus, caudate, angular gyrus.

steps.label: Microbleeds and siderosis
steps.detail: Describe microbleed number and distribution and cortical superficial siderosis.
findings: __ lobar microbleeds with cortical superficial siderosis (cerebral amyloid angiopathy pattern).
Deep microbleeds in the basal ganglia and pons (hypertensive pattern).
steps.look: Susceptibility-weighted or T2* images.
steps.tip: Lobar microbleeds and superficial siderosis suggest amyloid angiopathy and matter for anti-amyloid treatment eligibility.

steps.label: Treatable and alternative causes
steps.detail: Exclude mass, subdural collection, hydrocephalus, acute diffusion abnormality and other structural causes.

normal.ALTERNATIVE STRUCTURAL CAUSES: No mass, collection, hydrocephalus or diffusion abnormality.

findings: Ventriculomegaly disproportionate to sulcal widening with tight high-convexity sulci (normal pressure hydrocephalus pattern).
Cortical ribbon and deep grey diffusion restriction (Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease pattern).
Chronic subdural haematoma.
steps.look: DWI for cortical ribbon and deep grey restriction; ventricles versus sulci; subdural spaces.
steps.tip: Rapidly progressive symptoms need a different differential, including Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease.

measurements.name: Collection size
measurements.method: Measure three dimensions of drainable-appearing cavity and describe location.
measurements.pitfall: Restricted diffusion and rim enhancement support but do not prove purulence.

measurements.name: Mass effect
measurements.method: Record midline shift in mm and ventricular calibre with prior comparison.
measurements.pitfall: Small strategically located lesions may cause severe obstruction.

pitfalls: Normal imaging does not exclude meningitis.

steps.label: Meningeal and cranial nerve enhancement
steps.detail: Separate pachymeningeal (dural) from leptomeningeal enhancement and note cranial nerve enhancement.

normal.MENINGES AND CRANIAL NERVES: No abnormal meningeal or cranial nerve enhancement.

findings: Smooth diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement (e.g., intracranial hypotension, post-operative).
Nodular leptomeningeal enhancement along the [cerebellar folia / basal cisterns].
Enhancement of the [ ] cranial nerve.
steps.look: Post-contrast FLAIR and T1: dural enhancement follows the inner table; leptomeningeal enhancement enters sulci and cisterns.
steps.tip: Pachymeningeal enhancement follows the skull; leptomeningeal enhancement dips into the sulci.

steps.label: Parenchymal lesions
steps.detail: Characterise the pattern — ring, nodular, gyral, perivascular — with central diffusion and surrounding FLAIR.
findings: Smooth thin ring enhancement with central restricted diffusion (abscess pattern).
Incomplete (open) ring enhancement (demyelination pattern).
Gyral enhancement of the [ ] cortex (subacute infarct / encephalitis).
Punctate and curvilinear perivascular enhancement in the pons (CLIPPERS pattern).
steps.look: Post-contrast T1 with DWI/ADC and FLAIR.
steps.tip: An open ring facing the cortex suggests demyelination; a complete smooth ring with restricted diffusion suggests abscess.

steps.label: Extra-axial collections
steps.detail: Identify subdural or epidural collections, their thickness and diffusion.
findings: Subdural empyema along the [left] convexity, __ mm thick, with restricted diffusion.
Epidural collection adjacent to the [frontal sinus].
steps.look: DWI for empyema; adjacent sinuses and bone.

steps.label: Ventricles and CSF
steps.detail: Inspect ependymal enhancement, intraventricular debris and hydrocephalus.

normal.VENTRICLES AND CSF: No ependymal enhancement, debris or hydrocephalus.

findings: Ependymal enhancement with dependent debris (ventriculitis).
Hydrocephalus with obstruction at the [ ].
steps.look: Dependent layering debris on DWI and FLAIR; ependymal surfaces.

steps.label: Vascular complications and source
steps.detail: Check infarction, haemorrhage and venous or arterial complications, and look for a sinus, mastoid or operative source.

normal.VASCULAR AND SOURCE FINDINGS: No infarct, haemorrhage or vascular complication; no source identified.

findings: Venous sinus thrombosis adjacent to [mastoiditis].
Infarcts from vasculitis in the [ ].
Source: [frontal sinusitis / otomastoiditis / operative bed].
steps.look: Venous sinuses; arteries at the skull base; paranasal sinuses and mastoids.

protocol: Use HARNESS structural sequences: isotropic 3D T1, isotropic 3D FLAIR and high-resolution coronal T2 perpendicular to the hippocampal long axis; add sequences for the clinical question.
Review seizure semiology, EEG localisation and timing of recent seizures; consider age-related myelination when adapting paediatric protocols.

checklist.detail: Compare size, signal, internal architecture and orientation bilaterally.

checklist.label: Cortical development
checklist.detail: Inspect thickness, sulcation, grey-white junction and transmantle signal.

checklist.label: Dual pathology
checklist.detail: Search the entire brain even after detecting hippocampal sclerosis.

checklist.label: Other substrates
checklist.detail: Assess tumour, vascular malformation, gliosis, encephalomalacia and encephalocele.

checklist.label: Concordance
checklist.detail: Describe lesion location relative to supplied electroclinical localisation without inferring causality.

measurements.name: Lesion dimensions
measurements.method: Measure a suspected epileptogenic structural lesion in three planes and identify sequences.
measurements.pitfall: Transient peri-ictal swelling can alter apparent extent.

measurements.name: Hippocampal asymmetry
measurements.method: Use visual comparison or validated volumetry with age-appropriate reference data.
measurements.pitfall: Oblique planes and segmentation errors can create false asymmetry.

classification.name: HARNESS-MRI
classification.applicability: Dedicated structural epilepsy MRI; adapt for infants and specific clinical questions.
classification.summary: A standard acquisition protocol, not a diagnostic severity score. A normal study does not exclude epilepsy.

pitfalls: Normal MRI does not exclude epilepsy or subtle focal cortical dysplasia.
Peri-ictal diffusion and FLAIR change may be reversible; use the clinical timeline.
impression_prompts: Is there a structural lesion plausibly relevant to seizures?
Which side/region and associated second lesion are involved?
Is the examination adequate or is targeted expert review warranted?
escalation: Communicate acute haemorrhage, infarction, encephalitis pattern or a mass with threatening pressure effect.

steps.label: Hippocampi
steps.detail: Compare hippocampal size, signal and internal architecture bilaterally.

normal.MESIAL TEMPORAL STRUCTURES: Hippocampi symmetric with normal size, signal and internal architecture.

findings: [Left] hippocampal sclerosis: volume loss, increased T2/FLAIR signal and loss of internal architecture.
Atrophy of the ipsilateral fornix and mammillary body.
steps.look: High-resolution coronal T2 perpendicular to the hippocampal long axis; 3D FLAIR.
steps.tip: Look at the whole brain even after finding hippocampal sclerosis: dual pathology is common.

steps.label: Cortex and neuronal migration
steps.detail: Inspect cortical thickness, sulcation, grey–white junction, heterotopia and transmantle signal.

normal.CORTEX AND MIGRATION: Normal cortical thickness and grey–white junction; no heterotopia.

findings: Blurring of the grey–white junction with cortical thickening and a transmantle sign in the [right] [frontal] lobe (focal cortical dysplasia type II pattern).
Subependymal nodular heterotopia along the [ ] ventricle.
Polymicrogyria of the [ ].
steps.look: 3D T1 and 3D FLAIR in all planes; compare with the other hemisphere.
steps.tip: The transmantle sign — a funnel of FLAIR signal from the cortex towards the ventricle — indicates focal cortical dysplasia type IIb.

steps.label: Focal lesions
steps.detail: Look for tumours, vascular malformations, gliosis and encephalomalacia.

normal.FOCAL LESIONS: No tumour, vascular malformation or gliosis.

findings: Cavernoma __ mm in the [ ] with a haemosiderin rim.
Cortically based cystic lesion (DNET / ganglioglioma pattern).
Post-traumatic encephalomalacia and gliosis in the [ ].
steps.look: Susceptibility images for cavernomas; post-contrast images when acquired.

steps.label: Temporal encephalocele and dual pathology
steps.detail: Look for temporal encephalocele, prior injury and any second relevant lesion.
findings: Temporal pole encephalocele through a middle cranial fossa defect.
Second lesion: [ ] in addition to hippocampal sclerosis.
steps.look: Coronal and sagittal images of the middle cranial fossa floor.

steps.label: Electroclinical concordance
steps.detail: Relate the lesion to the supplied EEG and semiology localisation without assuming causality, and consider peri-ictal change.

normal.ACUTE AND ELECTROCLINICAL CORRELATION: No peri-ictal change. No structural lesion; this does not exclude epilepsy.

findings: Lesion concordant with the supplied [left temporal] EEG focus.
Transient cortical and hippocampal diffusion and FLAIR change, compatible with peri-ictal change; follow-up to confirm resolution.
steps.look: Supplied EEG and semiology; the timing of the last seizure.
steps.tip: A normal MRI does not exclude epilepsy or subtle focal cortical dysplasia.

notes: A normal CT does not exclude nonhaemorrhagic traumatic brain injury; contusions can evolve on follow-up.

steps.label: Extra-axial haemorrhage
steps.detail: Distinguish epidural, subdural and subarachnoid haemorrhage.
findings: Biconvex epidural haematoma over the [right temporal] convexity, __ mm thick, with an overlying fracture.
Crescentic acute subdural haematoma over the [left] convexity, __ mm thick.
Traumatic subarachnoid haemorrhage in the [ ] sulci.
steps.look: Brain window and a wider subdural window; epidural is biconvex and limited by sutures; subdural is crescentic and crosses sutures.
steps.tip: An epidural haematoma does not cross sutures; a subdural haematoma does not cross the midline.

steps.label: Parenchymal injury
steps.detail: Assess contusions, intraparenchymal haematoma and oedema.
findings: Haemorrhagic contusions of the [inferior frontal / anterior temporal] lobes.
Petechial haemorrhages at the grey–white junction and corpus callosum (diffuse axonal injury pattern).
steps.look: Frontal and temporal poles and inferior surfaces (coup and contrecoup sites).
steps.tip: Contusions often enlarge on early follow-up CT.

steps.label: Ventricles
steps.detail: Identify intraventricular blood and ventricular obstruction.
findings: Intraventricular blood layering in the occipital horns.
Early hydrocephalus.
steps.look: Occipital horns for layering blood; ventricular size.

steps.label: Mass effect
steps.detail: Measure midline shift and assess the basal cisterns and herniation.

normal.MASS EFFECT: No midline shift; basal cisterns patent.

findings: Midline shift of __ mm to the [left].
Effaced basal cisterns with uncal herniation.
Duret haemorrhage in the pons (secondary to descending herniation).
steps.look: Midline shift at the level of the septum pellucidum; ambient and quadrigeminal cisterns.

steps.label: Skull and comparison
steps.detail: Review skull and skull-base fractures, pneumocephalus and interval change.
findings: Fracture of the [right temporal] bone crossing the middle meningeal groove.
Skull-base fracture with pneumocephalus.
Increase in contusion size since [time].
steps.look: Bone window with multiplanar and 3D reformats.

checklist.detail: Count unequivocally new/enlarging T2 lesions and enhancing lesions on comparable studies.

checklist.label: Specificity markers

measurements.name: Interval lesion burden
measurements.method: Record new/enlarged T2 and enhancing lesion counts, locations and comparison date.
measurements.pitfall: Scanner, slice and sequence changes can create false interval activity.

measurements.name: Cord lesion extent
measurements.method: Describe vertebral levels, length in segments and cross-sectional position.
measurements.pitfall: Confluent lesions and artefact can distort apparent length; confirm on axial images.

classification.name: McDonald diagnostic criteria
classification.applicability: Clinical MS diagnostic pathway after appropriate exclusion of alternatives.
classification.summary: The revision includes optic nerve as a fifth topographic region and additional biomarker pathways. Report observed regions and activity; full diagnosis requires the applicable clinical and laboratory criteria.

pitfalls: Nonspecific white-matter foci are not sufficient for MS diagnosis.
A radiology report should describe criteria-relevant evidence, not diagnose MS without the required clinical/laboratory context.
Central-vein and rim markers cannot be assessed on every routine sequence.

Is there new or enhancing activity versus the named comparison?
What missing imaging or atypical feature limits application of diagnostic criteria?
escalation: Escalate unexpected extensive cord disease or a treatment-associated opportunistic-infection pattern to the treating team.

steps.label: Brain lesion distribution
steps.detail: Describe periventricular, cortical or juxtacortical, infratentorial and callosal lesions and their morphology.

normal.BRAIN LESION MAP: No white-matter lesions typical of demyelination.

findings: Ovoid periventricular lesions perpendicular to the lateral ventricles and involving the callosal undersurface.
Juxtacortical lesions in the [ ].
Infratentorial lesions in the [pons / middle cerebellar peduncle].
steps.look: Sagittal 3D FLAIR for callosal lesions; axial FLAIR and T2; lesions perpendicular to the ventricles.
steps.tip: Non-specific punctate white-matter foci are not enough for MS; look for the typical locations and morphology.

steps.label: Spinal cord and optic nerves
steps.detail: Report cord lesions by level, length and axial position, and optic nerve findings when imaged.

normal.CORD AND OPTIC PATHWAYS: Spinal cord and optic nerves not imaged / normal.

findings: Short-segment (under two vertebral segments) peripheral cord lesion at [C3].
Longitudinally extensive cord lesion over __ segments (consider NMOSD or MOGAD).
Optic nerve [T2 signal / enhancement].
steps.look: Sagittal and axial cord images; fat-suppressed coronal optic nerve images.
steps.tip: A longitudinally extensive cord lesion is atypical for MS.
steps.anatomy_note: The brain atlas does not contain the spinal cord or optic nerves. Review those structures on the relevant acquired images.

steps.label: Interval activity
steps.detail: Count unequivocally new or enlarging T2 lesions and enhancing lesions against a named comparison.

normal.INTERVAL ACTIVITY: No new or enlarging T2 lesions and no enhancing lesions compared with [date].

findings: __ new T2 lesions in the [ ] compared with [date].
__ enhancing lesions.
steps.look: Matched FLAIR with the comparison study; post-contrast T1 when given.

steps.label: Central vein sign and rim lesions
steps.detail: Report the central vein sign and paramagnetic rim lesions only when a suitable sequence was acquired.
findings: Central vein sign present in __ of __ assessed lesions.
Paramagnetic rim lesions: [number, sites].
steps.look: Susceptibility-weighted or FLAIR* images.
steps.anatomy_note: Central veins, paramagnetic rims and MS lesions are not represented in this atlas. Ventricular anatomy does not demonstrate these findings.

steps.label: Mimics and atypical features

findings: Punctate subcortical lesions sparing the callosum and periventricular regions (small-vessel pattern).

Area postrema lesion (NMOSD context).
steps.look: Lesion location and shape; diffusion and haemorrhage; cortex and deep grey matter.

steps.label: Gland and lesion epicentre
steps.detail: Identify whether the lesion arises from the gland, stalk or an extrasellar structure, and measure it.

normal.GLAND AND LESION: Normal pituitary gland; no focal lesion.

findings: Microadenoma __ mm in the [right] gland with delayed enhancement.
Macroadenoma __ × __ × __ mm with a snowman (figure-of-eight) configuration.
Non-enhancing midline cyst between the anterior and posterior lobe (Rathke cleft cyst pattern).
steps.look: Small-field coronal and sagittal T1 and T2; dynamic images for microadenoma when acquired.
steps.tip: Find the normal gland first: a lesion separate from the gland is not a pituitary adenoma.

steps.label: Signal and enhancement
steps.detail: Describe T1 and T2 signal, enhancement, haemorrhage, calcification and cystic change.
findings: T1-hyperintense haemorrhage within the macroadenoma (apoplexy in the appropriate clinical setting).
Mixed solid-cystic suprasellar mass with calcification (craniopharyngioma pattern).
Homogeneous enhancement with a dural tail (meningioma pattern).
steps.look: T1 pre-contrast for haemorrhage and proteinaceous content; post-contrast images.

steps.label: Stalk and suprasellar region
steps.detail: Assess stalk position and thickness, posterior pituitary bright spot and suprasellar extension.

normal.STALK AND SUPRASELLAR REGION: Stalk midline and normal in thickness; posterior pituitary bright spot present.

findings: Stalk deviated to the [left].
Thickened stalk __ mm with absent posterior bright spot (germinoma, histiocytosis or hypophysitis to be considered).
Suprasellar extension to the hypothalamus.
steps.look: Sagittal and coronal images of the stalk and hypothalamus.

steps.label: Optic chiasm and nerves
steps.detail: Describe the relationship to the chiasm and optic nerves.
findings: Lesion contacts and elevates the optic chiasm.
Compression of the chiasm with T2 signal change.
steps.look: Coronal T2 through the chiasm.

steps.label: Cavernous sinus and skull base
steps.detail: Describe cavernous sinus invasion, carotid encasement, sellar floor, sphenoid sinus and vascular mimics.

normal.CAVERNOUS SINUS AND SKULL BASE: No cavernous sinus invasion; sellar floor intact; no vascular lesion.

findings: [Right] cavernous sinus invasion with carotid encasement (Knosp grade __).
Erosion of the sellar floor into the sphenoid sinus.

steps.label: Dural sinuses
steps.detail: Assess each named dural sinus for patency or thrombus.
findings: Filling defect in the superior sagittal sinus (empty delta sign) extending to the [right transverse and sigmoid] sinuses.
Hyperdense [left transverse] sinus on non-contrast CT (dense clot sign).
steps.look: Non-contrast CT for dense clot or cord sign; CTV or contrast MRV source images for filling defects and the empty delta sign.
steps.tip: A hypoplastic transverse sinus or arachnoid granulation is a common mimic; check the source images.
steps.anatomy_note: The current brain atlas does not contain the dural venous sinuses.

steps.label: Deep and cortical veins
steps.detail: Inspect the deep venous system and cortical veins.
findings: Thrombosis of the internal cerebral veins and straight sinus.
Isolated cortical vein thrombosis (cord sign / susceptibility blooming).
steps.look: Internal cerebral veins, vein of Galen and straight sinus; cortical veins on susceptibility images.
steps.anatomy_note: Deep and cortical veins are not represented in this atlas. Ventricles are not venous structures.

steps.label: Parenchymal effects
steps.detail: Assess oedema, venous infarction and haemorrhage that do not follow arterial territories.

normal.PARENCHYMAL EFFECTS: No parenchymal oedema, infarction or haemorrhage.

findings: Venous oedema / infarction in the [ ] crossing arterial territories.
Bilateral thalamic oedema (deep venous thrombosis).
Haemorrhagic venous infarct __ mm.
steps.look: FLAIR and DWI; susceptibility for haemorrhage.
steps.tip: Parenchymal change that does not match an arterial territory, especially with haemorrhage, should prompt venous imaging.

steps.label: Mass effect
steps.detail: Review swelling, ventricles and herniation.
findings: Swelling with __ mm midline shift.
Effaced basal cisterns.
steps.look: Midline, ventricles and basal cisterns.

steps.label: Mimics and comparison
steps.detail: Distinguish hypoplasia, arachnoid granulations and technical signal loss, and compare patency over time.
findings: Hypoplastic [left] transverse sinus without thrombus.
Arachnoid granulation: rounded CSF-density filling defect.
Partial recanalisation since [date].
steps.look: Contrast-enhanced source images rather than time-of-flight alone.
steps.tip: Time-of-flight signal loss alone is not evidence of thrombosis.
steps.anatomy_note: Venous variants and flow-related mimics are not represented in this anatomical atlas.

findings: Anterolisthesis of [C5] on [C6] by __ mm.
Widened basion–dens interval (atlanto-occipital dissociation to be considered).
Loss of the spinolaminar line at [ ].

steps.label: Fractures
steps.detail: Describe fracture level, morphology, displacement and posterior element involvement.
findings: Type [II] odontoid fracture with __ mm displacement.
Bilateral C2 pars fractures (hangman fracture).
Jefferson fracture of the C1 ring with lateral mass offset.
Flexion teardrop fracture of [C5].
steps.look: Axial, sagittal and coronal CT; C1 ring, odontoid, C2 pars and each subaxial level.

steps.label: Facet joints and ligaments
steps.detail: Assess the facets and signs of ligament disruption.

normal.JOINTS AND LIGAMENTS: Facets aligned; no evidence of ligament injury.

findings: Unilateral facet dislocation at [C5–C6] on the [right] (perched / locked).
Bilateral facet dislocation at [ ].
MRI: disruption of the posterior ligamentous complex / anterior longitudinal ligament.
steps.look: Sagittal images through each facet column; MRI STIR for ligaments when acquired.
steps.tip: A jumped facet appears as a "naked facet" on axial images and as a locked facet on the sagittal facet column.

steps.label: Canal and cord
steps.detail: Describe canal compromise and cord signal when MRI is available.

findings: Retropulsed fragment narrowing the canal to __ mm.
Cord oedema from [C4] to [C6] [with haemorrhage].
Epidural haematoma compressing the cord.
steps.look: Axial CT for bone fragments in the canal; sagittal MRI T2 and STIR for the cord.

findings: Prevertebral soft-tissue swelling at [C2–C6].
Fracture through the [right] foramen transversarium: vertebral artery injury should be assessed with CTA.
Associated injury: [ ].
steps.look: Prevertebral soft tissue thickness; foramina transversaria; other injuries.
steps.tip: A fracture through the foramen transversarium or a subluxation should prompt vertebral artery assessment.

steps.label: Discs

normal.DISCS: Discs normal in height and signal; no herniation.

findings: [L4–L5]: [right paracentral] protrusion.

Sequestrated fragment behind the [L5] body.
Modic type [1] endplate changes at [ ].
steps.look: Sagittal and axial T2 at each level: bulge (over 25% of the circumference), protrusion, extrusion or sequestration.

steps.label: Central canal and lateral recesses

steps.look: Axial T2 at disc level; follow each traversing root in the lateral recess.

steps.label: Foramina and extraforaminal zone

findings: [Left] foraminal herniation at [L4–L5] compressing the exiting [L4] root.
Severe [right] foraminal stenosis at [L5–S1].
steps.look: Sagittal images through the foramina; axial images lateral to the pedicles.

findings: Severe canal stenosis with crowding of the cauda equina.
Synovial cyst from the [right L4–L5] facet.
Epidural lipomatosis.
steps.look: Sagittal T2 to the conus; axial images of the facets.

steps.label: Compression
steps.detail: First exclude extrinsic cord compression and canal disease.
findings: Cord compression at [C5–C6] by disc–osteophyte complex with cord signal change (compressive myelopathy).
Epidural mass compressing the cord at [ ].
steps.look: Sagittal T2 and axial images at every narrowed level.
steps.tip: Always exclude compression before considering an intrinsic cord disease.

steps.label: Longitudinal extent
steps.detail: Map cord signal by level and length.
findings: Short-segment lesion (under two vertebral segments) at [ ].
Longitudinally extensive lesion from [ ] to [ ] (three or more segments).
Multifocal cord lesions.
steps.look: Sagittal T2 and STIR; count vertebral segments.
steps.tip: Short peripheral lesions suggest MS; longitudinally extensive central lesions suggest NMOSD, MOGAD, ADEM or other causes.

steps.label: Axial pattern
steps.detail: Assess axial location and the proportion of the cord involved.
findings: Peripheral, dorsolateral lesion involving less than half of the cross-section (MS pattern).
Central grey matter involvement (owl-eye pattern: infarction, MOGAD).
Symmetric dorsal column involvement (metabolic pattern, e.g., B12 deficiency).
steps.look: Axial T2 through each lesion.

steps.label: Calibre and enhancement
steps.detail: Assess cord expansion, atrophy and enhancement.
findings: Cord expansion with heterogeneous enhancement (tumour pattern).
Patchy enhancement of the lesion.
Cord atrophy at [ ].
steps.look: Sagittal and axial post-contrast T1.

steps.label: Associated findings
steps.detail: Inspect perimedullary vessels, the conus and relevant brain findings.

normal.ASSOCIATED FINDINGS: No abnormal perimedullary vessels; conus normal.

findings: Dilated perimedullary veins on the dorsal cord with conus oedema (spinal dural arteriovenous fistula pattern).
Brain lesions typical of demyelination.
steps.look: Dorsal surface of the cord for flow voids; brain if imaged.
steps.tip: Flow voids on the dorsal cord surface with lower cord oedema suggest a spinal dural arteriovenous fistula.

steps.label: Dura and veins
steps.detail: Assess diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement and venous engorgement.

normal.DURA AND VEINS: No pachymeningeal enhancement; no venous engorgement.

findings: Smooth diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement.
Venous distension sign: convex inferior border of the dominant transverse sinus.
steps.look: Post-contrast T1; sagittal and coronal images of the transverse sinuses (convex lower border).
steps.tip: Diffuse smooth pachymeningeal enhancement with engorged sinuses is the typical cranial pattern.
steps.anatomy_note: Dura and venous structures are not represented in this atlas.

steps.label: Brain sagging
steps.detail: Review midbrain and brainstem sagging, the basal cisterns and tonsillar position.

normal.BRAIN POSITION: No brain sagging; basal cisterns normal.

findings: Sagging of the midbrain with reduced mamillopontine distance and effaced prepontine and suprasellar cisterns.
Low-lying cerebellar tonsils from brain sagging (not a congenital Chiari malformation).
steps.look: Midsagittal T1/T2: suprasellar and prepontine cisterns, mamillopontine distance, midbrain–pons angle, tonsils.
steps.tip: Tonsillar descent from sagging should not be called a Chiari I malformation.
steps.anatomy_note: Only gross cerebellar and fourth-ventricle context is highlighted. Brainstem landmarks and pathological sagging are not represented.

steps.label: Subdural collections
steps.detail: Describe subdural fluid or haematomas, their thickness and mass effect.
findings: Bilateral subdural hygromas, up to __ mm.
Subdural haematoma with mass effect.
steps.look: FLAIR and T1 over both convexities.
steps.anatomy_note: Hemisphere outlines provide orientation only; the dura and subdural collections are not represented.

steps.label: Pituitary and supportive findings
steps.detail: Assess pituitary engorgement and whether the findings fit together.

normal.OTHER SUPPORTIVE FINDINGS: Pituitary normal; no additional supportive findings.

findings: Enlarged hyperaemic pituitary gland.
Findings together give a [high / intermediate / low] Bern score probability.
steps.look: Sagittal images of the pituitary.
steps.tip: The Bern score combines these cranial signs to estimate the likelihood of a spinal CSF leak.
steps.anatomy_note: The pituitary gland and its disease-related changes are not represented in this atlas.

steps.label: Spinal assessment
steps.detail: Describe spinal extradural fluid and leak site only if the spine was studied.
findings: Spinal extradural fluid from [ ] to [ ] (ventral dural tear likely).
Meningeal diverticulum at [ ].
No extradural collection; CSF-venous fistula not excluded.
steps.look: Heavily T2-weighted fat-suppressed spine MRI; dynamic myelography for localisation.
steps.tip: A normal brain MRI does not exclude a spinal CSF leak.
steps.anatomy_note: The brain atlas does not show spinal anatomy, meningeal diverticula or a spinal CSF leak.

steps.label: Gas pattern
steps.detail: Assess the stomach, proximal bowel and distal gas, including gas in the rectum.

normal.GAS PATTERN: Normal neonatal bowel gas pattern with gas in the rectum.

findings: Double bubble with no distal gas (duodenal atresia pattern).
Few dilated proximal loops (high obstruction).
Many dilated loops with no rectal gas (low obstruction).
steps.look: Supine (and horizontal-beam) abdominal radiograph: is there dilatation, how many loops, and is there gas in the rectum?
steps.tip: The number of dilated loops separates high from low obstruction; the rectal gas tells you whether obstruction is complete.

steps.label: Level of obstruction and cause
steps.detail: Describe the distribution and the likely level, and the transition when demonstrated.
findings: Duodenojejunal flexure right of the left pedicle and below the pylorus: malrotation; corkscrew duodenum suggests midgut volvulus.
Microcolon with filling defects in the terminal ileum (meconium ileus pattern).
Transition zone in the rectosigmoid with a rectosigmoid ratio below 1 (Hirschsprung pattern).
Thickened pyloric muscle __ mm, length __ mm (hypertrophic pyloric stenosis).
steps.look: Upper GI study for the duodenojejunal flexure position; contrast enema for colon calibre and transition.
steps.tip: Suspected malrotation with volvulus is an emergency; an upper GI study or ultrasound should not wait.

steps.label: Bowel wall
steps.detail: Assess mural abnormalities: pneumatosis, thickening, peristalsis and perfusion when assessed.

normal.BOWEL WALL: No pneumatosis; normal bowel wall on ultrasound where assessed.

findings: Pneumatosis intestinalis in the [right lower quadrant].
Thickened hypoperfused bowel wall on ultrasound.
steps.look: Radiograph for bubbly or linear intramural gas; ultrasound for wall thickness and Doppler.

steps.label: Free gas and fluid
steps.detail: Look for free gas, ascites and collections.
findings: Pneumoperitoneum (football sign / Rigler sign).
Complex ascites on ultrasound.
steps.look: Horizontal-beam or left lateral decubitus view; football sign and Rigler sign on supine views.

steps.label: Targeted studies and other organs
steps.detail: Record the result of any targeted study, other organ findings and limitations.
findings: Whirlpool sign of the mesenteric vessels on ultrasound (midgut volvulus).
SMV lies to the left of the SMA (malrotation).
Incarcerated inguinal hernia.
steps.look: Ultrasound of the mesenteric vessels (SMV to the right of the SMA; whirlpool sign) when malrotation is suspected.
steps.tip: The gas pattern changes with time and feeding; a normal early radiograph does not exclude an evolving emergency.

steps.label: Organ of origin
steps.detail: Use continuity and organ displacement to localise the cystic mass.
findings: Cystic mass arising from the [right] ovary.
Cyst adjacent to the bowel with a gut signature wall (duplication cyst).
Renal cystic mass / hydronephrosis of the [left] kidney.
steps.look: Ultrasound first: claw sign with an organ, bowel continuity, relation to the kidney, ovary and bladder.
steps.tip: In children the organ of origin, together with age, narrows the differential more than the cyst appearance.

steps.label: Size and number
steps.detail: Record dimensions, multiplicity and distribution.
findings: Solitary cyst __ × __ × __ mm.
Multiple non-communicating cysts of varying size (multicystic dysplastic kidney pattern).
steps.look: Three orthogonal dimensions on ultrasound or MRI.

steps.label: Wall and contents
steps.detail: Assess simple fluid, septa, debris, fat and solid elements.
findings: Simple cyst.
Multiseptated cystic mass (lymphatic malformation pattern).
Cyst with fat and calcification (teratoma).
Echogenic layered contents (haemorrhage or debris).
steps.look: Ultrasound for echoes and septa; MRI or CT for fat and calcification.

steps.label: Flow and communication
steps.detail: Assess vascularity and any ductal, enteric or collecting-system connection.
findings: Cystic dilatation communicating with the common bile duct (choledochal cyst).
Communication with the collecting system (hydronephrosis).
Avascular septa.
steps.look: Doppler of septa and walls; continuity with the bile duct, bowel or renal pelvis.

steps.label: Mass effect and complications
steps.detail: Assess obstruction, torsion, haemorrhage and inflammation.
findings: Enlarged ovary with peripheral follicles and absent flow (torsion).
Bowel obstruction from the cyst.
Haemorrhage within the cyst.
steps.look: Adjacent bowel, ureters and vessels; ovarian flow when an adnexal cyst is present.

steps.label: Organ of origin
steps.detail: Identify the dominant organ or retroperitoneal compartment.
findings: Mass arising from the [right] kidney with a claw sign (nephroblastoma pattern).
Adrenal mass displacing the kidney inferiorly (neuroblastoma pattern).
Mass arising from the liver (hepatoblastoma to be considered in a young child).
steps.look: Ultrasound then MRI: claw sign with the kidney, relation to the adrenal, liver or bowel.
steps.tip: Neuroblastoma encases and lifts vessels and crosses the midline; Wilms tumour displaces vessels and arises from the kidney.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Describe size, solid tissue, necrosis, fat, calcification and enhancement.
findings: Heterogeneous mass __ × __ × __ mm with calcification (neuroblastoma pattern).
Heterogeneous mass with necrosis and no calcification (Wilms pattern).
Fat and calcification (teratoma).
steps.look: Ultrasound and MRI; CT or radiograph for calcification.

steps.label: Vessels
steps.detail: Assess displacement, encasement and intravascular extension.
findings: Encasement of the coeliac axis and SMA.
Tumour thrombus in the IVC.
Displacement of vessels without encasement.
steps.look: Aorta, IVC, coeliac axis, SMA and renal vessels.

steps.label: Local extent
steps.detail: Assess adjacent organs and neural foramina or spinal canal extension.
findings: Extension through the neural foramina into the spinal canal (dumbbell).
Invasion of the [liver / kidney].
steps.look: Axial and coronal MRI through the neural foramina.
steps.tip: Intraspinal extension can compress the cord and needs prompt communication.

steps.label: Nodes and spread
steps.detail: Review nodes and covered metastatic sites.

normal.NODES AND SPREAD: No nodes or metastases in the field.

findings: Retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.
Liver metastases.
Marrow infiltration.
steps.look: Retroperitoneal and mesenteric nodes, liver, bone marrow and lungs when covered.

steps.label: Renal origin
steps.detail: Confirm renal origin, side and pole with the claw sign, and measure the mass.
findings: Mass arising from the [left] kidney, [upper] pole, with a claw of renal parenchyma, __ × __ × __ mm.
steps.look: Ultrasound and MRI coronal images.
steps.tip: A claw of renal parenchyma around the mass confirms renal origin.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Describe solid, cystic or necrotic components, enhancement and calcification.
findings: Large heterogeneous solid mass with necrosis and haemorrhage (Wilms pattern).
Multilocular cystic mass with thin septa (multilocular cystic renal tumour).
Solid mass in a neonate (mesoblastic nephroma).
steps.look: MRI T2, DWI and post-contrast images.

steps.label: Other kidney and nephrogenic rests
steps.detail: Assess the remaining renal tissue and the contralateral kidney for further lesions or rests.

normal.MULTIFOCALITY: Contralateral kidney normal; no further lesions.

findings: Contralateral lesion __ mm (bilateral disease).
Subcapsular homogeneous rests (nephroblastomatosis).
steps.look: Both kidneys on T2 and post-contrast images.
steps.tip: Bilateral disease changes surgical planning; examine the other kidney carefully.

steps.label: Local and venous extent
steps.detail: Assess the capsule, sinus, adjacent tissues and renal vein and IVC thrombus.

normal.LOCAL AND VENOUS EXTENT: No capsular breach; renal vein and IVC patent.

findings: Tumour thrombus in the renal vein extending into the IVC to the [ ] level.
Tumour rupture with retroperitoneal fluid.
steps.look: Renal vein and IVC on ultrasound Doppler and MRI; record the cranial extent of thrombus.

steps.label: Nodes and metastases
steps.detail: Review regional nodes, liver and chest coverage.

normal.NODES AND METASTATIC SITES: No nodes or metastases in the covered field.

findings: Enlarged para-aortic nodes.
Lung metastases on chest CT.
Liver metastases.
steps.look: Retroperitoneal nodes; liver; chest CT for lung metastases.

steps.label: Testes
steps.detail: Record size, echotexture, lie and focal lesions of both testes.

normal.TESTES: Testes symmetric in size and echotexture with normal lie.

findings: Enlarged heterogeneous [left] testis with a horizontal lie.
Testicular rupture: disrupted tunica albuginea with heterogeneous parenchyma.
steps.look: Transverse view of both testes side by side for comparison; longitudinal views.

steps.label: Perfusion
steps.detail: Compare intratesticular arterial and venous flow with the other side using low-flow settings.

normal.DOPPLER: Symmetric intratesticular arterial and venous flow.

findings: Absent intratesticular flow in the [left] testis: testicular torsion.
Reduced flow compared with the other side (partial torsion possible).
Increased flow in the testis and epididymis (orchiepididymitis).
steps.look: Colour or power Doppler with low pulse repetition frequency; spectral waveforms in both testes.
steps.tip: Preserved flow does not exclude partial or intermittent torsion; peripheral hyperaemia is not central perfusion.

steps.label: Spermatic cord and epididymis
steps.detail: Look for twisting of the cord, epididymal enlargement or hyperaemia, and hernia.

normal.CORD AND EPIDIDYMIS: Straight spermatic cord; epididymis normal; no hernia.

findings: Whirlpool sign of the spermatic cord (torsion).
Enlarged hyperaemic epididymis (epididymitis).
Inguinoscrotal hernia containing [bowel / omentum].
steps.look: Follow the cord from the inguinal canal to the testis for a whirlpool sign.
steps.tip: The whirlpool sign of the cord is the most specific sign of torsion.

steps.label: Focal lesion
steps.detail: Describe any focal lesion as intratesticular or extratesticular with size and vascularity.
findings: Avascular nodule at the upper pole with surrounding hyperaemia (torsed appendix testis).
Intratesticular solid vascular mass __ mm.
Intratesticular haematoma.
steps.look: Grayscale and Doppler of any focal lesion.

steps.label: Extratesticular findings
steps.detail: Evaluate hydrocele, haematocele, scrotal wall, collections and varicocele.

normal.EXTRATESTICULAR FINDINGS: No hydrocele or scrotal wall thickening.

findings: Reactive hydrocele.
Haematocele.
Scrotal wall oedema without testicular abnormality (idiopathic scrotal oedema).
steps.look: Scrotal wall thickness; fluid around the testis; veins with Valsalva.

steps.label: Technique and lung volume
steps.detail: Assess rotation, inspiration and lung expansion.

normal.TECHNIQUE AND VOLUME: Supine AP radiograph without rotation; normal lung volumes.

findings: Low lung volumes.
Hyperinflated lungs.
Rotated to the [right].
steps.look: Anterior rib ends and clavicles for rotation; count ribs above the diaphragm.
steps.tip: Rotation and low volumes mimic disease in neonates.

steps.label: Lung pattern
steps.detail: Describe diffuse or focal opacity, air bronchograms and lucencies.
findings: Diffuse granular (ground-glass) opacity with air bronchograms and low volumes (respiratory distress syndrome pattern).
Streaky perihilar opacity with fluid in the fissures and normal or increased volume (transient tachypnoea pattern).
Patchy asymmetric opacity with hyperinflation (meconium aspiration pattern).
Coarse reticular opacity with cystic lucencies (bronchopulmonary dysplasia).
steps.look: Compare both lungs; look for granularity, streaky interstitial opacities or patchy asymmetric opacity.

steps.label: Air leak and pleura
steps.detail: Assess pneumothorax, pneumomediastinum, interstitial emphysema and effusion.
findings: [Right] pneumothorax.
Pneumomediastinum lifting the thymus (spinnaker-sail sign).
Pulmonary interstitial emphysema of the [ ] lung.
steps.look: Anterior pneumothorax on the supine film: a hyperlucent hemithorax and sharp heart border.
steps.tip: On a supine neonatal film, a pneumothorax collects anteriorly: look for a sharp heart border and hyperlucency.

steps.label: Heart, thymus and diaphragm
steps.detail: Assess the cardiothymic silhouette and diaphragm position.
findings: Bowel loops in the left hemithorax with mediastinal shift (congenital diaphragmatic hernia).
Cardiomegaly with increased pulmonary vascularity.
steps.look: Cardiothymic contour; bowel loops in the chest.

steps.label: Lines and tubes
steps.detail: Trace each device and locate its tip using the film anatomy.

normal.LINES AND TUBES: No lines or tubes. / All lines and tubes in satisfactory position.

findings: Endotracheal tube tip at [T2], above the carina.
Umbilical venous catheter tip projects over the [liver / portal vein]; not in the IVC.
Umbilical arterial catheter tip at [T8] (high position).
Gastric tube coiled in an upper oesophageal pouch (oesophageal atresia).
steps.look: Endotracheal tube between the thoracic inlet and carina; UVC tip at the IVC–right atrial junction; UAC in the high (thoracic) or low (below renal arteries) position; gastric tube in the stomach.
steps.tip: An umbilical arterial catheter goes down into the pelvis first (via the iliac artery); a venous catheter goes straight up through the liver.
